title: libmarmot: any member can post as any other member (inner event pubkey not bound to the MLS sender)
description: libmarmot-w19-review C1 (a7c1460d): the inner (rumor) event's pubkey is never checked against the MLS sender leaf's credential identity; Bob posted with Alice's pubkey and Charlie's result reported Alice. Both Marmot specs require the check; RFC 9420 §6.3 also calls for content signatures on application messages. Fix: verify inner pubkey == sender leaf's account identity (and the MLS FramedContent signature if required by the Marmot spec) before delivering; reject otherwise. Pre-existing; affects Gnostr's MLS groups.
notes: Fixed on marmot/w19-ratchet-persist in 6cfa86d5 (docs for review B1/N1 in 8ff2667b). RFC 9420 s6.3.1 signed PrivateMessageContent + s6.3.2 SenderDataAAD (RFC message-protection vector now unprotects end to end and re-signs byte for byte); receiver requires inner pubkey == sender leaf credential identity (live and retained-parent paths, relay and rumor) else MARMOT_ERR_AUTHOR_MISMATCH with no state change; create_message fills a missing pubkey and refuses another account's; dedupe by inner event id. libmarmot 0.9.0 (wire change). Tests: test_member_cannot_post_as_another, test_inner_event_delivered_once, test_failed_message_restores_ratchet, test_sender_data_aad_bound, interop assert_application_priv_unprotects; 7 mutations all caught.

title: libmarmot: persist the MLS secret-tree ratchet (message keys reused and replays accepted after reload)
description:
Found while doing nostrc-qp24.7. mls_group_serialize() stores the epoch secrets but not the secret tree: mls_group_deserialize() re-derives it from encryption_secret (mls_group.c, 'Re-derive the secret tree'), so every load starts each sender's ratchet at generation 0 with no consumed keys.

Consequences:
- Receiver: a message whose kind:445 was re-wrapped in a new envelope (new id, so no processed marker) decrypts again. Verified with a trio probe: Charlie accepts Bob's republished application message (err 0) in the live epoch. The retained-parent late-message path (qp24.7) has the same limit.
- Sender: marmot_create_message() loads the state fresh on every call, so, by reading the code, every message a member sends in an epoch uses generation 0: the same AES-GCM key, with nonces that differ only in the 4-byte reuse guard. This breaks RFC 9420 section 9 (keys used once, deleted after use), loses forward secrecy within the epoch, and risks GCM nonce reuse (a birthday bound of about 2^16 messages per epoch and sender).

Fix: serialize each sender's handshake and application ratchet (generation plus current secret), and the skipped-key cache (bounded), in a new MLS_GROUP_SERIAL_VER. Load older states by starting the own sender's generation past anything possibly used, and document it. Add tests: two sends in one epoch use distinct generations; a replay in a new envelope fails in the live epoch and on the retained-parent path. This is a state-format change (MINOR for 0.x).
notes: Branch marmot/w19-ratchet-persist: a7be92db (libmarmot fix, 0.8.0) + 9a421fe1 (Groundhog crash case, marmot-gobject regression). Bug confirmed empirically: test_sends_use_distinct_generations showed 5 sends at leaf/generation 1/0 x5 before the fix; live and retained-parent replays in a new envelope were accepted. Design: MlsGroup serial format 3 stores per-sender ratchets (next generation + secret, or unused leaf secret) and a skipped-key cache (32 below newest read, forward bound max_forward_distance), no encryption/joiner/welcome secret; failed decrypt restores the ratchet; send stores the step in the op transaction before returning the event; non-transactional receive failures write the previous state back. Legacy formats 1/2: own sender +512 generations; receivers accept a window bounded by max_forward_distance once. Versions: libmarmot 0.8.0; marmot-gobject/gnostr/groundhog no bump. Follow-ups: nostrc-ow0c (snapshot rollback rewinds ratchets), nostrc-dxb9 (MarmotConfig ratchet limits unused), nostrc-yd0q (self-update API, recommended by the advisory).

title: Groundhog CI red at 63f0317d (x86_64): groundhog-net public-only GLib critical; groundhog-media/blossom segfault; sanitizer build -Warray-bounds in test_media.c
description: Hosted run 36582171574 (ubuntu-24.04 x86_64). groundhog job: /groundhog/net/public-only 'g_task_get_cancellable: assertion G_IS_TASK (task) failed' (qi5e 98a5328a GNetworkAddress subclass); groundhog-media and groundhog-blossom SEGFAULT. groundhog-sanitizers build: gcc -Werror=array-bounds errors at tests/media/test_media.c:265,337-339,479 ('outside array bounds of guint8[0]'). comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Hint for the src/net public-only fix (found by the media/blossom agent; not touched): gnome/groundhog/src/net/gh-net-http.c:320 calls g_socket_address_enumerator_next_async(self->inner, g_task_get_cancellable(task), on_inner_next, g_steal_pointer(&task)). C leaves argument evaluation order unspecified. GCC x86_64 evaluates right-to-left, so g_steal_pointer(&task) NULLs task before g_task_get_cancellable(task) runs, which is exactly 'g_task_get_cancellable: assertion G_IS_TASK (task) failed'. arm64/clang go left-to-right, so it passes there. Same root-cause class as the media/blossom segfaults (g_memdup2(g_bytes_get_data(b, &size), size)).

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Media/blossom and sanitizer build: fixed in 674163e6 on fix/w18-amd64-media (not pushed). Root cause: g_memdup2(g_bytes_get_data(b, &size), size). Argument evaluation order is unspecified and GCC x86_64 goes right to left, so size is read as 0 and the copy is NULL, which segfaults. -Warray-bounds 'guint8[0]' is GCC seeing that same size-0 value. Fixed 5 sites plus the same class in tests/nip29 assert_json and nostr-share test_share.c. Test-only change, so no version bump. Verified on amd64 (qemu) and arm64 Docker: groundhog set 68/68, KC-6 and ASAN/UBSAN set 44/44; macOS 65/65. The amd64 all-green result needs the gh-net-http.c:320 hoist, which I applied locally only to verify and did not commit. Without it, groundhog-net /public-only and blossom test 8 (download-address-policy, reachable now that test 3 no longer crashes) fail on x86_64 with the G_IS_TASK critical.

The sanitizer build failed with -Werror=array-bounds at test_attachments.c:714. Fixed in dda60f71 on fix/w18-amd64-g22-attachments (not pushed). title: Groundhog CI (Linux/Xvfb) fails three W16 GUI tests: account-ui header-title-fits, group-ui-gui stale session bus, conversation-menu-gui menu
description: Hosted run 36554068900 at 74ced159 (job groundhog; sanitizers green): groundhog-account-ui /groundhog/account-ui/header-title-fits 'condition waited for at line 361 did not hold within 5s'; groundhog-group-ui-gui 'nostrc-test-bus: the session-bus connection belongs to another bus; something still references a session connection made before this bus came up'; groundhog-conversation-menu-gui /groundhog/conversation-menu-gui/menu 'condition waited for at line 473 did not hold within 5s'. All pass on macOS.
notes: Root causes (reproduced in scripts/groundhog-linux-ci.sh, Ubuntu 24.04 / GTK 4.14.5 / libadwaita 1.5.0 / Xvfb): (1) account-ui: Xvfb has no compositor, so GTK draws .solid-csd (5px border+padding) inside the window; a 360px window has 350px content, and is_laid_out compared content width. Now compares the border box (gtk_widget_compute_bounds). (2) group-ui-gui: gh_test_bus_up() (session-mode bus) ran after adw_init(), whose Linux settings-portal backend already holds the dbus-run-session connection. Now uses a NOT_SESSION bus beside GTK like send-stack.h/requests-gui (new gh_test_bus_up_beside_gtk()). (3) conversation-menu-gui: libadwaita 1.5 opens a dialog's sheet 2 frame ticks after map; force_close before that is lost. Tests wait for gh_test_dialog_shown() (content mapped) before closing (tests/ui/gh-test-dialog.h); also applied to group-ui-gui (join flaked the same way once its bus was fixed) and conversation-info. No product change; version impact: none (test-only + script). Follow-ups: qp24.89, qp24.90.
close_reason: Fixed in d9f44a1d (test-only, pushed); hosted Groundhog opt-in CI success on d9f44a1d; Linux container 62/62 x3.

This is the only combined go/no-go review and does not implement fixes.
design: Depends on E-A/B/C/D and D10, never on A-D epic closure. Any failed mandatory pillar yields NO-GO and remains open; do not narrow scope.
acceptance_criteria: Close only after both local and named external signing providers, ordinary local homes, standalone password-mediated SMB on Explorer/GNOME Files, conventional winbind domain GDM login, lock/unlock, break-glass, migration, disable/revoke/crash/rollback, CMake/Meson installs and security negatives all pass with zero required skips. Confirm no Nostr-to-Kerberos/passwordless claim, no custom GDM patch, no roaming evidence substitution, no unapproved SMB contract, no release/tag column update without tag, and no unresolved high/critical finding. Record exact versions/commands, reviewer identities, evidence paths, residual limitations and explicit GO/NO-GO.

acceptance_criteria: Close only with file:line/command evidence, no password/secret leakage, no account/SID takeover, crash-safe disable/reissue, old credential/replay negatives, actual Explorer and GNOME Files, actual joined-host GDM/winbind/cache/home tests, dedicated-instance revocation semantics, CMake/Meson parity, auth-required/no-FUSE packages, exact 0.2.0/manifest decisions, safe activation/rollback and no required skips. title: [D1] Obtain explicit approval or rejection of the proposed password-mediated standalone SMB contract
description:
Size: S. Product/security decision owner. The proposed v1 is not passwordless SMB and not Nostr-to-Kerberos: a fresh Nostr proof authorizes a dedicated random 24-hour Samba password for a managed standalone server, which the user enters into unmodified Explorer/GNOME Files. Record explicit authorized approval, requested amendments, or rejection before Phase 0b/implementation. State credential display/clipboard/export UX, caching limitations, active-session semantics, independent server mapping/revocation and dedicated-instance forced disconnect.

## Alternatives Considered
1. Approve the proposed standard-client password bridge with the documented limits. 2. Amend duration, delivery or revocation policy while preserving the same fundamental contract, then re-review Phase 0b. 3. Reject it and stop the mandatory standalone pillar pending a separately specified passwordless/KDC/certificate federation program. Silent omission or treating PAM/Nostr as SMB auth is not an alternative.
design: No implementation or feasibility claim. This decision blocks standalone Phase 0b and all standalone SMB code, but not the independent domain route.
acceptance_criteria: Done only with an explicit human decision and dated rationale in the bead. Approval must acknowledge password reuse window, NT-hash exposure, standard-client caching, no guaranteed active-session termination on rotation, separate workstation/server authority, and that forced revocation restarts the dedicated instance. Rejection blocks the required standalone pillar and triggers a separately reviewed federation/product redesign; it must not be interpreted as permission to silently omit the pillar. The plan alone is not approval.
notes: User approval requested for the proposed dedicated Samba password contract. No answer received; must not equate Nostr proof with native passwordless SMB or Kerberos. Portable independent work may proceed; credential issuance D3/D5 gated.

title: [C4] Enforce signed NIP-46 response admission and active-request correlation
description: Size: L. Protocol security owner. Before decrypting, validate outer canonical ID/signature, expected author, recipient p-tag, kind and configured transport mode; after decrypt, correlate only active request ID/method/purpose and preserve recognized intermediate auth_url state. Reject unsolicited, wrong-recipient/sender, malformed, late, cancelled, duplicate and cross-session responses. Affected files: nip46_session.c, nip46_msg.c, new tests/test_signed_response_admission.c.
design: Depends on C3 plus C1/C2 transitively. Relay AUTH may use only configured client transport identity, never implicit user signing.
acceptance_criteria: Done with valid response positives for equal and different signer-transport/user keys and negatives for bad ID/signature, unexpected author, missing/wrong/duplicate recipient, wrong kind/mode/request/method, replay across session/reboot, cancelled/expired response, malformed ciphertext/result/error, duplicate terminal and auth_url followed by terminal. Rejection occurs before secret-dependent side effects where applicable; atomic one-winner is proven under TSan. Upstream assumptions are not substituted for local admission tests.
notes: RESIDUAL (C4): auth_url intermediate NIP-46 responses currently parse as a normal result and are delivered as-is (provider_nip46 treats as error). Full auth_url intermediate/terminal state distinction needs a separate channel - follow-up, not blocking the signed-response admission work which is merged (commit 27bbe574).

title: [C3] Replace NIP-46 polling with event-driven subscription-before-publish relay lifecycle
description: Size: L. Relay lifecycle owner. Register session ownership before transport start; establish response subscription before each publish; accept live ephemeral responses without EOSE; restore on reconnect; replace startup/late-publish polling with state callbacks; handle OK reject, CLOSED, AUTH, disconnect and reconnect distinctly; reuse the same request/event identity across transport retry. Affected files: nip46_session.c and new tests/test_relay_lifecycle.c; narrowly extend libnostr relay hooks only if Phase contract proves missing. No sleep approximation.
design: Depends on C2. Any libnostr API addition is narrow, tested, and version-assessed by D.
acceptance_criteria: Done when deterministic controlled-relay tests cover late connect, multi-relay ordering, subscription failure, publish OK rejection, CLOSED, AUTH using transport identity only, disconnect/reconnect, no EOSE, duplicate delivery and cancel during reconnect. Assertions prove subscription precedes publish and one approval request identity is reused. No polling/sleep-based production workaround; sanitizer/race runs clean. Reconcile but do not duplicate nostrc-4cp F22/F25 and closed nostrc-0y02/4x9 behavior.

title: [C2] Add deadline/cancellation request ownership and fix callback plus GLib lifetimes
description: Size: L. NIP-46 lifecycle owner. Add request-options with absolute monotonic deadline and cancellation handle while retaining old signatures as wrappers; give pending requests explicit refs and atomic one-winner terminal completion; include connect/pacing/publish/wait in deadline; preserve intermediate states; honor caller-owned callback result/error; retain session in GLib tasks and route cancellation. Affected files: nip46_session.c, include/nostr/nip46/{nip46_client.h,nip46_types.h,nip46_client_g.h}, src/glib/nip46_client_g.c, tests/test_request_lifecycle.c, test_glib_lifetime.c.
design: Depends on C1 and C0. Published caller-owned contract is authoritative; a borrowed alternative requires a separately named API.
acceptance_criteria: Done when enumerated callers free exactly once; NULL callback, literal error, allocation failure, timeout/cancel/response races, session shutdown during callback, GLib task teardown, reentrant cancel, and late/duplicate completion are leak/double-free/UAF clean under ASan/TSan. Cancellation interrupts active RPC and deadline includes every phase. Old API behavior is covered by compatibility tests. Inspect live nostrc-4cp work but do not mark this complete from its notes or older app task closures.

title: [C1] Separate NIP-46 secret roles and harden URI/message parsing and request identity
description: Size: M. NIP-46 core owner. Separate connect authorization token from independent client transport secret; generate cryptographically random request IDs; harden bunker URI and message parsing against malformed escapes, embedded NUL, unbounded collections, duplicate/invalid fields, allocation failure and unsafe JSON IDs/errors; preserve partial-parse cleanup. Affected files: nips/nip46/src/core/{nip46_session.c,nip46_uri.c,nip46_msg.c}, tests focused on URI/messages. No broker, root build/version edits.
design: Depends on C0. Additive wire-compatible hardening; no invented NIP-46 version.
acceptance_criteria: Done when official/compatibility fixtures still pass and negatives cover token-as-key regression, empty/oversize/duplicate relay/token fields, percent-encoding/NUL, allocation failure, non-string/intermediate response forms, malicious ID/error escaping, request-ID collision simulation, and cleanup under ASan/UBSan. Token is used only for connect authorization; transport key persists separately; user pubkey comes from RPC. Reuse allowed relay examples only. Current code is tested, not assumed from nostrc-80qa closure.

title: [B6] Prove both-provider real GDM login, lock/unlock, recovery, and fault matrix
description: Size: M. Desktop acceptance owner. Run installed pinned GDM/PAM/systemd/logind cycles for local and external providers, provider choice, lock/unlock, suspend/resume, unknown/disabled users, route isolation, broker/provider/UI crash, greeter restart, reboot, console recovery and home/logind environment. B owns its redacted traces/recordings and machine-readable case bundle; D alone edits docs/ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md and registers tests/packages.
design: Final B installed gate; documentation, containers and synthetic pam tests cannot close it.
acceptance_criteria: Done only with 100 automated login/logout cycles per provider using cryptographic signers, at least 20 observed approvals for each claimed real external client, zero success in all negative/fault cases, no lingering workers, NSS p95 warm <10ms/cold <100ms on reference VM, local proof login <5s after passphrase excluding deliberate delay, and all external outcomes within 180s. Verify no user bus/home/Secret Service before proof and no automatic keyring/encrypted-home claim. D0, A5, B5 and C real-provider acceptance must exist; missing GDM lab or mock-only run keeps open.
notes: B6 nip46-at-greeter CLOSED 2026-09-22 (merge 9e9a8753): both providers now proven at the real gdm-password stack + live greeter — local-vault (earlier) and NIP-46 (QR via nostrconnect over nos.lol; pre-paired bunker via the one-time bundle over sharegap: authenticate (nip46) -> ok). Remaining for full B6: lock/unlock fresh-screen reauth + fault matrix.

title: [B5] Deliver standard GDM provider UX, fresh screen reauthentication, and protected post-login SMB prompt/display
description: Size: M. Desktop UX owner. Configure/document unmodified pinned GDM PAM conversation for provider selection, hidden local input, external approval text, cancellation and deadline. Determine actual login/unlock PAM service and peer credentials; implement purpose-limited fresh unlock proof if same-UID is required, without opening BeginLogin broadly. Implement nostr-auth-ui protected same-UID SMB unlock/display/explicit clipboard behavior; no custom greeter, QR/browser launch, attachment endpoint or persistent credential-store entry. Affected files: src/ui/nostr-auth-ui.c, packaging/gdm/README.md, PAM profile integration fixtures.
design: Depends on B4. D owns package activation files/build integration; D standalone SMB contract supplies server fields but B owns only reusable protected UX.
acceptance_criteria: Done when pinned GDM visibly renders exact prompts with hidden local input and cancel propagation; private-key canary never enters PAM; project-owned passphrase copies/logs/argv/env/core/disk are clean; unlock after idle and suspend requires a fresh proof and no second home session; provider/unavailability/denial are distinguishable without leaking secrets; console break-glass remains usable. Post-login SMB prompt derives own UID, uses same user.sock connection, clears clipboard best-effort after 30s with warning, and cannot attach to another transaction. Real GDM parts remain open until D0.
notes: 2026-09-23: NIP-05 login identifier live on the rig — type chebizarro@coinos.io at Not listed? -> resolves to n_bizarro (PAM_USER canonicalized) -> greeter shows avatar + Biz + NIP-05 line + centered QR from the real broker artifact (zbarimg-verified). Maintainer phone retest pending. Polish nit: avatar renders square (circle clip not applied to image actor).

title: [B4] Replace cache-auth PAM flow with broker proof, account policy, and local-session receipts
description: Size: L. PAM/Linux owner. Keep exported PAM signatures while implementing authenticate provider selection/hidden input/progress/cancel, pam_set_data connection/receipt cleanup, account readiness, no-op setcred, session revalidation/reference and best-effort close. Remove cache-presence success, session-bus signer, Homed1/FUSE/environment synthesis and XDG_RUNTIME_DIR assignment. Package exact Nostr/domain/local policy graph without globally sufficient fallback. Affected files: src/pam/pam_nostr.c, include/pam_nostr.h, packaging/pam/nostr-auth, integration/test_pam_broker.c. Root/install build wiring remains D-owned.
design: Depends on B1-B3 plus A authority/NSS/home code children; standard PAM conversation only, no greeter patch.
acceptance_criteria: Done when only exact n_ namespace enters Nostr branch; absent reserved name is fatal, non-Nostr is PAM_IGNORE, and every broker result maps as specified. Both-provider prompt accepts only local/remote, max three bad choices, no default/silent failover; hidden local input never enters PAM_AUTHTOK; responses and module copies wipe on all returns. Re-auth on same handle cancels old attempt; auth failure cannot open; disable/generation/home change between proof and session blocks open; pam_end cleanup invalidates receipts. Local/domain name collision and cross-route fallback negatives pass. Synthetic PAM tests are necessary but not real-GDM acceptance.
notes: 2026-09-22 (B6 real-GDM cross-reference): the broker-backed pam_nostr flow implemented under B4 has now been proven through the REAL /etc/pam.d/gdm-password (via pam-auth-update common-auth stacking), not just synthetic /etc/pam.d/nostr-login. pamtester on gdm-password + login: correct passphrase → PAM_SUCCESS, wrong → PAM_AUTH_ERR / PAM_MAXTRIES, unknown → user_unknown (falls through), local Unix users unaffected. Broker verdicts logged in auth.log correlate: 'nostr: authenticate n_gdm (local) -> ok / invalid_proof', 'nostr: begin_login b6local -> unknown_account'. Evidence: docs/reviews/b6-gdm-login-2026-09-22.md.

title: [B3] Implement encrypted local-key vault, provider worker, enrollment, and recovery
description: Size: L. Local-provider/security owner. Implement versioned OpenSSL scrypt plus AES-256-GCM vault, protected input/enrollment proof, locked non-dumpable secret buffers, descriptor-only sandbox worker, exact challenge signing, explicit wipes, no cross-transaction cache, passphrase change/backup restore/same-key reenroll/acknowledged identity replacement, and nostr-authctl command dispatch calling A handler APIs. Affected files: src/auth/{auth_vault.c,provider_local.c,nostr-auth-provider.c}, src/ctl/nostr-authctl.c, B-owned local worker systemd/AppArmor, unit/test_auth_vault.c, integration/test_provider_local.c. No A identity implementation or D root/build/version/Samba units.
design: Depends on B2 and A1. Passphrase min 12 bytes/max 1024, no normalization/trimming. Version contributes to homed 0.2.0.
acceptance_criteria: Done when fixed supported KDF parameters and bounds are enforced; random salt/nonce and length-prefixed AAD bind provider/account/pubkey/generation; wrong passphrase and tamper are indistinguishable to user; invalid scalar/pubkey mismatch fails; passphrase/key/derived material wipe on every success/failure/cancel/kill; memory/core/log/argv/env/persistent canaries are absent; two-worker memory limit and excess rate limiting hold; enrollment cannot enable until decrypt/sign/verify succeeds. Run 100 offline transactions with no home, user bus, keyring or network, plus cancel/kill and corruption tests. Do not claim copies inside GDM are wiped.

title: [B2] Implement immutable challenge construction and strict single-use proof verification
description: Size: L. Security owner. Build private never-published kind-1 challenge events, central application-kind constant, exact Jansson content, ordered tags, monotonic deadlines, complete signed-event parse/validation, authority/key-generation recheck, atomic one-winner transition and connection-bound receipts. Affected files: src/auth/auth_challenge.c, auth_transaction.c, unit/test_auth_challenge.c; reuse libnostr validation unchanged.
design: Depends on B0 and B1. Use existing nostr_event_validate and exact immutable challenge comparison; do not invent crypto.
acceptance_criteria: Done when valid bound proof succeeds and all mutations fail: old 128-char fake signature; event ID/signature; pubkey; kind; timestamp; content byte; tag value/order; nonce; authority/boot/account/username/UID/key_generation; service/purpose/resource; expired/cancelled/late/duplicate/replayed/other-connection response; disable or generation change during verification. Proofs are never published or normally logged. 100 consecutive bounded local verifier operations pass and zero negative accepts occur under ASan/UBSan/TSan as applicable. Only verifier can transition to VERIFIED.

title: [B1] Implement credential-bound broker IPC, transaction state, throttling, and cancellation
description: Size: L. Auth broker owner. Implement SOCK_SEQPACKET protocol/client, auth.sock and user.sock endpoints, SO_PEERCRED plus pidfd/process-start binding, same-connection transaction ownership, one-main-context state machine, deadlines, receipts/session references, worker supervision, max 8 transactions/2 scrypt workers, persistent rate limits, cancellation/kill/reap, strict auth config, audit redaction, broker/worker systemd and AppArmor. Affected files: src/auth/{nostr-authd.c,auth_protocol.c,auth_client.c,auth_peer.c,auth_transaction.c,auth_provider.c,nostr-auth-provider.c,auth_config.c}, include/nostr_auth_{protocol,client}.h, config/auth.conf.sample, systemd/nostr-auth*, packaging/apparmor/usr.sbin.nostr-authd, integration/test_broker_peers.c. No A identity internals or D root/build/version/Samba units.
design: Depends on B0. user.sock derives own account from kernel UID and only permits own SMB proof transaction operations. Authentication/account data comes through A interfaces; no cache-only fallback.
acceptance_criteria: Done when malformed packets, duplicate JSON keys, truncation, ancillary mismatch, wrong endpoint/op, wrong UID/PID/connection, transferred FD, wrong target/purpose/generation, cross-transaction SubmitUnlock, unprivileged admin operation, queue overflow and worker-origin client op fail before side effects. Disconnect/pid death/restart/cancel mark terminal first, erase input, kill/reap within 3s, PAM-facing ack within 1s, and late completion cannot mint a receipt. Restart preserves rate-limit policy but no proof/receipt. Sanitizer and fault-injection tests required; logging excludes all secrets/full proofs.
notes: 2026-09-21 Persistent rate-limit MERGED (a94a448d) + VM-verified: nh_auth_ratelimit_open_persistent (SQLite ratelimit_entries, WAL, wall-clock for the persistent variant) survives broker restart; opt-in via nh_auth_broker_set_ratelimit_path / NH_AUTH_RATELIMIT_PATH; in-memory mode preserved. homed_ratelimit_persist portable test passes (cooldown+reset survive close/reopen). 22/22 in loop. REMAINING B1: scrypt worker supervision + cancellation/reap.

title: [A-R1] Fix WarmCache relay-list use-after-free with ASan regression
description:
Size: S. Required experimental-roaming safety follow-up, explicitly outside local-home critical path and not a release prerequisite for A-E. Move relay ownership cleanup after the final nh_fetch_latest_secrets_json use and audit every early-exit cleanup. Affected file: gnome/nostr-homed/src/ctl/nostr-homectl.c around historical lines 309-314; add a focused relay-lifetime regression.

## Steps to Reproduce
In an ASan build, drive nh_warm_cache through a path with owned relay URLs and a subsequent secrets fetch. The current sequence frees relays and then passes the freed array to nh_fetch_latest_secrets_json; retain the pre-fix ASan UAF trace as counterfactual evidence.
design: No dependency and no downstream release/review dependency. Preserve unrelated roaming semantics.
acceptance_criteria: Done only when ASan reproduces the pre-fix use-after-free, the counterfactual fails, the corrected valid/error paths are leak/UAF clean, and the focused roaming test passes. Do not infer production readiness for roaming and do not couple this fix to the new authority.

title: [A5] Prove authority, migration, NSS, and local-home behavior on the pinned Linux lab
description: Size: M. A integration owner. Run the complete A data/ABI/filesystem matrix on the pinned disposable Linux image, including upgrade from reviewed legacy cache and rollback preserving ownership. Evidence commands include getent passwd n_test, id n_test, concurrent lookup loops during projection replacement, authority/projection consistency report, filesystem stat/mount/label inspection, disk-full and crash recovery. A owns its machine-readable evidence bundle and hands immutable paths/hashes to D; D alone edits docs/ACCEPTANCE_MATRIX.md and registers build/acceptance scripts.

acceptance_criteria: Done only with machine-readable pass/fail/skip inventory, exact packages/images, zero required skips, negative evidence for conflicts/corruption/symlinks/mounts/disk-full, and rollback retaining UID/GID/home ownership. Missing D0 lab keeps this open. A passing SQLite unit suite, container-only test, or documentation cannot close it.

A5 NSS fail-closed acceptance evidence complete.

title: [A4] Provision ordinary local homes with descriptor-safe staging and crash reconciliation
description: Size: L. Linux filesystem owner. Implement enrollment-time /home staging, safe /etc/skel copy, descriptor-relative ownership/modes/labels, no-replace rename, fsync, explicit adoption, operations.phase recovery, home validation and repair_required handling behind identity-owned handler APIs. Affected files: src/identity/local_home.c, identity_store.c, identity-owned tests. B owns command dispatch and AppArmor/systemd policy; D owns root build/version. No FUSE, Blossom, Homed1 or user signer.
design: Depends on A0, A1, and A3. Account becomes active only after home verification and projection publication.
acceptance_criteria: Done when fault injection kills after reserved/staged/installed/projected/complete and retry is idempotent; symlink traversal, mount, wrong owner/mode, existing unexpected/nonempty directory, parent writability, shell not in /etc/shells, label failure, cross-filesystem rename, and disk-full fail closed. Never recursively chown or delete ambiguous data. Real Linux evidence verifies /home ownership 0700, labels, reboot recovery and two concurrent sessions do not remove/disrupt the home. Portable tests may precede D0; installed claims require D0.
notes: 2026-09-20 A4 home provisioning wired + verified (master eb8b1c50). identity_home.c (nh_identity_home_prepare: descriptor-relative /home staging, safe skel copy, chown uid:gid, fsync, renameat2 RENAME_NOREPLACE adoption, evidence recording, repair_required on ambiguity) was implemented but never compiled — now in nostr_identity_core. nh-seed-authority provisions a real /home/<user> via it. title: [A3] Build atomic read-only NSS projection and correct passwd/group/initgroups semantics
description: Size: L. NSS owner. Implement minimal identity_reader, complete same-directory SQLite snapshot publication, and read-only libnss_nostr projection lookups. Correct initgroups membership, duplicate, limit, ERANGE/ENOMEM, NOTFOUND/UNAVAIL semantics while preserving existing ABI/caller buffers/per-call connections. Affected files: src/identity/identity_reader.c, identity_projection.c, src/nss/nss_nostr.c, include/nss_nostr.h, config/nss.conf.sample, unit/test_identity_projection.c, integration/test_nss_readonly.c. No crypto/network or root build edits.
design: Depends on A0 and A1. Never mutate an installed snapshot inode. Projection lag cannot authorize because B consults authority.
acceptance_criteria: Done when unprivileged lookups create no file/schema/journal/WAL and make no network calls; missing/corrupt snapshots return UNAVAIL; undersized buffers return TRYAGAIN/ERANGE; non-Nostr initgroups returns NOTFOUND; limits and duplicates are correct; disabled users remain resolvable; enrolling/repair-required users are not login-ready; concurrent readers survive atomic rename; disk-full/build failure preserves prior snapshot; fsync/permissions are asserted. Portable SQLite tests plus real Linux getent/id evidence are required; the latter is blocked on D0. ABI symbols remain unchanged.
notes: 2026-09-20 NSS runtime now BUILDS and INSTALLS and is verified on real Linux (Ubuntu 24.04 arm64). Added NOSTR_HOMED_ENABLE_NSS -> libnss_nostr.so.2 (commit 0bf2c52f) linking the tested identity_core reader; deps libsqlite3+libc only, all 5 _nss_nostr_* entry points exported. End-to-end getent/id verified against a seeded read-only projection: getpwnam/getpwuid/getgrnam/getgrgid + initgroups (primary gid) correct; disabled users resolvable; unknown -> NOTFOUND. Repeatable acceptance script run_nss_getent.sh (commit 09a0b50a) asserts 6/6 with clean teardown. REMAINING for A3/A5: full negative matrix on pinned lab (corrupt/missing snapshot UNAVAIL, ERANGE/TRYAGAIN buffer paths, symlink/mount rejection, concurrent atomic-rename readers, disk-full preserves prior snapshot) and supplementary-group membership beyond primary gid.

title: [A2] Implement collision-safe allocation, legacy takeover refusal, migration report, and reviewed import

Replace hash authority with lowest-unused persistent allocation in reserved ranges; harden legacy cache against UID/name/GID/home identity takeover; add read-only migration-report and explicit per-account import-reviewed flows. Affected files: src/identity/identity_migrate.c, identity_store.c, src/common/nostr_cache.c, include/nostr_cache.h, tests/unit/test_cache.c, test_uid_map.c, unit/test_identity_migration.c. Preserve legacy hash helper only as labeled legacy behavior.

Approved legacy UID/GID exceptions persist; import requires fresh provider proof and never infers rightful ownership from a surviving overwritten row. Produce redacted before/after migration reports and retry evidence. Focused tests must demonstrate the old ON CONFLICT takeover counterfactual fails. No automatic roaming copy/unmount.

title: [A1] Implement sole-writer identity authority and root administration lifecycle
description: Size: L. Identity/storage owner. Implement private authority.db schema/user_version, serialized writes, metadata/generations, accounts/identities/providers/operations, and identity/admin handler APIs for enrollment lifecycle, disable/enable/retire/replace/change/repair/check/inspect/export. acceptance_criteria: Done when focused tests prove unique immutable username/uid/gid/home/pubkey ownership, no implicit active state, retired IDs never recycle, operation-id retry idempotence, current-generation recheck, disable/replace cancellation signals, root-only secret-safe CLI output, WAL/foreign-key/durability behavior, corrupt/unsupported schema refusal, disk-full rollback, and at least two concurrent enrollments cannot claim the same resource. Run both build-system-exposed identity tests in isolated paths plus ASan/UBSan; retain command/output evidence. No test-only private function or schema document counts as wiring.

title: [C0] Audit NIP-46 callers and freeze additive lifecycle/provider compatibility contract
description: Size: M. Nostr protocol owner. Enumerate every current callback/async caller and actual ownership, inspect current code including live nostrc-4cp overlap, and freeze the additive absolute-deadline/cancellation/request API, caller-owned callback result/error contract, URI/token/transport-key roles, signer transport/user-key roles, NIP-44 v2-only profile, relay lifecycle/admission expectations, and named real-signer contingency. acceptance_criteria: Done when a checked caller inventory records ownership and terminal paths; old APIs remain specified as wrappers; NULL callback, literal error, timeout, cancel, duplicate, late, intermediate auth_url, and reconnect states have explicit outcomes; transport key and connect token are never conflated; get_public_key_rpc establishes enrolled user identity without assuming equality or inequality with signer transport key; Amber or another named signer has pinned capability criteria and failure contingency. Define include/nostr_auth_protocol.h plus docs/AUTH_PROTOCOL.md: 64-KiB SOCK_SEQPACKET framing, duplicate-key rejection, result taxonomy, exact operation x endpoint x SO_PEERCRED/pidfd ACL with default deny, transaction/receipt binding, account-generation rechecks, immutable challenge bytes, PAM return mapping, exact local/remote prompt grammar and retry budget, secret packet limits/wiping boundary, worker descriptor launch and cancellation. title: [D0] Provision and pin the real Linux desktop, Samba, AD, relay, signer, and Windows acceptance lab
description: Size: M. Required: snapshot-capable Ubuntu 24.04 amd64 GDM/GNOME VM with console break-glass; standalone Samba VM; separate Samba AD DC and joined desktop VM; Windows 11 24H2 client; GNOME Files/GVfs client; deterministic relay fault injector; controllable cryptographic NIP-46 signer; named real external signer/device; package repository snapshot; network/clock/disk/process/database fault injection. title: Signet: persistent NIP-46 client bindings — pair once, reconnect without connect_secret
description: Provisioned agents (identity custodied in Signet, never exported) cannot autonomously recover their NIP-46 session after restart: the connect_secret is single-use and the agent cannot sign a self-service reissue without its identity key. Root cause: Signet verifies the client_pubkey<->agent binding during the secret-authorized first connect but does not persist it, so the verified binding is forgotten. Fix (standard bunker behavior, cf. nsecbunker/Amber): (1) new table agent_clients(agent_id, client_pubkey, bound_at, last_used, revoked_at); (2) on first connect, consume the secret AND record the binding in the same transaction; (3) on reconnect, resolve the agent by bound non-revoked client_pubkey and accept connect (and requests) with no secret; (4) deny-list precedence unchanged; (5) management ops agent/list-clients + agent/revoke-client; (6) agent/reissue-connect remains the forced-re-pair tool for lost/compromised client keys. Security: binding is created under the one-time secret's authority (same trust root as today); reconnects prove possession of the bound client key per-request via NIP-44; nothing claimed/spoofable. Restores full restart autonomy for provisioned agents without exporting identity keys.
acceptance_criteria: Restarted provisioned agent with persistent nip46Secret reconnects with no connect_secret, no provisioner, no ExecStartPre hack; unknown client pubkeys still rejected; revoked binding rejects reconnect; deny-listed agent cannot reconnect; first-connect secret consumption + binding recorded atomically; reissue-connect still forces re-pairing; tests cover all paths.
close_reason: Persistent NIP-46 client bindings implemented: agent_clients table (identity-pinned, secret-hash recorded), atomic consume+bind transaction, connect accepts secretless/own-stale-secret reconnects from bound clients while arbitrary wrong secrets fail, per-request resolution via the persistent table (revocation immediate, coalesced last_used writes), deny-list injected into NIP-46 server (suspension precedence on all paths), revocation revokes bindings, mgmt agent/list-clients + agent/revoke-client + signetctl commands, docs. Oracle-reviewed: P0 atomicity + revocation race fixed via single-txn pairing + identity pinning; deny bypass fixed; hot-path write coalesced. 8 binding tests incl. daemon-restart recovery, stale/wrong secret, suspension, rotation invalidation, reprovision resurrection guard; full suite 17/17. Provisioned agents now recover restarts autonomously with zero plugin changes (openclaw-nostr sends its stale secret, Signet accepts via hash-pinned binding). Follow-up nostrc-3ga (reply routing race), new bead for transactional revocation.

title: Signet: D-Bus Credentials interface leaks credentials and mints fake sessions
description: dbus_common.c credential handlers do not enforce per-agent scoping and do not perform real credential exchange. (1) GetToken (dbus_common.c:396-426) looks up a secret by credential TYPE only, ignoring the caller's agent_id, then returns the DECRYPTED payload hex-encoded to the caller. Any authenticated D-Bus/TCP client can retrieve any credential of a given type regardless of ownership. (2) GetSession (dbus_common.c:346-393) generates a random 32-byte token locally and returns it with a 24h expiry; it never exchanges the stored credential with a service (no session_broker/HTTP). In store-less mode it returns an untracked opaque token; with a store it records a lease keyed by token hash but the token is still just random bytes. README claims GetSession 'exchanges a stored credential for a service session token'.
acceptance_criteria: 1) GetToken requires and enforces agent_id ownership of the credential; unauthorized access is denied. 2) GetToken returns a leased/brokered token, not the raw stored secret (or is explicitly documented as returning the credential with tight authz). 3) GetSession performs real credential exchange via session_broker (or fails closed when no service configured) rather than minting a random bearer token. 4) Tests cover cross-agent denial and exchange behavior.
notes: Evidence: dbus_common.c:346 randombytes_buf token; :358 store-less opaque token; :396-426 GetToken by type, no agent_id, returns payload hex. Also D-Bus TCP shares this dispatch.
close_reason: Fixed the P0 authz leak: GetToken now enforces per-agent ownership (returns NotFound + audits deny on mismatch) across D-Bus Unix and TCP; store-less GetSession refuses instead of minting an untracked token. NOTE: the store-backed GetSession still issues a Signet-minted, lease-tracked bearer token rather than performing an external service credential-exchange (the session_broker path, hardened in nostrc-e5y, does real exchange but takes a credential_id, not a service_url). Wiring D-Bus GetSession through a real service exchange is a design enhancement, not a leak; deferred.

title: Signet: revoke_agent bypasses deny list, lease revocation, and revocation audit
description: Management REVOKE_AGENT handler (mgmt_protocol.c:475) calls only signet_key_store_revoke_agent(h->keys, agent_id), which wipes the key from cache/store. It does NOT call the full revocation path in revocation.c (signet_revoke_agent), so the agent pubkey is NEVER added to the deny list, active leases are NOT revoked, and no revocation audit entry is written. README states revoke 'adds to deny list' and 'deny list takes precedence over all other authorization'. Consequence: a revoked agent that already holds a live NIP-46 session/lease, or that gets re-provisioned, is not actually denied.
acceptance_criteria: 1) REVOKE_AGENT adds the agent pubkey to the SQLCipher deny list. 2) Active leases/sessions for the agent are revoked. 3) A revocation audit entry is recorded. 4) After revoke, any subsequent request from that pubkey is denied by deny-list precedence even if a session/policy would allow it. 5) Test proves deny-list precedence post-revoke.
notes: Evidence: mgmt_protocol.c:475 signet_key_store_revoke_agent only; revocation.c signet_revoke_agent unused by mgmt path.
close_reason: Implemented: mgmt REVOKE_AGENT now resolves the agent pubkey and calls signet_revoke_agent (deny-list add + lease burn + key wipe + audit) via the shared live deny list wired through signet_mgmt_handler_set_deny_list in signetd_main. Falls back to cache-only key wipe when no persistent store. Builds clean; deny-precedence e2e test tracked by nostrc-4dp.

title: Signet: bootstrap tokens are not single-use (consume never called; replayable)
description: POST /bootstrap (bootstrap_server.c handle_auth) verifies a token via signet_store_verify_bootstrap_token() (line ~204) and then binds a handoff secret via signet_store_bind_bootstrap_token_handoff() (line ~283), but NEVER calls signet_store_consume_bootstrap_token(). verify only increments attempt_count; it does not set used_at. So a valid token can be redeemed repeatedly until it hits max_attempts or expiry, contradicting the README 'single-use bootstrap tokens' guarantee. The consume function exists but is dead code on this path. Token verify+attempt-increment is also split across two non-atomic SQL statements (store_tokens.c:44 UPDATE then :61 SELECT), racy under concurrency, and lookup uses ordinary SQL equality (not constant-time).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A token that successfully mints a bunker URI is marked used (used_at set) atomically and cannot be redeemed again (returns ALREADY_USED). 2) verify+consume is a single transaction or otherwise race-safe. 3) Test: redeem once succeeds, second redeem of same token fails with ALREADY_USED.
notes: Evidence: bootstrap_server.c:204 verify, :283 bind_handoff, no consume; store_tokens.c:44,61,91 (used_at never set on verify); signet_store_consume_bootstrap_token exists but unused on /bootstrap.
close_reason: Implemented: POST /bootstrap now calls signet_store_consume_bootstrap_token after minting the URI, atomically marking the token used (UPDATE ... WHERE used_at IS NULL). Concurrent/replayed redemptions are rejected with 403 token already used. Builds clean; single-use regression test tracked by nostrc-4dp.

title: Signet: SQLCipher at-rest encryption is not enforced (silent plaintext DB)
description: store.c opens the DB with plain sqlite3_open() then runs PRAGMA key, but if PRAGMA key fails (regular SQLite, not SQLCipher) the error is swallowed: store.c:255-259 comment 'If this is regular SQLite ... We continue'. CMakeLists.txt:40,131 links PkgConfig::SQLITE3 (plain sqlite3), NOT sqlcipher. Result: in default builds the DB is unencrypted at rest. There is no PRAGMA cipher_version verification and no keyed-read validation. README claims 'AES-256 encrypted SQLite database'. Worse, agents.connect_secret and bootstrap token/handoff secrets are stored as plaintext TEXT (store.c:117), so with no SQLCipher these secrets sit in cleartext on disk. Envelope encryption only covers encrypted_nsec and secret payloads, not connect secrets.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Build links SQLCipher (or fails loudly if unavailable when encryption is required). 2) On open, verify SQLCipher is active (PRAGMA cipher_version non-empty AND a keyed read of sqlite_master succeeds); refuse to start (or require explicit opt-in) if the DB is unencrypted. 3) connect_secret and bootstrap handoff secrets are either envelope-encrypted or documented+gated. 4) Test proves DB bytes on disk contain no plaintext connect_secret and that a wrong key fails to open.
notes: Evidence: store.c:236 sqlite3_open; store.c:251-259 PRAGMA key failure ignored; CMakeLists.txt:40,131-132; store.c:117 connect_secret TEXT plaintext.
close_reason: Implemented runtime SQLCipher detection + keyed-read validation + optional hard enforcement (SIGNET_REQUIRE_ENCRYPTED_DB) + meson -Dsignet_use_sqlcipher build option. Default plain-sqlite build now warns loudly instead of silently claiming encryption. Remaining: connect_secret is still plaintext when SQLCipher is off (mitigated by the warning/enforcement; envelope-encrypting connect_secret tracked separately if desired). At-rest test tracked by nostrc-23g.

title: Signet production-readiness: eliminate fake/incomplete security behavior
description: Umbrella epic tracking a deep app-wide review of the signet NIP-46 bunker (2026-07-03). A read-only audit across all subsystems (sign path, storage/crypto, mgmt protocol, auth/bootstrap, transports, config, tests) found multiple places where the code reports success without performing its stated security work, with no TODO/marker comments. Child issues capture each defect with file:line evidence. Priorities: P0 = at-rest encryption + authz/replay/revocation correctness; P1 = fail-open behavior, transport auth, delivery integrity, fake tests; P2 = doc/impl mismatches and hardening.
notes: Children (18 issues): P0 nostrc-1ww (SQLCipher), nostrc-ufh (bootstrap single-use), nostrc-sd3 (revoke deny-list), nostrc-8q2 (D-Bus cred leak/fake session). P1 nostrc-593 (relay publish false success), nostrc-aoe (mgmt plaintext ACK), nostrc-e5y (session_broker fake token), nostrc-t04 (SO_PEERCRED unwired), nostrc-zi6 (ssh wrong-identity), nostrc-lt1 (no SIGHUP reload), nostrc-hx9 (missing nip44 handlers), nostrc-o02 (relay recv no verify), nostrc-5tc (rotation non-txn), nostrc-dhd (fake rate/auth tests), nostrc-23g (no at-rest/sign/nip44 tests). P2 nostrc-d75 (set_policy best-effort), nostrc-fao (replay fail-open), nostrc-9np (DB key/KDF docs), nostrc-op9 (single DEK), nostrc-p0s (wipe/audit-chain/policy-default grab-bag), nostrc-aff (FIDO half-wired), nostrc-a6g (FIDO test shims/CI gating), nostrc-4dp (missing e2e tests). Audit doc: this session 2026-07-03.
close_reason: All 23 child issues resolved on branch signet/security-hardening-2026-07-03 (+ 1 discovered latent bug nostrc-3x5). P0: SQLCipher enforcement (1ww), bootstrap single-use (ufh), revoke deny-list (sd3), D-Bus credential ownership (8q2). P1: relay publish false-success (593), plaintext ACK fail-closed (aoe), session_broker fail-closed (e5y), SO_PEERCRED uid_resolver (t04), SSH key-blob binding (zi6), SIGHUP reload verified (lt1), nip44 handlers (hx9), relay-recv verify (o02), transactional rotation (5tc), real rate/auth tests (dhd), crypto/at-rest tests (23g), + auth JSON-backend bug (3x5). P2: set_policy code (d75), replay fail-closed (fao), DB-key/KDF docs (9np), per-agent DEK (op9), secure-wipe grab-bag (p0s), FIDO UV (aff), e2e tests (4dp), signet CI (a6g). Test suite grew from 5 to 10 meson tests (16 CMake ctests incl passkeys); all pass. Signet now builds clean and is materially more real.

title: NIP-29 join to a closed group sticks short of CLOSED under load (Linux): nip29-service denied-and-closed, group-ui join-states, group-ui-gui join
description: Found in the W19 reliability work (branch tests/w19-reliability). In the Linux gate container (arm64, 14 CPUs), ctest -R 'groundhog-(group-ui|group-ui-gui|nip29-service|conversation-menu|e2e-dm)$' -j12 beside 10 CPU hogs failed 5 of 30 runs; also 2 of 10 loaded full Groundhog runs there. Never seen on macOS in 100 loaded suite runs. Failures: /groundhog/nip29-service/denied-and-closed 'condition waited for at line 844 did not hold within 10s' (wait_join(closed, GH_NIP29_JOIN_CLOSED)), /groundhog/group-ui/join-states line 606 (wait_join(closed, CLOSED) for the invite-only 'vip'), /groundhog/group-ui-gui/join line 1294 (wait_join_title 'Invite Only'). The failing log shows the relay's OK false 'restricted: this group is closed' reaching the client ([PUBLISH] REJECTED), then the relay connection and subscription 7 closing, and no further progress. apply_join_result() maps a rejection to CLOSED only if room->closed is already known, else DENIED, and room_apply_metadata() later turns DENIED into CLOSED when the 39000 says closed: if the rejection wins the race against the metadata and the metadata never arrives afterwards (its subscription closed with the connection?), the room stays DENIED. Hypothesis, not verified. Full logs of 5 failures: docker volume nostrc-linux-gate-arm64 under /work/w19-groupui/. Blocks the Linux pre-push gate's smoke run under load (absorbed by the rerun, now visible via nostrc-16yi).

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Branch tests/w19-reliability (W19 reliability). Stress: macOS 14 cores; 'loaded' = ctest -R groundhog- -j12 beside 10 CPU hogs; targeted = 96 runs of one test, 12 parallel, beside 10 hogs. Root cause: test, not product. assert_no_short_timers() (tests/app/test_background.c) removed its own 2 s deadline after it had fired, when the in-flight portal SetStatus reply landed in the same main-loop turn -> 'Source ID N was not found'; a reply just after the deadline failed the twin way ('[gio] send_message_with_reply_unlocked fires in 22994 ms while idle'). GhBackground calls no g_source_remove(); GhNotifier zeroes its ids before G_SOURCE_REMOVE and removes via gh_clock_source_remove() (looks up first). Fix 2c78e8ac: no window; D-Bus replies in flight are waited out (10 s failure bound), any other timer due within a minute fails at once, named. Evidence: starved (nice 19, 24 hogs) before 1/120 with the exact critical; portal reply delayed from a thread (experiment): before 24/24 failed at >=2000 ms, after 0/40 at 1500-3000 ms. title: Pre-push gate: add a Linux (Docker) compile of all targets so glibc-only breaks are caught before push
description: 7aae0d39 passed the macOS-only pre-push gate (424/424) but broke every Linux CI job: go_channel_mpmc_slot_test.c used nanosleep without _POSIX_C_SOURCE under -std=c11. Extend the tracked pre-push hook (or an opt-in companion) to run a Linux container build of all targets (scripts/groundhog-linux-ci.sh shows the pattern) when Docker is available, failing on compile errors; keep it fast (build only, or build + a smoke subset).
notes: Implemented on infra/w19-linux-gate (commit 8b49743a, not pushed). scripts/pre-push now runs the static checks, then the macOS build+ctest and in parallel scripts/linux-gate.sh on a second checkout: GCC build of every default target + BUILD_GROUNDHOG=ON in Ubuntu 24.04 (scripts/linux-ci.Dockerfile, shared with groundhog-linux-ci.sh, drift-checked by scripts/check-linux-ci-packages.py), with -Werror=implicit-function-declaration/implicit-int/int-conversion/incompatible-pointer-types/array-bounds, then a 416-test smoke set (failures rerun once alone, by name). Source mounted read-only and checksum-synced into volume nostrc-linux-gate-<arch>; BLUEPRINT_COMPILER=OFF. No Docker = push blocked; NOSTRC_SKIP_LINUX_GATE=1 skips with a banner; NOSTRC_GATE_AMD64=1 = linux/amd64 under emulation. Timings (M-series, 14 cores): Linux stage 31-58 s warm, 1m41 cold (+3.7 min one-time image); it finishes inside the macOS build, so a clean push is ~10 min, all macOS. Proof: dropping 7d11ec86's _POSIX_C_SOURCE is blocked (implicit declaration of nanosleep) 8 s into the Linux stage, push blocked at 221 s, right after the macOS build. amd64 mode on the pre-fix qp24.91 tree fails groundhog-net/media/blossom (arm64 passes). Fixed on the way: libgo weak metrics stubs (gnostr link), gnostr image-viewer test -lm, mls-groups storage cast, relayd peercred test race. Follow-ups: nostrc-taue, nostrc-5djt, nostrc-rjz2.

title: libmarmot: full Marmot convergence (multi-Commit branches, witnesses, bounded passes, branch invalidation)
description: nostrc-9ata implements a bounded subset of protocol-core/convergence.md (marmot-protocol/marmot @26fa6a6): one retained parent (depth 1), same-epoch one-Commit branches ordered by CommitOrderingSuffix (privileged < ordinary, committer, SHA-256 digest). Missing: retained states up to max_rewind_commits=5 and deeper branches (a competing branch of depth 2 is undecryptable/deferred today); app-payload witness scoring and the bounded depth boost; bounded collection passes (settlement_quiescence_ms / max_convergence_pass_ms) instead of apply-on-arrival; invalidation of app messages and state notifications delivered on a losing branch (and joiners admitted by a losing branch's Welcome); disband lifecycle forcing Recovering; deferred-Commit queue with epoch-based expiry. Producers also merge before publishing, so a failed publish forks the committer (overlaps nostrc-qp24.7 staged publish lifecycle).
notes: W17 review (docs/reviews/libmarmot-w17-review-2026-09-29.md, B3/N1): verified permanent split via a depth-2 race isolating the only admin. Also required: retain undecryptable kind:445 input (transport_deferred) and retry after an epoch change/branch switch; withdraw app payloads delivered on a losing branch; joiners admitted by a losing branch. Documented in libmarmot README 0.5.0 'Known limitations'.

title: libmarmot: marmot_add_members/create_group with >1 KeyPackage make N Commits but publish only the last
description: Found while fixing nostrc-9ata. marmot_add_members() and marmot_create_group() call mls_group_add_member() once per KeyPackage, so N invitees produce N Commits (and N Welcomes, each for a different epoch), but only the final Commit is returned/published. Now that marmot_process_message() ingests Commits, existing members cannot apply that last Commit (they miss Commits 1..N-1: MARMOT_ERR_NIP44/WRONG_EPOCH), and in create_group every invitee but the last joins at a stale epoch. Fix: one Commit with N Add proposals (RFC 9420 §12.4) and one Welcome carrying N EncryptedGroupSecrets, each with its own LCA path_secret (nostrc-il4i); receivers already apply multi-Add commits. Tests: Marmot-API three-invitee create and two-KeyPackage add, every member converged. Version: libmarmot PATCH (behavioural fix) unless the API changes.
notes: Implemented on marmot/w17-welcome-commits (review B2): mls_group_add_members/remove_members make one Commit with N proposals and one Welcome with per-joiner LCA path secrets; marmot_create_group/add_members/remove_members use them. Tests: test_commits test_multi_member_commits_converge (3 invitees, 2 adds, 2 removes), test_mls_group test_multi_add_welcome_each_joiner_follows. Not closed: awaiting review/merge.

title: libmarmot: committer never records a new member's leaf in parent nodes' unmerged_leaves on Add (receivers do)
description: From docs/reviews/libmarmot-w16-review-2026-09-29.md (on branch marmot/w16-review 1ab7d115): when libmarmot commits an Add, the committer does not append the new leaf to the unmerged_leaves of the parent nodes on its direct path, while receivers do (RFC 9420 §7.8/§12.1.1). In an 8-member scenario every receiver rejects the Add and the new member cannot join. Reproduces before and after lz4f/2io4. title: libmarmot Welcome omits and ignores GroupSecrets.path_secret; joiner cannot follow Commits encrypting to its committer common ancestor
description: Found while fixing nostrc-va60/nostrc-5q55. RFC 9420 §12.4.3.1: the Welcome's GroupSecrets carries path_secret for the lowest common ancestor of the committer and the joiner, from which the joiner derives the keys of that node and the nodes above it on the committer's filtered path (verifying them against the tree). serialize_group_secrets() always writes path_secret absent and mls_welcome.c parse_group_secrets() discards it, so a joiner never holds those keys (the UpdatePath correctly does not encrypt to it, nostrc-5q55). Any later Commit whose copath resolution contains the LCA node is undecryptable for the joiner. Repro (verified on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes): ThreeMemberFixture; Charlie (leaf 2) adds Dave (leaf 3) -> LCA node 5; Alice self-updates, Bob and Charlie follow, Dave fails rc -116. Also breaks OpenMLS/MDK Welcomes, which do send path_secret. Fix: add_member passes the LCA path secret into GroupSecrets; mls_welcome_process derives/verifies/caches the path keys into own_path_keys; regression = the repro plus an OpenMLS Welcome with path_secret. Version: PATCH.
notes: Fixed on marmot/w17-welcome-commits in 2f487f8a (libmarmot 0.4.1 PATCH; gobject/gnostr/groundhog no bump). Committer sends LCA path_secret; joiner derives/verifies/caches keys; 8 OpenMLS passive-client Welcomes now verified. Not closed: awaiting review/merge.

title: libmarmot Add producer omits the new leaf from unmerged_leaves off its own path; receivers' tree hash differs
description: Found while fixing nostrc-5q55. process_commit_impl adds a newly added leaf to unmerged_leaves of every non-blank parent on its direct path (RFC 9420 §12.1.1); mls_group_add_member did not, relying on its UpdatePath to re-key its own path. A non-blank parent that is on the new leaf's path but not on the committer's path keeps the unmerged leaf on receivers only, so their provisional tree hash / UpdatePathNode HPKE context differs and every receiver rejects. Repro (verified): 5 members in an 8-leaf tree; Bob removes Alice (re-keys node 3 above her blank leaf 0); Eve (leaf 4) adds Frank into leaf 0 -> Bob, Charlie, Dave rc -4. Fix: shared tree_add_unmerged_leaf() used by producer and processor; regression test_add_unmerged_leaf_off_committer_path. Fixed on branch marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in the nostrc-5q55 commit. Version: PATCH (covered by libmarmot 0.3.8).

title: nostr-gobject EOSE-order test: a round timed out (no EOSE+24 events in 10 s) under concurrent ctest load
description: test_nostr_gobject_subscription_eose_order failed twice at 143d1b86+ on macOS while the Groundhog suite ran concurrently (-j6/-j8): test_subscription_eose_order.c:296 'round.timed_out' should be FALSE. Not reproduced in 25 standalone runs under 4x CPU load. Determine whether this is a lost EOSE/event in the new ordered queue (553e6cef: monitor thread queue_pending_events, single drain idle, event_idle_scheduled flag), a missed wakeup, or test-relay starvation; fix the root cause (no bigger timeout as the fix).
notes:
Root cause (instrumented repro: 25/300 loaded runs failed on 90c1f9ed while ctest -R groundhog- -j8 looped). Not the nostr-gobject queue: two lower-level bugs.
1) libgo MPMC channels (default GO_CHANNEL_MPMC_SLOTS=ON): only the lock-free try fast paths followed the per-slot sequence protocol. After 64 spins on a slot a sender had claimed (in advanced) but not yet published, go_channel_try_receive fell through to a mutex path that ignored slot_seq, read buffer[out] (NULL), advanced out and returned success -> the element was skipped for good. Its masked go_channel_inc_out also corrupted in-out once tickets passed capacity (channel 'full' forever). go_channel_receive/_with_context read unpublished slots the same way; go_channel_send_with_context used the masked ring increment and never published slot_seq. Evidence: 18/25 failures = 23/24 events + EOSE with core_enq=24 core_drop=0, core channel empty (monitor got NULL); 5/25 = connection recv_channel depth 2048/4096 > capacity + 'drop: recv_channel full after retries'; 2/25 = relay reader got NULL frame -> 'Receive channel closed' -> disconnect.
2) libnostr connection.c: CLIENT_WRITEABLE cleared writable_pending on an empty try_receive; a writer's (no-op) set landing between the check and the clear stranded the frame (sweep gated on the flag). With (1) fixed this surfaced as 3/600: relay_reqs one short, send_ch_depth=1 (REQ never sent).
Fix: libgo mpmc_push/mpmc_pop used by every MPMC path (BUSY -> try paths report full/empty, blocking paths yield+retry; signed ticket math; occupancy/depth load out first); connection.c re-checks send_channel depth after clearing the flag. Tests: libgo go_channel_mpmc_slot_test (4 of 6 cases fail on old code; stress: 16/200000 received, 8 NULL), tests/test_connection_writable_rearm (old: frames stranded). Loaded after fix: 300/300 sequential + 600/600 (3 copies) + 900/900 instrumented, all alongside ctest -R groundhog- -j8. Versions: libgo 0.1.2, libnostr 1.0.9; nostr-gobject unchanged (no bump). Follow-ups: nostrc-v624, nostrc-9a2b; admin-gating flake is nostrc-qp24.87; poll(2) EBADF is nostrc-qp24.10.13.

title: marmot_update_group_metadata changes MLS GroupContext extensions without a GroupContextExtensions proposal; other members cannot follow the Commit
description: Found while fixing nostrc-2io4 (reviewing callers of mls_group_self_update). groups.c marmot_update_group_metadata rebuilds the 0xF2EE extension, swaps it into mls.extensions_data locally, then commits an empty self-update. The Commit carries no GroupContextExtensions proposal, so receivers keep the old extensions: their provisional GroupContext (UpdatePathNode HPKE info) and key schedule differ from the committer's, so the path secret cannot decrypt and the confirmation tag cannot match. Every other member rejects the rename and the group forks. Tests only look at the committer (test_protocol.c step 5, groundhog test_store_marmot.c). Fix: commit a real GCE proposal (RFC 9420 §12.1.7, path required) built from the new extension; add a two-member receive regression. Version: PATCH.

title: libmarmot UpdatePath encrypts path secrets to members added by the same Commit; receivers skip them and decrypt the wrong ciphertext
description: Found while fixing nostrc-lz4f. RFC 9420 §12.4.1/§12.4.2: path secrets are not encrypted to leaves added by the Commit (they get the joiner secret via Welcome), and receivers compute their ciphertext index over the resolution minus those leaves. process_commit_impl/decrypt_path_secret already exclude added_leaves, but generate_update_path (mls_group_add_member) encrypts to the full resolution including the new leaf, so the indices disagree whenever a new member precedes an existing one in a copath resolution. Repro (verified): ThreeMemberFixture + Dave at leaf 3; Alice removes Charlie (leaf 2); Alice adds Eve (fills leaf 2); node 3's copath resolution is [Eve, Dave]; Bob processes fine, Dave fails with rc -21 (reads Eve's ciphertext). OpenMLS/MDK receivers would also reject the ciphertext count. Fix: pass the Commit's added leaves to generate_update_path and exclude them from encryption (and from secret_count); add the repro plus an MDK-shaped check. Version: PATCH.
notes: Fixed on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in e938bb31 (also nostrc-v79g unmerged leaves; receiver ciphertext-count check). Follow-up nostrc-il4i (Welcome path_secret). Version: libmarmot 0.4.0.

title: libmarmot committer does not keep its own UpdatePath node private keys; cannot process the next Commit that encrypts to them
description: Found while fixing nostrc-lz4f (branch marmot/w16-leaf-validation). generate_update_path derives each filtered-path node keypair from path_secrets[i] and zeroes node_sk without remember_own_path_key(), so the committer never holds the private keys of the parent nodes it just installed. Any later Commit whose copath resolution contains such a node is undecryptable for the original committer: decrypt_path_secret finds no own key -> MARMOT_ERR_MLS_PROCESS_MESSAGE (-116). Repro (verified): ThreeMemberFixture (Alice added Bob and Charlie, so node 1 is Alice's); mls_group_self_update(&charlie); Bob processes it (rc 0), Alice fails (rc -116) because Charlie's copath resolution at node 3 is [node 1]. Fix: cache (node, sk, pk) for every generated path node in generate_update_path (own_path_keys, already persisted) and invalidate on overwrite; regression = ThreeMemberFixture Charlie self-update processed by Alice with matching epoch secrets. Also check the fixed-size cache (MLS_OWN_PATH_KEY_CACHE_SIZE) against tree depth. Version: PATCH.
notes: Fixed on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in 5b184066 (+ staging of producers). Regressions test_committer_keeps_own_path_keys, test_commit_producers_fail_closed. Version: libmarmot 0.4.0 (MINOR, set in 00c701c8 per W16 review F1).

title: libnostr nostr_escape_string corrupts UTF-8 under non-glibc UTF-8 locales (iscntrl on bytes >= 0x80)
description: libnostr/src/utils.c nostr_escape_string() escapes any byte for which iscntrl(c) is true as \u00XX, byte by byte. iscntrl() is locale-dependent: once an application calls setlocale(LC_ALL, "") (every GTK app does in gtk_init) on macOS/BSD UTF-8 locales, iscntrl(0x80..0x9F) is true, so a UTF-8 continuation byte in that range (e.g. U+2615 ☕ = E2 98 95, U+1F97E 🥾 = F0 9F A5 BE) is replaced by a \u0098-style escape. The serialized event JSON is then invalid UTF-8 (a lead byte followed by a backslash): its id is computed over mangled text, and GDBus refuses the string (g_variant_new_string critical). Found by G13's groundhog-composer screenshot case on macOS (the mock signer's NIP-44 decrypt of a rumor with 🥾). glibc returns false for bytes >= 0x80 in UTF-8 locales, so Linux builds are unaffected today. Fix: escape only c < 0x20 and 0x7f (JSON requires only U+0000..U+001F), never by iscntrl(); add a unit test that serializes content with ☕ and 🥾 under setlocale(LC_ALL, "en_US.UTF-8") and checks the round trip and g_utf8_validate. libnostr PATCH bump.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: From G02: GhStoreMarmot can use gh_store_get_db() for the mls_groups, mls_kv and mls_snapshots tables (schema v1), and gh_store_begin/commit/rollback for T-mls. Nested begins are savepoints, so the gh_store_seal/admit primitives commit atomically with MLS state inside the caller's transaction. Map SQLite failures with gh_store_set_sqlite_error() so SQLITE_FULL stays GH_STORE_ERROR_FULL. Crash tests can arm the txn:before-commit and txn:after-commit cut points (GH_STORE_TEST_HOOKS builds, tests/store/crash-harness.h).

comments.author: Biz
comments.text:
G03 (nostrc-qp24.20) key API for the store key provider — gnome/groundhog/src/store/gh-store-key.h, CMake target groundhog-store-key:
- GhStoreKey *gh_store_key_new(NULL)  (NULL = session Secret Service; tests pass a FakeSecret from tests/store/fake-secret.h). Use ONE instance per process (per-account ordering is per instance).
- gh_store_key_lookup_or_create_async(self, account_hex, flags, cancellable, cb, data) / _finish(self, res, &store_id, &created, &error) -> GBytes (exactly 32 bytes, sodium_malloc guarded, read-only, wiped on last unref). ONLY when no store.db exists yet.
- gh_store_key_lookup_async(...) / _finish(self, res, &store_id, &error) when store.db exists: NOT_FOUND there = STORE_KEY_MISSING (never create).
- gh_store_key_destroy_async(self, account_hex, flags, ...) / _finish: forget; deletes every item of the account; run before unlinking the directory.
- flags: GH_STORE_KEY_FLAGS_NONE never prompts (background); GH_STORE_KEY_FLAGS_INTERACTIVE may show unlock/create prompts.
- store_id out param = item's store-id attribute: write it to meta.store_id at creation, compare on open (KC-5 -> GH_STORE_ERROR_FOREIGN).
- gh_store_key_dup_sqlcipher_key(key) -> GBytes "x'<64 hex>'" (size 67, NUL after) in guarded memory for PRAGMA key/sqlite3_key; drop both refs right after keying.
- Errors (GH_STORE_KEY_ERROR): UNAVAILABLE->STORE_UNAVAILABLE, LOCKED->STORE_LOCKED, NOT_FOUND->STORE_KEY_MISSING (if db exists), INVALID (unusable/duplicate/foreign item), NEWER_VERSION (never offer destroy), FAILED; bad account -> G_IO_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT; G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: From G02 (branch groundhog/w13-g02-store): GhStore wiring for G03's async GhStoreKey. (1) gh_store_exists(data_dir, account) runs the same safety checks as an open; PERMISSIONS means an unsafe layout. (2) If a store exists, call gh_store_key_lookup_async; NOT_FOUND then maps to STORE_KEY_MISSING. Otherwise call gh_store_key_lookup_or_create_async. (3) Run gh_store_open_with_key(config, key GBytes, store_id, CREATE?) in a GTask worker. The key is only read, so G03's read-only guarded GBytes is fine; the key provider is optional there. Error map: KEY -> wrong key; FOREIGN; NEWER_SCHEMA ('Created by a newer Groundhog'); CORRUPT -> STORE_CORRUPT, then reopen with GH_STORE_OPEN_ALLOW_CORRUPT for a read-only view (identity is still checked; SQLCipher's page-auth failure is sticky per handle); BUSY -> already open in this process. (4) Forget: gh_store_close, then gh_store_key_destroy_async, then gh_store_delete_files; or gh_store_forget when a sync GhStoreKeyProvider is set. (5) gh_store_open_ephemeral covers 'Continue Without Saving Messages' (KC-4). groundhog already links groundhog-store with libsqlcipher first; GROUNDHOG_HAVE_STORE=1/0.

title: GNostrSubscription can emit EOSE before stored EVENTs (breaks one-shot 10050 lookups)
description: libnostr enqueues an EVENT on the events channel before EOSE on the eose channel, but nostr-gobject/src/nostr_subscription.c's monitor thread uses go_select_timeout (randomised start among ready cases) and then dispatches EOSE via g_idle_add at G_PRIORITY_DEFAULT while events drain from a G_PRIORITY_DEFAULT_IDLE queue. EOSE can therefore reach the main loop before a stored event received earlier. Groundhog's GhInboxLookup (gh-inbox-lookup.c) completes at EOSE and defers completion to G_PRIORITY_LOW, which narrows but cannot close the cross-thread race: in a real-socket loop (nostrc-qp24.10.4 development) ~25% of lookups missed the recipient's kind-10050 and reported NO_RECIPIENT_INBOX. The same race can make GhAccountRelays report COMPLETE before the own 10050 is admitted (DM send then flags NO_OWN_INBOX). Fix in nostr-gobject: deliver EOSE through the same ordered queue as events (or drain events before emitting EOSE). Then add a real-REQ wire test for GhInboxLookup to tests/app/test_dm_send.c (currently the wire test records REQs and only publishes over real sockets).

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Fix on branch groundhog/w15d-eose-ordering. Root cause: nostr_subscription.c monitor picked among ready events/eose channels at random (go_select) and posted EOSE via its own G_PRIORITY_DEFAULT idle, ahead of the G_PRIORITY_DEFAULT_IDLE event queue. Fix: one ordered FIFO of EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED items drained by a single idle source; on EOSE/CLOSED the monitor first drains ch_events (libnostr's reader thread dispatches in wire order, so every pre-EOSE event is already there). Capacity cap drops only events, never markers; EOSE/CLOSED after CLOSED are not re-emitted. libnostr subscription dispatch does not reorder (single reader thread; relay_optimized.c async-verify path is not compiled) - no libnostr change. Groundhog G_PRIORITY_LOW workarounds removed (gh-inbox-lookup, gh-contact-directory, gh-dm-inbox, gh-dm-send); idle deferral kept for re-entrancy. Versions: nostr-gobject 2.0.1 -> 2.0.2 (PATCH, behavioural bug fix, no API change; CMake + meson + manifest); groundhog 0.7.0 -> 0.7.1 (PATCH); libnostr no bump (unchanged). title: libmarmot Commit processor does not verify Update proposal leaf-node signatures
description: Found while fixing nostrc-jnfp (e63633dc): the W12 Update-by-ref fixture's leaf node is not re-signed yet is accepted, because process_commit_impl applies Update proposals without verifying the LeafNode signature (RFC 9420 §7.3 leaf node validation: signature over LeafNodeTBS with group_id/leaf_index, encryption key uniqueness, capabilities, lifetime rules for commit/update sources). A member could install an unauthenticated leaf for itself (or a malformed one). Validate Update leaves (and UpdatePath leaf nodes) fully before application; reject with no mutation.
acceptance_criteria: Regressions: Update with bad leaf signature, wrong leaf_node_source, duplicate encryption key, and UpdatePath leaf with bad signature are each rejected without state change; counterfactual shows the old code accepted them; MDK interop still passes.
notes: W16 review F1-F4 addressed on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in 00c701c8 (0.4.0 MINOR + README notes, gnostr group-error toast, committer path blanking, M1/M2/M3/M4/M7 tests, dependent version decisions).

title: libmarmot mls_group_remove_member fails when removal filters the root out of the committer's path
description: Found while implementing nostrc-jnfp. In a 3-member group (Alice leaf 0, Bob 1, Charlie 2; 4-leaf tree, leaf 3 blank) mls_group_remove_member(alice, 2) returns MARMOT_ERR_INTERNAL: after blanking Charlie, copath node 5 has an empty resolution so Alice's filtered direct path is [1] and excludes the root. generate_update_path (libmarmot/src/mls/mls_group.c, parent_hash loop: 'if (path_pos + 1 >= fdp_len) goto fail') treats a non-root top filtered node as an error, but RFC 9420 §7.9 computes parent_hash relative to the parent on the FILTERED direct path, so the topmost filtered node carries an empty parent_hash. Fails closed (no Commit emitted, never a pathless one) but blocks removing the last member of the opposite subtree -- a common case that live member-removal UI will hit. Fix must keep receiver (mls_treekem_apply_update_path / parent-hash verification) and MDK treekem/passive-client vectors in agreement. Repro: ThreeMemberFixture in libmarmot/tests/test_mls_group.c, call mls_group_remove_member(&f.alice, 2, ...). nostrc-jnfp tests deliberately remove Bob (leaf 1) instead. Version: PATCH.
notes: W16 review F2 (committer blanks unfiltered direct path) fixed on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in 00c701c8.

title: libmarmot Commit processor does not require UpdatePath when proposals demand it
description: RFC 9420 §12.4: a Commit MUST carry an UpdatePath if it covers any Update, Remove, ExternalInit or GroupContextExtensions proposal, or has no proposals; receivers must verify this. libmarmot/src/mls/mls_group.c process_commit_impl only branches on commit.has_path (around the 'Process UpdatePath if present' block) and never rejects a pathless Commit whose proposals require a path, so a member can commit e.g. a Remove without refreshing the tree (no post-compromise security refresh, divergence from conformant peers). Found while building the W10 pathless Add-by-ProposalRef fixture (7f99ca5f), which is legitimately pathless. Fix: validate path requirement after proposal resolution and before applying, reject with MARMOT_ERR_MLS_PROCESS_MESSAGE, add pathless Remove/Update/GCE/empty negative tests plus a pathless Add/PSK positive; check MDK passive-client vectors still pass. Version: PATCH.
notes: Raised to P1 at W10 integration: without a required UpdatePath a Remove commit derives the next epoch from secrets the removed member still holds (commit_secret zero), so removal does not exclude them. Must precede any live member-removal UI.
close_reason: Fixed in e63633dc: receive-side §12.4 path rule (staged rollback, PROCESS_MESSAGE) + encoder guard; regressions incl. counterfactual; ctest marmot 21/21, meson 20/20, ASAN+UBSAN clean, MDK 226 commits. Version libmarmot 0.3.5->0.3.6 PATCH. Follow-up nostrc-lz4f.

title: W1b signer cancellation must revoke pending approval work
description: Groundhog gh-signer passes GCancellable to g_dbus_connection_call on a shared bus. Cancelling on account switch abandons the local reply but does not cancel a parked signer-service approval; later approval may execute under the original identity. The client call timeout has been extended beyond the service 300-second TTL to expose typed ApprovalTimedOut, but server-side revocation is still required before a send-capable UI relies on cancellation. Design explicit cancel protocol or per-account private bus connection closure with service pending removal; retain fail-closed identity checks.
acceptance_criteria: Account switch/cancel while approval is pending removes or invalidates server pending request; ApproveRequest afterward cannot execute the abandoned operation or save an allow grant; tested against real D-Bus service with selected identity binding and no message publication.
notes: 2026-09-27 integrated f2ae3b58: account private bus closes on cancellation/switch and real signer service refuses disconnected pending sender.
