title: W1c reconnect cursor must replay same-second Nostr events
description: Review of Groundhog relay foundation found pre-existing core loss: libnostr/src/subscription.c advances last_seen_created_at at enqueue, and libnostr/src/relay.c reconnects with since=last_seen+1. Since is second-granularity; a second event from the same second delivered only after disconnect is excluded. Groundhog dedup cannot recover an omitted event. Preserve inclusive overlap with ID dedup and EOSE-aware backfill; do not use sleeps or weaken protocol behavior.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic local relay test disconnects after one signed event and reconnects with another different ID sharing created_at; both delivered exactly once; EOSE/live behavior correct; existing libnostr/Groundhog relay tests pass.
notes:
Implemented inclusive last-seen-second reconnect REQ with per-cursor event-ID dedup; remote WebSocket close now wakes reader for re-REQ; reset EOSE for each REQ and keep live duplicate suppression. Deterministic signed loopback regression uses no sleeps. Version policy: libnostr 1.0.0 -> 1.0.1 PATCH (backward-compatible reconnect bug fix), CMake and VERSION_MANIFEST updated; Groundhog no bump (no Groundhog source/public-surface change). Verification: cmake -S . -B _build -DBUILD_GROUNDHOG=ON -DBUILD_TESTING=ON; focused targets built; ctest --test-dir _build -R "^(libnostr_|groundhog-relay)" --output-on-failure (12/12); ctest --test-dir _build -R "^libnostr_reconnect_same_second$" --repeat until-fail:10 --output-on-failure (10/10). With F1 fixed but old EOSE send, nine undrained EOSE rounds stalled before tenth REQ; nonblocking EOSE send now coalesces when full while first empty-channel EOSE remains delivered. F2 unbounded same-second ID memory/CPU remains tracked in nostrc-qp24.4.2. Commit locally only; do not merge/push/close.

title: nips/nip17: seal/gift-wrap timestamps come from uninitialised stack bytes (same hex2bin(…,4) bug as rd8j)
description: nips/nip17/src/nip17.c get_randomized_time() calls nostr_hex2bin(rand_bytes, 64-hex-key, 4) and ignores its return; hex2bin requires strlen==2*len, so it always fails without writing and rand_bytes[4] is read uninitialised (UB; often constant/zero -> real send time or a predictable offset). Used for kind-13 seal and kind-1059 gift wrap created_at by nostr_nip17_create_seal/create_gift_wrap/wrap_dm (callers: signet bootstrap_delivery, apps/gnostr DM send). Fix: OpenSSL RAND_bytes with rejection sampling over [1, 2d], fail (return NULL) instead of falling back; test distribution. Found while fixing nostrc-rd8j.
close_reason: Merged to master in e011e74d (worker N, fix/libs-nip59-relay-nip46). Follow-ups: dcqz, k1ym (P2 mock-relay tests never run in Linux CI), hg1n.

title: nips/nip59: gift-wrap timestamps are never randomised (RNG helper always fails); throwaway key not wiped on failure paths
description: ROOT CAUSE: nips/nip59/src/nip59.c get_random_bytes() calls nostr_hex2bin(out, rand_key, copy_len) with rand_key = a 64-hex private key and copy_len = 4; nostr_hex2bin requires strlen(hex) == 2*bin_len, so it ALWAYS returns false, get_random_bytes returns -1, and nostr_nip59_randomize_timestamp() falls back to base_time. Every nostr_nip59_wrap()/wrap_with_key() therefore stamps the gift wrap with the true send time (NIP-17/59 metadata protection silently off). Found by a tripwire in nostr-share --private (nostrc-k95e), which now builds its wraps itself (CSPRNG timestamps) - no other in-tree production caller of nip59 wrap (nip17 has its own get_randomized_time()). Fix: take hex2bin of the first 2*copy_len hex chars (or use a real CSPRNG, e.g. RAND_bytes / getrandom), and make randomize_timestamp FAIL instead of returning base_time; add a test asserting created_at < now. Also: wrap_with_key wipes eph_sk_hex only on success (early returns after nostr_bin2hex leave it in the heap); modulo bias in rand_val % window (harmless).
close_reason: Merged to master in e011e74d (worker N, fix/libs-nip59-relay-nip46). Follow-ups: dcqz, k1ym (P2 mock-relay tests never run in Linux CI), hg1n.

title: nostr-home-syncd: snapshot.json over 32 MiB fails to load silently, so the daemon runs with no state baseline
description: nh_syncd_state.c read_file_bytes() caps snapshot.json at 32 MiB ('way more than any conceivable snapshot'). On the aarch64 lab a 203,561-entry home produced a 64 MB snapshot. nh_syncd_state_load then returns NH_SYNCD_ERR_IO WITHOUT setting snapshot_unknown, and main() ignores the rc (void)nh_syncd_state_load(...). The daemon then runs with state == NULL: no additive rescan and no partial marker, force_rescan logs 'no state baseline', the nostrc-lqm2 fallback rescan diffs nothing, and pushes get a NULL state. JSON errors take a similar path: snap_unknown is set but state stays NULL, so rescan_home_additive(NULL) returns ERR_ARG. Fix: raise or remove the cap (stream-parse, or cap on entries), treat any load failure as snapshot-unknown with a fresh empty state, and check the rc in main. Found by worker K during the lqm2 lab demo.
notes: Worker O, branch fix/syncd-snapshot-and-seed @ 18169446. Stream-parsed loader (1 GiB ceiling, env NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES), taxonomy TOO_LARGE/SCHEMA/JSON/IO; corrupt -> quarantined snapshot.json.corrupt.<epoch> + additive rebuild under partial; other failures exit 7 untouched; --check read-only. Lab (aarch64, real 64,384,736 B snapshot): old binary --check printed 'state=loaded' while the load had failed; new: 203,561 entries loaded in 0.68 s, unit MemoryPeak 344 MiB (360,656,896 B), max RSS 298 MB for --check; 32 MiB ceiling -> exit 7, sha unchanged. Tests homed_syncd_state + homed_syncd_snapshot_load. Follow-up nostrc-6oaq (resident jansson tree).
close_reason: Merged to master in e6c61828 (worker O, fix/syncd-snapshot-and-seed). Lab: 64 MB snapshot loads in 0.68 s, MemoryPeak 344 MiB; exit 7 on oversize with file untouched. Follow-ups: 6oaq, 1xbk.

title: nostr-home-syncd: uncapped recursive inotify over $HOME exhausts the per-user watch budget, silently breaking every GFileMonitor in the session
description: Root cause of nostrc-twwl, found 2026-09-26 on the aarch64 lab. The packaged /usr/bin/nostr-home-syncd (user unit nostr-home-sync.service, started 18:45:46 — between the passing and failing ctest sweeps) held 65,145 inotify watches against fs.inotify.max_user_watches=65536: gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-syncd/nh_syncd_watcher.c is a 'recursive inotify watcher over $HOME' with no cap, and that HOME holds many build trees. Every other inotify_add_watch for uid 1000 then fails ENOSPC. GLib still returns a GInotifyFileMonitor (inotify_init works) that parks the path in its missing list and never fires — so Nautilus, tracker, gnome-settings-daemon, GTK file choosers, the shell extension's budgets.json monitor, etc. all stop seeing file changes with no error. Repro: gjs Gio.File.monitor_file on a fresh file -> no event in 30 s as uid 1000, 0.11 s as root. Fix directions: cap watches (a budget well below max_user_watches, e.g. <= 1/4) and degrade to periodic rescan for the rest; honor excludes (build dirs, caches, node_modules, .git objects); log loudly on ENOSPC; consider fanotify (FAN_REPORT_FID, per-filesystem marks) which needs no per-directory watches. Add a test that runs the watcher under a small max-watches budget and asserts it stays under it.
notes: K: fixed on branch fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups dc388c2c + 89d26229 (not merged). Lab: syncd watches 65,145 -> 0 (unmanaged home), 8192 cap in managed mode on the 93k-dir home; GFileMonitor probe fires in 0.001-0.1 s.
close_reason: Merged to master (worker K, fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups). Lab: syncd watches 65,145 → 0 (8,192 cap with seed). Follow-ups: 5y2t (P1 snapshot >32MiB), p8y6, ix3n, ixra.

title: nostr-session-relay.service crash-loops under systemd --user: 218/CAPABILITIES (ProtectClock/ProtectKernel* in a user unit)
description: Found on the aarch64 lab (192.168.64.3) during nostrc-1xak verification: journalctl --user -u nostr-session-relay.service shows 'Failed to drop capabilities: Operation not permitted' → status=218/CAPABILITIES, NRestarts=22+. The socket unit still owns $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nostr/relay.sock, so clients connect and then hang forever (a raw WebSocket upgrade over relay.sock gets no response; nostr-share's publish to it times out after ok_wait_sec). gnome/nostr-homed/systemd/user/nostr-session-relay.service.in sets ProtectClock=yes, ProtectKernelLogs/Modules/Tunables=yes, ProtectHostname=yes etc.; in a user manager those imply CapabilityBoundingSet drops that an unprivileged systemd --user cannot perform (they need PrivateUsers=yes or must be removed). Fix the unit (drop the capability-implying directives or add PrivateUsers=yes), then re-verify: a WebSocket REQ over relay.sock must get EOSE. Every relay.sock consumer (nostr-notify, nostr-dav session modes, nostr-share's session copy) is affected. Check nostr-notify.service / nostr-dav.service for the same pattern.
notes: Part 2 FIXED on branch fix/session-relay-followups, commit 0b480812 (not merged). Two root causes in libnostr-relay-server (apps/relayd/src/relay_server.c): (1) accept starvation -- Unix-fd loop poll()ed the listen fd 50 ms then called lws_service(ctx,0); since lws 3.2 the timeout is ignored and lws sleeps until one of ITS fds/timers fires, and the listen fd was not one, so late clients waited ~3 s for an unrelated lws wakeup or were never accepted. Fix: adopt a dup of the listen fd into lws as a raw descriptor (accept in-loop), 1 s lws_sul wake for stop_flag/retention. (2) NIP-01 clients send no Sec-WebSocket-Protocol; lws binds such upgrades to protocols[0]=='http', so frames hit lws_callback_http_dummy and REQ/EVENT were dropped (also on TCP nostrc-relayd). Fix: 'nostr' is protocols[0] and forwards HTTP reasons. Also added the promised SO_PEERCRED uid check, fixed a double close. Test relayd_session_relay_ws: old core 3032 ms upgrade + no replies + 2nd client never accepted; new 0-1 ms. Lab (installed debs, socket-activated relay.sock): 101 in 40 ms, NRestarts=0. Part 1 was already fixed. Remaining for close: merge.
close_reason: Merged 9c4e1dcf (0b480812 q9ba pt2, 1dab5499 prqu.14, dfa72bfc prqu.5, a4e465dc ig4k). Session relay stores events (nostrdb static, libnostr.so untouched, dep-purity ok), WS upgrade over relay.sock works, every REQ ends in EOSE/CLOSED, porthome user units start. Lab: 101 in 40ms, EOSE 0ms, EVENT OK+readback across re-activation.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Second, independent problem: even started by hand outside systemd (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR=/tmp/x /usr/libexec/nostr-session-relayd → 'nostr-relay-server: listening on Unix fd 3 (per-user session)'), a raw RFC 6455 upgrade over the relay.sock it bound gets no response and lws never creates a client wsi (log shows only pipe/netlink/default vhost). So the Unix listener is not being serviced by the lws event loop even when the process is healthy. Repro: python3 AF_UNIX connect + 'GET / HTTP/1.1 / Upgrade: websocket' → recv times out.

title: nip55l: NIP04Decrypt/NIP44Decrypt/NIP44DecryptB64 are not approval-gated
description: Found in the nostrc-da9c Oracle review. signer_service_g.c answers NIP04Decrypt, NIP44Decrypt and NIP44DecryptB64 immediately, without ACL or ApprovalRequested. SignEvent and (since nip55l 0.3.0) NIP44DeriveConversationKey both go through the approval flow, so any same-uid D-Bus client can get around that gating by asking the signer to decrypt payloads directly (including a nostr-seal stanza via the NIP44DecryptB64 fallback). Fix: put the decrypt methods behind the same ACL / ApprovalRequested / ApproveRequest flow (kinds nip04_decrypt / nip44_decrypt) and migrate the existing callers (gnostr, nostr-dav, notify) with ACL defaults so they don't prompt on every DM. This changes behavior for existing clients, which is why it wasn't done in da9c.
notes: branch fix/signer-hardening-2 (not pushed, based on 3835b81f): 61eb1dfd gates NIP04/NIP44(+B64) decrypt/encrypt, GetPublicKey, GetRelays, DecryptZapEvent behind the approval flow (kinds nip04_decrypt, nip44_decrypt, ...); 02e4fd9a makes the ungated NIP-5F socket in gnostr-signer-daemon opt-in. Default grants for nostr-homed headless helpers. Contract test gating phase green on aarch64 lab + macOS.

title: nostr-notify: libnip19.so runtime dep not shipped in any .deb
description:
nostr-notify-daemon has a dynamic link edge to libnip19.so, but the shipped .deb doesn't include the library. Runtime failure:

  /usr/libexec/nostr-notify-daemon: error while loading shared libraries: libnip19.so: cannot open shared object file
  Main process exited, code=exited, status=127/n/a

Root cause: debian/not-installed lists usr/lib/*/libnip19.so as a dropped artifact (comment cites plan D-6: 'NIP libraries are aggregated into libnostr1'). But that aggregation wasn't done, and no other package ships libnip19.

Additionally, libnip19.so is built as a versionless single .so (no SONAME chain / no .so.1.0.0 symlink), which will fail dpkg-shlibdeps ABI tracking. Both are Wave-4 packaging defects.

Interim fix (nostrc-qngf scope): add libnip19.so to debian/nostr-notify.install and remove from not-installed. Follow-up: (a) proper SONAME versioning for libnip19, (b) canonical aggregation into libnostr1 per plan D-6.

title: nd-publisher: sqlite3_int64 vs gint64 format mismatch breaks aarch64 -Werror build
description:
During nostrc-qngf Debian installed-unit acceptance on Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64, dpkg-buildpackage failed at target 596/609 in gnome/nostr-dav/src/nd-publisher.c:1031:

  error: format `%li` expects argument of type `long int`, but argument 2 has type `sqlite3_int64` {aka `long long int`} [-Werror=format=]

Root cause: G_GINT64_FORMAT expands to "li" on 64-bit Linux (gint64 = long int) but sqlite3_int64 is always `long long int`. On x86_64 they happen to be the same size, so no warning fires; on aarch64 GCC's -Werror=format catches the typedef mismatch.

Fix: cast sqlite3_column_int64() return to (gint64). Same 64-bit signed integer, just aligned to the format's expected type.

Introduced by: Wave 4 Quebec's tombstone landing (e8eafde7 in gnome/nostr-dav/src/nd-publisher.c load_pending_tombstones()).
close_reason: Closed

title: nostr-smbd share access blocked: /var/lib/nostr-auth 0700 blocks force-user traversal to share-root
description:
During Wave 4 Oscar Windows/GNOME acceptance for #16b (Ubuntu 24.04, Samba 4.19.5, aarch64):

The shipped smb.conf.standalone.sample sets `path = /var/lib/nostr-auth/share-root` with `force user = nostr-smb-share`. The parent state directory /var/lib/nostr-auth is provisioned mode 0700 root:root (nostr-smbd.service.in `StateDirectoryMode=0700`, and nostr-authd.service similarly). Samba's smbd, after force-user'ing to nostr-smb-share, cannot traverse into /var/lib/nostr-auth (no x bit for non-root) and every share operation returns NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED, even though share-root itself is mode 0750 owned by nostr-smb-share:nostr-smb-share.

Repro:
1. Deploy nostrc-samba-server per gnome/nostr-homed/config/smb.conf.standalone.sample + systemd unit.
2. mkdir -m0750 /var/lib/nostr-auth/share-root && chown nostr-smb-share:nostr-smb-share /var/lib/nostr-auth/share-root
3. smbpasswd -s -a -c /etc/nostr-auth/smb.conf nostr (in nostr-smb-share group)
4. smbclient //127.0.0.1/nostr-home -U nostr%pw -c ls  →  NT_STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED listing \*

Root cause: 0700 on /var/lib/nostr-auth is incompatible with a subdir that is meant to be traversed by an unprivileged force-user account. Either:
- Loosen the state dir to 0711 (execute-only for others, keeps contents opaque), OR
- Move share-root out of the state dir (e.g. /var/lib/nostr-smb-share, /srv/nostr-home), OR
- Give smbd CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH ambient + keep euid=root during traversal only (already has bounding, but drops on force-user).

Recommendation: bump StateDirectoryMode to 0711 and add a dedicated `ShareStateDirectoryMode=0755` under packaging for the subtree owned by nostr-smb-share, OR change the shipped share path to /srv/nostr-home (aligns with Debian policy for served content). The FUSE mount path would follow.

Workaround applied on lab VM for acceptance run: chmod 0755 /var/lib/nostr-auth. Documented in docs/reviews/samba-server-windows-acceptance-2026-09-26.md.

Discovered by: Wave 4 Oscar (rp-agent-a2973b22-feat-samba-windows-acceptance).
notes: ROOT CAUSE isolated: Samba's smbd CHMODs the directory pointed to by `state directory` / `private dir` back to 0700 on every start. My deployed smb.conf had `state directory = /var/lib/nostr-auth` (matching the packaged intent that nostr-authd share state with smbd), so every `systemctl restart nostr-smbd` reverted /var/lib/nostr-auth to 0700, blocking force-user traversal to /var/lib/nostr-auth/share-root. This is a hard invariant: Samba WILL chmod its state/private dir to 0700 for security reasons — you can't work around that at the smbd layer. Two valid production fixes: (a) SEPARATE the state dir from the share-root parent — put share-root at /srv/nostr-home or /var/lib/nostr-home-share with its own StateDirectory=; keep /var/lib/nostr-auth exclusively for smb.db/passdb/private state at 0700, OR (b) put samba's state at a subdir like /var/lib/nostr-auth/samba-state, keep /var/lib/nostr-auth at 0711, share-root inside it. The plan §4.2 B2/B3 says 'the mount root materialized by porthome/FUSE' — the FUSE mount path can and should be independent of the authority's private state. Verified by tracing that testparm-reported `state directory` == `/var/lib/nostr-auth` and observing `ls -ld /var/lib/nostr-auth` flipping 0755→0700 immediately after every `systemctl restart nostr-smbd`.
close_reason: Closed

title: nostr-smbd.service.in: missing --no-process-group causes setsid() EPERM under systemd
description:
During Wave 4 Oscar Windows/GNOME acceptance for #16b, the shipped systemd unit at gnome/nostr-homed/systemd/nostr-smbd.service.in fails to start on Ubuntu 24.04 (Samba 4.19.5-Ubuntu, aarch64). Journal shows:

  become_daemon.c:119(exit_daemon)
  exit_daemon: daemon failed to start: Failed to create session, error code 1

The ExecStart line uses only `-F` (foreground). Ubuntu's stock /lib/systemd/system/smbd.service uses `--foreground --no-process-group`; without `--no-process-group` smbd calls setsid() which fails with EPERM because systemd has already made smbd the process-group leader. Repro:

  sudo /usr/sbin/smbd -F -s /etc/nostr-auth/smb.conf   # under systemd → immediate exit 1

Fix: add `--no-process-group` to ExecStart (matches stock samba.service). Acceptance for #16b was unblocked by patching the deployed unit on the lab VM only; the .in template in the repo is unchanged.

Expected: nostr-smbd starts, binds 445/139, accepts client sessions.
Actual: exit 1 within milliseconds; systemd restart loop hits StartLimitBurst.

Discovered by: Wave 4 Oscar (rp-agent-a2973b22-feat-samba-windows-acceptance).
close_reason: Closed

title: nostr-dav publisher calls SignEventJson but signer exports SignEvent
description: Live smoke against wss://relay.sharegap.net (see docs/reviews/nostr-dav-publish-live-2026-09-26.md) shows every publish attempt fails with 'org.freedesktop.DBus.Error.UnknownMethod: No such method SignEventJson'. Root cause: gnome/nostr-dav/src/nd-signer-dbus.c:20 hardcodes ND_SIGNER_METHOD_NAME="SignEventJson" and calls it with args "(s)", but nips/nip55l/dbus/org.nostr.Signer.xml exports "SignEvent (in s eventJson, in s identity, in s app_id, out s signed_event)". Both the method name and argument tuple diverge, so the publisher hits UnknownMethod on every attempt. Blocks all outbound publish for nostr-dav — the Wave-3 tu6y "enable_publish default ON" landing is not functional end-to-end. Fix: rename to SignEvent and pass '(sss)' with identity="" and app_id="nostr-dav". Ideally generate the client from the same org.nostr.Signer.xml the daemon uses so the two stay in sync.
close_reason: Fixed in nd-signer-dbus.c — SignEventJson→SignEvent with (sss) args. Rebuilt clean -Werror on darwin dev host.

description: gnome/nostr-homed/src/pam/pam_nostr.c pam_nip46_challenge (lines 58-108) still parses the SignEvent reply as a bare 128-hex signature (strlen(sig)==128). After nip55l 0.2.0 (feat/signer-hardening) the D-Bus method returns the complete signed event JSON, so the current strlen check fails every request and pam_sm_open_session refuses on session bring-up. This bead was NOT fixed in the signer-hardening PR: the maintainer's resume instructions explicitly place gnome/nostr-homed/src/pam/* under the auth/Samba track and forbid editing it from the signer branch. Migration steps: (1) parse the reply as JSON via nostr_event_deserialize_signed + nostr_event_check_signature; (2) drop the strlen check; (3) log the returned event id, not a truncated sig; (4) keep the 30s user-approval timeout. Blocking: feat/signer-hardening merge to master.
close_reason: Not a shipping regression: pam_nostr.c is unbuilt legacy code. CMake builds pam_nostr.so solely from pam_nostr_broker.c, which contains no SignEvent call, signature parser, or 128-hex check; it delegates authentication over auth.sock and consumes a broker result. No Milestone A PAM parser fix or component version bump is needed. P3 follow-up filed to remove/deprecate the confusing legacy file.

title: gnostr-signer Online Accounts wizard fabricates DAV token + uses port 7654
description: apps/gnostr-signer/src/ui/sheets/sheet-online-accounts.c:17-18,112-159 generates its own random base64 token (never known to nostr-dav) and hard-codes http://127.0.0.1:7654. title: porthome: fix shim manifest chunk_hash to be sha256(shim||ct)
description: cmd_push in gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome/nostr-homed-provision.c records chs[ci].sha256 = addr (pre-shim sha256(ct) from nh_porthome_encrypt_chunk) BEFORE nh_porthome_blossom_upload_batch runs the shim wrap. The batch upload with shim (nostrc-bpum path) then computes and stores sha256(shim||ct) in blobs[i].sha256_hex, but the manifest chunk row is never updated to match. Result: with NOSTR_HOMED_BLOSSOM_PNG_SHIM=1 the pusher publishes a self-inconsistent bundle — chunks upload to Blossom under sha256(shim||ct), manifest asks the puller to fetch sha256(ct), pull returns 404 and exits 71. Empirically confirmed against blossom.primal.net during hy3e's two-machine demo (see docs/reviews/porthome-hy3e-shim-live-probe-2026-09-25.md §8 and docs/reviews/porthome-jmx0-two-machine-2026-09-25.md Part 2). Push side of §9.4 is now green (min_replication=2 across sharegap+primal), pull side is blocked on this fix. Fix options: (A) compute sha256(shim||ct) in cmd_push before add_file_v2 when shim is enabled (cleanest, avoids double-hashing); (B) after upload_batch, walk the manifest and overwrite chs[].sha256 with batch[].sha256_hex (requires manifest mutation API). Fix must also cover the single-blob nh_porthome_blossom_upload path used by syncd on-going pushes (nh_syncd_pusher.c). Add a regression test: encrypt one chunk, push with shim on, decode+refetch, assert manifest hash matches Blossom URL hash.
notes: Fixed by commit ebb4b1b5. Added hanami_blossom_shim_active() + hanami_blossom_shim_sha256() helpers in libhanami; cmd_push (nostr-homed-provision.c) and nh_syncd_pusher.c both now record sha256(shim||ct) as the manifest chunk row when the shim is active. cmd_push also passes the shim-inclusive hash as expected_sha256_hex to nh_porthome_blossom_upload_batch so any future divergence fails fast. Regression test tests/unit/test_porthome_shim_manifest.c locks the invariant with 4 cases (shim-on matches upload path, shim-off = sha256(ct), env-var strict '1', deterministic). Aarch64 gcc-13 -Werror clean; four regression cases pass in-process. Empirical: pre-wmb5 pull emitted 'chunk 11150cd7… not on sharegap /list nor primal HEAD' and exited 71 — that error signature no longer occurs (see review §Part 3, missed=0 across all pulls).
close_reason: wmb5 code + regression test landed in ebb4b1b5; shim manifest chunk_hash now agrees with Blossom URL on both cmd_push and syncd paths.

title: [security] greeter artifact leaks NIP-46 pairing secret to local users (P1)
description: See docs/reviews/greeter-artifact-secret-confidentiality-2026-09-22.md. /run/nostr-auth/greeter/current.{json,png} + avatar.png are published mode 0644 world-readable so gdm and the locked-session user can read them; but current.json contains the full nostrconnect:// URI including the one-time secret pairing token, and current.png encodes the same URI in its QR. Any local unprivileged user can read the manifest during a QR login and race the phone signer — the pubkey gate refuses them but they BURN the single-use secret so the victim's login/unlock fails (griefing / DoS). Fix: create a nostr-auth-greeter group, give it gdm (and the seated user for unlock-dialog) via pam_group; publish /run/nostr-auth/greeter dir 0750 group=nostr-auth-greeter, files 0640 root:nostr-auth-greeter atomically via fchown+fchmod before rename. References nostrc-zcll.6.
notes: Fix landed on branch rp-agent-922f5522-fix-greeter-artifact-secret-conf-f823b519. Proof: docs/reviews/greeter-artifact-secret-confidentiality-2026-09-22.md. Broker+unit+sysusers installed on gnome-dev; homed_greeter_artifact_perms test green (headless + live-rig mode). Directory /run/nostr-auth/greeter is 0750 root:nostr-auth-greeter; files 0640 root:nostr-auth-greeter. Non-member cat denied; member cat succeeds. Ready to close after commit.

title: [B5-NIP-05] NIP-05 as GDM login identifier
description: At the GDM greeter ("Not listed?"), a user types their NIP-05 address (e.g. chebizarro@coinos.io) instead of a Linux username. The system resolves the NIP-05 → pubkey via an SSRF-safe unprivileged helper, maps the pubkey to the ENROLLED nostr account, canonicalizes PAM_USER, and continues the QR (nostrconnect) flow for that account showing the account's avatar/name (via the greeter artifact 'account' object). Authentication semantics unchanged: the signed challenge is bound to the account pubkey — spoofing NIP-05 cannot grant access. Guards: SSRF/DoS from the greeter (unprivileged helper with peer-address SSRF check, per-address + global rate limits, https-only, 10 s / 64 KiB / <=3 redirects), strict JSON parse. v1 policy: alias to an enrolled account only; UNKNOWN_ACCOUNT otherwise (no JIT enrollment). Additive protocol fields on BEGIN_LOGIN reply: account_username + identifier. Greeter artifact contract addition: current.json 'account' object + avatar.png sibling copied from AccountsService icon.

title: [B4/B5-harden] pam_nostr invalid_proof should map to PAM_AUTH_ERR; decide strict-deny vs additive-over-Unix GDM stacking
description: Installed-system pamtester proof (merge pending) showed a WRONG passphrase makes pam_nostr_broker return AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL (message 'Authentication service cannot retrieve auth info'), not PAM_AUTH_ERR. The shipped gdm-password.sample stacks it as [success=done authinfo_unavail=ignore default=ignore] then @include common-auth, so a wrong nostr proof FALLS THROUGH to Unix auth instead of a hard deny. For a nostr-only account (no Unix password) the net result is still denial, but if an account also had a Unix password a wrong nostr proof + correct Unix password would authenticate, bypassing nostr. Decide product policy: (a) strict nostr-only -> map invalid_proof to PAM_AUTH_ERR and stack as required/[default=die] so denial is hard; vs (b) additive factor over Unix -> keep fall-through but document it. Reserve AUTHINFO_UNAVAIL strictly for broker-unreachable/unknown-account so a stopped broker never bricks GDM. Modules: gnome/nostr-homed/src/pam/pam_nostr_broker.c, packaging/pam/gdm-password.sample. Bucket B (nostrc-zcll).
close_reason: Closed

title: [A-bug] provider enrollment cannot produce a working local vault: provider_id is AAD-bound but assigned after the secret
description: Discovered wiring the broker login proof (zcll.2 stage 2). nh_auth_vault_seal/open bind the vault AEAD AAD to provider_id (auth_vault.c make_aad), but nh_identity_provider_stage generates provider_id via uuid_generate() AFTER receiving secret_blob and digest-binds the blob (identity_store.c ~1230-1264). So a caller cannot seal a vault to the provider_id the store will assign, and there is no reseal/update-secret API — real local-provider enrollment cannot store an openable vault. Options: (a) let provider_stage accept a caller-provided provider_id (client generates it, seals, stages), or (b) add a provider_reseal(provider_id, new_blob) op, or (c) drop provider_id from the vault AAD (weaker binding; needs B0 sign-off). Broker stage-2 test works around this by sealing with the assigned id and swapping providers.secret_blob directly (test-only).
notes: FIXED master 63c59e7d: added nh_identity_provider_reseal (NH_IDENTITY_OPERATION_PROVIDER_RESEAL) — replaces a staged providers.secret_blob via a normal replay-safe operation, so enrollment can seal the vault to the store-assigned provider_id and store it (stage->seal->reseal->activate). Removed the test-only sqlite swap from nh-seed-authority and test_broker_login. Verified on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64: random keypair authenticates via the reseal path; mismatched vault key rejected. In the VM loop (13/13).
close_reason: Closed

title: [libnostr-bug] nostr_tag_free leaks the NostrTag (StringArray) struct
description: Found via nostr-homed ASan/LSan pass on Linux arm64 (homed_auth_challenge/provider_local: 216 bytes leaked in 9 allocations). nostr_tag_new() returns a heap StringArray via new_string_array() (mallocs the struct), but nostr_tag_free() only calls string_array_free(tag), which frees tag->data and the strings but NOT the StringArray struct itself. So every NostrTag struct (24 bytes) leaks. string_array_free cannot free(array) because it is also used on embedded/stack arrays (filter->ids/authors/relays, tests). Fix belongs in nostr_tag_free: free(tag) after string_array_free. Related: nips/nip98/src/nip98.c calls string_array_free(tags->data[i]) directly on heap NostrTags — same struct leak; should use nostr_tag_free (separate follow-up).
notes: FIXED in master 84948e20. nostr_tag_free now free(tag) after string_array_free (+ NULL guard). Verified end-to-end: homed portable suite 11/11 under ASan+UBSan on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, zero leaks (was 216 bytes / 9 allocs). Follow-up remains: nip98.c string_array_free(tags->data[i]) on heap NostrTags should use nostr_tag_free.
close_reason: Closed

title: [B-bug] homed_auth_challenge segfaults on Linux (arm64/GCC) in 2nd event serialize
description: Found via VM loop (rb0e.15) on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64, GCC 13.3, Debug. homed_auth_challenge SEGVs at tests/unit/test_auth_challenge.c:12 during the SECOND nostr_event_serialize_compact(c.event), called after the test directly overwrites c.event->content=strdup("{}"). Crash is in nostr_escape_string (libnostr/src/utils.c:179) with a garbage s pointer; the first serialize at line 10 succeeds on the same event. Nondeterministic: gdb reproduces the SEGV, but valgrind runs clean (exit 0, no invalid-access reports) — signature of uninitialized-memory / heap-layout dependence. Passes on macOS/Clang. Suspects: libnostr event content ownership vs the test poking c.event->content directly, or an uninitialized field in event serialize. Next step: MSan or instrument nostr_event_serialize_compact/escape_string; consider whether the test's direct struct mutation is legitimate. Repro: make -f Makefile.vm vm-test VM_SSH=...
notes: FIXED in master cd345e76. Root cause: -std=c11 + CMAKE_C_EXTENSIONS OFF made glibc hide strdup; implicit int return truncated the 64-bit pointer (sign-extended garbage) → SEGV in nostr_event_serialize_compact. Confirmed via gdb (event->content=0xffffffffaab08da0) and the compiler warning (implicit declaration / makes pointer from integer). Fix: add_compile_definitions(_DEFAULT_SOURCE) in homed CMakeLists (root _POSIX_C_SOURCE was added after homed add_subdirectory, so never inherited) + <stdlib.h> in test_identity_config.c for mkstemp. Verified 11/11 portable pass, 0 implicit-decl warnings, on Ubuntu 24.04 arm64 via vm-linux-ci.sh.
close_reason: Closed

title: go_context_background() contexts are treated as canceled (vtable never set)
description: go_context_background() in libgo/src/context.c calloc's a GoContext and never sets ctx->vtable. go_context_is_canceled() (context.c:106) returns TRUE when vtable or vtable->is_canceled is NULL, so any background context reads as already-canceled. Consequence: go_channel_send_with_context(chan, data, background_ctx) fails immediately with 'channel closed or context canceled' even on an open, empty channel — e.g. nostr_connection_write_message() with a background context can never enqueue. Discovered while writing tests/test_connection_idle_writable.c for libnostr-idle-writable-busy-poll-20260817 (test works around it by passing ctx=NULL). Fix: give background contexts a proper vtable (or default go_context_is_canceled/go_context_done/go_context_err to not-canceled semantics when vtable is NULL), and audit other vtable-NULL defaults in context.c for the same inverted fallback. Add a regression test: go_channel_send_with_context with a background context on an open channel must succeed.
acceptance_criteria: Background contexts are not reported canceled; send_with_context succeeds with a background ctx; regression test added; existing libgo/libnostr tests green
notes: Implemented background-context base vtable and unconditional send-with-context regression coverage. Version assessment: libgo PATCH bug fix; libgo has no authoritative version declaration beyond VERSION_MANIFEST.md and is Unreleased, so no version bump applied.

title: gnostr DM: cache decrypted rumors to eliminate NIP-46 decrypt RPC storms
description: Every gift wrap costs 2 sequential remote nip44_decrypt RPCs (seal, rumor) with dedup only while in-flight. The startup history load replays up to 200 gift wraps from nostrdb -> up to 400 RPCs at every launch, plus reconnect/EOSE replays - remote signer relays rate-limit the storm (nostrc-0fvh mitigated pacing; this removes the demand). Fix: persistent decrypted-rumor cache keyed by gift-wrap id (JSONL in XDG data dir, 0600), checked before any RPC; entries stored only after full validation (seal sig, kind, pubkey binding) and re-validated on cache hits. Cache hits also work with no signer connected.
close_reason: Closed

title: nip46: rate-limited relay NACKs treated as permanent; no backoff feedback into RPC pacing
description: Relays answering 'rate-limited: slow down, please' (NIP-01 transient prefix) were treated like permanent policy rejections by nostrc-xjgo's NACK handling - the request was abandoned on that relay and the session kept firing subsequent RPCs at the same 4-inflight/150ms pace, feeding the limiter during DM nip44_decrypt storms. Fix: classify rate-limited as transient (rc -2), retry the same relay with escalating backoff (2s/4s/6s, max 3 tries) inside the response wait loop, and push the session's global next-send slot out 2s on every rate-limited NACK so the rest of the storm slows down.
close_reason: Closed

title: nip46: relay PoW rejections invisible to RPC; nos.lol unusable as NIP-46 default
description: nos.lol rejects kind-24133 RPC events with 'pow: 28 bits needed' (unmineable for interactive signing). The RPC published fire-and-forget, so the NACK was only visible as a RELAY_OK_FAIL stderr line from relay.c and the caller burned the full 30s timeout (seen in DM_SERVICE nip44_decrypt). Fix: (1) nip46_publish_rpc_event uses nostr_relay_publish_and_wait with a 2s OK window - acceptance logged, explicit rejections counted and not retried, and the response wait aborts early with the relay's reason when every reachable relay rejected the request; (2) default relay list drops nos.lol for wss://relay.primal.net; (3) NIP46_FALLBACK_RELAY_COUNT is now derived via G_N_ELEMENTS - a hand-edit had shrunk the array to 2 entries while the count stayed 3, copying the NULL sentinel as a relay.
close_reason: Closed

title: simplepool: subscriptions silently dropped for unconnected/reconnecting relays
description: nostr_simple_pool_subscribe fires REQs once; nostr_subscription_fire fails when a relay's websocket is not yet connected, the error is swallowed (freed without logging), and there is no retry - the pool stays permanently deaf on that relay. Same for relays that drop and reconnect mid-session: the closed-channel handler removes the sub and nothing re-fires it. Bit us in NIP-46 QR login (nostrc-0y02): response sub raced relay connect. Fix: reconcile pass in the worker loop - any connected relay lacking a live sub while filters_shared is set gets prepare+fire (skipped when auto_unsub_on_eose, which intentionally drops subs after EOSE). Also log fire failures in subscribe instead of swallowing them.
close_reason: Closed

title: nip46: RPC pool races multi-relay connect; request lost before signer relay connects
description: After nostrc-koso multi-relay pairing, client_start waited only for the FIRST relay to connect, then the response subscription silently failed on still-connecting relays (nostr_subscription_fire requires a live connection, never retried) and nip46_rpc_call published only to relays connected at that instant. Kind 24133 is ephemeral, so the get_public_key request never reached signers listening on a single relay (nsec.app on relay.nsec.app) when another relay won the connect race - login stuck on Getting user identity with no request visible in the signer. Fix: (1) client_start grants up to 3s grace for ALL relays to connect before subscribing (exits early when all up); (2) nip46_rpc_call waits in 500ms slices and late-publishes the request to relays that finish connecting during the wait.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr QR login: RPC response misread as connect ack; multi-relay listener raced to single relay
description: Two regressions after nostrc-80qa/nostrc-koso: (1) With the client key fix, the get_public_key RPC response is p-tagged to the same client pubkey as the login listener's filter; the lenient '64-char result = valid connect' branch misread it as another connect ack, re-entering on_nip46_connect_success which frees self->nip46_session while nip46_get_pubkey_thread is using it (use-after-free / repeated RPC spawning). Fix: nip46_connect_handled latch - first valid connect response wins, all later listener events ignored; reset on listener start. (2) gnostr_pool_subscribe() only subscribes to the FIRST connected relay, and connect_all_async returns on the first relay to win the race, so the listener could end up on a different relay than the signer responds on. Fix: use gnostr_pool_subscribe_multi() which subscribes on all relays and auto-subscribes late-connecting ones.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr QR login: pairing pinned to single relay (relay.nsec.app) with no user override
description: The nostrconnect QR flow uses only nip46_get_default_relay() (first built-in entry, wss://relay.nsec.app) for both the URI relay param and the response listener. When that relay is down/intermittent, QR pairing silently never completes, and there is no way to change the relay except the GNOSTR_NIP46_RELAY env var. Fix: advertise and listen on the full relay list (percent-encoded relay params), and add a GSettings key nip46-connect-relays (org.gnostr.Client) so users can override the pairing relays. Priority: env var > GSettings > built-ins. connect_all_async already succeeds on first relay, so partial outages are tolerated.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr QR login: session uses handshake token as client key after hq-9ohcb secret split
description: Commit cf32ae1c (hq-9ohcb) split the nostrconnect ?secret= handshake token from the client private key in generate_nostrconnect_uri, but on_nip46_connect_success still calls nostr_nip46_client_set_secret() with self->nostrconnect_secret (now the token, not the key). The get_public_key RPC is then signed/encrypted with a key derived from the token, whose pubkey the signer never authorized, so the RPC times out and QR login fails mid-auth. Also save_nip46_credentials_to_settings persists the token instead of the client key. Fix: keep hex of nostrconnect_secret_bytes (client_seckey_hex), pass it to set_secret and persist it; keep the token only for ack validation.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr: kind-1/kind-7 publishing fails under nostrconnect (NIP-46) login
description: Notes (kind 1), NIP-25 reactions (kind 7), and likely other GNostrJsonBuilder-built events (kind 5/6/1111/1985, NIP-34 bug report) fail to publish when logged in via nostrconnect, while NIP-17 DMs work. Root cause analysis: unsigned templates built by GNostrJsonBuilder omit the pubkey field, unlike the working NIP-59 seal/gift-wrap path which serializes a NostrEvent with pubkey set via nostr_event_serialize_compact. Remote NIP-46 signers commonly reject or mis-handle templates without pubkey. Fix: normalize NIP-46 sign requests centrally in GnostrSignerService (inject user pubkey, validate mismatches, validate signed result), improve NIP-46 failure classification, and make the kind-7 reaction publish path handle an empty write-relay list explicitly.
notes: 6378eff9: ROOT CAUSE of the Post-button segfault found via lldb backtrace and fixed. title: Fix shutdown use-after-free on git_client_window in nip34-git plugin
description: nip34_git_plugin_deactivate calls gtk_window_destroy() on self->git_client_window, a raw pointer with no lifetime tracking. GTK4 destroys the toplevel when the user closes it (or during app shutdown), freeing the object but leaving the pointer dangling. On exit, gtk_window_destroy() runs on freed memory -> EXC_BAD_ACCESS (fault addr decodes to reused heap string). Fix: register g_object_add_weak_pointer at creation so the field auto-NULLs when the window dies.
close_reason: Fixed shutdown use-after-free: registered g_object_add_weak_pointer on git_client_window at creation so the field auto-NULLs when GTK destroys the toplevel (user close or shutdown teardown). deactivate now removes the weak pointer before gtk_window_destroy and only runs when the window is genuinely alive. Plugin rebuilds clean; normal run crash-free. Interactive repro (open git client -> close -> quit) not automatable in sandbox.

title: libgo select channel-lifetime race: EXC_BAD_ACCESS in go_channel_ref from pool query thread
description: After ~10min gnostr runtime with ~30 relays / ~270 threads, pool query thread (nostr_pool.c query_thread_func:765 -> go_select_timeout -> ref_channels select.c:283 -> go_channel_ref channel.c:940) crashes with EXC_BAD_ACCESS code=2 addr=0x17523bff0 (thread-stack guard-page address => cases[i].chan was garbage, likely read from a freed NostrSubscription: nostr_subscription_get_events_channel returns raw sub->events with no ref; subscription free calls go_channel_free). The magic-check defense in ref_channels/go_channel_ref is unsound: it dereferences potentially unmapped memory. Fix direction: pool query loop must hold strong refs on subs/channels for select duration (go_channel_ref taken while sub known-alive at case-build time, unref after select+drain), and audit which thread can free the sub while the query thread owns it (server-side CLOSED path / lifecycle thread). Full backtrace: docs/analysis/gnostr-pool-select-race-crash-2026-07-24.log. Distinct from and unmasked by the timeline-load crash fixes in nostrc-rt7.
notes: Root causes found via ASAN (2 distinct bugs behind the pool-thread crashes): (1) UAF in nostr_subscription_dispatch_event — read event->created_at after successful go_channel_try_send handed ownership to consumer; fixed by capturing before send. (2) Stack overflow: g_newa (alloca) inside per-event select loops in nostr_pool.c query_thread_func + three sites in nostr_simple_pool.c (two are app-lifetime streaming pumps) — alloca accumulates until function return; one iteration per received event ⇒ guard-page EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=2) on pool-N threads. All hoisted to heap allocations outside the loops. This also explains the original lldb crashes at stack-guard addresses with 'garbage' channel pointers. 18/18 pool/subscription/relay/timeline tests pass; final ASAN soak running.
close_reason: All three root causes fixed and verified via ASAN iteration: dispatch_event use-after-handoff UAF, alloca-in-loop stack overflows in pool/simple-pool select loops (the actual cause of the guard-page 'garbage channel pointer' crashes), and concurrent refire_since filter race. Final 10-min ASAN soak clean (1259 queries, zero reports).
