title: Signet: self-service authorization for agent/reissue-connect (sender == agent identity)
description: agent/reissue-connect currently requires a provisioner key. Allow an existing agent to reissue ITS OWN connect_secret over the management plane: authorize if the signed sender pubkey (from the unwrapped gift-wrap seal) is a provisioner OR equals the target agent's identity pubkey. All other management methods stay provisioner-only. Audit records auth path (provisioner|self). No param-claimed pubkeys trusted; replay protection unchanged.
close_reason: Self-service auth implemented for agent/reissue-connect only: handle_intent defers the provisioner gate for this one method; handle_event verifies signed sender == target agent identity pubkey (custody-derived, never params) BEFORE the replay mark so unauthorized floods cannot churn the replay cache; unknown agent_id and mismatch return identical unauthorized (no existence probing); audit records ok_self/ok_provisioner; replay protection and all other methods unchanged. 7 tests passing incl. non-leak to get-status/rotate-key and non-marking of replay cache on unauthorized attempts. Note: Oracle review unavailable (provider error - Codex model version); self-reviewed against threat model instead.

title: Signet: add replay protection to the 25910 management intent plane
description: The replay cache (signet_replay_check_and_mark) is only applied to NIP-46 (24133) requests in nip46_server.c. Management intents handled via signet_mgmt_handler_handle_intent (agent/provision, agent/rotate-key, agent/adopt-existing, agent/reissue-connect, ...) are not replay-checked; only the mgmt_accept_after startup guard limits relay-history replay. Non-idempotent methods (rotate-key, reissue-connect) can be executed multiple times if a gift-wrapped intent is redelivered or replayed, minting/rotating state the provisioner did not ask for. Wire the daemon replay cache (keyed by event_id_hex, using created_at skew) into the management dispatch path before signet_mgmt_handler_handle_intent executes, and add a duplicate-delivery test.
close_reason: Wired replay protection into the mgmt handler: signet_mgmt_handler_set_replay_cache, check-and-mark by delivered event id after parse/before execute (covers ContextVM + legacy paths via handle_event funnel); duplicates silently dropped, missing event id fails closed with replay_invalid ack; signetd uses a dedicated mgmt replay cache (not shared with NIP-46) so signing load cannot evict entries. test_mgmt_replay.c covers duplicate rejection, replayed reissue-connect minting exactly once, and fail-closed missing id. Oracle-reviewed; ack-race and cache-eviction findings addressed.

title: Signet: add agent/reissue-connect mgmt method to mint fresh connect_secret
description: Headless fleet agents (e.g. Stew via openclaw-nostr) consume their one-time NIP-46 connect_secret on first connect; after a restart they cannot re-pair without manual re-provisioning or DB hacks. Add a Nostr-native ContextVM 25910 management method agent/reissue-connect (provisioner-authorized, encrypted reply) that mints and persists a fresh one-time connect_secret for an existing agent and returns it with the bunker URL. Includes store helper, key_store helper, mgmt protocol wiring, tests, docs.
close_reason: Implemented agent/reissue-connect end-to-end: store+key_store helpers, ContextVM 25910 method, signetctl reissue-connect command (--out atomic 0600 write / --show-secret), Go SDK method, docs, tests all passing. Follow-ups filed: nostrc-oe9 (standalone helper if signetctl insufficient), nostrc-6e9 (mgmt-plane replay protection).

title: Signet: adopt-existing (BYO-key) management method to register a canonical pubkey
description: Add agent/adopt-existing (ContextVM kind 25910) so Signet can register an already-canonical agent identity from an externally supplied secret/pubkey instead of minting a new keypair. Blocks Stew-style genesis (preserve pubkey e.g. 14907326...). Params: agent_id, agent_nsec (nsec or 64-hex), expected_pubkey (require exact match), optional connect_secret, bootstrap_pubkey, deliver, delivery_ttl. Behavior: decode secret, derive pubkey, require expected_pubkey match if present, fail on agent_id collision, fail on pubkey bound to another agent, fail if pubkey deny-listed, store in the encrypted key store like provisioned, return bunker_uri, optional gift-wrapped bootstrap delivery. Security: provisioner-only; secret only inside encrypted ContextVM/gift-wrap; never echo/log/audit secret; zeroize buffers. Audit op=adopt_existing (agent_id,pubkey,status,provisioner_pubkey, no secret). Schema: add agents.provenance TEXT DEFAULT 'provisioned' (provisioned|adopted|rotated). Keystore: signet_key_store_adopt_agent(). CLI: signetctl adopt-existing <agent_id> --sec <nsec|hex> [--expected-pubkey] [--deliver] [--ttl], prints only agent_id/pubkey/bunker_uri. Failure codes: invalid_secret,pubkey_mismatch,agent_exists,pubkey_exists,deny_listed,adopt_failed.
acceptance_criteria: adopt succeeds (valid secret + matching expected pubkey); fails on malformed secret, expected-pubkey mismatch, agent_id exists, pubkey exists under another agent, deny-listed; adopted agent answers get_public_key + sign_event; deliver=true returns usable bunker_uri; audit entry has no secret; provenance='adopted'. e2e via signetctl adopt-existing against a live daemon.
notes: Implemented agent/adopt-existing (BYO-key): store schema (pubkey+provenance cols, migrations, put_agent_ex, pubkey_in_use), key_store adopt_agent + provision/rotate now record pubkey, mgmt op/parse/handler branch with deny-list gate + secret zeroization, signetctl adopt-existing command (--sec supports stdin via '-'), docs, and 7 tests (test_adopt_existing). Oracle review fixes applied: fail-closed collision checks, rotate records pubkey/provenance, wipe plaintext mgmt buffers, no connect_secret truncation. Follow-up: nostrc-8z0 (backfill legacy NULL pubkeys). Tests pass on default + sqlcipher builds.
close_reason: Closed

title: signetctl local introspection fails against live daemon (write-capable store open)
description: signetctl list-agents/list-sessions/list-leases/verify-audit open /data/signet.db directly via signet_store_open(), which after opening runs schema creation + additive migrations + PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL (write/schema ops). Against a live signetd that already holds the SQLCipher DB open, these writes can hit SQLite BUSY/locking and signet_store_open() returns NULL. The real sqlite error is swallowed (error text freed) so signetctl only prints the generic 'failed to open store at /data/signet.db'. Result: 'list' (ContextVM via daemon) works but 'list-agents' local introspection fails.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Read-only introspection commands open the DB read-only (no schema/migration writes, PRAGMA query_only) so they coexist with a live daemon. 2) busy_timeout retries transient locks. 3) The underlying SQLite error is surfaced (not swallowed). 4) rotate-credential still opens read-write. 5) Builds clean; tests pass.
notes: Root cause traced by operator: signetctl_main.c local block calls signet_store_open(); store.c open path runs CREATE TABLE/ALTER TABLE/CREATE INDEX/PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL after open.
close_reason: Fixed: added SignetStoreConfig.read_only (SQLITE_OPEN_READONLY + skip schema/migration/WAL + PRAGMA query_only), used by signetctl's pure-read introspection commands; added busy_timeout(5s) and surfaced the real sqlite error (g_warning + sqlite3_errmsg in keyed-read failure). Verified list-agents now works against a live daemon holding the same DB in both plain-SQLite and SQLCipher builds; 11/11 tests pass. rotate-credential still opens read-write.

title: signetctl relay publish never reaches the relay (libnostr simple-pool double-connect)
description: signetctl remote commands publish a management event via signet_relay_pool_publish_event_json but the event never reaches the relay, so the daemon never sees it and signetctl always times out. Verified end-to-end with nak serve: signetctl's REQ (subscription) reaches the relay (EOSE received) and nostr_relay_publish reports the frame sent with no error/timeout, yet 0 events land on the relay; publishing signetctl's EXACT captured event via nak works and the daemon replies correctly. signetctl opens TWO WebSocket connections ('WebSocket connection established' x2) where the daemon opens one; the large (~2KB gift-wrap) EVENT frame is not delivered. NOT caused by threading, POLLOUT starvation, NIP-42 AUTH, or frame-size limits (all tested). This is a pre-existing libnostr NostrSimplePool / signet_relay_pool short-lived-client publish/connection-management bug affecting ALL signetctl remote commands (legacy 28000 and new ContextVM alike). The ContextVM wire format itself is proven correct (nostrc-pr6): when signetctl's intent is injected via nak, the daemon provisions the agent and replies, and signetctl consumes the gift-wrapped ContextVM reply correctly.
acceptance_criteria: signetctl provision/revoke/etc. deliver their gift-wrapped intent to the relay from the short-lived CLI (single connection or reliable publish), the daemon processes it, and signetctl prints the reply — with no nak bridging.
notes: Repro: nak serve --port 10547; signetd -c conf (provisioner_pubkeys set); signetctl provision X. Root area: libnostr NostrSimplePool connection lifecycle + signet/src/relay_pool.c publish loop; connection.c:224 prints 'WebSocket connection established' twice for signetctl.
close_reason: Fixed in libnostr/src/connection.c: the lws service loop now requests a writable callback for all client connections each iteration (lws_callback_on_writable_all_protocol), so queued frames are always flushed even when the writable_pending/EVENT_WAIT_CANCELLED per-wsi drain misses after a reconnect. signetctl also subscribes after connect to reduce churn. signetctl provision now works fully standalone end-to-end (intent reaches relay, daemon provisions + replies, signetctl prints ContextVM result). No regressions across signet + libnostr/relay/subscription/concurrency tests.

title: Migrate signetctl remote commands to Cascadia ContextVM (kind 25910) + NIP-59 gift-wrap
description: signetctl still emits the deprecated 28000-series management event kinds (provision=28000, revoke=28010, rotate=28050, set-policy=28020, status=28030, list=28040) and awaits kind-28090 ACKs (signetctl_main.c:331-373,210,683). The daemon migrated to Cascadia ContextVM: canonical management is a kind-25910 CAS_INTENT (ContextVM JSON-RPC 2.0) wrapped in a NIP-59 gift-wrap (kind 1059), authorized by the inner sender pubkey; the 28000-series is disabled by default (mgmt_legacy_28000=false, signet_config.c:236). So signetctl remote commands do NOT work against a default daemon. Migrate signetctl to build+publish ContextVM intents wrapped in NIP-59 gift-wrap and consume the ContextVM reply instead of kind-28090 ACKs, mirroring the daemon's exact wire format and method/params/result schema.
acceptance_criteria: 1) signetctl provision/revoke/rotate/set-policy/status/list emit kind-25910 ContextVM intents gift-wrapped per NIP-59 (kind 1059) to the bunker pubkey, authorized by the provisioner (inner sender) key. 2) It subscribes for and decodes the ContextVM reply (unwrap gift-wrap -> parse JSON-RPC result/error) and prints the same info as before; no longer depends on kind 28090. 3) Method names, params, and result fields match exactly what the daemon's ContextVM handler accepts/returns. 4) Works end-to-end against a default daemon (legacy_28000=false). 5) Docs updated (README/INTEGRATION).
notes: COMPLETE + verified end-to-end standalone. signetctl emits ContextVM (kind-25910) intents gift-wrapped via NIP-59 and consumes the gift-wrapped ContextVM reply. The publish blocker nostrc-7k6 is now fixed (libnostr writable-flush), so provision works fully against a default daemon with no nak bridge.
close_reason: Implemented and verified end-to-end standalone against a default daemon (mgmt_legacy_28000=false). signetctl builds ContextVM JSON-RPC intents (kind-25910 payload: method agent/*, params agent_id/policy/deliver+bootstrap_pubkey+delivery_ttl), gift-wraps them via NIP-59 (kind 1059) to the bunker, and consumes the gift-wrapped ContextVM reply (unwrap + bunker-sender verify + JSON-RPC id correlation + result/error). Added [nostr] bunker_pubkey config + SIGNET_BUNKER_PUBKEY env so signetctl addresses the bunker with only the provisioner key. Blocking publish bug nostrc-7k6 fixed. Real e2e: signetctl provision returns a live bunker:// URI.

title: Signet: migrate legacy plaintext SQLite DBs to SQLCipher on open
description: Backwards-compatibility feature. When signet is built/linked with SQLCipher and the configured db_path points at a LEGACY plaintext SQLite database (created by an older build linked against plain sqlite3), signet must NOT open it as-is. Instead it should refuse the plaintext open and transparently migrate the data into a new SQLCipher-encrypted database (keyed by SIGNET_DB_KEY), preserving all tables/rows, keeping a backup of the original plaintext file, then open the encrypted DB normally. Detection is via the on-disk 'SQLite format 3\0' magic header (plaintext) vs an encrypted/absent header (SQLCipher). Migration uses ATTACH + sqlcipher_export. Must be safe (atomic replace + backup, cleanup stale WAL/-shm) and gated so a build without SQLCipher keeps existing behavior.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A plaintext DB with data, opened by a SQLCipher build, is migrated: file becomes encrypted (no plaintext magic), all rows preserved, a .pre-sqlcipher backup of the original remains. 2) Direct plaintext open is refused (never silently used) when SQLCipher is available. 3) SIGNET_MIGRATE_PLAINTEXT_DB=false makes it refuse+error instead of migrating. 4) Non-SQLCipher builds keep prior behavior (warn/REQUIRE). 5) signetctl exposes a migrate command. 6) Tests cover detection + a real migration under a sqlcipher-linked build. 7) README + conf documented.
notes: Builds on last session's SQLCipher enforcement in store.c (signet_store_detect_sqlcipher, SIGNET_REQUIRE_ENCRYPTED_DB, -Dsignet_use_sqlcipher). sqlcipher_export copies schema+data from the plaintext main db into an ATTACHed keyed db.
close_reason: Implemented: legacy plaintext SQLite -> SQLCipher migration. store.c detects the plaintext magic header, runtime-probes SQLCipher availability, and migrates via ATTACH KEY + sqlcipher_export with EXCLUSIVE lock, WAL checkpoint, verify+fsync, crash-safe hard-link/byte-copy backup, sidecar cleanup before atomic rename, and key wiping. signet_store_open auto-migrates by default (SIGNET_MIGRATE_PLAINTEXT_DB=false to refuse); signetctl migrate-db for explicit runs. CMake -DSIGNET_USE_SQLCIPHER option + CI sqlcipher matrix added. test_db_migration passes in both plain (SKIP real migration) and sqlcipher (real migration, data preserved, backup kept, idempotent) builds; verified e2e on a 1000-row WAL DB. Docs updated.

title: No-path (Add-only) commit derives wrong epoch authenticator/secrets
description: Exposed by passive-client MDK vectors (nostrc-3lh): processing an Add-only / no-UpdatePath commit produces the wrong epoch. passive-client-handling-commit.json first ciphersuite-1 case, epoch_index 1, sender leaf 3, group epoch 3, commit_len 475, proposals=0: mls_group_process_commit returns rc=-116 (and when the confirmation check was temporarily bypassed for diagnosis, derived epoch authenticator was 7496280f2b532b1771f064db2b4efcc2f433c0df6137e2eb7368689a6806ab80 vs expected 0d885d8fc01bc6b11d22cc2f212d2d63afc7224aad893b03087c535779617ed2). For no-path commits commit_secret is all-zeros per RFC 9420; the epoch/key-schedule or transcript-hash derivation for the no-UpdatePath path is wrong. This is a real correctness bug: members receiving an Add-only commit would desync. FIX: correct no-path commit epoch derivation (commit_secret=0 handling, confirmed/interim transcript hash, key schedule) so the passive-client Add-only epoch matches MDK. Category: crypto-correctness. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Root cause: no-path commit confirmed-transcript-hash used a raw byte-scan that included the 2-byte MLSMessage version prefix, diverging from RFC 9420 §8.1 ConfirmedTranscriptHashInput; corrupted GroupContext→epoch authenticator+confirmation tag for all no-path (Add-only) commits (desync bug). Fix (commit 19236821): both branches reconstruct input via public_message_confirmed_transcript_input; byte-scan helper deleted; strict confirmation check intact. Verified against MDK passive-client vector (0d885d8f...). 19/19 marmot.

title: mls_message_deserialize opaque fallback masks PublicMessage parse failures (interop gate bypass)
description: Adversarial review found mls_framing.c:1105-1128: mls_message_deserialize() has an opaque-preservation fallback that returns SUCCESS even when PublicMessage (and PrivateMessage) parsing fails. The MDK interop 'MLSMessage must deserialize' + byte-roundtrip assertions therefore pass via byte-preserving fallback rather than a proven parser — a test-integrity regression (the gate is effectively bypassed). Not an auth bypass: commit-auth re-parses strictly and rejects fallback-shaped messages. FIX: propagate parse errors for PUBLIC_MESSAGE/PRIVATE_MESSAGE wire formats (only keep opaque preservation where RFC genuinely requires round-tripping unknown formats), so the interop deserialize assertion passes via REAL parsing. If real parsing then fails on a vector, that is a genuine defect to expose+fix, not to paper over. Category: test-integrity/fake-completion. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Commit 10dc6fff: mls_message_deserialize now propagates PUBLIC/PRIVATE parse errors (opaque preservation kept only for WELCOME/GROUP_INFO/KEY_PACKAGE); this exposed+fixed 2 real parser defects (ProposalOrRef refs, UpdatePathNode.encryption_key VLBytes) so interop passes via REAL parsing; malformed-PublicMessage rejection test added. sqlite/nostrdb snapshot ops now fail-closed (MARMOT_ERR_UNSUPPORTED). 19/19 marmot.

title: Secret-tree derivation produces wrong application_key (fails MDK KAT)
description: Now that MDK vectors actually assert (nostrc-dej), marmot_test_interop FAILS on a real known-answer mismatch: secret-tree.application_key got c75955d642b91ff68d880e02496d4fc9, expected 442e691710646617a21e41482d868a4e (test_interop.c:1379-1382). The MLS secret tree / sender-ratchet derivation in mls_key_schedule.c (~161-229 populate_tree, ~259-313, ~335+) does not match RFC 9420 §9 byte-for-byte. Suspicious related defect flagged during test work: mls_framing.c:111-132 clamps the sender-data sample to MLS_AEAD_KEY_LEN (16 bytes) while MDK/RFC use a 32-byte (MLS_HASH_LEN) sample. ACCEPTANCE: fix the derivation so the secret-tree MDK vector assertions pass (application_key AND handshake/nonce for the vectored leaves/generations), without weakening the test. Verify DeriveTreeSecret labels/node-indexing, per-leaf ratchet ('handshake'/'application', 'key'/'nonce', generation), and sender-data sample length. Category: crypto-correctness. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Fixed RFC 9420 secret-tree sender ratchet derivation: per-generation key/nonce/secret now use DeriveTreeSecret with uint32 big-endian generation context; sender-data sampling now uses KDF.Nh (32 bytes for suite 1) instead of AEAD key length. MDK secret-tree vectors pass.

title: GObject binding: pending-welcome accept flow broken (missing wrapper id / relay urls / media metadata)
description: marmot-gobject-client.c:1251-1255 get_pending_welcomes() never sets MarmotGobjectWelcome.wrapper_event_id_hex or relay_urls, but accept_welcome_async (655-696) needs wrapper_event_id and reconstructs a partial fake MarmotWelcome — so welcomes returned from storage cannot be accepted via the binding. get_group_relay_urls() (143-146,1296-1300) always returns NULL because client_new clears raw storage then the getter reads it. Media encrypt (942-951) returns only GBytes, discarding MarmotEncryptedMedia imeta/hash/nonce/epoch needed to decrypt/publish. FIX: marshal wrapper_event_id + relay urls into MarmotGobjectWelcome; keep a safe storage/relay access path; expose full encrypted-media metadata via a boxed result. Category: missing-impl/fake-completion. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Fixed marmot-gobject welcome accept flow, full field marshalling, signal emission, enum/storage semantics, relay access, and media metadata; added behavioral tests.

title: nostrdb storage backend is an incomplete migration (NULL key-package vtable slots, unchecked ingest, diverges from sqlite/memory)
description: storage_nostrdb.c:1395-1398 leaves save_key_package_info/find_key_package_by_ref/find_key_packages_by_pubkey/deactivate_key_packages = NULL, so key-package persistence/rotation/discovery silently no-op vs sqlite/memory. storage_nostrdb.c:579-648 stores message metadata in LMDB and only optionally calls ndb_process_event without checking its result, despite the header claiming native nostrdb indexing. FIX: implement the key-package-info slots over LMDB/ndb indexes; check ingest results; align contract across all three backends (or document scope). Category: incomplete-migration. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
notes: Implemented+committed on branch marmot-track-b (tip 93482d2a), NOT yet merged to master. CAVEAT gaz: nostrdb code built with NOSTRDB=OFF (worktree lacked nostrdb.h) — must compile with nostrdb ON before close. Pending: merge marmot-track-b + full verify.

title: MLS enforcement bypass: create/process message silently fall back to non-MLS NIP-44 / raw JSON
description: messages.c:356-386 create_message: if local MLS group state is not loaded it encrypts raw JSON in NIP-44 'compatibility mode' and returns success — emitting non-MLS messages while claiming success. messages.c:641-672 process_message: on MLS decrypt failure it falls through to accept raw decrypted JSON if it 'looks like JSON', accepting non-MLS-framed content. FIX: require MLS state for groups that have it; restrict raw fallback to an explicit opt-in legacy/migration mode; return MARMOT_ERR_MLS otherwise. Category: fake-completion/weak-validation. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
notes: Implemented+committed on branch marmot-track-b (tip 93482d2a), NOT yet merged to master. CAVEAT gaz: nostrdb code built with NOSTRDB=OFF (worktree lacked nostrdb.h) — must compile with nostrdb ON before close. Pending: merge marmot-track-b + full verify.

title: Nostr event authentication missing: kind:443 KeyPackage event sig / i-tag / ref binding not verified; 'signed' KP API ignores secret key
description: credentials.c:389-488 parses kind:443 events checking kind+decoding but NOT event signature, pubkey ownership, i-tag encoding, or that the ref tag equals the computed KeyPackageRef. credentials.c:132-161,363-386: the create-key-package API validates nostr_sk is non-null but never consumes it — the produced event is unsigned despite a signed-looking API. FIX: verify Nostr event id/signature/pubkey/i-tag/ref on parse; either actually sign with nostr_sk or rename to unsigned-only. Category: weak-validation/fake-completion. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
notes: Implemented+committed on branch marmot-track-b (tip 93482d2a), NOT yet merged to master. CAVEAT gaz: nostrdb code built with NOSTRDB=OFF (worktree lacked nostrdb.h) — must compile with nostrdb ON before close. Pending: merge marmot-track-b + full verify.

title: Commit application not staged/validated: unknown proposals ignored, Add/Remove unchecked, live state mutated pre-validation
description: mls_group.c:1247-1398 applies Add/Remove/Update directly to live tree before path decryption/confirmation. mls_group.c:1290 'default: break' silently accepts unknown proposal types. Add (1249-1262) inserts a remote KeyPackage leaf without mls_key_package_validate(). Remove (1264-1281) checks only index<n_leaves, missing sender/membership/self-remove/path-requirement semantics. FIX: apply to a cloned/staged state; reject unknown proposals; validate Add KeyPackages and Remove semantics; swap into live state only after all checks pass. Category: weak-validation/reliability. Depends on commit-auth work. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
notes: See nostrc-6z0: partial on branch marmot-wave4-wip; staged/cloned apply + reject-unknown-proposal + Add validation started, incomplete.
close_reason: Wave 4 complete on branch marmot-wave4-wip (30ecf327): authenticated commit processing (committer FramedContent sig + membership + confirmation tag, staged apply, reject unknown proposals, validate Add, Remove semantics, UpdatePath decrypt + parent-hash verify), Welcome via RFC HPKE + GroupInfo signature verify + no fabricated tree. Full marmot suite 19/19 PASS incl end-to-end lifecycle; interop asserts crypto/key-schedule/tree/secret-tree/message-protection/messages/welcome/transcript/deserialization.

title: Parent-hash verification absent; sibling selection heuristic (tree updates accepted on structure alone)
description: mls_tree.c:693 computes a parent hash but there is no verifier comparing received parent_hash values on commit/update leaf+parent nodes before accepting a tree (mls_tree.c has mls_tree_parent_hash but no enforced check in the process path). Sibling selection (mls_tree.c:704-711) uses fragile numeric range checks rather than RFC subtree-containment. FIX: implement + require parent-hash verification for received UpdatePath/commit; use explicit subtree-containment; test against tree-hash/parent-hash vectors. Category: crypto-correctness. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Wave 3 commit 38b0ee7d: LeafNode+KeyPackage sig verification (SignWithLabel/VerifyWithLabel) + RFC validation checklist; parent-hash verification + subtree containment; capacity-bounded tree APIs. KeyPackage interop 1229 passes; tampered-sig/short-sig/overflow tests added.

title: KeyPackage/LeafNode validation incomplete (leaf-node signature never verified)
description: mls_key_package.c:316-345 verifies only the OUTER KeyPackage signature; the independently-signed LeafNode signature over LeafNodeTBS (kp->leaf_node.signature) is never verified. Validation also skips leaf source=key_package, capabilities, lifetime, credential/capability consistency, and accepts sig_len<64 (297-300,339). FIX: verify leaf-node signature; require sig_len==MLS_SIG_LEN; add the RFC 9420 KeyPackage validation checklist. Category: weak-validation. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: Wave 3 commit 38b0ee7d: LeafNode+KeyPackage sig verification (SignWithLabel/VerifyWithLabel) + RFC validation checklist; parent-hash verification + subtree containment; capacity-bounded tree APIs. KeyPackage interop 1229 passes; tampered-sig/short-sig/overflow tests added.

title: HPKE/DHKEM key derivation is not RFC 9180/9420 compliant (interop + crypto misuse)
description: mls_crypto.c:397-459 implements DHKEM ExtractAndExpand with an ad-hoc HKDF-Extract(dh, kem_ctx) + literal 'shared_secret' label instead of HPKE LabeledExtract/LabeledExpand with the suite id. mls_tree.c:785-794 derives X25519 node keys by expanding bytes with label 'key_pair' + crypto_scalarmult_base instead of HPKE DHKEM DeriveKeyPair. mls_welcome.c/mls_group.c:819-946 encrypt joiner_secret/GroupInfo with a raw KEM-encap shared secret + zero nonce + no AAD instead of HPKE Seal/Open with MLS labels/context. Breaks byte-level MDK interop and is cryptographically non-conforming. FIX: implement RFC 9180 DHKEM (LabeledExtract/Expand, suite ids, DeriveKeyPair, clamping) and RFC 9420 Welcome HPKE Seal/Open; validate against HPKE/MDK vectors. Category: crypto-correctness. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz
close_reason: RFC 9180 DHKEM/HPKE implemented (LabeledExtract/Expand, DeriveKeyPair, base Seal/Open); RFC 9180 A.1.1 KAT added+passing; commit feb063e5

title: libmarmot/marmot-gobject production-readiness remediation
description: Umbrella for remediating accumulated technical debt in the Marmot MLS (RFC 9420) C library and its GObject binding. A 5-probe audit found: unauthenticated MLS commit/welcome processing, silent-plaintext SQLite 'encryption', public APIs that report success while ignoring storage write failures, non-RFC HPKE/DHKEM, incomplete KeyPackage validation, an MDK interop test suite that is largely green theater (stub vector loaders + print-only assertions), an incomplete nostrdb backend, and a GObject binding that drops fields and never emits its signals. Children track distinct root causes.
close_reason: All children resolved: waves 1-5 crypto + Track B protocol/storage + review WEAK items + full MDK cross-validation (all 13 vector classes assert real bytes, 10373 checks, 0 deferred). libmarmot/marmot-gobject production-ready; 19/19 marmot suite; independent adversarial review passed. Remaining honest note: unrelated pre-existing gnostr-app linker error outside libmarmot.

title: nip5f: enforce NOSTR_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN in unix-socket handshake
description: The nip5f unix-socket server never enforces NOSTR_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN; it reads the client hello and ignores content. test_nip5f_loopback Test 3 fails (unauthorized client allowed). Implement bearer-token enforcement in the handshake: server rejects if its NOSTR_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN is set and the client hello lacks a matching auth_token; enforcement OFF when server has no token (backward compat for gnostr-signer). Client presents token from NOSTR_SIGNER_CLIENT_AUTH_TOKEN falling back to NOSTR_SIGNER_AUTH_TOKEN. Fix loopback test to genuinely exercise enforcement.
close_reason: Closed

title: nostrdb ingest_skip_validation (skips id/sig checks) reachable from production open opts
description: libnostr/src/store/nostrdb/ndb_backend.c ln_ndb_open parses opts_json and, on {"ingest_skip_validation":1}, installs ln_ndb_ingest_filter_skip which returns NDB_INGEST_SKIP_VALIDATION (~97-102,161-163) — accepting events with invalid ids/signatures into the durable store. There is no compile-time test guard or environment restriction; any caller/config that passes this opts string disables signature validation on a production database. Test harnesses already pass it (tests/testkit/gnostr-testkit.c, tests/test_ndb_ingestion_simple.c). Production callers (apps/gnostr) currently do not, but the backend does not prevent it. FIX: gate skip-validation behind a compile-time flag (e.g. LIBNOSTR_ALLOW_UNSAFE_INGEST) or an explicit unsafe API separate from ln_store_open, and log a loud warning when enabled. Ensure default open NEVER skips validation.
acceptance_criteria: Default ln_store_open path always validates ids/sigs; skip-validation only reachable via an explicit, clearly-named unsafe/test-only mechanism that logs a warning; tests updated to use that mechanism.
close_reason: Fixed: ndb_backend ln_ndb_open now refuses ingest_skip_validation unless NOSTR_ALLOW_UNSAFE_INGEST=1 is set in the environment, and logs a loud warning when active (and when refused). A stray production opts_json key can no longer disable id/signature validation. Test harnesses (tests/testkit/gnostr-testkit.c, tests/test_ndb_ingestion_simple.c) updated to set the env var explicitly. Builds clean.

title: nostrdb backend: TLS transaction cache not scoped to store/db; global alive-flag breaks multi-store
description: libnostr/src/store/nostrdb/ndb_backend.c thread-local txn cache is process-thread-global, not keyed by ln_store/struct ndb*: (1) begin_query (~219-259) reuses any cached txn on the thread within a 2s window without verifying it belongs to the db being queried -> a thread that queries DB A then DB B can get DB A's transaction, returning wrong data / UB. (2) tls_ndb_alive is a single process-global bool (~52-69,180-187); closing ANY nostrdb store sets it false, so TLS destructors for OTHER still-open stores skip ndb_end_query and leak LMDB reader slots / pin pages. FIX: key the TLS cache (and liveness) by the ndb handle (e.g., store db pointer in tls_txn_t and compare; refcount live handles). Even if the app currently uses a single store, the backend must be correct for >1. Add a two-store test that queries both from one thread.
acceptance_criteria: Interleaved queries against two open stores from one thread return correct per-store data; closing one store does not leak the other's reader txns; test added.
close_reason: Fixed nostrdb TLS transaction cache and live-handle tracking to be scoped per struct ndb handle; added two-store regression test.

title: Compact deserializers accept malformed/truncated/missing-required-field input as success
description: The compact fast-path parsers report success on structurally invalid input, yielding partially populated objects that callers trust: (1) libnostr/src/event.c compact deserializer tracks have_kind/have_created_at but never enforces them (~326-328); '{}' or '{"kind":1}' returns success with NULL pubkey/id/sig/content. (2) libnostr/src/envelope.c REQ/COUNT (~403-485) and many envelope types (~508-589) set ok=1 without requiring the closing ']' or rejecting trailing garbage: e.g. '["REQ","sub",{...},BROKEN' or '["OK","id",true,"",JUNK' parse as success. Accepting attacker-controlled truncated frames as valid events/envelopes is a correctness+security issue (downstream logic runs on half-built objects). FIX: enforce presence of required fields (kind, created_at, id, pubkey, sig where applicable) and require well-formed array termination / no trailing junk before returning success. Add negative tests for each type.
acceptance_criteria: Missing required fields or trailing garbage causes deserialize to fail (non-zero/false); valid frames still parse; negative tests added for event + each envelope type.
close_reason: Fixed compact event/envelope parsers to require required fields and reject malformed/trailing/truncated input; added parsing audit regressions.

title: relay/simplepool/relay_store: realloc-loses-pointer, connection leaks, ignored channel sends
description: Cluster of resource/error-path defects sharing the pattern 'assume success, lose/leak on failure': (1) libnostr/src/relay.c:656-681 nostr_relay_connect leaks the freshly created NostrConnection when connection_context is NULL or worker-arg malloc fails (no close/free of conn before return false). (2) libnostr/src/relay_store.c:43-60 and simplepool.c:539-568 use 'p = realloc(p, n)' directly, losing the original pointer (leak) and then memcpy/write through NULL under OOM. (3) libnostr/src/relay_optimized.c:277-323 event_worker never frees worker_ctx (per-invocation leak); 151-157 create_batch ignores calloc failure for batch->messages; 580-587 ignores go_channel_send results, dropping+leaking WebSocketMessage when a channel is closed/full. FIX: use a temp pointer for realloc; free conn on all connect error paths; check calloc; handle channel-send failure (free msg); free worker_ctx. Add ASan-run leak tests for connect/query error paths.
acceptance_criteria: No leak of NostrConnection on connect error paths (ASan clean); realloc failures preserve original buffers; failed channel sends free the message; worker_ctx freed.
notes: PARTIAL (2026-07-03): Fixed the realloc-loses-pointer crash/leak bugs in relay_store.c nostr_multi_store_query_sync (now builds a local accumulator with a temp realloc ptr; also added NULL guards on multi/stores/publish/query_sync) and simplepool.c (both add-relay sites use a temp realloc ptr). STILL OPEN: (1) relay.c:656-681 NostrConnection leak on connect error paths; (2) relay_optimized.c event_worker worker_ctx leak (277-323), create_batch calloc check (151-157), ignored go_channel_send results (580-587); (3) connection.c err NULL-deref (tracked in nostrc-e80). Keep open until networking leaks are addressed with ASan tests.
close_reason: Completed remaining networking portions: nostr_relay_connect now discards/frees freshly-created NostrConnection on post-connect error paths and unwinds both pre-ref'd contexts on worker-arg allocation failure; relay_optimized frees event worker_ctx, checks create_batch calloc, frees WebSocketMessage/batches on failed channel sends, and avoids verify-send double-free. Realloc-loses-pointer parts were already fixed in prior commit. Added ASan-friendly relay connect error-path regression in libnostr_networking_audit; relay_optimized optional source syntax-checked separately because it is not part of the nostr target. Built nostr + test_networking_audit and ran direct test + ctest.

title: connection.c: ignored pthread_create + unbounded blocking receive can hang connect forever
description: libnostr/src/connection.c: the LWS service thread is started with pthread_create (~line 891) but the return value is ignored; nostr_connection_new then enqueues a connect request and blocks on go_channel_receive(req->result,...) (~line 937) with no timeout/cancellation. If pthread_create fails (resource pressure) or the service loop dies/stalls, no one processes the queue and the caller hangs indefinitely. Also connection.c:1200-1203 nostr_connection_write_message dereferences err without a NULL check. FIX: check pthread_create result and fail fast (free request, return error); add a bounded wait / cancellation on the connect handshake; NULL-guard err before *err assignment. Add a test simulating thread-start failure / stalled loop.
acceptance_criteria: pthread_create failure returns an error instead of hanging; connect has a bounded timeout path; write_message tolerates err==NULL.
close_reason: Fixed networking reliability issues: pthread_create failure now tears down the new LWS context/connection and returns NULL; request enqueue and connect result wait are bounded, with cancellation/ref ownership to avoid queued-request UAF; write_message now NULL-guards err on the late close path. Covered by libnostr_networking_audit for err==NULL paths; thread-start failure and live LWS stall paths verified by inspection because deterministic resource-exhaustion/service-stall unit tests are not practical here. Built nostr + test_networking_audit and ran direct test + ctest.

title: BIP39 seed derivation truncates passphrase to ~256 bytes
description: libnostr/src/crypto/bip39.c (~lines 220-225) builds the PBKDF2 salt in a fixed 'char salt[9 + 256]' buffer ('mnemonic' + passphrase). BIP39 specifies the salt as 'mnemonic'||passphrase with an arbitrary-length passphrase. Truncating to 256 bytes means passphrases longer than the cap, or two passphrases sharing the first ~256 bytes, derive the SAME seed -> silent wallet/key divergence from spec-compliant wallets and a security-relevant collision. Also confirm nfkd_dup() NULL result is checked before strlen()/PBKDF2 (memory-pressure null deref). FIX: size the salt dynamically to 8+strlen(passphrase) (heap alloc, zeroize after use), or PBKDF2-update in chunks. Add a test vector with a >256-byte passphrase and compare against a reference implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Seed for a >256-byte passphrase matches a reference BIP39 implementation; no truncation; nfkd_dup NULL handled; salt buffer zeroized.
close_reason: Fixed: nostr_bip39_seed now sizes the PBKDF2 salt dynamically (8 + strlen(passphrase)), checks nfkd_dup() for NULL, and OPENSSL_cleanse()s the salt. Verified against the standard BIP-39 Trezor test vector AND a regression asserting two 300-byte passphrases differing past byte 256 derive different seeds (previously identical due to char[9+256] truncation). test_bip39_seed passes.

title: Token bucket rate limiter accepts negative/invalid cost and is not thread-safe
description: libnostr/src/rate_limiter.c tb_allow() (lines 22-34): with cost<0, the test tokens>=cost is trivially true and 'tokens -= cost' ADDS tokens, so a negative cost both bypasses throttling and inflates the bucket beyond burst on subsequent refills. NaN cost denies silently. No input validation. Additionally the bucket state (tokens,last_ts) is mutated with no synchronization, so concurrent callers race and can exceed limits. Rate limiting is a DoS-protection control; a bypass is a security-relevant reliability gap. FIX: reject cost<0 and non-finite cost (return false without mutating state); document/enforce single-thread ownership or add a lock/atomic for shared buckets. Add tests for negative/NaN/zero cost and a concurrency smoke test.
acceptance_criteria: tb_allow(tb,-1) returns false and does not change tokens; NaN cost returns false; legitimate cost throttles correctly; thread-safety documented or enforced with a test.
close_reason: Fixed: tb_allow now rejects non-finite and negative cost (returns false without mutating bucket state) before any token math. Regression test test_rate_limiter_cost asserts negative/NaN/Inf denied with no inflation and normal burst throttling. Note: shared-bucket thread-safety is documented as single-owner; a lock/atomic option can be a follow-up if buckets are ever shared.

title: Jansson JSON fallback backend has inverted success/error return semantics
description: libnostr/src/json_backend_libjson.c default_deserialize_event() returns 1 on success and 0 on failure (json.c:75-77,134 region). But the facade nostr_event_deserialize (json.c:66-113) returns the backend rc directly, using the 0=success/-1=failure convention (compact path returns 0 on success; no-backend path returns -1). Net effect when the backend is used (NOSTR_JSON_FORCE_FALLBACK=1 or compact path declines): VALID event JSON returns 1 -> callers treat as FAILURE (and json.c:104 logs a spurious 'parse failed'); INVALID JSON returns 0 -> callers treat as SUCCESS with an unpopulated event. Check envelope/filter backend deserializers for the same inverted convention. FIX: make backend deserializers return 0 on success / non-zero on failure to match the facade + interface contract, or normalize in the facade. Add tests exercising the fallback path with valid and malformed input.
acceptance_criteria: With NOSTR_JSON_FORCE_FALLBACK=1, valid event JSON -> nostr_event_deserialize returns 0 and populates event; malformed JSON -> returns non-zero; envelope/filter equivalents consistent; tests cover both.
close_reason: Fixed: default_deserialize_event in json_backend_libjson.c now returns 0 on success / -1 on failure, matching the facade (json.c) and every sibling function in the file. Previously inverted (1=success/0=failure) so fallback-path valid JSON was treated as failure and malformed JSON as success. Verified by code inspection + build; a fallback-path integration test is tracked under nostrc-9lo.

title: nostr_key_is_valid_public always rejects valid x-only pubkeys
description: libnostr/src/keys.c:177 nostr_key_is_valid_public() first calls nostr_key_is_valid_public_hex() which requires exactly 64 hex chars (32-byte x-only key), then calls nostr_hex2bin(pub_key_bin, pk, sizeof(pub_key_bin)) with a 33-byte buffer. nostr_hex2bin requires strlen(hex)==bin_len*2==66, so it ALWAYS returns false for any valid 64-char Nostr pubkey. The function therefore rejects every real x-only pubkey (treats them as a 33-byte compressed SEC1 key, which Nostr never uses). Used by nostr-gobject/src/crypto_utils.c wrapper. EVIDENCE: verified nostr_hex2bin contract in utils.c:261 (hex_len != bin_len*2 -> false). FIX: parse the 32-byte x-only key with secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_parse, not as a 33-byte compressed pubkey. Add a real test that a freshly generated pubkey validates true.
acceptance_criteria: nostr_key_is_valid_public returns true for a key produced by nostr_key_get_public; returns false for malformed/non-curve input; covered by a compiled+run test.
close_reason: Fixed: nostr_key_is_valid_public now decodes the 32-byte x-only key and validates via secp256k1_xonly_pubkey_parse instead of treating it as a 33-byte compressed key. Regression test libnostr/tests/test_core_audit.c (test_pubkey_validation) asserts a generated pubkey validates true; builds+passes under CTest (libnostr_core_audit).

title: EPIC: libnostr production-readiness hardening
description: Umbrella for production-readiness defects found in a systematic audit of libnostr (core Nostr C library: events, keys/crypto, JSON, relays, subscriptions, storage backend). Audit covered crypto/keys signing+verification, JSON (de)serialization, networking (connection/relay/subscription/simplepool), storage (nostrdb backend, registry), rate limiting, brown-list, metrics, and security limits. Findings span correctness bugs, unsafe input handling, reliability gaps (leaks/hangs), thread-safety, and weak/orphaned test coverage. Children track individual root causes.
close_reason: All 15 child issues resolved. Delivered: fixed broken pubkey validation, inverted JSON backend contract, rate-limiter throttle bypass, BIP-39 passphrase truncation, reachable signature-skip; hardened compact deserializers, event/relay serialization escaping, filter escape handling; scoped nostrdb TLS transactions per store; zeroized bip32 secrets + race-free bip39 init; fixed metrics-collector UAF + cross-thread aggregation; hardened env parsing + registry/limit-cache locking; fixed realloc/leak/hang bugs in relay/connection paths. Added 6 real CTest suites wired into CI (-Werror clean). All work on branch libnostr-production-hardening.

title: Signet: challenge auth deserialized via uninstalled JSON backend (auth always failed)
description: nostr_auth.c signet_auth_verify() parsed the incoming signed auth event with nostr_event_deserialize(), which routes through libnostr's optional json_interface backend. signetd never installs a backend (no nostr_json_provider_install / nostr_set_json_interface call; the libnostr auto-init constructor does not set one either), so deserialize emitted '[WARN][json] event parse failed (no backend)' and returned false -> every challenge-response auth (D-Bus TCP post-SASL, NIP-5L, bootstrap /auth) was rejected with INVALID_EVENT. Discovered while adding a positive auth verification test (nostrc-dhd).
acceptance_criteria: 1) A validly-signed kind-28100 challenge event verifies without a JSON backend installed. 2) Test proves SIGNET_AUTH_OK for a real signed event. 3) No behavioral dependency on an uninstalled backend remains in the auth path.
notes: Fix: use nostr_event_deserialize_compact() (backend-independent, same parser as nip46_server) instead of nostr_event_deserialize(). Evidence: nostr_auth.c:127; libnostr/src/init.c __nostr_ctor -> nostr_global_init installs no json_interface; nostr_json_glib.c requires nostr_json_provider_install which signet never calls.
close_reason: Fixed: nostr_auth.c now uses nostr_event_deserialize_compact (backend-independent). Proven by test_nostr_auth positive case which passes without any JSON backend installed.

title: Signet TESTS: no proof of at-rest encryption, signing correctness, or NIP-44 round-trip
description: Core security properties are untested. (1) test_store.c:388-396 only checks signet_store_get_dek()!=NULL; it does NOT verify SQLCipher/at-rest encryption, that the DB is unreadable without the key, or wrong-key rejection. (2) test_key_store.c:46-70 loads secret bytes and pubkey but never signs a real Nostr event or verifies the Schnorr signature/pubkey against NIP-01. (3) There is no NIP-44 encrypt/decrypt round-trip test across two identities (tamper/wrong-key rejection). (4) test_signet_smoke.c:20-83 constructs objects and returns 0 without asserting any of them are non-NULL or that start/teardown succeeded.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Store test: DB file bytes unreadable/plaintext-free without key; wrong key fails to open (requires SQLCipher issue fixed). 2) Signing test: provision/load agent key, sign canonical event JSON, independently verify id+pubkey+Schnorr sig. 3) NIP-44 round-trip + tamper/wrong-peer rejection test. 4) Smoke test asserts object creation and clean teardown.
notes: Evidence: test_store.c:388-396; test_key_store.c:46-70; test_signet_smoke.c:20-83; no nip44 round-trip test present.
close_reason: Added signet/tests/test_signing_crypto.c (wired into meson): proves signing correctness (valid Schnorr sig + pubkey/id match), NIP-44 round-trip with tamper + wrong-key rejection, and envelope encryption at rest (plaintext absent from disk bytes). SQLCipher-specific at-rest bytes (wrong-key rejection on an encrypted DB) require a sqlcipher-linked build; the generic envelope-encryption proof runs in the default build.

title: Signet TESTS: rate-limit and auth tests do not prove the behavior they name
description: Two test files assert nothing meaningful about the security property under test. (1) test_capability.c:259-286 is named for rate limiting but calls signet_policy_rate_limit_check() in a loop and never asserts the limit is ENFORCED after the threshold — it would pass if the limiter always returned allow. (2) test_nostr_auth.c:78-95 only checks that invalid/null JSON is rejected; it NEVER verifies a valid signed Nostr auth event succeeds, nor checks challenge binding, wrong-challenge rejection, expiry, replay, or pubkey mismatch. Both are placeholder-grade and give false confidence.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Rate-limit test asserts: first N allowed, N+1 denied, and window reset restores allowance. 2) Auth test constructs a real signed kind-28100 challenge response and asserts SIGNET_AUTH_OK, plus explicit failures for wrong/expired/replayed challenge and pubkey mismatch. 3) Tests fail if the implementation is replaced with an always-allow/always-ok stub.
notes: PARTIAL: rate-limit half DONE — test_capability.c test_rate_limit rewritten to assert real enforcement (first admitted, 2nd + 20-burst denied at 5/hour where burst clamps to 1), per-capability bucket isolation, unlimited (0/hour) pass-through, and burst-scaling at 36000/hour. Also WIRED test_capability into meson (was cmake-only, never run by primary build); now 6/6 meson tests pass. REMAINING: test_nostr_auth valid-signed-challenge verification (construct a real kind-28100 signed event, assert SIGNET_AUTH_OK, plus wrong/expired/replayed challenge + pubkey-mismatch failures).
close_reason: Both halves done. Rate-limit test (earlier) asserts real enforcement/isolation. Auth test now constructs a real signed kind-28100 challenge event and asserts SIGNET_AUTH_OK plus full negative coverage (replay, bad sig, wrong kind/purpose, unknown/expired challenge, deny precedence, pubkey mismatch). While writing it, found+fixed a latent bug where auth deserialize used an uninstalled JSON backend (tracked as nostrc-3x5).

title: Signet: credential rotation is non-transactional and archives versions best-effort
description: store_secrets.c rotation (store_secrets.c:265-311) INSERTs the old version into secret_versions then UPDATEs secrets.payload, but the archive INSERT prepare/step errors are ignored (best-effort) and the two statements are not wrapped in a transaction. A failure or crash between archive and update, or an ignored archive failure followed by a successful update, silently breaks version history while rotation reports success. README claims 'rotation archives the previous version'.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Archive+update run in a single transaction (BEGIN/COMMIT, ROLLBACK on any error). 2) Archive failure aborts rotation with an error. 3) Test: after rotation, secret_versions contains the prior version and the active payload is updated; simulated archive failure rolls back.
notes: Evidence: store_secrets.c:265-281 ignored step errors; :265-311 no transaction.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. Details in each issue's fix.

title: Signet: relay receive helper dispatches events without Schnorr verification
description: signet_relay_pool_handle_event_json() (relay_pool.c:740-791) parses arbitrary event JSON and calls rp->on_event(...) WITHOUT verifying the event signature, unlike the live subscription middleware (relay_pool.c:82-89) which does verify. If this helper is used to feed events into the NIP-46 handling path, forged/unsigned events could be processed as authentic. Confirm all production receive paths verify signatures before dispatch.
acceptance_criteria: 1) handle_event_json verifies the Schnorr signature (and id) before dispatching, or is removed if unused. 2) A forged event (bad sig) is rejected. 3) Test covers rejection of tampered event.
notes: Evidence: relay_pool.c:740-791 no verify vs :82-89 verify in live path.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit.

title: Signet: NIP-46 dispatch missing nip44_encrypt/nip44_decrypt handlers
description: nip46_server.c method dispatch implements sign_event, nip04_encrypt, nip04_decrypt, connect, ping, get_public_key, get_relays and webauthn_* but has NO handler for nip44_encrypt/nip44_decrypt. These fall through to 'unsupported_method' (nip46_server.c:699-702). NIP-44 encryption is a core capability advertised in the README and is the modern encryption standard; NIP-46 clients requesting nip44_encrypt/nip44_decrypt will be rejected.
acceptance_criteria: 1) nip44_encrypt/nip44_decrypt handlers implemented, delegating to libnostr nostr_nip44_* with the agent key. 2) Policy/capability gating applies. 3) Round-trip test through the server path (encrypt then decrypt) passes.
notes: Evidence: nip46_server.c:544 dispatch chain only nip04_*; :699-702 unsupported fallthrough.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. Details in each issue's fix.

title: Signet: no SIGHUP handler in signetd — runtime policy/config reload does not work
description: signetd installs only SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers (signetd_main.c:464-469) and loads config once (signetd_main.c:473-475). There is no SIGHUP handler despite the file header (signetd_main.c:13-14) and README claiming SIGHUP triggers policy-file reload without restart. Sending SIGHUP to signetd has no effect (default action may even terminate the process).
acceptance_criteria: 1) SIGHUP is handled and triggers a safe reload of the policy store (and any other reloadable config). 2) Reload is atomic and does not drop in-flight requests. 3) Test/integration: edit policy file, send SIGHUP, observe new policy takes effect without restart.
notes: Evidence: signetd_main.c:464-469 only SIGINT/SIGTERM; :473-475 one-time load; header:13-14 claims reload.
close_reason: INVALID as filed / already implemented. SIGHUP-driven policy reload IS wired: signetd calls signet_policy_store_file_new (signetd_main.c:610), which self-installs a SIGHUP handler (policy_store.c:1018) that sets g_signet_policy_sighup_requested and requests audit-log reopen (policy_store.c:85). On the request path signet_policy_engine_eval -> signet_policy_store_get -> signet_policy_store_maybe_reload_locked (policy_store.c:651,593) consumes the flag and reloads the policy file. The signetd header comment is accurate: reload is intentionally handled in the policy module, not signetd_main. Verified by tracing the eval path.

title: Signet: SSH agent ignores requested key blob and lacks ECDSA (wrong-identity signing)
description: ssh_agent.c handling of SSH_AGENTC_SIGN_REQUEST skips the requested key blob (ssh_agent.c:199-204 'dp += kb_len; /* skip key blob */') and signs with the mapped agent's key regardless of which identity the client asked for. If an agent has (or is expected to present) multiple identities, the wrong key can sign. Additionally only ed25519 is implemented (ssh_agent.c:225-258); ECDSA identities are not supported and all identities are hardcoded to ssh-ed25519, so listed keys may not match what actually signs.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sign request matches the requested key blob against the agent's available identities and signs with the correct key, or rejects if no match. 2) Identity list reflects the real key type(s). 3) ECDSA either implemented or explicitly unsupported/omitted from the identity list. 4) Test: sign request for a non-owned/unknown blob is rejected.
notes: Evidence: ssh_agent.c:199-204 skip key blob; :225-258 ed25519-only.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. p0s: all sub-items addressed (secure wipes, rotate store lookup, policy-default clarification, audit-chain doc scope).

title: Signet: SO_PEERCRED UID-to-agent auth is unwired in production (no uid_resolver)
description: signetd_main.c wires the D-Bus Unix transport (signetd_main.c:777-779) and SSH agent (signetd_main.c:857-859) with .uid_resolver = NULL / .uid_resolver_data = NULL. The dispatch layer's signet_dbus_resolve_sender() therefore always fails, meaning the advertised SO_PEERCRED UID->agent mapping is non-functional in the production build. Either these transports cannot authenticate callers to an agent, or they fall back to some default — either way the README's 'auth via SO_PEERCRED UID-to-agent mapping' is not delivered.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A real uid_resolver is wired in production config that maps peer UID -> agent_id from configuration/store. 2) Requests from an unmapped UID are denied. 3) SSH agent uses the same mapping. 4) Test/integration proves a mapped UID signs and an unmapped UID is rejected.
notes: Evidence: signetd_main.c:777-779, 857-859 uid_resolver=NULL; dbus_common signet_dbus_resolve_sender depends on it.
close_reason: Implemented [uid_map] config section + signetd_uid_resolver wired into D-Bus Unix and SSH agent production configs. Peer UID (SO_PEERCRED/getpeereid) now maps to an agent_id; unmapped UIDs are rejected. Documented in signet.conf.example.

title: Signet: session_broker returns fake local token on exchange failure and ignores lease persistence errors
description: session_broker.c GetSession falls back to a locally generated random token when the HTTP credential exchange fails, no service URL is provided, or curl is unavailable (session_broker.c:235 'if (!exchanged) generate_local_token(...)'). Callers cannot distinguish a real brokered service session from a meaningless random token. It also ignores lease persistence failure ((void)signet_store_issue_lease at :263), so it can return success without recording lease state. There is no HTTPS scheme enforcement (comment at :137 claims it but no check), so credentials may be POSTed to plaintext HTTP.
acceptance_criteria: 1) On exchange failure GetSession fails closed (error), not a fake token — or the fallback is a clearly-typed Signet-issued session with tracked lease, never silently substituted for a service token. 2) Lease persistence failure is surfaced as an error. 3) service_url must be https (reject http) unless explicitly allowed for localhost. 4) Tests cover failure and http-rejection.
notes: Evidence: session_broker.c:235 fallback, :263 ignored lease error, :137 unenforced HTTPS comment.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit.

title: Signet: management ACKs fall back to unencrypted plaintext when NIP-44 encryption fails
description: The mgmt ACK builder (mgmt_protocol.c:359) does nostr_event_set_content(evt, encrypted_content ? encrypted_content : ack_content) — if NIP-44 encryption of the ack fails, it silently publishes the ACK content in PLAINTEXT rather than failing closed. Management ACKs can contain provisioning results (agent_id, pubkey, bunker_uri). This is a fail-open information leak that contradicts the 'management events are NIP-44 encrypted' guarantee. Related: get_status/list_agents requests with empty content bypass NIP-44 decryption entirely (mgmt_protocol.c:108), accepting unencrypted management requests.
acceptance_criteria: 1) If ack encryption fails, the ACK is NOT published in plaintext; the handler fails closed and logs an error. 2) Management requests are required to be NIP-44 encrypted (including get_status/list_agents) or the exception is explicitly justified and authorized. 3) Test: forced encryption failure produces no plaintext ACK on the wire.
notes: Evidence: mgmt_protocol.c:359 plaintext fallback; :108 empty-content bypasses decryption.
close_reason: Implemented: signet_mgmt_publish_ack now fails closed — if NIP-44 encryption of the ACK fails or no recipient resolves, it logs a warning and refuses to publish, never falling back to plaintext. Builds clean and all signet tests pass.

title: Signet: relay publish reports success even when zero relays are connected
description: signet_relay_pool_publish_event_json() (relay_pool.c:611-644) and signet_relay_pool_publish_event_json_ack() (relay_pool.c:685-735) loop over relays, publish only to connected ones, and unconditionally return 0. If no relay is connected (or all skipped), they still return 0 = success. The NIP-46 sign path (nip46_server.c:~770) treats return 0 as published=true, so a signed response can be reported delivered when nothing was actually sent. Same silent-success issue affects start/subscribe (relay_pool.c:475-488, 541-608): they return 0 without confirming any connection/subscription.
acceptance_criteria: 1) publish returns a distinct non-success code when no relay accepted the event (0 relays connected / 0 sends). 2) The NIP-46 path distinguishes enqueued-and-sent from dropped and audits/metrics accordingly. 3) Optionally track per-event OK acks to confirm at least one relay accepted. 4) Test with a pool of 0 connected relays asserts publish does not report success.
notes: Evidence: relay_pool.c:611-644, 685-735 return 0 regardless of send count; nip46_server.c published=(...==0).
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. Details in each issue's fix.

title: [F13] Emit EOSE signal in gnostr-thread-subscription
description: HIGH: GNostrThreadSubscription declares SIGNAL_EOSE and registers it in class_init, but never calls g_signal_emit. Consumers waiting for EOSE to switch from loading to live state will hang forever. Emit the signal in on_ndb_batch after the loop processes all n_keys (or when batch is empty). Also needs EOSE concept for the EventBus subscription path. Ref: docs/audits/nostr-protocol-audit-2026-04-29.md F13
close_reason: Implemented in parallel bucket remediation commit b17e2a6e

title: [F11-F12] Implement NIP-47 relay subscription layer and event signing

Add NostrNwcClientSession with response subscription using kinds:[23195], #p:[client_pubkey], since:[now]. (F12) nostr_nwc_request_build creates unsigned events that any real relay would reject. Either sign in the builder or document+assert the signing precondition. Ref: docs/audits/nostr-protocol-audit-2026-04-29.md F11, F12
close_reason: Implemented in parallel bucket remediation commit b17e2a6e

title: [F08-F09-F10] Fix critical concurrency and safety bugs
description: HIGH: Three safety-critical issues. (F08) relay_fetch.c uses static global channel pointers — race condition on concurrent fetches, use per-call userdata or mutex. (F09) relayd auth challenge uses time(NULL) instead of existing gen_nonce() — predictable nonces enable replay attacks. (F10) nostr_relay_store.c casts GObject interface to C vtable struct — undefined behavior from type-punning incompatible layouts. Ref: docs/audits/nostr-protocol-audit-2026-04-29.md F08, F09, F10
close_reason: Implemented in parallel bucket remediation commit b17e2a6e

title: [F05-F06-F07] Wire NIP-42 AUTH end-to-end and fix neg-client auth handling
description: HIGH: Three interrelated auth issues. (F05) neg-client NEG-OPEN filter missing authors constraint, syncing against global relay DB. (F06) neg-client discards AUTH frames from relays, so auth-required relays silently fail. (F07) NIP-42 is stubs only — no challenge parser, no signing path, no relay-client integration. Fix: Add nip42_parse_challenge() and nip42_build_auth_response(), wire into relay message handler, and add author scoping to negentropy filters. Ref: docs/audits/nostr-protocol-audit-2026-04-29.md F05, F06, F07
close_reason: Implemented in parallel bucket remediation commit b17e2a6e

title: [F03-F04] Fix publish OK acknowledgment and blocking COUNT
description: HIGH: Two related relay response handling issues. (F03) nostr_relay_count() blocks forever on go_channel_receive if relay doesn't support NIP-45 COUNT — add go_select_timeout with configurable deadline. (F04) nostr_relay_publish() only confirms transport write, ok_callbacks map is dead code, and gnostr_relay_authenticate() sets authenticated=TRUE before OK arrives. Implement per-event OK tracking and delay auth confirmation until OK received. Ref: docs/audits/nostr-protocol-audit-2026-04-29.md F03, F04
close_reason: Implemented in parallel bucket remediation commit b17e2a6e

title: BUD-02 auth validation has no pubkey check — any key passes

title: Contradictory curl options in blossom upload
description: hanami_blossom_upload sets both CURLOPT_UPLOAD=1 (expects read callback) and CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS (POST body). These are mutually exclusive in libcurl. Fix: remove CURLOPT_UPLOAD and CURLOPT_INFILESIZE_LARGE; use only CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST=PUT + CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS. File: libhanami/src/hanami-blossom-client.c lines 516-523.
close_reason: Removed contradictory CURLOPT_UPLOAD and CURLOPT_INFILESIZE_LARGE. Now uses only CURLOPT_CUSTOMREQUEST=PUT + CURLOPT_POSTFIELDS.

title: Heap buffer overflow in collect_local_refs on realloc failure
description: In hanami-grasp.c collect_local_refs(), when realloc fails, cap is already doubled but the array was not grown. The HEAD insertion then writes past the end of the old allocation. File: libhanami/src/hanami-grasp.c lines ~453-480.
close_reason: Fixed by deferring cap update until after successful realloc. Now cap only changes when the allocation succeeds.

title: blossom_push publishes stale pre-push refs and drops HEAD

Return value of hanami_nostr_publish_state is ignored — push always returns success. File: libhanami/src/hanami-transport.c lines 339-405.

title: groundhog-blossom download-rebinding hang and groundhog-net tor-fail-closed: a dial to a wildcard test listener never reaches it under the full loaded suite
description:
Seen in the W19 reliability stress (50 loaded runs of ctest -R groundhog- -j12 beside 10 CPU hogs, macOS 14 cores, branch tests/w19-reliability), once each, never in 96+96 loaded runs of either test alone:
- groundhog-blossom: /groundhog/blossom/download-rebinding hung until the 120 s ctest timeout; its spin_until() (tests/media/test_blossom.c:41) has no deadline, so the wait is unnamed; the likely one is spin_until(at_least_one, &accepted) for its GSocketService.
- groundhog-net: /groundhog/net/tor-fail-closed failed after 20 s in wait_at_least(&tripwire.accepted, 1) (test_relay_soup.c:939) while GNostrRelay reported 20 cycles of connecting->connected->'Connection lost' to ws://127.0.0.1:55547/relay, i.e. something accepted and closed the direct dials but the tripwire's incoming handler never counted one.
Both are the only listeners in the suite made with g_socket_listener_add_any_inet_port() (one dual-stack [::] socket); every other test listener binds 127.0.0.1 specifically. Checked and ruled out on macOS: an ephemeral 127.0.0.1:0 bind (listener or outgoing connection, same or other process, with or without SO_REUSEADDR) never landed on a port held by a [::] or 0.0.0.0 listener, nor the reverse (0 of 2000 each). An explicit 127.0.0.1:P bind does take such a listener's IPv4 dials. Next steps: bound spin_until in test_blossom.c so the wait is named; log the tripwire port; try binding both listeners to 127.0.0.1 (as test_relay_guard.c and the privacy tripwires do) and compare over 100+ loaded suite runs.

title: Groundhog GUI tests assert window-activation-dependent state while another test process can take activation
description: Found in the W19 reliability stress (50 loaded runs of ctest -R groundhog- -j12 beside 10 CPU hogs, macOS): groundhog-conversation-view failed 2/50: /groundhog/conversation-view/compact-and-keyboard asserted GTK_STATE_FLAG_FOCUS_WITHIN on the message list (test_conversation_view.c:1621) and /groundhog/conversation-view/scrolling asserted the polite-announcement count against gtk_window_is_active() sampled after the event (:1271, 0 == 1). Window activation is the desktop's and is shared: another parallel test process presents a window and takes the key window (macOS) or input focus (shared Xvfb) at any moment; GTK then clears FOCUS_WITHIN along the focus chain (_gtk_window_set_is_active -> synthesize_focus_change_events) and the view does not announce (charter 7.14: only while active). Fix: assert the logical focus (gtk_root_get_focus) instead of the focus state flags, and judge activation-dependent effects against a GhTestActiveSpan (tests/ui/gh-test-active.h) that watches is-active over the turns in which the code decides; same pattern fixed in test_composer.c and test_notifier.c. Test-only.

title: libmarmot: MarmotStorage.rollback_snapshot rewinds MLS sender ratchets (key reuse if used within an epoch)
description: Found in nostrc-ai04. Since libmarmot 0.8.0 the stored MLS state holds the sender ratchets. The storage vtable still offers create/rollback/release_snapshot (for commit race resolution), and GhStoreMarmot implements them by copying the group-state labels. libmarmot never calls rollback_snapshot (the commit lifecycle uses the retained parent instead), but an application that rolls a group back within an epoch would rewind the sender ratchet: the next marmot_create_message() reuses a generation (the key and nonce of a message already sent), and replays decrypt again. 0.8.0 documents the hazard on the hook. Fix: remove the snapshot hooks from the public contract, or make a rollback advance/retire the own sender (e.g. keep a per-epoch high-water mark outside the snapshot, or refuse to send until the next epoch after a rollback). Add a test.

title: relayd_session_relay_storage fails on linux/amd64: event lost across restart
description: Found by the Linux pre-push gate's amd64 mode (nostrc-y9xg, NOSTRC_GATE_AMD64=1, Docker Desktop Rosetta emulation on arm64): test_session_relay_storage.c:242 'event lost across restart' fails deterministically on linux/amd64 (3/3 runs, 0.9 s, not a timeout) and passes on linux/arm64 and macOS. Hosted CI never builds relayd on x86_64 (nostrc-ci uses BUILD_RELAYD=OFF), so this may be a real x86_64 bug (argument order, struct layout, or LMDB/nostrdb durability) or an emulation artifact (mmap/msync or file locking under Rosetta). Reproduce: NOSTRC_GATE_AMD64=1 scripts/linux-gate.sh <checkout>, then docker run --rm --platform linux/amd64 -v nostrc-linux-gate-amd64:/work nostrc-linux-ci:amd64 ctest --test-dir /work/build -R relayd_session_relay_storage --output-on-failure. Confirm on real x86_64 (a hosted runner). Then fix it, or move it to EMULATION_ONLY in scripts/linux-gate.sh with the reason. Until then the gate's amd64 mode excludes it (AMD64_KNOWN).

title: libmarmot: transaction hooks for the built-in SQLite and nostrdb backends
description:
libmarmot 0.7.0 (nostrc-qp24.7) added optional MarmotStorage begin/commit/rollback hooks. With them, every writing operation is one transaction and a crash cannot leave a partial epoch. Groundhog's GhStoreMarmot implements them. The built-in backends do not: storage_sqlite.c (Gnostr's marmot.db via marmot-gobject), storage_nostrdb.c (LMDB) and storage_memory.c still rely on compensating writes and marmot_group_reconcile(), so a crash can still leave a partial epoch or a half-written Welcome join there.

Implement the hooks:
- SQLite: BEGIN IMMEDIATE / COMMIT / ROLLBACK on its connection, turning any internal per-call transactions into savepoints.
- nostrdb: one LMDB write txn per operation, with reads through it.

Then run libmarmot's storage contract tests and a crash-injection test (fork + SIGKILL after each write) per backend.

title: gnostr tests linked with --unresolved-symbols=ignore-in-object-files fail to load on Linux
description: Found by the Linux pre-push gate (nostrc-y9xg). On Linux these tests link with -Wl,--unresolved-symbols=ignore-in-object-files (macOS: -undefined dynamic_lookup), but the tree-wide -Wl,-z,now makes glibc resolve every PLT slot at load, so they abort before main: gnostr-test-plugin-raw-relay-api (gnostr_signer_service_sign_event_async), gnostr-test-image-viewer-remote-media (gnostr_main_window_show_toast), gnostr-test-delete-authorization, gnostr-test-ndb-main-thread-violations, gnostr-test-real-bind-latency (gnostr_mute_filter_should_hide_fields). Adding -z lazy is not a fix: on aarch64 it makes gnostr-test-dm-files-key-encoding and gnostr-test-sync-bridge-user-state fail with 'unexpected PLT reloc type 0x00' (ld emits R_AARCH64_NONE for the ignored symbols). Fix: link the missing objects or provide test stubs so the tests link completely, then drop them from SMOKE_EXCLUDE in scripts/linux-gate.sh. Hosted CI never runs them (BUILD_APPS=OFF, or BUILD_TESTING=OFF in the AppImage job). Test-only; no version bump.

title: Static check: flag calls whose arguments both read and modify the same variable (unsequenced; x86_64 GCC evaluates right-to-left)
description: Two P0 CI breaks (nostrc-qp24.91) were unspecified argument evaluation order: f(g_task_get_cancellable(task), g_steal_pointer(&task)) and g_memdup2(g_bytes_get_data(b,&size), size). macOS clang/arm64 GCC evaluate left-to-right, so local tests passed. Add a check (clang-tidy bugprone-unsequenced? or a check_privacy.py-style regex for 'X' and '&X' / g_steal_pointer(&X) in one argument list) to CI and the pre-push gate.
notes: Implemented on infra/w19-linux-gate (commit 3963ab46, not pushed). scripts/check-unsequenced-args.py: token-level scan of tracked C outside vendored trees; per call, a path modified by one argument (&P inside a nested call, ++/--, assignment) and read/read-through/modified by a sibling. Excludes sizeof-like contexts, g_assert_cmp*, non-call parens, and sibling struct-member reads (documented miss). --self-test: 15 bad shapes + 29 near misses. Pre-fix versions of files fixed in 79843768/2ab1325f/3c9e2581: all 21 historical sites flagged. Tree: 0 hits, 4 justified exceptions (libmarmot CHECK macro, read-only fixture lookup, libgo example getters). Runs in static-checks.yml, groundhog-ci.yml (groundhog job), and the pre-push gate; a planted gh-net-http.c shape is blocked in 10 s before any build. clang-tidy/-Wunsequenced cannot see writes through pointers passed to nested calls.

title: Groundhog attachment card: decode photos to a bounded thumbnail
description: G22 (nostrc-qp24.40): the attachment card decodes a downloaded photo with gdk_texture_new_from_bytes() at full resolution and keeps the texture on the GhAttachmentTransfer, while showing it at most 280 px. G21's decode guard allows up to 8192x8192, so one photo can hold ~256 MiB of pixels. GhAttachments now counts 4 bytes per pixel against GH_ATTACHMENTS_HELD_MAX (older READY transfers are let go), but the newest is always kept, so a single large photo still costs its full size. Decode (or render via GskRenderer/gtk_snapshot) to a thumbnail bounded to the displayed size, drop the full texture, and count the thumbnail instead; keep the decode guard before any decode. Test: a 4096x4096 PNG's preview paintable is at most 280x280 (or 2x for HiDPI) and the transfer's cost reflects the thumbnail.

title: groundhog-e2e-dm: A's self-copy asserted right after SENT (race under load)

title: Groundhog: persist per-server Blossom account-upload consent
description: G21 (nostrc-qp24.39): GhBlossomClient signs kind-24242 upload auth with a fresh throwaway key; only for a server the user consented to (gh_blossom_client_set_account_consent) is the account signer asked (charter §6 step 4, D6, AT-6). The consent is in memory per client and cleared with the account signer, so it is lost on restart and account switch. Persist it per account inside the encrypted store (not GSettings: server choice + account linkage is private; PT-11), keyed by the normalized server URL, and load it into the per-generation client. The G22 UI asks when an upload fails with GH_BLOSSOM_ERROR_AUTH_REQUIRED ("<host> only accepts uploads from accounts it knows") and offers a way to revoke. Test: consent survives a restart for that account only; revoked consent means signer calls = 0 again.

title: Groundhog: purge decrypted attachment cache rows with their message (expiry, retention, forget, block)
description: G21 (nostrc-qp24.39) keeps downloaded attachment plaintext in the encrypted store's media table (src/store/gh-store-media.c), keyed by the file's x, evicted only as a 200 MiB LRU. When the kind-15 message that named it goes (NIP-40 expiry purge in gh-expiry.c / gh_store_purge, retention, Forget conversation, block, request deleted), its cached plaintext stays until LRU eviction. A disappearing photo must disappear from the cache too (charter §3.7, EX-3, P3). Fix: in T-purge/forget, delete media rows whose sha256 is the x of a purged kind-15 message and no other remaining message (gh_nip17_file_from_rumor on raw_json, or a message->media link column in a schema migration); secure_delete already overwrites pages. Test: EX-3 with a cached kind-15 message leaves no media row and H7 finds no plaintext in the -wal.
