title: libmarmot: no public self-update API (members cannot rotate leaf keys via Marmot)
description: Only admins can commit through the Marmot API (add/remove/metadata); there is no marmot_self_update(m, gid, &out_commit_json), so ordinary members never refresh their leaf and path keys (no post-compromise security). nostrc-9ata tests build self-update Commits through internal helpers (mls_group_self_update + marmot_commit_authorize/persist + marmot_commit_build_event); expose that as a public API plus a marmot-gobject binding. Version: libmarmot MINOR, marmot-gobject MINOR.

title: libmarmot: GroupData relay changes are not mirrored into stored group relays
description: marmot_update_group_metadata() can change the GroupData relay list and receivers now apply that Commit (nostrc-9ata), but neither the committer nor receivers call replace_group_relays(), so marmot_get_group_relay_urls() (used by gnostr to publish group events) keeps the old relays. Mirror gde->relays into the relay table inside the same compensated persistence as marmot_commit_persist(); test with a three-member relay change.

title: libmarmot: a received Commit that removes us fails with MLS_PROCESS_MESSAGE instead of evicting the group
description: Found while fixing nostrc-9ata. marmot_process_message() now applies Commits, but when a Commit removes our own leaf, mls_group_process_commit() cannot find our position on the committer's path and returns MARMOT_ERR_MLS_PROCESS_MESSAGE; gnostr shows the 'group may be out of sync' toast and the group stays ACTIVE at the old epoch. Needed: authenticate the Commit (signature, membership tag, confirmation tag are computable without the new epoch's path secret only partly -- see RFC 9420 §12.4.2 for a removed member), detect our Remove, mark the group MARMOT_GROUP_STATE_INACTIVE (use-after-eviction), return a distinct result, zeroize the MLS state. Test: Alice removes Charlie via the API; Charlie processes the kind:445 and the group becomes inactive with no toast-level error.

title: libgo single-lock ring (MPMC slots off, every TSAN build): one-empty-slot discipline makes capacity-1 channels permanently full and capacity-N hold N-1
description: From the nostrc-75rv review (F8). With GO_CHANNEL_MPMC_SLOTS=OFF and DERIVE_SIZE=ON (what GO_ENABLE_TSAN forces), go_channel_is_full() is next_in == out over a ring of exactly capacity slots. For capacity 1, mask = 0, so it is always true: a capacity-1 channel can never accept an element. Every context done channel, ticker and wake channel is capacity 1, so TSAN builds do not model the shipped library, and GoSelectTest, GoChannelCloseTest, GoSelectMultiTest and GoTickerTest time out deterministically under TSAN; libgo-ci.yml excludes them as flaky. Capacity N holds only N-1. Fix: in that mode allocate ring = pow2(capacity + 1), compute occupancy over the ring (mask + 1, not capacity), make is_full occupancy >= capacity, and apply the same to the ATOMIC_TRY lockless pre-check. Then drop the TSAN exclusions. go_channel_mpmc_slot_test skips its capacity-1 cases in this mode until then.

title: libnostr/libwebsockets: verify and disable TLS session resumption for Groundhog's direct relay connections (PD-6)
description: nostrc-qp24.87 turned TLS session resumption off for every libsoup/GIO connection in Groundhog (gh-net-tls.h). System and No Proxy relays still use GNostrRelay -> libnostr's one global libwebsockets context (libnostr/src/connection.c:1031). The target libwebsockets is built with LWS_WITH_TLS_SESSIONS (Homebrew 4.5 lws_config.h; check Ubuntu 4.3.3), and libnostr does not set LWS_SERVER_OPTION_DISABLE_TLS_SESSION_CACHE, so a relay may see one account's connections resume another account's TLS session (charter PD-6, P7: per account generation), which links accounts even across IP changes. Verify with a ClientHello fixture like tests/net/test_tls_resumption.c, then disable the client session cache for Groundhog's use (context option or per connection) and add the test. Moot for relays once nostrc-253z moves System mode to libsoup.

title: Groundhog: a build without libsoup ignores a stored network-mode=tor and connects directly (fail open)
description: W16 review non-blocking #6 (docs/reviews/groundhog-w16-review-2026-09-29.md). Without groundhog-net, GROUNDHOG_HAVE_TOR=0: no dispatcher is installed and every scope uses GNostrRelay directly; gh_net_relay_url_allowed is never called, so .onion URLs even reach local DNS. A user who chose Tor in a full build keeps network-mode=tor in dconf; a distro/dev build without libsoup-3 then connects directly with no warning (P5). Fix: in a non-Tor build treat any network-mode other than system/none as 'connect nowhere' (install a refusing transport, show the Tor banner). Note the mode-aware copy added in nostrc-qp24.87 (onboarding Check Privacy note, New Message) reads network-mode directly and would also claim Tor there.

title: groundhog-e2e-dm two-accounts flakes under CPU load: asserts A's self-copy wrap already reached A's inbox after wait_sent
description: Reproduced on unmodified 90c1f9ed (and equally after the nostrc-75rv fix) with 12 CPU hogs: ctest -R '^groundhog-e2e-dm$' --repeat until-fail failed on iteration 10: test_e2e_dm.c:452 test_two_accounts: assertion failed (wraps_for(&inbox_a, stack_hex[1]) == 1): (0 == 1). In an A/B of 150 loaded runs each, e2e-dm failed 1x (baseline) vs 2x (fixed): same pre-existing rate. wait_sent() waits for the message to be sent (recipient copy accepted), then line 452 checks A's self-copy gift wrap on A's inbox relay synchronously; the self-copy is an independent publish and can land later. Fix the test to wait (gh_test_spin_until) for the self-copy wrap, or make 'sent' cover both copies if that is the product contract. Related: the group-ui admin-gating load flake is tracked in nostrc-qp24.87.
notes: Product semantics confirm it is a test race: gh_dm_send_status_get_message_status() (gh-dm-send.c) returns SENT once recipients_reached == total; the self-copy leg completes independently (all_legs_complete/gh_dm_send_status_self_copy_stored). wait_sent() therefore does not imply the self-copy has reached inbox_a. Fix: spin until wraps_for(&inbox_a, self) == 1 (or wait for gh_dm_send_status_self_copy_stored). Seen at plain 'ctest -R groundhog- -j8' too (2/12 rounds on the nostrc-75rv branch, 0/12 on 90c1f9ed; 1/30 vs 2/30 under 12 CPU hogs; baseline until-fail hit at iteration 10).

title: libnostr: WebSocketMessages still queued in recv_channel leak when a connection closes
description: Seen by the Groundhog sanitizer job (run 36541484717, groundhog-nip29-service): websocket_callback (libnostr/src/connection.c:180,183) mallocs a WebSocketMessage and its data and queues them on conn->recv_channel; when the relay closes (connection.c:425-434 close+unref, and 1041-1042 go_channel_free) messages still in the channel are never drained and freed. Drain and free queued WebSocketMessages on close. Then drop the 'leak:websocket_callback' line from gnome/groundhog/tests/lsan.supp.

title: libmarmot Commit producers mutate the live group before generate_update_path can fail
description: Found while fixing nostrc-lz4f. mls_group_remove_member blanks the removed leaf and its direct path, and mls_group_add_member adds the leaf, on the live group before generate_update_path runs. When generate_update_path (or later steps) fail they return an error with the tree already changed and the epoch not advanced, leaving local state that matches no epoch. That is what lz4f's MARMOT_ERR_INTERNAL did to Alice before the fix. Producers should stage on a clone (like process_commit_impl) and swap only on success; regression = force a path failure and assert the serialized state is unchanged. Version: PATCH.
notes: Addressed on marmot/w16b-commit-fixes in 5b184066: add/remove/self-update (and new GCE producer) build on a staged clone; regression test_commit_producers_fail_closed. Not closed.

title: libmarmot Add proposals are not checked for group compatibility (RFC 9420 §7.3 steps 3-4)
description: Found while fixing nostrc-2io4. Committed Adds only get mls_key_package_validate() (KeyPackage self-consistency and signatures) plus, since 2io4, key uniqueness. They are not checked against the group: GroupContext extensions and required_capabilities support, credential type mutually supported with existing members (§7.3 steps 3-4, §12.1.1), on either the receiver (process_commit_impl) or the sender (mls_group_add_member). Reuse leaf_node_validate's capability/credential checks (the key_package source has no group_id/leaf_index binding and keeps its own lifetime checks). Mind the adopted profile: adopted KeyPackages advertise only 0x0006, not 0xF2EE. Version: PATCH.

title: libmarmot Welcome join does not validate the ratchet tree's LeafNodes (RFC 9420 §12.4.3.1)
description: Found while fixing nostrc-2io4. mls_welcome_process verifies parent hashes and the GroupInfo signature but never validates leaf nodes of the received ratchet tree: RFC 9420 §12.4.3.1 requires each non-blank leaf to pass §7.3 (LeafNodeTBS signature bound to group_id/leaf_index for update/commit sources, source rules, capabilities/credential support, encryption and signature key uniqueness). The §7.3 helpers now exist in mls_group.c (leaf_node_validate, leaf_keys_unique) and mls_tree.c (mls_leaf_node_verify_signature). Caveat: trees from libmarmot <= 0.3.6 carry commit leaves signed without the group_id/leaf_index suffix and will fail, which is correct (MDK already rejects them) but must be called out. Version: PATCH (or MINOR if treated as a behavior break).

title: libmarmot does not reject UpdatePaths whose node keys disagree with the decrypted path secrets
description: Found while fixing nostrc-2io4. RFC 9420 §12.4.2/§7.5: after decrypting its path secret the receiver derives the node keypairs up the filtered path and MUST verify they equal the UpdatePath's encryption_key values; otherwise the Commit is invalid. process_commit_impl only skips remember_own_path_key() when they differ (memcmp mismatch) and still accepts, so a malicious committer can give different members inconsistent tree views (TreeKEM consistency). Fix: reject with MARMOT_ERR_MLS_PROCESS_MESSAGE on any mismatch from our_path_idx to the top (staged clone, no mutation); regression via the test_mls_group UpdatePath builder with one node key swapped. Version: PATCH.

title: Groundhog NIP-29: page backfill with until when a relay caps its answer; flag rooms 'may be incomplete'
description: W15 review non-blocking #1, remainder after nostrc-qp24.82. qp24.82 made the NIP-29 since-cursor advance only for durably stored events and, for backfill, only at EOSE (a cut-off backfill is asked again). What remains: relays usually answer newest-first and cap stored results (100-500). After a long offline period with more messages than the cap, EOSE arrives after the newest N, the cursor commits to the newest one, and everything older in between is never requested. Fix: when a backfill answer reaches the relay's cap (NIP-11 limitation.max_limit if known, else a count heuristic), keep the cursor below the oldest received event and page older history with until (a second REQ per group) until the gap closes; if it cannot be closed, mark the room 'History may be incomplete' in GhNip29Room (G20b shows it). gh_nip29_service_load_older only reads the local store today. Tests: fake relay with a cap in tests/nip29/nip29-relay.h.

title: Groundhog notifier: messages that arrived before the session bound (backfill) are never notified
description: W14 review non-blocking #8: gh-notifier.c skips every message whose created_at precedes the account's binding, so with autostart at login nothing that arrived overnight is ever notified. Charter §5.2 N1 does not list this case. Choose: notify a backfill burst once at hidden level (one coalesced 'N new messages', no sender), or add the rule to N1 with its rationale. Mind NIP-59's randomized created_at (up to 2 days back) when deciding what counts as backfill versus new. Accept: a test_notifier case for the chosen rule.

title: Pool/one-shot consumers of core sub channels can lose stored EVENTs racing EOSE
description:
Found while fixing nostrc-qp24.10.6 (GNostrSubscription now queues EVENT/EOSE/CLOSED in one ordered FIFO and drains ch_events before every EOSE). Other code multiplexes libnostr's separate events/eose channels directly and has the same class of race:
- nostr-gobject/src/nostr_pool.c gnostr_pool_query loop (~L769-835): if go_select picks a relay's EOSE case, item->eosed=TRUE and the greedy drain then skips that item, so stored events still in its events channel are dropped from the results. The greedy drain also drains events *then* try_receives EOSE, so an event pushed between the two is lost once eosed.
- nostr-gobject/src/nostr_simple_pool.c paginate (~L570-600) and stream (~L815-850) drains: same drain-then-check-EOSE window (EOSE emitted to the event bus before a trailing stored event).
- libnostr/src/simplepool.c (~L1076) auto_unsub_on_eose: drains events, then on EOSE unsubscribes/frees the sub, dropping any event that landed in between.
Fix pattern (as in nostr_subscription.c queue_eose_for_main): after receiving EOSE from ch_eose, drain ch_events again before acting on EOSE. The relay reader dispatches in wire order, so every pre-EOSE event is in ch_events by then. Add a burst regression (N stored + EOSE, many rounds) per consumer.

title: G20b NIP-29 group UI (group info, new group relay part, composer send into relay groups)
description:
Charter §8.2 G20b (docs/designs/groundhog-privacy-ux-charter-2026-09-28.md; §7.5, §7.7, §7.9, §7.10). G20a landed the service: GhNip29Service/GhNip29Room (join/read/relay-key states, members 'may be incomplete', closed/private/restricted, permission checks), GhNip29Outbox (durable kind 9/9021/9022/admin ops with results), group rooms in the conversation model, gh_app_outbox_get_nip29_service(). What is left:

- Join flow: relay URL + group id (host'group-id) entry, gh_nip29_service_join, UX copy for pending, denied, duplicate and closed states (qp24.12 accept).
- Group info: relay-signed name/about/picture, members list with 'may be incomplete' when 39002 is partial, admins/roles, relay key state, leave (9022), admin put/remove user, edit metadata, delete event, create invite, gated by gh_nip29_room_check_permission.

- Conversation view: load older via gh_nip29_service_load_older; read/sync/refused states from GhNip29ReadState.
- Per-relay GhNip29RolePolicy source (gh_nip29_service_set_role_policy) or UNKNOWN_POLICY 'attempt and show OK' (qp24.12.2).
- Acceptance: qp24.12 criteria in the UI, screenshots, a11y.

title: Groundhog read marker counts a same-second message with a lower rumor id as read
description: Found by the G24 privacy harness (tests/privacy/test_privacy_e2e.c, NO-1). GhConversation's read marker is a position in message order, and gh_message_compare() orders by rumor created_at (whole seconds) and then rumor id. A message that arrives after the user read the conversation but carries the same created_at second as the last-read message and a lexically smaller rumor id sorts before the marker: it is counted as read (unread count 0), the notifier drops it as read before sending (no notification), and it is listed above already-read messages. Bursts (two messages within a second, the first read at once) hit this about half the time. Fix: track read state by admission (a per-room receive sequence or the received_at column plus id) rather than by sender-claimed order, or advance the marker only over messages that were listed when mark_read ran. The harness waits for the wall-clock second to change between NO-1 sends until this is fixed; remove that wait with the fix.

title: Groundhog outbox: manual Retry never re-reads the recipient 10050 when every recipient target was finally refused
description: Found in G13 (tests/ui/test_composer.c failed-retry): gh_outbox_retry() on a NEEDS_ATTENTION message whose only recipient relay answered a final refusal (blocked:, invalid:, restricted:, sign-in) sets manual/targets_fresh=FALSE, but msg_eval() calls round_end() when !msg_has_due(msg, manual), before round_begin() would re-resolve the recipient's kind-10050. Fix: on a manual retry, re-resolve (round_begin's refresh) before deciding nothing is due; test with a directory that answers a new relay after the refusal.

Move start_publish onto gh_auth_policy_apply_publish(policy, publish, GH_AUTH_PURPOSE_OWN_LIST_PUBLISH, url) so its signer prompts share the policy's per-generation GhAccountAuth with the inbox and the self-copy (charter §4.4 R6), drop GhInboxSetupConfig.auth, and remove the two allowlist entries.

title: Groundhog mute/block UI must withdraw notifications via gh_notifier_withdraw_conversation()
description: G16 stores mutes in conversations.muted_until (gh_store_conversations_set_muted_until) and GhNotifier re-reads mute/block at every send, but a notification already on screen is only withdrawn at the next update or when the conversation is read. G19 (conversation info: mute 1h/8h/1w/Always, block) should call gh_notifier_withdraw_conversation(gh_notifier_get_for_application(app), room_id) right after muting or blocking (N3).

title: Groundhog onboarding: turn notifications-enabled on with background delivery (PD-9)
description: Charter PD-9/§7.11: notifications-enabled (default false) becomes true once onboarding chooses background delivery. G16 (GhNotifier, nostrc-qp24.34) consumes the key, but G14 onboarding (gh-onboarding-view.c) never sets it, so notifications stay off until the user finds Preferences. Set it with the explicit run-in-background choice (and leave it alone otherwise); add an onboarding test assertion.

title: Preferences: 'Private Message Relays…' subpage reusing GhInboxSetup
description: Charter §7.11 (Network / Relays) and §7.8 ('each page is reachable again from Preferences') ask for an inbox editor + publish subpage that reuses GhInboxSetup (src/app/gh-inbox-setup.h, G14). Today the onboarding inbox step is reachable only from the 'no inbox relays' banners ([Set Up] -> win.setup-inbox); once a 10050 list exists there is no way back to change it. Either push GhOnboardingView's inbox step from GhPreferencesDialog or build a preferences subpage on GhInboxSetup (plan/start/probe) and the reviewed suggestions.
close_reason: Duplicate of nostrc-qp24.61 item 1

title: G14 follow-ups: first-run marker, onboarding privacy page, shared account AUTH, suggestion i18n
description:
Residual items from G14 onboarding (nostrc-qp24.32):
1. First run is detected as 'current-npub is empty', so a user who chose 'Use Without an Account (Read-Only)' sees the welcome page on every launch. A proper 'onboarding done' marker needs a charter §7.11 row and a G01 GSettings allowlist entry (tests/check_privacy.py).
2. Charter §7.8 step 5 (privacy page: notification content, 'Receive messages when Groundhog is closed' D11, network mode) is not in the G14 flow; its keys are owned by G15/G16/G17. D11 says background delivery is asked explicitly during onboarding.
3. Charter §4.4 R6 (one account-AUTH prompt per relay per session): GhInboxSetup accepts a shared GhAccountAuth (GhInboxSetupConfig.auth) but the app passes none, and GhDmInbox keeps its own, so a relay used for both inbox reads and list publication may prompt twice. Expose one GhAccountAuth per generation from app services and pass it to both.
4. data/relay-suggestions.json names and descriptions are English only (not gettext-extracted); decide on translation (e.g. its-rules for xgettext) and set a re-review cadence for the three reviewed relays (last checked 2026-09-28).

title: G07 follow-ups: expose GhExpiry to UI, gschema descriptions, notification withdrawal
description: From G07 (nostrc-qp24.25, commit 00a12136): (1) gh-app-services has no getter for the per-store GhExpiry, so the per-conversation timer UI (G19 Conversation Info / G12 timeline row) cannot call gh_expiry_get_timer/set_timer yet; add gh_app_services_get_expiry() when that UI lands. (2) gschema keys retention-days and default-disappearing-seconds are now used but their descriptions still say 'Reserved; not used yet' (G01 owns gschema.xml; needs an allowlist follow-up). (3) EX-3 'notification withdrawn': GhExpiry emits 'purged' with the purged rumor ids; G16 must connect it to withdraw notifications. (4) Charter EX-1 wording says the seal carries the exact expiration; G07 jitters it like the wrap per the task brief; confirm and update the charter text.

title: G17 follow-ups: Private Message Relays entry, relay status, storage used, identity Verify, resolved signer
description:
Charter §7.11 rows that GhPreferencesDialog (G17, src/ui/gh-preferences-dialog.c) does not show yet because their source does not exist in this tree:
1. Network/Relays 'Private Message Relays…' (inbox 10050 editor + publish, reusing G14's GhInboxSetup / onboarding inbox step). G14 exposes no action or page for it yet; add a row (AdwActionRow + suffix button, §7.2) that opens it once G14 lands, on the Network or Account page.
2. Network/Relays 'Relay Status' list (host, purpose, state, 'Signed in as you'): needs a per-relay status source from GhDmInbox/GhAccountRelays (and G09's GhNet). Banner #8 [Details] (nostrc-qp24.48 item 3) should open it: app.preferences plus adw_preferences_dialog_set_visible_page_name("network") (pages are named privacy/messages/network/account).
3. Account & Storage/Messages 'storage used': needs a GhStore size query.
4. Account 'Identity … Verify' and 'signer requested vs resolved': the Signer row binds signer-method (requested) and its footer states the NIP-46 limit; show the resolved signer (GhAccountController availability) and a Verify action (G19) when those exist.
No new GSettings keys are needed for any of these.
notes: Item 1 entry point from G14 (nostrc-qp24.32): the window action win.setup-inbox (GH_STATUS_ACTION_SETUP_INBOX, installed by gh_onboarding_attach) opens the onboarding inbox step on the window's root stack; GhInboxSetup (src/app/gh-inbox-setup.h) offers plan/start/probe for a dedicated subpage.

title: Groundhog gettext domain, translate account-limit strings, selectable message text
description: docs/reviews/groundhog-w13-review-2026-09-28.md non-blocking 8: bind a gettext domain in main.c (§7.14), mark gh-account-controller limit strings translatable, make message text selectable/copyable (G12 view).

title: Outbox: D8 jitter for relays added after seal; retain-limit signed wraps 7 d after settle
description: docs/reviews/groundhog-w13-review-2026-09-28.md non-blocking 7b/7c: not_before decided at seal time misses overlap from relays added later (OB-8); §3.3 'event_json NULLed 7 d after settle' not implemented.

title: Outbox self-copy: account NIP-42 AUTH on own inbox relays via GhAuthPolicy
description: G06 publishes every wrap with GH_RELAY_AUTH_EPHEMERAL, including the self-copy to the account's own 10050 relays. Charter §4.3 allows AUTH as the account for the DM self wrap (own inbox), and an own inbox relay that only accepts writes from whitelisted/authenticated users will refuse an ephemeral AUTH, so the self-copy ends AUTH_REQUIRED/restricted and the message shows 'Not saved to your other devices'. With G08's GhAuthPolicy: set ACCOUNT for self-copy URLs only (never recipient relays), sign through GhAccountAuth (R6: one prompt per relay per session, declined relays not asked again), add src/app/gh-outbox. to check_privacy.py ACCOUNT_AUTH_FILES with purpose 'own self-copy publish', and extend test_outbox.c (auth pubkey == account only on own inbox, never on recipient relays).
acceptance_criteria: Self-copy to an AUTH-gated own inbox is accepted after one account AUTH; recipient relays still only see ephemeral AUTH keys; privacy-static passes.

title: Unify GhMessage:status stub enum with G06 gh-message-status.h
description: gh-message.h (qp24.10.5 conversation model) defines its own interim GhMessageStatus enum (NONE=0, no CANCELLED), GH_TYPE_MESSAGE_STATUS and gh_message_status_get_type() registering GType "GhMessageStatus". G06's src/app/gh-message-status.h (charter §3.6 enum + derivation) defines the same typedef with different values, so a translation unit including both gh-message.h and gh-dm-send.h/gh-outbox.h does not compile, and a second GType registration would collide. G06 therefore registers no GType (GhOutboxItem:status is an int holding GhMessageStatus values). When G12/G13 bind message status: make GhMessage use gh-message-status.h (add a 'no status' value or a separate has-status flag for incoming messages), register one GType there, and switch GhOutboxItem:status to it.
acceptance_criteria: One GhMessageStatus definition and one GType; gh-message.h and gh-outbox.h can be included together; GhMessage:status and GhOutboxItem:status share the enum; UX-5 still passes.
close_reason: Done in G13: GhOutboxItem:status is now a GH_TYPE_MESSAGE_STATUS enum property (one enum, one GType in gh-message-status.c; GhMessage:status already used it since G12); gh-message.h and gh-outbox.h are included together by src/app/gh-send-ui.c, which keeps GhMessage:status in step with its GhOutboxItem. UX-5 (groundhog-conversation-view, groundhog-outbox) still passes.

title: MLS tables under retention, expiry and group-forget purges (GhStoreMarmot)
description: G23 (nostrc-qp24.41) keeps libmarmot's MarmotStorage records in the encrypted GhStore (schema v2 mls_* tables). libmarmot's save_message persists decrypted MLS content and the inner event JSON in mls_messages, and welcome rumors land in mls_welcomes. Everything is inside SQLCipher (no plaintext on disk), but gh_store_purge (T-purge, charter §3.7) only deletes from messages, and MarmotStorage.delete_group removes only mls_group_info + mls_group_relays (the vtable contract), leaving the group's mls_kv 'mls_group' state, mls_exporter_secrets, mls_snapshots/mls_snapshot_rows, mls_messages and mls_processed_messages. Needed: (1) G07's purge engine also purges MLS message plaintext by the same retention/expiry rules (processed_at/created_at) and truncates the WAL; (2) one store-level call for qp24.13's leave/forget-group flow that deletes every row of an MLS group across all mls_* tables in one transaction. Acceptance: tests show purged/forgotten MLS content absent from every table and from store.db/-wal after the purge checkpoint (canary scan).

title: Migrate remaining GTestDBus tests to tests/common/nostrc-test-bus
description:
W13 (nostrc-doif/ic36/qp24.8.5) added tests/common/nostrc-test-bus.{c,h} + cmake/NostrcTestBus.cmake: a private bus under a lifeline supervisor (daemon can never outlive the test or hold ctest's pipes), a session connection held for the bus's lifetime, and a teardown that never closes a connection to a live bus. GTestDBus on macOS aborts ~1/10 under load with 'poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor' and orphans its dbus-daemon, turning the abort into a 30 s ctest timeout.

Still on GTestDBus (in the default pre-push build, migrate first):
- apps/gnostr/tests/test_keystore.c (gnostr-test-keystore: service activation + libsecret, g_test_dbus_stop dance)
- nips/nip55l/tests/test_signer_dbus_contract.c (nip55l_dbus_contract: keyring, singleton workaround, deliberate close_sync at ~1289)
Opt-in components:
- apps/gnostr-signer/tests/test-dbus.c; apps/gnostr-signer/native-host/tests/test_nm_e2e.c, test_nm_webln_e2e.c, test_nm_webln_paired_e2e.c
- apps/relayd/tests/test_session_federation.c, test_session_relay_dbus.c, test_session_relay_federation.c
- gnome/libnostr-publish/tests/test_session_relay.c (+ np-fake-session-relay.h)
- gnome/nostr-homed/tests/integration/test_mock_signer_contract.c, tests/unit/test_notify_unread.c
- gnome/nostr-seal/tests/test-nseal-signer.c; gnome/nostr-search-provider/tests/test_nsp_dbus.c
- gnome/nostr-settings/tests/test_identity.c, test_relay_stats.c, test_systemd.c
- gnome/nostr-share/tests/test_share.c, test_share_e2e.c (+ ns-fake-signer.h); gnome/nostr-wallet-agent/tests/test_dbus.c
Pattern: see apps/gnostr/tests/test_nwc_wallet_agent.c and gnome/groundhog/tests/app/gh-test-signer.h. Also update READMEs that recommend GTestDBus (nostr-share, nostr-settings, nostr-search-provider, nip55l, gnostr-signer native-host). Once none remain, the pre-push hook no longer needs to reap orphaned g-test-dbus daemons (nostrc-doif asked for that; migrated tests cannot orphan).

Acceptance: each migrated binary 50 runs x8 concurrent under CPU load on macOS with zero aborts/timeouts and zero leftover dbus-daemons; test semantics unchanged.

title: groundhog-dm-send: under heavy load /groundhog/dm-send/interrupts aborts and orphans its GTestDBus dbus-daemon (ctest waits 90 s)
description: Seen while proving the G03 store-key fix (nostrc-qp24.20) on macOS: master's full suite, ctest -R groundhog- -j6 --repeat until-fail:5, with the host heavily loaded (28-42 busy-loop hogs on 14 cores, load average ~120-180). groundhog-dm-send failed in 2 of 3 rounds: 'not ok /groundhog/dm-send/interrupts - FATAL-ERROR: condition waited for at line 1293 did not hold within 15s'. Each abort left a g-test-dbus dbus-daemon orphaned (ppid 1). The orphan held ctest's output pipe, so the test was reported as a 90 s Timeout. With 14 hogs and no load stacking it passed (25/25). Two parts: (1) decide whether the 15 s wait at test_dm_send.c:1293 is a real ordering bug or just too tight for loaded CI hosts; (2) GTestDBus orphans its daemon on macOS whenever the test process dies (its crash watcher never fires there) — adopt the lifeline-supervised private bus from gnome/groundhog/tests/store/test_store_key_keyring.c, or at least keep the daemon off ctest's pipes. Root-cause notes: comment on nostrc-qp24.10.13.

title: Signer: typed NIP-44 decrypt failure so undecryptable wraps are final, not transient
description: gh-signer.c maps every org.nostr.Signer error other than the typed approval ones to GH_SIGNER_ERROR_UNAVAILABLE. A kind-1059 wrap whose content does not decrypt (anyone can publish one, p-tagged to the account) therefore looks like a signer outage: GhDmInbox defers it, holds the checkpoint for the session and asks the signer again every session (nostrc-qp24.10.11 records only GH_NIP17_INBOX_ERROR verdicts as rejected). Add a typed service error (e.g. org.nostr.Signer.Error.DecryptFailed, nip55l) and GH_SIGNER_ERROR_DECRYPT_FAILED, and record such wraps in the rejected seen namespace.

title: DM inbox: honor a relay's NIP-11 limitation.max_limit when judging truncated backfill
description: GhDmInbox treats a relay answer (live REQ or older page) with fewer than its REQ limit (1000) wraps as complete (nostrc-qp24.10.10). A relay that silently caps limit lower (NIP-11 limitation.max_limit, commonly 500) returns a full-for-it page that looks short, so the checkpoint can still advance past its older wraps. Fetch NIP-11 for own inbox relays (network-mode aware) and use min(limit, max_limit) per relay (gh_dm_inbox_set_backfill_limits is only global today), or require an empty page before completing.

title: Flatpak/packaging: bundle SQLCipher and re-prove ST-4 in the shipped runtime
description: The charter (§3.1) notes Flatpak needs a SQLCipher module. G02 proves ST-4 on Ubuntu 24.04: groundhog's first DT_NEEDED is libsqlcipher.so.1, every sqlite3_* binding goes to it, a libsoup preload stays shadowed, and a libsqlite3 preload is refused. Each packaging (Flatpak, distro packages) must keep libsqlcipher linked first and run groundhog-store-sqlite (LD_DEBUG loader-scope check) in its runtime, or fall back per D1 to per-record XChaCha20-Poly1305.

title: G11 follow-ups: relative-time refresh, header density, banner actions
description:
Follow-ups from G11 (nostrc-qp24.29):
1. Conversation-row times (gh_conversation_row_format_time) are computed on bind/notify only; 'Today HH:MM' goes stale across midnight until the row rebinds. Add a local-midnight (and weekly) refresh.
2. Collapsed sidebar header at exactly 360 px: account, search, new, menu + GTK's default window controls (minimize, maximize, close) need ~5 px more than the 350 px content area (libadwaita warns). GNOME's close-only layout fits; GUI tests pin gtk-decoration-layout=appmenu:close. Resurfaces when G18 enables New Message: consider a compact header (e.g. search affordance in the list, or merging New into a menu) and test the min/max/close layout.
3. Banner action buttons listed by charter §7.15 have no destination yet: #7 [Set Up] (G14 onboarding inbox step), #6 [Network Settings] and #8 [Details] (G17 preferences), #9 empty-state [New Message] (G18). GhStatus returns no button/action for them; add them in gh_status_banner_get_button_label/_get_action when those surfaces land.
4. Signer banner (#3) copy deviates from the charter ('messages can't be unlocked or sent' instead of 'you can read, but not send'): unwrap needs the signer and the store is in-memory until G05. No [Start Signer]: every signer call already D-Bus auto-starts an activatable signer; ABSENT means activation is impossible. Amend charter §7.15 or revisit when G05 persists messages.
5. libadwaita 1.5 AdwToolbarView sizes a wrapping bottom-bar label as one line (clipped at 360 px); G11 moved its read-only reason into a plain box. G13's composer 'disabled reason' must avoid a wrapping label in a toolbar bottom bar or be tested at 360x294 on Adw 1.5.
notes: Item 3: [Set Up] for banner #7 (INBOX_MISSING) and NO_RELAYS now points at the onboarding inbox step (GH_STATUS_ACTION_SETUP_INBOX = win.setup-inbox, installed by gh_onboarding_attach; G14 nostrc-qp24.32). [Network Settings] (#6), [Details] (#8) and [New Message] (#9) remain.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: G18 (nostrc-qp24.36, 86b16535) enabled New Message; the header button was already visible, so the collapsed header width is unchanged. On macOS (GTK 4.22) /groundhog/shell/minimum-size-layout passes at 360x294 with appmenu:close, appmenu:minimize,maximize,close and icon:minimize,maximize,close, with no libadwaita size warning. Item #2 still needs the check on Linux/Adwaita with GTK's default min/max/close layout.

title: Relay scope mid-session reconnect wire test + nostr-gobject barrier races
description: docs/reviews/groundhog-w12-review-2026-09-28.md items 7-8: add a wire test that drops the relay after EOSE and asserts one DISCONNECTED, one fresh REQ+EOSE, no duplicate subscriptions (no sleeps); fix nostr-gobject state_serial ordering (take the serial before the atomic state store or lock both) and document that the disconnect barrier holds only on the default main context (Groundhog publish transport disconnects on its owning context).

title: Recipient 10050 lookup also queries own NIP-65 read/write relays (wider than charter §4.3)
description: docs/reviews/groundhog-w12-review-2026-09-28.md item 5: gh-inbox-lookup.c:421-425 sends the recipient-10050 REQ to discovery-relays plus the account's own read/write relays; charter §4.3/PD-12 names discovery-relays plus the contact's own 10002 write relays. Own relays learn whom you are about to message. Drop own relays (or amend the charter with rationale); later G10 directory replaces send-time lookup.
notes: Implemented in 9948123d (worktree branch groundhog/w13-inbox-hardening), pending integration. Lookup sources = discovery-relays only; own read/write relays and the own-list wait removed; gh_inbox_lookup_new() drops GhAccountRelays. Charter unchanged (already §4.3). Tests: dm-send lookup_scope asserts exactly discovery relays (two), own NIP-65 relays never sources. check_privacy.py lookup-sources rule. Contact's own 10002 write relays need G10.

title: GhStoreKey: refuse a non-persistent default keyring (session collection)
description: If the Secret Service default alias points at a non-persistent collection (gnome-keyring's 'session' collection, e.g. some autologin setups), GhStoreKey stores the store key there, it vanishes at logout, and the next login reports STORE_KEY_MISSING: silent loss of all local history. Detect it in the libsecret backend (compare the default collection's object path with the 'session' alias, or check for a non-persistent collection) and fail the store with an explicit error/state instead of creating a store whose key cannot survive. Accept: unit test via FakeSecret + KC-6-style real-keyring test where the default alias is set to session.

title: GhStoreKey: Secret Service access under Flatpak (portal or talk-name)
description: G03's production backend (gnome/groundhog/src/store/gh-store-key.c) talks to org.freedesktop.secrets directly through libsecret's SecretService API (needed for the explicit locked/missing/unavailable distinction and no-prompt background mode). Charter §3.4 assumes Flatpak per-app isolation through the Secret portal, which only libsecret's SecretBackend/secret_password_* file backend uses. Decide: either (a) add a second GhStoreKeyBackend over secret_backend_get() used when /.flatpak-info exists (map its errors onto GH_STORE_KEY_ERROR_*; portal has no 'locked' state), or (b) grant --talk-name=org.freedesktop.secrets and document the weaker isolation. Accept: a Flatpak build stores/looks up/destroys the key; KC-1..KC-5 semantics preserved; decision recorded in the charter.

title: Reconcile recipient-10050 lookup relay sources with charter §4.3
description: In-flight qp24.10.4 gh-inbox-lookup.c asks discovery-relays PLUS the account's own NIP-65 read/write relays (gh_account_relays_get_{read,write}_relays) for a recipient's kind 10050. Charter §4.3 lists contact-directory destinations as discovery-relays (+ that contact's 10002 write relays), and PD-12 says lookups run only on discovery connections (unauthenticated or ephemeral AUTH). G01's check_privacy.py deliberately exempts gh-inbox-lookup*/gh-contact-directory* from the getter ban (it only binds DM publication sources), so this is not enforced statically. Decide: (a) amend §4.3 to allow own read relays as lookup sources, or (b) have qp24.10.4/G10 drop them. Whichever is chosen, if lookup sources are narrowed, extend check_privacy.py's nip17 rules to cover the lookup.

title: libnostr publish_and_wait timeout races relay_fail_pending_ok (waiter use-after-free)
description: libnostr/src/relay.c: relay_fail_pending_ok() swaps priv->ok_callbacks under the mutex, then sends into each old waiter->done WITHOUT the lock. nostr_relay_publish_and_wait() timing out concurrently removes its id from the NEW map (no-op) and relay_ok_waiter_free()s the waiter that the fail iterator may be sending into. Reachable on disconnect during an in-flight publish_and_wait. Fix: refcount the waiter (map + publisher) or hold the lock across the fail iteration. Not used by Groundhog; spotted in review for nostrc-qp24.4.9.

title: libnostr nostr_relay_auth sends kind-22242 in an EVENT envelope; gnostr_relay_set_auth_handler unusable for NIP-42
description: libnostr/src/relay.c nostr_relay_auth() signs synchronously and sends the AUTH event via nostr_relay_publish(), i.e. ["EVENT",...] instead of ["AUTH",...]; it also reads priv->challenge without the mutex. nostr-gobject gnostr_relay_set_auth_handler()/auto-auth in auth_challenge_on_main_thread and the NIP-11 auth_required path in gnostr_relay_publish() build on it, and it auto-auths with whatever handler is set (no per-connection identity policy, see Groundhog privacy charter 4.4). Groundhog (nostrc-qp24.4.9) bypasses it with its own AUTH frame write. Fix: send ["AUTH",event], async signer, lock challenge; consider deprecating the auto-auth handler. Found during nostrc-qp24.4.9.

title: groundhog-account flakes: fatal 'poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor' around GTestDBus up/down
description: tests/app/test_account_controller.c brings a GTestDBus up and down per test. On macOS about 1 run in 15 aborts in /groundhog/nip17/envelope-cancel-switch with GLib-FATAL-WARNING 'poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor', logged right after GTestDBus setenv/unsetenv. It looks like a GDBus worker poll racing g_test_dbus_down or connection close; g_test_init makes warnings fatal. test_dm_send.c (nostrc-qp24.10.4) hit the same race about 2 in 25 runs until it switched to one shared test bus per binary (0/30 afterwards). Fix it the same way in test_account_controller.c (a shared bus, with only the mock object registered per test), or find the racing close. Owners of test_account_controller.c should coordinate; another agent is editing it.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text:
Root cause found while fixing the same symptom in groundhog-store-key (G03 follow-up c9b34380 on master):

1. The fatal "poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor" is a GLib/GDBus race that is fatal only on macOS. When a GDBusConnection is closed or finalized, the worker thread closes the socket in continue_writing() -> g_io_stream_close_async() -> g_socket_close(). That close is guarded only by !g_input_stream_has_pending(), but on Unix sockets the worker reads through _g_socket_read_with_control_messages() (a private GTask plus a GSocketSource), which bypasses the input stream's pending flag. The read source is therefore still attached when the fd closes. The next iteration of the gdbus thread polls the dead fd. GLib on macOS polls with select(), which fails the whole call with EBADF, and g_test_init makes the warning fatal. Linux poll() only reports POLLNVAL, so Linux never fails. Traced with a DYLD close()/select() interposer: the dead fd was last closed by the gdbus thread at g_socket_close <- g_socket_connection_close_async <- g_io_stream_close_async <- continue_writing.
   Trigger: any connection close or finalize, e.g. GTestDBus up/down per test (the session-bus singleton is only a weak ref), or libsecret failing to init with nothing else holding the bus.
   Avoid it: hold ONE session-bus connection for the whole binary and never close or finalize it before exit (a peer that goes away only marks it closed; that path never closes the socket). Or never establish a connection at all.
2. Why it shows up as a 30-90 s ctest TIMEOUT plus an orphaned dbus-daemon: GTestDBus's dbus-daemon inherits the test's stdout/stderr (ctest's pipe), and on macOS GTestDBus's crash watcher never kills it after the test dies. The orphan (reparented to launchd) keeps ctest's pipe open until the timeout. Measured with the old G03 test: 19 orphaned dbus-daemons in 200 SIGKILL-chaos runs.
   Fix used in G03: gnome/groundhog/tests/store/test_store_key_keyring.c "Private daemons". Each daemon runs under a small sh lifeline supervisor. A pipe whose only write end the test holds reaches EOF however the test ends (teardown, abort, SIGKILL) and the supervisor kills its daemon. Daemons log to files, never to ctest's pipes. Result: 0 orphans in 350+ SIGKILL/SIGABRT chaos runs on macOS and Linux.

comments.author: Biz

title: DM inbox: wraps rejected after a signer call re-prompt on every restart
description: GhNip17Seen only records validated messages, so a wrap that fails after decrypt (bad seal, sender mismatch, kind 15, not a participant) is re-unwrapped - with 1-2 signer approvals - on every session that backfills it. Record rejected wrap ids (e.g. a rejected namespace in the G05 seen table) without admitting them. Wrong-p/invalid outer wraps are already rejected before any signer call.
notes: Implemented in 9948123d (worktree branch groundhog/w13-inbox-hardening), pending integration. gh_nip17_unwrap_get_signer_calls(); GhNip17Seen rejected namespace ('x <id>', old files load); inbox records GH_NIP17_INBOX_ERROR after >=1 signer call, never signer errors (those are deferred, not re-asked in-session). Tests: dm-inbox rejected-not-reprompted, signer-denied-defers (denial re-prompts next session), account nip17/seen-rejected, unwrap reject table checks signer_calls. Follow-up: nostrc-qp24.10.17 (typed decrypt failure).

title: DM inbox: page backfill when a relay truncates at the REQ limit
description: GhDmInbox asks since=checkpoint-(2d+1h), limit=1000. A relay holding more wraps returns the newest 1000 then EOSE, and the checkpoint can then advance past the truncated older wraps, which are never fetched. The scope's cross-relay dedup hides per-relay counts, so truncation is not reliably detectable today. Add until-based paging (or per-endpoint raw counts from GhRelayScope) and hold the checkpoint until every endpoint's window is complete.
notes: Implemented in 9948123d (worktree branch groundhog/w13-inbox-hardening), pending integration. Per-URL live scopes; until-paging with fresh one-shot page scopes, dedup by id, stop at a short page; no-progress second, failed page or 16-page bound => relay INCOMPLETE, checkpoint held, counters pages/backfill_incomplete, gh_dm_inbox_get_relay_state. Tests: dm-inbox backfill-paging, backfill-page-bound (incl. reconnect retry and failed page), backfill-tied-second. Follow-ups: nostrc-qp24.10.16 (NIP-11 max_limit), nostrc-qp24.4.11 (page on same connection). Version: Groundhog PATCH due at integration (not bumped here).

title: Retry AUTH_REQUIRED DM wraps after NIP-42 AUTH lands; durable DM outbox
description: gh-dm-send reports per-relay AUTH_REQUIRED (GH_DM_SEND_FLAG_AUTH_REQUIRED) but performs no NIP-42 AUTH and no retry. Once the relay layer's GhAuthPolicy lands (nostrc-qp24.4.9 / qp24.4.7), publish recipient wraps with EPHEMERAL or NONE auth only, never the account (charter §4.4 R1/R7); the self-copy may use account AUTH. The durable outbox (charter §3.6, G06) should persist GhDmSendStatus after gh_dm_sender_seal() and republish with gh_dm_sender_publish(), which already sends the stored wraps byte-for-byte only to non-ACCEPTED targets without signer calls. The outbox owns outcome classes and backoff, adding new 10050 targets for the same wrap (OB-8), and the D8 self-copy jitter when own and recipient inbox sets overlap (the send path does not delay the self-copy today).

title: Bound Groundhog DM send RESOLVING wait on own relay-list discovery
description: GhDmSend and GhInboxLookup wait (signal-driven) for GhAccountRelays to leave DISCOVERING before resolving the recipient inbox / choosing self-copy relays. A discovery source that connects but never sends EOSE, CLOSED or an error keeps the send in RESOLVING until the caller cancels (the lookup's own deadline only starts at its REQ). Add a failure bound (proceed with the lists admitted so far, flagging the own-list state), or a settle deadline in GhAccountRelays, with a test.

title: Groundhog window lacks minimum size required by its AdwBreakpoint
description: Pre-existing since the W3a shell (confirmed on pristine 9efd0ad9 under Xvfb, libadwaita 1.5): every launch logs 'Adwaita-WARNING: AdwApplicationWindow ... does not have a minimum size, set the width-request and height-request properties'. The window has the 600sp AdwBreakpoint but no size request, so libadwaita cannot guarantee breakpoint evaluation below the unconstrained minimum. nostrc-qp24.8.3 (Blueprint migration) deliberately preserved this behaviour and its new mapped breakpoint test tolerates exactly this warning. Fix: set width-request/height-request on the GhWindow template (GNOME HIG 360x294, as the plan's adaptive checks name), confirm compact layout at 360x294, then drop the tolerance in tests/app/test_shell_layout.c.

title: libnostr reconnect re-fires subscriptions whose caller-owned filters may be freed
description: Hosted nostrc CI run 36386967615 (macOS ASAN) hit heap-use-after-free in nostr_subscription_fire from relay_refire_subscriptions: test_profile_fetch_stress freed its NostrFilters after nostr_subscription_free_async()+abandon while the subscription was still registered, and a reconnect re-fired it reading sub->filters. The test is fixed to keep filters alive until pool teardown, but the library contract is fragile: re-fire should skip unsubscribed/context-cancelled subscriptions, and free_async/abandon must document (or take) filter ownership.

title: GhRelayPublish: failed EVENT write and pre-established disconnect only surface at deadline
description: W10 review (docs/reviews/groundhog-w10-review-2026-09-27.md item 2): gh-relay-publish-gnostr.c publish_thread only logs a failed nostr_relay_publish write, and deliver() drops a DISCONNECTED/ERROR state delivered before handle->established. The URL still ends CONNECTION_FAILED but only when the 30 s failure deadline fires. Return the write status from the worker and report it on the owning context; treat pre-established loss as CONNECTION_FAILED. Related: nostrc-qp24.4.5 (state-changed suppression).
acceptance_criteria: Wire test: relay closes socket before OK and a forced write failure each yield CONNECTION_FAILED well before the deadline, event-driven (no sleeps); existing publish tests stay green.
close_reason: Fixed in 5e851310: publish EVENT/AUTH writes via gh-relay-gnostr-write report failure as CONNECTION_FAILED on the owning context; any DISCONNECTED/ERROR before OK (pre- or post-handshake) is immediate CONNECTION_FAILED. Wire test /groundhog/relay-publish-wire/connection-lost-before-ok (socket closed on EVENT, and right after upgrade) — event-driven, not the deadline. Groundhog version untouched (integrator bumps).

title: W5b NIP-29 core residuals: unknown 39000 tags, future-dated snapshots, timeline source, NIP-29 build wiring
description:
Residuals from the GTK-free core (gnome/groundhog/src/nip29, nostrc-qp24.12.1) to settle before W5 wiring:
- gh_nip29_template_edit_metadata emits only modelled fields (name/picture/banner/about, private/restricted/hidden/closed/livekit, supported_kinds, parent, child). kind:9002 is PUT, so relay-specific 39000 tags would be dropped by an edit; decide whether to preserve unknown tags.
- Relay-signed snapshots are admitted with any non-negative created_at; a far-future timestamp from a bad relay clock pins that kind until restart. Decide a skew bound or surface it.
- The service must feed GhNip29TemplateContext.recent (newest-first, same relay, author known) from its EOSE-aware timeline; no ring buffer exists yet.
- Relay key comes from NIP-11 self (legacy pubkey); key rotation requires a new GhNip29Group (by design).
- Groundhog's CMake add_subdirectory's nips/nip29 when ENABLE_NIP29=OFF (same pattern as seahorse); integrator may prefer forcing ENABLE_NIP29 when BUILD_GROUNDHOG=ON at top level.
- Role capabilities are unknown without a caller GhNip29RolePolicy; W5 needs a per-relay policy source or must use UNKNOWN_POLICY as 'attempt and show OK'.

Result: a plain 'all' build fails and groundhog-relay, groundhog-relay-wire, groundhog-account, groundhog-account-relays, groundhog-version and groundhog-launch are 'Not Run' under ctest -R 'groundhog-|nip29'. Acceptance: either gate storage_ndb.c/nip57 on the nostrdb option (with a working fallback) or document that Groundhog gates require nostrdb.

title: libnostr: nostr_normalize_url corrupts http(s) schemes (https://x -> wssps://x)
description: libnostr/src/utils.c:72-82 rewrites the scheme with memcpy(url, scheme, strlen(scheme)) after strcpy'ing 'ws'/'wss' into the old scheme buffer, without shifting the rest of the string: 'https://x' becomes 'wssps://x' and 'http://x' becomes 'wstp://x'. It also lowercases the whole URL including the path. Groundhog's NIP-29 core does not use it (own GUri-based normalizer, nostrc-qp24.12.1). Acceptance: unit tests for http/https/ws/wss/bare-host inputs and case-preserving paths; audit callers.

title: Wire GhRelayPublish into Groundhog send paths with NIP-42 AUTH handling
description: GhRelayPublish (nostrc-qp24.4.4) surfaces AUTH_REQUIRED but performs no AUTH; nothing in src/app uses it yet. Needs: account-generation-owned publish per send, UI of per-relay outcomes (relay-local OK != delivery), cancellation on account switch, and a caller-driven AUTH-then-new-publish flow (no automatic retry inside the publisher).
close_reason: Superseded per charter §8.5 by nostrc-qp24.23 (outbox/send wiring) + nostrc-qp24.26

title: GNostrRelay state-changed suppressed/misordered for core-driven transitions
description: nostr-gobject/src/nostr_relay.c on_core_state_changed() atomically stores self->state = new_state on the worker thread BEFORE queuing set_state_on_main_thread(); gnostr_relay_set_state_internal() then early-returns because self->state == new_state, so state-changed/notify::connected never fire for a single transition (e.g. connection lost), and rapid CONNECTING->CONNECTED produces a bogus CONNECTED->CONNECTING emission. Impact: Groundhog publisher (gh-relay-publish-gnostr.c) cannot promptly report CONNECTION_FAILED when a relay drops after the EVENT is sent; it falls back to the per-relay failure deadline (30 s). The scope's on_state reconnect path is likewise mostly dead. Fix belongs in nostr-gobject (keep a separate main-thread-visible state or pass old/new through the idle); needs a nostr-gobject version assessment. Found during nostrc-qp24.4.4.
close_reason: Fixed in 5e851310: emitted_state + serial/barrier; every core transition emitted on the default main context in order; regression /relay/state/every-transition-emitted (fails on old code). nostr-gobject PATCH 2.0.0->2.0.1 (CMake+Meson+VERSION_MANIFEST). gnostr consumers (publish/DM attempts, plugin publish-ack, pool relay-state-changed, multi-sub) now see real DISCONNECTED/CONNECTED transitions; default BUILD_APPS=ON build + 67 nostr-gobject/gnostr/nostr-gtk tests pass. Follow-up nostrc-kbfe.

title: Guard empty NostrTag prefix before prefix_len minus one
description: libnostr/src/tag.c:51-63 nostr_tag_starts_with computes prefix_len - 1 and indexes prefix->data[prefix_len - 1] without checking zero. nostr_tag_new(NULL) can construct a zero-size NostrTag, so a public caller can trigger size_t underflow/out-of-bounds instead of a defined false result. Found in W8 independent review; do not conflate with duplicate-tag ownership fixes.
acceptance_criteria: Empty prefix returns false or another documented safe result without UB; ASAN/UBSAN counterfactual regression exercises nostr_tags_get_first and append_unique with empty prefix; normal prefix/dedup behavior unchanged; libnostr version assessed, full gates/review pass.

title: Avoid EVENT subscription ID leak on envelope backend fallback
description: The public nostr_envelope_deserialize path first attempts the compact parser (libnostr/src/json.c:140-149) and then falls back to Jansson (150-153). For ["EVENT","sub",{"kind":1,"created_at":123,"content":"x"}], compact parsing stores subscription_id at libnostr/src/envelope.c:358 but rejects the unsigned event at 365-372. Jansson then overwrites that pointer at libjson/src/json.c:293-296 without freeing it. A correctly heap-allocated NostrEventEnvelope run under Linux Clang ASAN/UBSAN libFuzzer/LSan reports a deterministic 4-byte leak from this seed. This is independent of nostrc-cs0s stack-owned fuzz harness teardown; do not suppress LeakSanitizer. Fix parser fallback ownership and add a regression for partial compact parse followed by backend fallback.
acceptance_criteria: A correctly sized EVENT receiver with the reproducer deserializes/tears down without sanitizer leaks; compact/backend fallback behavior remains compatible.
close_reason: W8 fefff3af retains compact EVENT subscription ID locally until full parse success, avoiding overwrite/leak on Jansson fallback; correctly heap-owned fallback regression and Ubuntu arm64 Clang18 ASAN/UBSAN corpus replays with LSan passed, independent review APPROVED, clean combined macOS build/full CTest passed. libnostr 1.0.2 -> 1.0.3 PATCH.

title: Fix envelope-deserialize fuzz harness stack-owned envelope teardown
description: Ubuntu ASAN/UBSAN Actions run 36350837333 (0e2e90ec) has Short fuzz failure: stack-buffer-overflow in nostr_envelope_free at libnostr/src/envelope.c:719 when tests/fuzz_envelope_deserialize.c:23 passes &env to the free function. The harness declares `NostrEnvelope env = {0}` on the stack and calls nostr_envelope_free(&env), while the free function handles subtype fields and always free(envelope). This is a harness ownership/layout error, not yet evidence of a production envelope parser defect. Fix the harness to use the library allocation contract, preserve fuzz coverage, and add a deterministic regression/seed that executes teardown under ASAN; do not disable fuzz/ASAN.
acceptance_criteria: The CI Short fuzz target runs its seed corpus and a bounded randomized campaign under ASAN/UBSAN without invalid free or subtype over-read; a deterministic reproducer fails pre-fix and passes post-fix; production parser behavior is not weakened.
notes:
Test-only harness/corpus/CI wiring change; no tracked component version bump and no shipped artifact change. Pre-fix Apple Clang ASAN/UBSAN driver: NOTICE seed caused stack-buffer-overflow in nostr_envelope_free:719; EVENT/sub seed caused stack-buffer-overflow in nostr_envelope_deserialize_compact:358. Post-fix macOS ASAN/UBSAN seed driver and focused test_envelope_parse/test_json_envelope CTest pass. Linux Ubuntu arm64 Clang 18 ASAN/UBSAN libFuzzer target: 3 seeds, -max_total_time=30, 34,781,054 executions in 31 seconds, exit 0, no sanitizer findings. CI Ubuntu amd64 run not performed locally; libFuzzer coverage feedback remains limited to its harness target. Separate production fallback leak discovered with correctly allocated EVENT receiver and filed as nostrc-y9rd. User requested commit but no merge, push, or bead close.
W7 worktree 18805cd3 integrated as ecd236c6: fuzz harness now uses heap-owning nostr_envelope_parse/free contract and envelope-specific seed corpus in CI/CMake. Pre-fix NOTICE/EVENT ASAN stack overflow reproduced; post-fix Ubuntu arm64 ASAN/UBSAN libFuzzer 34,781,054 executions/31s and focused CTests pass. Test-only no bump. Separate production fallback leak tracked nostrc-y9rd. Remains open until Actions proof.
Hosted proof: nostrc CI Actions 36353147203 Ubuntu ASAN/UBSAN Short fuzz step completed envelope corpus 26,959,703 executions/31s with no sanitizer report; full 223/223 CTest stage passed. Short fuzz remains non-gating (nostrc-pozg); this bead covers harness ownership and seed routing only. Test-only no bump.

title: Drain untrusted-approver async reply before Watch leaves scope

Source: test_untrusted_approver at lines ~1396-1426 parks watch_call then returns with pending_replies==1 and only unsubscribes signals, so teardown dispatches its callback against stack Watch. This predates the new disconnected-sender test and is a test-lifetime bug, not evidence the service liveness guard failed. Drain/cancel the parked reply while Watch is alive, preserve unauthorized-approver assertions, and prove sanitizer-clean under the CI configuration; do not suppress ASAN.

Fix committed on separate worktree groundhog/w6-signer-asan as cc7f2e3f98d0c1f9e764d0dd997752c7e99c5e03; leave open for integration/review, no merge/push. Only nips/nip55l/tests/test_signer_dbus_contract.c changed. test_untrusted_approver now cancels its parked async NIP04Encrypt call, waits for callback, asserts one NULL reply with G_IO_ERROR_CANCELLED, and watch_stop asserts pending_replies==0. Focused Docker build used GNOSTR_ENABLE_ASAN/UBSAN=ON with CI-like flags; nostrdb optional backend OFF because submodule absent and libsecret not installed, so keyring phases skipped. macOS ASAN CTest pass was not counted because its GLib test-bus helper crashed. This closes the scoped Watch lifetime issue; job-level macOS dbus-daemon failure is separate nostrc-ay3z, and later optional vector/fuzz sanitizer diagnostics are separately tracked/not attributed to this test. Test-only: no component bump.

title: libnostr relay close drops queued CLOSE and never closes the WSI
description: Found while wiring Groundhog account relay discovery (nostrc-qp24.9). gnostr_subscription_close() -> nostr_subscription_close() queues ["CLOSE",id] fire-and-forget via nostr_relay_write(); an immediately following nostr_relay_close() cancels the context and closes write_queue, so the queued CLOSE can be dropped. nostr_connection_close() (libnostr/src/connection.c) only detaches the WSI ('let the WSI close naturally') and never initiates a websocket close. Result: after a Groundhog account switch the previous account's REQ and socket can remain open on the relay until the peer times out (observed ~1/15 runs in a local libsoup relay: neither CLOSE frame nor socket close seen within 15s). Client-side callbacks are already discarded, so this is a relay-side privacy/resource leak, not stale delivery. Fix belongs in libnostr close path: flush pending CLOSE before teardown and request lws close from the service thread; add a wire test asserting the relay observes CLOSE or socket close after gh_relay_scope_cancel.
notes: Implemented on groundhog/w6-relay-close: connection teardown queues service-thread lws_wsi_close so relay socket shuts down even if queued Nostr CLOSE is lost. No added UI wait. Lifetime re-audit: relay removes recv/send pointers under priv->mutex, the same mutex callbacks use to take GoChannel refs; go_channel_free only drops the relay refs, so retained callback refs remain valid. Close queue snapshots every pending entry under g_lws_mutex and drains the snapshot; concurrent enqueues remain on the global queue for the next iteration. Do not unlink requests when service loop cannot process them. Real local libsoup test starts two scopes/REQs, cancels both, and requires two socket-closed signals within 3s; 10 repeats passed. Focused build and 5 tests passed. Version decision for combined Groundhog wave: dedup already used the single libnostr PATCH 1.0.1 -> 1.0.2; retain 1.0.2 in CMake and VERSION_MANIFEST, no second 1.0.3 bump. Bead remains in progress; no merge or push.
close_reason: Service-thread WSI shutdown integrated as e8633a45; relay-side socket-close loopback regression passes repeatedly, sufficient even when Nostr CLOSE frame is dropped; same-wave libnostr PATCH 1.0.2; independent addendum approved.

title: Bound reconnect boundary-ID dedup without losing same-second events
description: Independent W5 review F2 found libnostr seen_cursor_events is an unbounded linked list. A hostile relay can pin a future created_at and stream many signed same-second events, causing subscription-lifetime memory growth and O(n^2) scanning on the relay reader thread. Preserve inclusive replay correctness; do not fall back to since=cursor+1, which can drop legitimate unseen same-second IDs.
acceptance_criteria: Bound per-subscription memory/CPU for repeated same-second IDs while proving no event loss and deterministic dedup across oldest-first and newest-first reconnect replay; stress with local signed relay fixture and keep existing EOSE/live behavior.
notes: Committed d3303a30 on groundhog/w6-relay-dedup for review; remain IN_PROGRESS, not merged/pushed/closed. libnostr PATCH 1.0.1 -> 1.0.2: backward-compatible bug fix, no public API/ABI change; CMake source and VERSION_MANIFEST declared version updated, release columns unchanged. Cursor and replay-boundary ID caches each retain <=1024 IDs with fixed hash buckets/FIFO eviction; retained IDs dedup exactly. Overflow may redeliver evicted IDs (at-least-once), but unseen signed IDs are not rejected by dedup; cache OOM degrades to untracked delivery. Inclusive since, EOSE/live preserved. Signed loopback test covers oldest/newest replay, EOSE pressure, future same-second overflow, retained duplicate suppression, evicted redelivery, unseen ID delivery, and cap assertion. Focused CMake builds passed; 4/4 adjacent libnostr CTest cases passed; reconnect test repeated 3x plus final rerun passed; git diff --check passed. Full build/full CTest not run (no push requested). bd dolt pull unavailable: no Dolt remote. Awaiting user review/integration.
close_reason: Bounded 1024-ID hash caches integrated as 01c1214d; signed oldest/newest and hostile same-second replay passes, no unseen ID loss; combined libnostr PATCH 1.0.2; independent W6 review approved.

title: nostr-dav: DAV edit after first publish re-sends the stale signed event
description: nd_publisher_stage_calendar_put/_contact_put (stage_row) set publish_state='pending' but keep signed_event_json, and dispatch_row publishes signed_event_json when present (sign-once so retries never re-prompt). So once a row has been published, every later DAV PUT of that UID re-publishes the ORIGINAL signed event: the edit never reaches relays (and relays answer duplicate:, so the row even reads 'published'). Found while wiring nostrc-t24q. Fix: re-staging clears signed_event_json (and upstream_event_id) so the next tick signs the current content; retries of the same staged version still reuse the signature. Test: PUT, publish, edit, re-stage, tick -> the signer sees the edited content and the relay gets a new id.

title: nostr-home-syncd: additive rescan slurps each file whole into memory to hash it (2 GB RSS peak on the lab)
description: nh_syncd_reconcile.c rescan_walk() (used by nh_syncd_rescan_home_additive when the snapshot base is unknown) mallocs st_size bytes (up to NH_SYNCD_CHUNK_SIZE * NH_PORTHOME_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_ENTRY) and reads the whole file before hashing. The packaged daemon on the aarch64 lab showed Memory peak 2.0G. Hash with a streaming SHA-256 over a fixed buffer instead. nostrc-lqm2 stopped unseeded daemons from running this walk at all, but a managed home with large files still pays it. Found by worker K.
notes: Partial in e6c61828 (fd9aeb7b): rescan hash streams via 1 MiB buffer. Push path still reads whole files.

title: nostr-home-syncd: decide sync scope for cache-like trees (CACHEDIR.TAG, containers, flatpak, .var/app, snap, node_modules)
description: nostrc-lqm2 made these trees watch-skipped but still synced through the fallback rescan (every NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_FALLBACK_RESCAN_SEC, default 600 s), which walks and stats them on every tick. CACHEDIR.TAG is by convention an opt-out from backup/sync, and container/flatpak/snap storage is machine-local runtime state that can hold millions of files. Decide which belong in the static ignore set (nh_syncd_ignore.c STATIC_PREFIX/GLOB) rather than the watch-skip list, measure one fallback tick on a realistic home, and document the policy in design §6.2. Raised by the Oracle review of nostrc-lqm2 (worker K).
notes: Lab measurement 2026-09-26 (worker K, nostrc-lqm2 demo): real home of 93k dirs / ~290k files, managed-mode syncd with budget 8192 -> 12,477 unwatched roots. One fallback tick over them walked about 262k files: ~9.9 s CPU, VmHWM 166 MB (the jansson seen-set and batcher entries scale with the file count under unwatched roots). The default 600 s interval keeps that to ~1.7% of one core on this pathological home. A steady-state tick with no diffs will be cheaper but still holds a seen-set of every path. Consider excluding cache-like trees from sync, or a delete sweep without the seen-set.

title: nostr-home-syncd: a broker home seed dropped after the daemon starts is never picked up
description: The seed at /run/nostr-auth/session/<uid>/home_seed is read once in load_cfg (nostr-home-syncd.c). If the user unit starts before the broker writes the drop (PAM/user-manager ordering), the daemon never becomes managed: since nostrc-lqm2 it idles unwatched (before, it watched $HOME but deferred every batch). Either watch /run/nostr-auth/session/<uid>/ for the drop and arm the watcher when it appears, or order the unit after the broker's session hook with a condition + restart. Raised by the Oracle review of nostrc-lqm2 (worker K).
notes: Worker O, branch fix/syncd-snapshot-and-seed @ 0e70ecc6. Unmanaged daemon waits for the drop: inotify on the deepest existing ancestor (re-armed per event; IN_ATTRIB covers the broker's mkdir-0700-then-chown window) + backstop poll NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_SEED_POLL_SEC (default 30). On arrival: start_managed() = additive baseline + partial marker + budgeted watcher, no restart. Test homed_syncd_seed_late (poll off; path created late; dir inaccessible until chmod) — removing IN_ATTRIB makes it fail. Live lab unit is running unmanaged and logs 'Waiting for /run/nostr-auth/session/1000/home_seed'; a real drop was NOT exercised on the lab (it would start a full managed rescan/push of the lab home).
close_reason: Merged to master in e6c61828 (worker O, fix/syncd-snapshot-and-seed). Lab: 64 MB snapshot loads in 0.68 s, MemoryPeak 344 MiB; exit 7 on oversize with file untouched. Follow-ups: 6oaq, 1xbk.

title: session relay federation: group relay resolution by bare h id mis-routes NIP-29 forks/migrations (owner: F)
description: Found by the nostrc-rxxx NIP-29 audit against db5fe3d 'clarify group relay migration and forks'. NIP-29 now states a group is (relay, id): the same id can simultaneously be different communities on different relays (forks), each with its own 39000/39001 and history. F's in-flight resolve_group() (apps/relayd/src/session/session_fed_policy.c, feat/session-relay-federation) resolves by bare id: nsr_fed_group_relay_from_10009 returns the FIRST 10009 group tag whose id matches, so a user in two forks of 'pizza' gets every message routed to whichever fork is listed first. Also: step 3 derives a relay from an h value of the form host'id, but the NIP-29 h tag carries only the bare group id (host'id is a client-side addressing form a group relay would reject), and step 1's ['h', id, relay] hint is not a NIP-29 shape (harmless, but document it as a nostrc extension). Fix: when several 10009 entries share the id, return UNROUTABLE with a reason unless the event carries an explicit relay hint; never silently fall back to another relay for the same id (that is a different community per the fork rules); when the group relay stays unreachable keep the write queued and surface it (NIP-29 says clients MUST then consult admins' 10009 -- a client decision, not a relay reroute). Tests: two 10009 entries same id different relays => unroutable without hint, routed with hint.
notes: branch fix/relayd-federation-followups (wJ, not pushed): 5b109e7d. Group = (relay,id): ['h',id,relay] (nostrc extension) wins; else exactly one distinct 10009 relay for the id; forks -> unroutable with reason; no host'id derivation; never another relay/home. Tests: /fed-policy/route-group-forks. Oracle-reviewed. Lab aarch64 ~/nostrc-ci/wJ-relayd @43469db5: 13/13 relayd ctests green under ASan (default ASAN_OPTIONS, no detect_odr_violation=0), -Werror build ok, dep-purity ok, debs rebuilt + nostrc-session-relay installed (user relay restarted, outbox migrated to v2).
close_reason: Merged to master in 74b5158c (worker J, fix/relayd-federation-followups). 9tdc: code fix was F's d4346f8d; G had tested a pre-fix deb; regression test added. Follow-ups: btzb, dm6d, nfnw, z1my, pw0d.

title: session relay routing: NIP-29 kind 39005 and h-tagged non-9..12 kinds route to home_relays (owner: F, apps/relayd)
description: Found by the nostrc-rxxx NIP-29 audit (docs/reviews/nip29-conformance-2026-09-26.md). apps/relayd/src/session/session_routing.c classifies NSR_ROUTE_GROUP_RELAY by kind only: 9-12, 39000-39004 (master) plus 9000-9030 (F's in-flight feat/session-relay-federation). Gaps vs docs/nips/29.md @ db5fe3d: (1) kind:39005 group pinned events (f19d0e3) falls through to NSR_ROUTE_HOME_RELAYS -- widen to 39000-39005 (nostr-kinds.h now has NOSTR_KIND_SIMPLE_GROUP_PINNED_EVENTS / NOSTR_KIND_SIMPLE_GROUP_UPDATE_PIN_LIST 9010, landed by worker H). (2) NIP-29 'Normal user-created events': groups may accept ANY kind (kind 1, 30023 long-form, 31922 calendar...) as long as it carries an h tag. Classifying by kind alone sends those to the user's NIP-65 home relays, leaking group content (including private groups') outside the group relay. The classifier needs the event (h-tag presence => GROUP_RELAY), not just the kind. Acceptance: table test for 39005 and for a kind-1 / kind-30023 event with an h tag routing to group_relay; kind 10009 and 10011 (NIP-51 lists) still route home_relays.
notes: branch fix/relayd-federation-followups (wJ, not pushed): 0a553bef (+ 77b9ec9a review msg fix). nostr_session_route_class_event(): any h-tagged kind -> group relay except NIP-17, replaceable 0/3/10000-19999, ephemeral; 39000-39005 (id in d). Tests: /fed-policy/route-class-event, /route-group-any-kind. Lab aarch64 ~/nostrc-ci/wJ-relayd @43469db5: 13/13 relayd ctests green under ASan (default ASAN_OPTIONS, no detect_odr_violation=0), -Werror build ok, dep-purity ok, debs rebuilt + nostrc-session-relay installed (user relay restarted, outbox migrated to v2).

title: packaging: packaged installs have no nip55l approval UI, so first-use prompts cannot be answered
description: debian/rules builds BUILD_APPS=OFF: gnostr-signer (the only approver allowed by nip55l 0.4.0: <bindir>/gnostr-signer or the org.gnostr.Signer Flatpak) is not packaged, and neither is gnostr-signer-daemon. A gated call without a grant fails fast ('no approval agent'); first-party headless services have built-in grants (NIP55L_DEFAULT_GRANTS). title: nip55l: D-Bus identity selector treats any 64-hex (and nsec) as caller-supplied key material
description: Found by worker C (gnostr bookmarks passed a hex pubkey as current_user; merged fix 55bb44e5). resolve_seckey_hex() in nips/nip55l/src/core/signer_ops.c uses any 64-hex selector as the raw secret key and any nsec1 as key material, so a D-Bus caller's pubkey is silently used as an nsec (events signed by a key derived from the pubkey bytes). Fix (defence in depth, branch fix/signer-hardening-2): the daemon normalises caller-supplied selectors - nsec rejected, bare 64-hex read as an x-only pubkey and accepted only if it names a known identity, npub selectors must resolve to exactly that npub; in-process core API unchanged. Contract-test phase.
notes: branch fix/signer-hardening-2 (not pushed, based on 3835b81f): c30f8088 - nostr_nip55l_normalize_selector in the daemon: nsec refused, 64-hex = pubkey that must name a known identity, npub must resolve exactly; contract phase green on lab + macOS.

title: libhanami: test-hanami-blossom-batch probe_records_capabilities put_count != 4 (hidden failure exposed by live asserts)

The test used bare assert() and the tree builds Release (NDEBUG), so until nostrc-xw95 made asserts live in test executables this test executed its checks as no-ops and always passed. title: nostr-dav: nd-ical emits DTSTART;TZID=... with a Z-suffixed UTC time (RFC 5545 3.3.5 violation)
description: Finding 3 of docs/designs/eds-nostr-backends.md §1. The iCal generator in gnome/nostr-dav/src/nd-ical.c writes DTSTART/DTEND as ';TZID=<tzid>:<YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS>Z'. RFC 5545 §3.3.5 forbids the TZID parameter on the UTC (Z) form; libical-based clients treat the value as malformed or drop the TZID. Fix: when a tzid is known emit local wall-clock time in that zone under TZID (no Z); emit UTC with Z only when there is no tzid (fall back to UTC if the zone cannot be resolved). Round-trip parse must keep working. Tracked under wave-4 item D.

title: relayd: cache-less session relay never sends EOSE/CLOSED for a plain REQ (clients hang to their timeout)
description: apps/relayd/src/protocol_nip01.c REQ path: when ctx->storage is NULL (session relay started without a storage driver, the packaged WITH_NOSTRDB=OFF case, see nostrc-prqu.5) the 'else if (st && st->vt && st->vt->query)' branch is skipped and NOTHING is sent: no EVENT, no EOSE, no CLOSED. NIP-01 requires EOSE (or CLOSED). Every local client (nostr-dispatcher nd-fetch 1.5 s, nostr-search-provider 800 ms deadline, notify) waits its full timeout on every REQ. Search REQs are fine (protocol_nip50.c sends CLOSED 'unsupported: search' when storage is NULL), so the packaged relay also has no NIP-50 and nostr-search-provider falls back to its bounded scan, which also gets nothing. Fix: with no storage, reply EOSE immediately (empty store), or CLOSED 'unsupported: no storage'. nostr-search-provider works around it with a circuit breaker (skips the relay 30 s after an EOSE-less timeout). Acceptance: relayd test REQ against a storage-less server gets EOSE within one round trip.
notes: FIXED on branch fix/session-relay-followups, commit 1dab5499 (not merged). Contract (apps/relayd/src/protocol_nip01.c handle_req): every REQ ends in EOSE (all stored matches sent -- immediately with no storage / empty / NULL-err0 query) or CLOSED with NIP-01 prefix (auth-required, invalid: bad/over-long sub id|no filter|malformed|>max_filters, unsupported: search w/o index|COUNT w/o storage, rate-limited: >max_subs in flight, error: query failed). No sub id -> NOTICE. Also fixed: std multi-filter REQs parsed only f1 and store got arr[0] as a contiguous array; filters calloc'd not nostr_filter_new'd (heap overflow in int_array_add, ASan); COUNT freed a stack filter + unterminated sub id; 2nd REQ leaked iterator -> per-connection FIFO of pending subs (min(max_subs,16)), max_subs default 1->8. Tests: relayd_req_contract (no storage + scripted fake storage), relayd_session_relay_ws asserts EOSE. ask_oracle-reviewed. Clients' workarounds (search-provider breaker, dispatcher 1.5 s) can now be relaxed -- not done here. Follow-ups filed: nostrc-pnc7 (libnostr ignores limit:0), nostrc-6tuz (libgo array growth from cap 0).

title: nip55l: app_id + approval for GetPublicKey/NIP04*/NIP44*, and bind app_id to the D-Bus caller
description: org.nostr.Signer gates only SignEvent (by caller-supplied app_id). GetPublicKey, GetRelays, NIP04Encrypt/Decrypt, NIP44Encrypt/Decrypt(+B64) take no app_id and raise no approval, so any session-bus client can decrypt the user's DMs silently; the NIP-07 bridge (nostrc-jjyp) compensates with an extension-side per-origin prompt, which is not a boundary against local processes. Also app_id is unauthenticated: any client can claim 'https://snort.social' and inherit its ACL and dialog label. Wanted: (1) app_id arg + ACL + ApprovalRequested for decrypt (and optionally encrypt/GetPublicKey), via new method names to keep the contract backwards compatible; (2) bind app_id claims to the caller (peer credentials / Flatpak app id / a trusted-bridge allowlist so only nostr-signer-webext-host may assert web origins). Bridge will adopt (1) in nm_provider_nip07.c when available.

title: nip55l: SignEvent remember-ACL saved under resolved npub but looked up under caller's identity selector
