title: session relay: upstream federation client (store-and-forward writes to NIP-65 / group / inbox relays)
description: apps/relayd/src/session/session_routing.h defines the per-class routing table but explicitly leaves the 'actually connect to upstream' client out of scope. Consequence (found in nostrc-1xak): an event published only to $XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/nostr/relay.sock never leaves the machine, so nostr-share defaults to upstream_mode=session_relay_and_direct (session copy + direct NIP-65 write relays; session ACK alone is not success), and session_relay_or_direct / session_relay_only are unsafe everywhere (nostr-share, nostr-dav nostrc-862u, nostr-notify). Build the federation client: store-and-forward with backoff for writes per session_routing class, persist the queue across restarts, report per-event upstream status. Then flip nostr-share's default to session_relay_or_direct. Clients can now reach the socket via nostr_publish_transport_new_websocket_unix() (libnostr-publish, a8a36720).
notes:
wF (branch feat/session-relay-federation, NOT pushed): d4346f8d relay-core fix (replaceable stale check passed a pointer array as the NostrFilter array; + regression test), cf5dce87 federation client, 666fe4e1 packaging (glib-networking Depends/Requires, one line each). Merges cleanly onto master 07941649.

CONTRACT (apps/relayd/README.md "Upstream federation" is normative): OK true on relay.sock = stored in nostrdb AND durably queued (outbox.sqlite3, WAL, synchronous=FULL; store first, queue second). Never forwarded: NIP-70 ["-"] (the app-side local-only marker), kinds 13/14/22242/20000-29999, federation_local_only_kinds, non-local-account authors (federation_accounts, else org.nostr.Signer.GetPublicKey, lazily; 1059 exempt). Targets only from user data: author 10002 write relays; NIP-29 9-12/9000-9030 -> group relay (h hint / author 10009 / host'id); 1059 -> recipient 10050; kind 5 also to where deleted events were acked. Per-relay OK tracking, backoff, lazy NIP-42 via org.nostr.Signer (relay holds no keys); gift wraps never sent authenticated (reason prefix auth-refused-for-gift-wrap:). Point-in-time routing.

D-BUS (additive): FederationState, PendingUpstream, ForwardedCount, FailedUpstream, LastUpstreamError; GetStats federation_* keys; GetEventUpstream(id)->(state,detail,a(sssuxx)); GetUpstreamRelays(); signal UpstreamStatusChanged(event_id,relay_url,relay_state,reason,event_state); CLI --upstream [ID]. Retention hook nsr_outbox_eviction_eligible() for 8rxk/prqu.17.

CONSUMERS TO FLIP (not edited here): nostr-dav (862u merged: session_relay_only targets only the session relay and treats its OK as PUBLISHED) -> require FederationState in {active, waiting-for-account} before honouring session_relay_only (fail closed/hold otherwise, incl. older daemons without the property) and report upstream success from UpstreamStatusChanged/GetEventUpstream (forwarded|partial) instead of the local OK. nostr-share (owner E) -> default session_relay_or_direct per this bead's description, drop the session_relay_only warning when FederationState is active, same upstream-status wait. Consumer state table in the README.

EVIDENCE: all 13 relayd ctests pass under ASan on aarch64 (lab 192.168.64.3, ~/nostrc-ci/wF-federation), incl. new test_session_fed_policy/outbox/federation/relay_federation; dpkg-buildpackage ok; dep-purity gate ok; installed nostrc-session-relay+nostrc-relayd, kind 10002 + kind 1 to relay.sock arrived on a real nostrc-relayd at ws://127.0.0.1:7447 (REQ by id returns it), --upstream shows forwarded/acked, ForwardedCount=2, NIP-70 event stayed local (unknown).

title: nip55l: signer ACL is keyed on a client-supplied app_id
description: Found in the nostrc-da9c Oracle review. The ACL entries for SignEvent and NIP44DeriveConversationKey are keyed "<app_id>:<identity>", where app_id comes from the caller (it falls back to the D-Bus unique name, which changes on every connection). Any same-uid client can claim another app's app_id and inherit its remembered allow decisions. Fix: derive the caller identity on the server side (GetConnectionCredentials -> pid -> /proc/<pid>/exe, or a portal/flatpak app id) and key the ACL on that; show both the claimed and verified identity in ApprovalRequested.

Spoofed-origin phase green on lab. macOS bus gives no PIDs: documented claimed:<app_id> degraded mode.

title: libmarmot: KeyPackage LeafNode capabilities list no extensions/proposals, contradicting the mls_extensions/mls_proposals tags
description:
Found while doing nostrc-s2bz. libmarmot/src/mls/mls_key_package.c mls_key_package_create() sets leaf_node.cap_extensions = NULL and proposals = NULL ('extensions: none', 'proposals: none'). The kind:30443 event still advertises mls_extensions=[0x000a,0xf2ee] (as the old 443 events did) and mls_proposals=[0x000a], because MDK 0.8 parsers require those exact tags and the MDK vectors pin them. The tags are advertisement/fetch filters only; receivers are supposed to validate the decoded LeafNode, and that exposes the gap:
- MDK groups put 0xF2EE in GroupContext RequiredCapabilities (MDK v0.8 constant.rs GROUP_CONTEXT_REQUIRED_EXTENSIONS), so an OpenMLS-based inviter should refuse to add a libmarmot KeyPackage whose leaf capabilities omit 0xF2EE. This is a real interop gap, independent of the transport kind.
- libmarmot has no SelfRemove (proposal 0x000a) handling (src/mls/mls_group.h lists proposals 1-7 only), so the mls_proposals tag over-claims.
Fix: advertise 0x000a (last_resort) and 0xf2ee in leaf capabilities; either implement SelfRemove or stop advertising it (coordinate with nostrc-prqu.9, whose adopted profile uses app_data_update 0x0008 instead); derive the event id-list tags from the actual capabilities so they cannot drift. Add an MDK interop test that adds a libmarmot KeyPackage to an MDK-created group.
notes: Wave4 G: 2b3780d8. All libmarmot leaves (KP, creator, commit path) advertise extensions [0x000a,0xf2ee], proposals [] (SelfRemove not implemented; MDK 0.8 derives required proposals as intersection of invitee leaves so it will not require it); mls_extensions tag derived from caps; mls_proposals tag stays 0x000a because MDK 0.8 parser requires exactly that (commented at the write site). KeyPackage Lifetime was 0..0 (expired) -> now-1h..+84d. ctest -R marmot 20/20 macOS + aarch64 lab; MDK interop 10373 checks; vectors unmodified. No MDK add-member interop test (no Rust toolchain run here).

title: RPM: nostr-notify-daemon links libnip19.so but the spec deletes it
description: packaging/rpm/nostr-login.spec removes %{_libdir}/libnip19.so while nostr-notify-daemon (gnome/nostr-homed) links nip19 dynamically (BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON) -> unresolvable auto-Requires / runtime failure. title: Session relay ships cache-less in packaged builds (WITH_NOSTRDB=OFF)
description: Lab (Wave-4 debs): nostr-session-relayd logs "storage driver 'nostrdb' unavailable; the session relay will run cache-less (queries return empty)". debian/rules + RPM set WITH_NOSTRDB=OFF. So nostr-dispatcher's local lookup (and notify's session_relay mode) can never hit in packaged installs. Also: a python EVENT publish to the packaged relay got no OK reply (hung) -- investigate. Decide: ship nostrdb in the session relay, or an in-memory LRU store.
notes: DECISION: ship storage. Branch fix/session-relay-followups, commit dfa72bfc (not merged). debian/rules + RPM spec: only WITH_NOSTRDB OFF->ON; LIBNOSTR_WITH_NOSTRDB stays OFF (ON would link nostrdb+LMDB+libsodium PUBLICLY into libnostr.so = authd/pam). components/nostrdb builds a private static nostrdb (cmake/NostrdbVendored.cmake) linked only into nostr-session-relayd + nostrc-relayd; mains register the driver explicitly (static-archive constructor was dropped by the linker). Driver read path had never worked (nostrdb returns nonzero on success; NULL scratch buffer) -- fixed, plus count/note_json/mkdir. nostrc-relayd now opens storage in $STATE_DIRECTORY. storage_driver="none" = explicit cache-less. EVIDENCE (aarch64 lab): no new build-deps (libsodium-dev/libsecp256k1-dev present; LMDB+flatcc vendored in submodule like nsync); private nostrdb cold compile 1.8 s wall/5.7 s CPU; dpkg-buildpackage -b -j4 ok; dep-purity 'ok: dep-purity gate clean', libnostr.so 0 ndb_* symbols, no sodium/LMDB; session relay +1 DT_NEEDED libsodium23, 0 symbol collisions; installed debs over relay.sock: REQ->EOSE 0 ms, signed EVENT->OK true, served back by id and after service restart; SessionRelay1 storage_backend=nostrdb event_count=1. The earlier 'EVENT got no OK' was q9ba part 2 (frames never reached NIP-01). Not done: gnome/nostr-settings/README.md:139 still says packaged relay is cache-less (E's tree); SessionRelay1 Version empty in debs (no -DNOSTR_SESSION_RELAYD_VERSION in debian/rules, D's).
close_reason: Merged 9c4e1dcf (0b480812 q9ba pt2, 1dab5499 prqu.14, dfa72bfc prqu.5, a4e465dc ig4k). Session relay stores events (nostrdb static, libnostr.so untouched, dep-purity ok), WS upgrade over relay.sock works, every REQ ends in EOSE/CLOSED, porthome user units start. Lab: 101 in 40ms, EOSE 0ms, EVENT OK+readback across re-activation.

title: libnostr: prepare_subscription rejects NULL ctx; nostr_subscription_new subs are never registered for dispatch
description: relay.c nostr_relay_prepare_subscription() returns NULL when ctx==NULL, but apps/gnostr/src/sync/neg-client.c passes NULL (so its fetch path always fails). Separately, only prepare_subscription inserts the sub into relay->subscriptions (the map message_loop dispatches from); gnome/nostr-homed/src/notify/notify_subs.c uses nostr_subscription_new()+fire and therefore looks like it can never receive events. Verify both with a mock relay; fix API (accept NULL ctx; register in fire or new). nostr-dispatcher passes nostr_relay_get_context() as a workaround.
notes: Fixed in a2b93d96 on branch fix/libnostr-dav-packaging-followups (not pushed); test_subscription_dispatch (loopback lws fixture relay) fails 3 ways pre-fix, green after.
close_reason: Merged aa84da77 (D branch, 11 commits a2b93d96..dfade292). Details in the merge message; ctest matrix docs/reviews/ctest-sweep-aarch64-2026-09-26.md.

title: nostr-dav: nostr_dav_upstream_mode is not enforced (session_relay_only still publishes/syncs direct to home relays)
description: Found during nostrc-tmsc. nd-config documents nostr_dav_upstream_mode as a privacy control (session_relay_only = never contact home relays), but it is stored and ignored: nd-relay-sync.h calls it 'currently informational' and nd-publisher publishes to home_relays regardless. A user with session_relay_only therefore leaks publishes + REQs directly to their home relays. libnostr-publish now offers NostrPublishPolicy.upstream + nostr_publish_policy_select_targets() (returns NO_RELAYS for session-only with no session relay). Fix: plumb a session relay URL (nostrc-session-relay listens on a unix socket, so the transport needs a unix-socket path or a ws bridge), map upstream_mode onto the policy in nd_publisher_configure, route publisher + relay-sync targets through select_targets. This is a behaviour change, so it was kept out of the tmsc extraction on purpose.
notes: Fixed in bb7e4caf on branch fix/libnostr-dav-packaging-followups (not pushed); session_relay_only holds/stays local (7d96) and is documented+logged.
close_reason: Merged aa84da77 (D branch, 11 commits a2b93d96..dfade292). Details in the merge message; ctest matrix docs/reviews/ctest-sweep-aarch64-2026-09-26.md.

title: gnostr-signer-daemon fails to link with libsodium: gn_key_provider_ed25519_register undefined (bunker core)
description: Pre-existing on master 49b5a486 (reproduced on aarch64 lab and macOS, 2026-09-26). When libsodium is found, gnostr_signer_bunker_core gets GNOSTR_HAVE_SODIUM=1, so src/key_provider.c:419 calls gn_key_provider_ed25519_register(). But key_provider_ed25519.c is not in the bunker core source list (apps/gnostr-signer/CMakeLists.txt, add_library(gnostr_signer_bunker_core ...)). Result: 'undefined reference to gn_key_provider_ed25519_register' when linking apps/gnostr-signer/gnostr-signer-daemon. Fix: add src/key_provider_ed25519.c (and its deps) to the bunker core, or gate the registration on a define only the GUI sets.

title: gnostr-signer: dormant GNOSTR_HAVE_LIBSECRET keyring writers (secret_store.c identity, sessions, TPM) — route via daemon or delete
description: GNOSTR_HAVE_LIBSECRET has never been defined for the gnostr-signer GUI or gnostr_signer_bunker_core on any build: the only definer was 'if (TARGET gnostr-secret)' in apps/gnostr-signer/CMakeLists.txt, which ran before gnome/seahorse was configured. nostrc-bml6 (branch fix/keyring-schema-unify) removed those blocks on purpose, because nip55l now builds gnostr-secret first and the define would have switched this code on. The code is still in tree and is a second writer to the daemon-owned schema: apps/gnostr-signer/src/secret_store.c:122 (org.gnostr.Signer/identity with fingerprint/created_at), client_session.c:985 (org.gnostr.Signer.ClientSessions), session-manager.c:127 (org.gnostr.Signer.Session), hsm_provider_tpm.c:909 (MASTER_KEY_SCHEMA). On Linux the GUI and bunker therefore run on their non-libsecret fallbacks. Decide per file: route key material through org.nostr.Signer StoreKey/ClearKey (the daemon is the sole key holder) or delete it; non-key secrets such as session passwords may legitimately keep their own schemas. The unified schema already declares fingerprint/created_at, so secret_store.c could adopt gnostr_secret_schema if it survives.
notes: branch fix/signer-hardening-2 (not pushed, based on 3835b81f): 95d7f7d2 - secret_store add/remove/generate via daemon StoreKey/ClearKey, no keyring label writes, TPM software master-key store (libsecret + Keychain, non-crypto PRNG) removed. Kept: client_session / session-manager non-key secrets.
close_reason: Merged to master in 5ea6cfc9 (worker B, fix/signer-hardening-2)

title: Marmot: migrate KeyPackage kind 443 -> 30443 (prereq for Groundhog MLS)
description: 30443 appears only in libmarmot/tests/test_interop.c:559-560 and test vectors (protocol-vectors.json:165-166); zero implementation source in libmarmot/src or marmot-gobject/src. Implement per current Marmot spec; keep interop vectors green.
notes:
Implemented on branch feat/marmot-keypackage-30443 (worktree .repoprompt-worktrees/nostrc/feat-marmot-keypackage-30443). Not pushed; bead left open for review.
Commits: 38c3de4f libmarmot 30443; ad77a0a8 marmot-gobject API; 33a2f3f4 gnostr mls-groups kind switch; d1c1c2da interop test working dir.
Spec: marmot-protocol/marmot @26fa6a6 transports/nostr.md (KeyPackage publication; Event identity and tag cardinality), foundation/key-packages.md. Emitted tags match the MDK 0.8 vectors (libmarmot/tests/vectors/mdk/protocol-vectors.json, unchanged).
Decisions:
(1) Legacy 443 read: strict cutover, 443 not accepted. The adopted spec removed it, MDK v0.8 accepted it only until 2026-05-31, and MDK master rejects it. Welcomes for KeyPackages already published as 443 still work (key material is looked up by KeyPackageRef).
(2) d slot: 32 random bytes per account, persisted through mls_store label kp_slot (no schema change) and reused on every rotation.
(3) NIP-70 '-' tag dropped (not in the 30443 tag set; relays without AUTH reject protected events).
(4) The adopted strict profile (MLSMessage framing, app_components 0x8009, no encoding/relays tags) is deferred to nostrc-prqu.9. The LeafNode capabilities vs id-list tags mismatch is nostrc-prqu.10. Gnostr 10002-based discovery and select usage is nostrc-prqu.11.
Version decisions: libmarmot 0.1.0->0.2.0 (breaking wire change on 0.x, MINOR); marmot-gobject 1.0.0->1.1.0 (additive API; wire kind follows libmarmot; the maintainer may prefer MAJOR); gnostr no bump (its own public surfaces are unchanged; the next release notes should mention it). Test-harness commit: no bump.
Tests: ctest -R marmot 19/19 on macOS and on the aarch64 lab (~/nostrc-ci/w5-marmot, out-of-tree, MDK vectors exercised). test_protocol 58/58 (11 new 30443 cases). Interop: 4 MDK 30443 events accepted, 443 rejected, tag parity 8/8. mls-groups plugin builds with no new diagnostics.
close_reason: Merged a17f13b1 (38c3de4f, ad77a0a8, 33a2f3f4, d1c1c2da). libmarmot 30443 addressable KeyPackages w/ slot reuse + strict tag rules + select(); marmot-gobject additive; gnostr mls-groups switched. 19/19 tests macOS+aarch64; MDK vectors exercised and unchanged. Follow-ups prqu.9/10/11.

title: GVfs backends blossom:// and nostr://npub/files/ — the GNOME-native 'relays as filesystem'
description: Both existing FUSE trees (gnome/nostr-homed/src/fs/nostrfs.c legacy; src/porthome-fuse Phase-4) mount portable HOME, not raw relay content. title: nostr-seal: encrypt files for an npub (NIP-44 key agreement + porthome chunked AEAD container) and NIP-49 passphrase mode
description: NIP-44 v2 is a message cipher (65535-byte cap, no streaming) — not a file format. Design: use NIP-44 conversation-key derivation (ECDH secp256k1 + HKDF) as root key into the already-approved chunked sealed-blob container from docs/designs/porthome-crypto-spec.md (nh_porthome_crypto.h: version|nonce|ct|tag, per-chunk HKDF nonce/key, address verified before decrypt). Multi-recipient by wrapping the file key per recipient (age-style). Passphrase mode via NIP-49 scrypt->XChaCha20-Poly1305 (nip49-keyencrypt already implements for nsec). Signer seam: add NIP44DeriveConversationKey(peer_pubkey)->s to nips/nip55l/dbus/org.nostr.Signer.xml (approvable permission; nsec stays in daemon) or fd-passing EncryptFile. Register .nsealed / application/vnd.nostr.sealed MIME so double-click decrypts. Optional publish sealed blob to Blossom + kind 1063 p-tagging recipient.
notes: Branch feat/nostr-seal (NOT pushed), rebased on origin/master f1c2aa4f: 2e1ed96a nip55l 0.3.0 NIP44DeriveConversationKey; ba1ea025 gnome/nostr-seal + debian/RPM nostr-seal. Oracle review adopted (key commitment, nostr-seal/v1 HKDF root, index version, overflow-free ceil, log_n cap 20, monotonic request ids + pending cap). Lab aarch64 (~/nostrc-ci/w4-seal): dpkg-buildpackage EXIT=0, dep-purity clean, nostr-seal_0.4.0-1_arm64.deb; seal+signer tests pass; 3 GiB sparse sealed 5.7s / opened 4.7s at 8 MiB RSS. Follow-ups: nostrc-y02q, nostrc-phk4, nostrc-f7hk, nostrc-hby8.
close_reason: Merged 4b7b4b41 (2e1ed96a nip55l 0.3.0 NIP44DeriveConversationKey; ba1ea025 nostr-seal). .nsealed v1 format w/ per-recipient NIP-44 wrap, passphrase NIP-49 stanza, porthome chunked AEAD, key commitment; aarch64 deb clean, dep-purity ok, 3 GiB streaming test. title: Audit nostrc NIP-29 implementation against upstream spec revisions (docs/nips pin bump d37b566b→db5fe3d)
description:
Bumped docs/nips submodule pin from d37b566b to db5fe3d (commit forthcoming). The 8+ commits between those pins add or clarify several NIP-29 group-chat mechanics that the nostrc implementation may not yet handle:

  db5fe3d nip29: clarify group relay migration and forks
  bdfa7e6 NIP-29: allow 'a' tags in pin list (#2416)
  da1629e NIP-29: add banner tag to group metadata (kind:39000) (#2383)
  223ddb3 NIP-29: add subgroups spec (#2319)
  6834e8b NIP-29: invite code suffix for group identifiers (#2380)
  f0af204 Avoid nip46 silent timeouts (#2375)     [NIP-46, incidental]
  f19d0e3 NIP-29: add message pinning (update-pin-list and kind:39005) (#2379)
  436d9fd add kind:10011, favorite follow sets (#2413)     [not NIP-29 but new kind]

Action items:
1. Audit current NIP-29 handling in nostrc (session-relay routing, nostr-notify daemon's NIP-29 preview logic, any group-chat code paths) against each of these upstream revisions.
2. For each divergence: either implement the spec update, or explicitly document why nostrc's implementation deliberately diverges.
3. Cross-check the notify daemon's 80-char NIP-29 preview logic — new kinds (kind:39005 message-pin-list) may need routing decisions.

title: nostr-homed-seed populates authority.db but user not visible via nostr-homectl show
description:
On lab (192.168.64.3), ran:
  nostr-homed-seed /var/lib/nostr-auth testuser smoke-test-passphrase
  nostr-homectl publish-projection /var/lib/nostr-auth
  # -> published /var/lib/nostr-auth/nss.db @ generation 1

But subsequent:
  nostr-homectl show /var/lib/nostr-auth testuser
  # -> not_found: testuser

Direct sqlite3 inspection of authority.db shows the accounts table has a different schema than expected (my `SELECT hex(id), name FROM accounts` returned 'no such column: id'). nss.db has no `users` table at all despite publish-projection reporting success.

Symptoms suggest either:
- nostr-homed-seed writes to a different table than nostr-homectl show reads, OR
- publish-projection queues work but doesn't actually project on generation 1 empty base

Blocks the E2E provisioning leg of nostrc-0xd3. Needs schema audit + tracing seed -> publish -> show path.
notes: Corrected repro: unprefixed testuser violates the load-bearing n_ username contract. The prior 'seed: enroll' line was an error (exit 1), not success; authority.db had zero account rows. Use n_testuser. Fix scope: reject invalid names before authority creation with explicit error, retain n_ invariant; lab seed n_testuser -> publish -> show succeeds. Do not close pending requester verification.

title: nostr-authd fresh install: smb.db reconcile-required refusal blocks first-boot
description:
On a fresh nostrc-samba-server + nostr-authd install (bizarro@192.168.64.3, Ubuntu 24.04 aarch64), starting nostr-authd fails:
  nostr-authd: cannot open smb journal /var/lib/nostr-auth/smb.db: reconcile-required

This is the Wave 3 Hotel NH_SMB_RECONCILE_REQUIRED drift-detector (bead #18) doing its job — detecting that the smb.db journal and the tdbsam passdb are out of sync. But on FIRST BOOT after a fresh install (empty smb.db, freshly seeded tdbsam), authd refuses to open at all, creating a chicken-and-egg problem for initial provisioning.

The Wave 3 landing didn't document the FIRST-BOOT reconciliation procedure. There should be either:
(a) A first-boot initializer that seeds smb.db from an empty tdbsam without triggering the drift-detector.
(b) A --force-first-boot flag on nostr-authd or a nh_smb_reconcile CLI that emits both blobs from a known-good state.

title: nostr-authd + nostr-smbd StateDirectory=nostr-auth mode conflict (0700 vs 0755)
description:
Both nostr-authd.service (StateDirectoryMode=0700) and nostr-smbd.service (StateDirectoryMode=0755, per Wave-5 nostrc-45b2 fix) declare StateDirectory=nostr-auth. Whichever unit restarts LAST wins the chmod on /var/lib/nostr-auth. This races between:

- nostr-authd wants 0700 (protects passdb blob + authority.db from other users)
- nostr-smbd needs 0755 (force-user nostr-smb-share account must traverse into share-root/)

Discovered by nostrc-0xd3 (live smoke lab). Fix options:
1. Move share-root out of /var/lib/nostr-auth (e.g. /srv/nostr-home or /var/lib/nostr-home-share) — cleanest but changes shipped semantics.
2. Loosen nostr-authd's StateDirectoryMode to 0755 (parent traversable; sensitive files still 0600 by application).
3. Have nostr-smbd RequiresMountsFor=/var/lib/nostr-auth/share-root and let it manage its OWN StateDirectory in a sibling location.

Preferred: option 2 (matches Wave-5 posture on smbd; passdb blobs are 0600 by smbpasswd, authority.db is 0600 by authd — parent traversability doesn't leak contents).
close_reason: Fixed in 2184b22d. nostr-authd.service.in StateDirectoryMode 0700→0755 (matches smbd Wave-5 posture); nips/nip34/CMakeLists.txt gains install(TARGETS nip34) + libnip34.so shipped in libhanami0.deb. Verified end-to-end: libhanami0_0.4.0-1_arm64.deb now contains libnip34.so; nostr-homed-provision --help runs cleanly; installed nostr-authd.service has StateDirectoryMode=0755.

title: nostr-notify.service.in: ProtectKernelLogs/Modules break systemd --user (218/CAPABILITIES)
description:
During nostrc-qngf Debian installed-unit acceptance, nostr-notify.service under systemd --user fails immediately with:

  (y-daemon)[N]: nostr-notify.service: Failed to drop capabilities: Operation not permitted
  systemd[U]: nostr-notify.service: Main process exited, code=exited, status=218/CAPABILITIES

ProtectKernelLogs=yes tries to drop CAP_SYSLOG and ProtectKernelModules=yes tries to drop CAP_SYS_MODULE from the bounding set. systemd --user is not privileged to modify capabilities, so the pre-exec setup EPERMs and exit=218.

The sibling nostr-dav.service already documents the exact same fix ("No ProtectKernelModules=: ... systemd --user cannot do (the unit fails with 218/CAPABILITIES)") — the fix simply wasn't ported to nostr-notify's template.

Fix: remove both directives from gnome/nostr-homed/systemd/user/nostr-notify.service.in with the same commentary as the dav unit. An unprivileged user service never holds those caps anyway.

Discovered by: nostrc-qngf.
close_reason: Closed

title: porthome: manifest schema v2 — carry sealed plaintext names alongside path_enc
description:
Blocking nostrc-bms6 (fetch-materializer path decrypt). The Phase-1 manifest schema (v1) stores path_enc (48-hex per component, one-way HMAC via nh_porthome_encrypt_name) but does NOT carry the plaintext path components. Because path_enc is a KEYED HASH (HMAC-SHA256(name_key, component)[0..24]) it is one-way — even the caller with home_key cannot reverse it to plaintext. Consequently the fetch materialiser has no source of plaintext names and cannot rename its written tree back to the operator-visible layout.

Design proposal (schema v2):
1. Bump NH_PORTHOME_MANIFEST_SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 (decoder retains strict version enforcement).
2. Add K_E_NAME_SEALED = 10 to entry map: the AEAD-sealed plaintext path (relative, slash-joined, no leading/trailing slash), sealed under a new domain "porthome/v1/name" HKDF salt (independent from chunk/manifest keys). Store as CBOR bstr.
3. Encoder (nh_porthome_manifest_add_file/add_dir/add_symlink) gains a plaintext-name parameter OR the encoder derives it from a sidecar helper; caller-facing shape TBD in review.
4. Decoder (nh_porthome_manifest_decode) MUST decrypt K_E_NAME_SEALED when present and expose it as a new e->name_plain field. v1 manifests continue to decode with name_plain=NULL (backwards-read compat; new writers refuse to write v1).
5. Fetch materialiser: after materialising the path_enc tree, walk depth-first and rename each component from path_enc → name_plain using renameat/renameat2. Symlinks whose target field is also encrypted get a parallel field K_E_SYMLINK_TGT_SEALED (or lift the existing K_E_SYMLINK_TGT to be sealed; TBD in design).
6. Storage cost: 48-hex + AEAD(29-byte overhead + component length) per component per entry; for a 3-component path with 8-byte components: current ~150 bytes/entry becomes ~250 bytes/entry — well under NH_PORTHOME_MAX_CBOR_BYTES (1 MiB) for the 100-file demo.

Rationale: without this change, bms6 cannot ship as described. Alternative (walking the source-side plaintext-name list) is only feasible for the pushing party — the pulling party never had access to those names.

Acceptance:
- Design doc: docs/designs/porthome-manifest-schema-v2.md with wire layout, HKDF domain string, and decoder rules.
- Header + codec change: nh_porthome_entry gains name_plain (owned char *); encoder writes v2 layout by default; decoder accepts both v1 and v2 (name_plain NULL in v1) but strict about ONLY those two versions.
- Test: encode-then-decode round-trip preserves name_plain (test_manifest_schema_v2 in gnome/nostr-homed/tests/unit/).
- Push path (nostr-homed-provision.c cmd_push) populates name_plain when it computes path_enc; a smallhome driver test asserts the manifest carries both fields.
- Discovered: docs/reviews/porthome-89rj-live-e2e-2026-09-25.md §12 (spinoffs).
- Filed by: nostrc-bms6 follow-up (2026-09-25).

title: sharegap.net nginx client_max_body_size below DESIGN chunk (1 MiB vs 4 MiB)

Options:
  A. Raise the nginx client_max_body_size on sharegap to ≥ 8 MiB (cheapest — we operate it).
  B. Extend hanami_server_capabilities_t with a probed 'max_put_bytes' field and have the chunker pick min(DESIGN_CHUNK, server_cap). Costs one HEAD/PUT round trip at connect and per-server chunker branching.

A is a config change; B is durable across other-operator community servers with tight caps. Do A immediately, file B as a P3 hanami follow-up.

title: libhanami: batch BUD-02 auth event + hanami_blossom_upload_batch()
description: Follow-up to nostrc-yo44 (D8 probe verdict: BATCH-VIABLE). Add hanami_bud02_create_batch_auth_event(action, sha256_hex_array, count, expiration, server_url_or_null) that mints ONE kind-24242 event with N ['x', h_i] tags and one shared ['expiration', …] tag; then a hanami_blossom_upload_batch() (or extend hanami_blossom_upload with a batch API) that PUTs an array of blobs sharing that Authorization header. Wire into nh_porthome_blossom_upload from the Phase-2 provisioner (nostrc-89rj). Include: (a) on 401 for any PUT in a batch, fall back to per-blob auth for that server for the rest of the session (session-scoped negative cache) and file a diagnostic; (b) do NOT include a 'server' tag by default — blossom.band rejects any variant we tried, sharegap and primal accept both. Evidence: docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md.
close_reason:
Delivered in commit ed446dae. libhanami now exposes:
- hanami_bud02_create_batch_auth_event(action, hashes, count, expiration, server_url_or_null)
  Mints one kind-24242 with N ["x", h_i] tags + one ["expiration", ts];
  server tag OMITTED by default (blossom.band-safe). Default expiration
  120s, capped at 900s.
- hanami_blossom_upload_batch(client, blobs, count, out_results)
  Shared Authorization across N PUTs; on any 401 in-flight, drops the
  batch header and falls back to per-blob auth for the remainder of the
  call; results carry error_class="batch-fell-back".
- Session-scoped negative-capability cache at hanami-server-capability.
  {h,c} (batch_ok / server_tag_ok / strict_x_binding / last_probe_ts
  / last_401_ts) attached to each client handle. Future calls in the
  same session skip batch on a server that already refused it.

Wired into porthome as nh_porthome_blossom_upload_batch() with per-server
accounting (chunks_uploaded, bytes_uploaded, chunks_failed, batch_fell_
back). Provisioner-first: syncd's per-chunk pushes stay on the single-
blob path this pass.

Tests: 4 new cases in test_hanami_bud02_auth (batch-event shape,
server-tag opt-in, expiration cap, null args) + 7 new cases in
test_hanami_blossom_batch (fallback + cache-latch, probe kill-switch,
probe shape recording; uses an in-process HTTP/1.1 stub). All 29
hanami tests pass under ctest.

Live smoke: docs/reviews/porthome-hanami-batch-and-capability-live-
2026-09-25.md — verdicts match yo44's D8 evidence on sharegap, band,
and primal.

title: porthome-fuse: fall through to tier-3 Blossom fetch on tier-2 AEAD failure (design §3.1/§3.3)
description: Design §3.1 tier-3 line specifies re-population on tier-3 success; §3.3 explicitly says a pinned blob missing tier 2 due to on-disk corruption "is treated as a tier-3 fetch, not as an error". Current nh_fuse_source_chunk in gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-fuse/nh_fuse_source.c returns -EIO immediately on nh_porthome_decrypt_chunk failure of tier-2 bytes and does not attempt tier 3. Impact: cache corruption is terminal EIO for that chunk until the entry is manually cleared. The safety invariant "corrupt cache never emits wrong plaintext" is preserved — this is a self-heal gap, not a correctness one. Confirmed live 2026-09-24 in docs/reviews/porthome-fuse-live-2026-09-24.md case (d).
notes: Fixed on branch fix/porthome-fuse-stabilize @ 79f4ab15. nh_fuse_source_chunk now logs NOTICE + unlink(2)s the poisoned tier-2 blob on decrypt failure and falls through to tier-3 (Blossom or optional test seam). Safety invariant preserved. New unit: gnome/nostr-homed/tests/unit/test_fuse_source_poison.c (mirrors live-smoke case (d)). Verified full homed_porthome/fuse/syncd 30/30 green on aarch64 with all EXPERIMENTAL gates ON; default-OFF nostr-authd builds clean, test_syncd_off_closure.sh reports ok. Evidence: docs/reviews/porthome-fuse-live-2026-09-24.md observed-gaps §3. Case (f) inotify auto-reload (nostrc-plo4) remains open; nostrc-1u55 stays open until that lands.
close_reason: fixed

title: porthome-fuse: wire inotify-driven snapshot reload (design §7.3 F4)
description: Design §7.3 D10 and §13 F4 call for an inotify watcher on $XDG_STATE_HOME/nostr-homed that debounces 500 ms on IN_MOVED_TO of snapshot.json / generation, rebuilds the nh_fuse_table into a new immutable struct, atomically swaps the g_table pointer while old handles hold refcounts, re-applies the pin ring, and issues fuse_invalidate_path per changed entry (with the 512-path degradation fallback). Current code in gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-fuse/nostr-home-fuse.c declares <sys/inotify.h> but starts no watcher — fresh open() after a gen-2 publish still returns gen-1 bytes until unmount+remount. Confirmed live 2026-09-24 in docs/reviews/porthome-fuse-live-2026-09-24.md case (f). Per-open pinning (in-flight fh keeps its generation) is already working correctly.
notes: New nh_fuse_reload module: inotify on state_dir, 250ms debounce, pthread + pthread_rwlock swap. Per-open GENERATION binding preserved. Parse-failure fires throttled fuse-snapshot-reload-failed notify. Escape hatch NOSTR_HOMED_PORTHOME_FUSE_NO_INOTIFY=1. Live-smoke on bizarro@192.168.64.3: gen1 → gen2 → gen3 within 600ms without remount. Commit cb7f4c39.
close_reason: Closed

title: porthome syncd I1 followups: multi-server replication + rescan on missed inotify
description:
Follow-ups from I1 (nostrc-p6qp).

1) nh_syncd_pusher upload_chunk currently uses nh_porthome_blossom_upload which uploads to EVERY configured server via libhanami. That covers min_replication>=2 by construction when >=2 servers are healthy, but does not surface per-server success counts. If a server is transiently down the upload returns OK on the first success and continues to the others silently. Add explicit per-server success accounting so the pusher can honor min_replication as a hard requirement (and refuse to advance generation if <min_replication servers accepted).

2) inotify recursive watcher does not perform a full-tree rescan on missed events (queue overflow / dropped events / add_watch race on rapid mkdir+rmdir+mkdir). The 15-minute force-flush picks up eventual changes, but a rescan on IN_Q_OVERFLOW would close the gap. I2's rescan-and-reconcile pipeline is the natural place to add this — audit that landing.

3) The daemon still reads home_key seed from an env var (NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_SEED_HEX). I3 must wire the real broker credential handoff (either via SO_PEERCRED-authenticated D-Bus / SEQPACKET or a mlock'd file the broker drops on session open).
close_reason: Landed in 2b989b41. Part 1: nh_syncd_pusher iterates per-server, min_replication is HARD (new NH_SYNCD_ERR_INSUFFICIENT_REPLICATION), status file surfaces last_upload_servers_ok/_total/_error_class, NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_MIN_REPLICATION env accepted. Part 2: watcher detects IN_Q_OVERFLOW → nh_syncd_rescan_diff (public) → pushes CREATE/MODIFY/DELETE into batcher; idempotent; periodic tick via NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_RESCAN_INTERVAL_SEC. Part 3 audit: broker seed drop path was already landed (Phase 3 W3, read_seed_from_broker_drop); env fallback NOW gated behind NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_TEST_MODE=1, systemd unit has audit note. Tests: test_syncd_pusher_multi_server + test_syncd_rescan_overflow both pass; 18/18 syncd ctest on aarch64 lab. Live-smoke transcript: docs/reviews/porthome-syncd-multi-server-live-2026-09-24.md. ldd unchanged (no new .so dep).

title: porthome: NIP-46 nip44_decrypt of wrapped_home_key + first-login enrollment
description: Phase 2 wrap-seed cache is populated only by the local vault provider today (HKDF from unlocked private key). This bead wires the NIP-46 path: (1) provider_nip46 grants 'sign_event,nip44_encrypt,nip44_decrypt' at connect. (2) On successful sign_event, if the account's provider record carries wrapped_home_key, RPC nip44_decrypt(peer=account_pubkey, ct=wrapped_home_key) -> 32-byte seed, deposit into wrap-seed cache. (3) If porthome_enroll_wrap_key=on AND wrapped_home_key is absent, generate a fresh seed (nh_porthome_wrap_seed_random), RPC nip44_encrypt, persist ciphertext to the provider record. (4) Extend qr_signer_standin to answer nip44_encrypt/_decrypt so the integration test (round-trip via a mock signer) is headless. Depends on nostrc-89rj (done).
notes: Landed on branch feat/porthome-nip46-wrapkey-live @ commits a7d876af (bead code), 8fd89ddd (publisher), 0834b2c8 (acceptance doc). Live end-to-end verified against wss://relay.sharegap.net + https://blossom.sharegap.net from bizarro@192.168.64.3 — see docs/reviews/porthome-live-e2e-2026-09-23.md. title: porthome: source home_key from NIP-46 nip44_decrypt in signer flow
description: Phase 1 exposes nh_porthome_key_derive(seed[32]) that takes a caller-supplied fixture seed. Production must instead: broker requests wrap_key via NIP-46 nip44_decrypt of the kind-30078 pointer's wrapped_home_key, then derives home_key. Requires provider_nip46 to grant 'sign_event,nip44_encrypt,nip44_decrypt' at connect time; test with qr_signer_standin + mock_signer. Belongs with Phase 2 provisioner (bd nostrc-h10m; sibling of the provisioner bead).
notes:
Closed in commit 07692159 on feat/porthome-nip46-wrap-key.

Close criteria (a)-(f) held at commit time:

(a) nip44_encrypt / nip44_decrypt client RPCs land at
    nostr_nip46_client_nip44_encrypt_rpc / nip44_decrypt_rpc
    (nips/nip46/src/core/nip46_session.c) — sibling to sign_event,
    same wire spec.

(b) provider_nip46 + provider_nip46_qr requested the extra grants at
    connect / QR pairing before this bead (perms CSV
    "sign_event,sign_event:1,nip44_encrypt,nip44_decrypt" and
    "sign_event:1,nip44_encrypt,nip44_decrypt"). This bead added the
    graceful degradation: any nip44 RPC failure downstream is logged
    with an explicit class (wrap-key-denied / signer-offline /
    decrypt-failed) and the broker's post-verify hook returns -1
    which is IGNORED by the provider — SIGNED_EVENT still emits,
    login succeeds, and PROVISION_HOME falls back to LIMITED_MODE
    on the empty wrap-seed cache (design §5.3).

(c) auth_porthome.nh_auth_broker_porthome_maybe_enroll_or_unwrap_nip46
    orchestrates fetch provider record → nip44_decrypt(wrapped_home_key)
    → seed-parser → deposit_wrap_seed → PROVISION_HOME takes seed →
    home_key derivation. Timeout applied via new
    porthome_nip46_decrypt_timeout_sec (default 30 s, hard-cap 120 s).

(d) Enrollment path (fresh wrap seed → nip44_encrypt →
    wrapped_home_key persist → deposit) lives in the broker's
    weak-linked post-verify hook, gated by
    porthome_enroll_wrap_key=on in auth.conf. Local vault path
    unchanged (HKDF from unlocked privkey). CLI enrollment is
    unchanged because for local-key accounts the wrap seed is
    derived from the privkey and for NIP-46 accounts the broker's
    first-successful-login hook is authoritative — no CLI-side RPC
    to a remote signer needed.

(e) Three unit tests (unwrap / enroll / denied) pass under -Werror
    on aarch64 as sub-tests of homed_porthome_wrapkey_nip46. The
    hook-seam nh_auth_broker_porthome_set_nip44_hooks replaces the
    real client RPCs without requiring a bunker or relay pool.
    Existing homed_porthome_wrapkey / homed_auth_conf remain green.

(f) Dep-purity: ldd nostr-authd and ldd pam_nostr.so match the
    pre-bead baseline. auth_porthome's nip46 client calls stay
    behind NH_AUTH_BROKER_ENABLE_PORTHOME + weak linkage; nothing
    new pulled into the base daemon or PAM closure.

Deferred / follow-up: see nostrc-ck6i-fu1 and nostrc-ck6i-fu2
(nip46 error-object introspection so wrap-key-denied vs
wrap-key-signer-offline can be split from actual response type;
per-account nip46_wrap_key_ok session flag caching so an older
bunker that repeatedly refuses does not keep retrying).
close_reason: Closed

title: [E-portable-home] Portable $HOME from relays + Blossom (home-from-relay)
description: A user logs into GNOME with their Nostr identity on any Linux box and their $HOME materializes from nostr-native storage: small encrypted pointer/manifest events on relays, content-addressed encrypted blobs on Blossom via libhanami. Design freeze lives at docs/designs/home-from-relay.md. Depends on nostrc-rb0e (Samba/packaging/release gates) and the merged roaming safety fixes (nostrc-nxpb.7/.8 UAF + false-success in nh_warm_cache/nh_open_session). No implementation until the maintainer confirms the open decisions in the design doc.
design: Design freeze: docs/designs/home-from-relay.md (commit 674037bb, branch design/home-from-relay). Data model: kind-30078 NIP-44-encrypted home pointer on relays; Merkle manifest nodes + 4MiB file chunks as NIP-44-sealed blobs on Blossom (BUD-01/02/04 via libhanami). Eager local copy for v1; FUSE re-scoped to Phase 4 lazy overlay. Materialization writes into the nh_identity_home_prepare staging descriptor. 18 decisions D1-D18; 10 need maintainer confirmation before Phase 1 (notably D4 convergent encryption, D16 plaintext-at-rest/LUKS, D10 eager-vs-FUSE, D11 limited mode).
notes: 2026-09-22 Phase 0 complete. Doc committed on branch design/home-from-relay, NOT pushed. Phase 1 (library primitives in src/home/) is blocked on the maintainer answering section 12 of the design doc.

title: [B5-profile] Nostr kind-0 profile → GDM avatar/name via AccountsService
description: At the GDM greeter, nostr accounts show a generic avatar and the gecos 'Nostr User'. Replace with the user's real Nostr profile (kind-0 metadata: name, display_name, picture) via AccountsService (org.freedesktop.Accounts SetIconFile/SetRealName), so stock GDM tile, login dialog, and lock screen all show it with no extension hacks. Fetch kind-0 via libnostr from configured relays; download the picture in a dropped-privilege helper with strict SSRF/size/type guards; re-encode via GdkPixbuf to a bounded PNG; install via AccountsService as root. Run at seed-time (nh-seed-authority/nh-seed-nip46-authority --fetch-profile) and post-login (rate-limited). Config in auth.conf: profile_relays, profile_fetch.

title: [identity] seeder/authority must skip uids already present in /etc/passwd; acceptance scripts must userdel throwaway users
description: Real-phone greeter test: loginctl showed the nip46qr session (uid 200000, n_bizarro) as user n_smbd7g because a leftover local /etc/passwd user from the D7 gvfs acceptance still holds uid 200000 and nsswitch resolves files before nostr for uid lookups. Cosmetic in this case but a real collision class: nh-seed-* / the authority uid allocator should refuse/skip uids present in /etc/passwd (getpwuid via files), and run_smb_mount_vm.sh / other acceptance scripts must remove their throwaway users on exit. Bucket A (nxpb.3 collision-safe allocation).

title: [pkg] release source tarball must bundle submodules (nsync, nostrdb) — git archive/GitHub tag tarballs omit them
description: With nsync vendored as a git submodule (third_party/nsync) and nostrdb also a submodule, the Fedora spec Source0 (GitHub tag tarball) and the README's git-archive recipe both EXCLUDE submodule contents, so a stock build from a release tarball cannot use the vendored fallback (or nostrdb). Add a dist script/target (e.g. scripts/make-dist.sh or a CMake 'dist' target) that produces nostrc-<ver>.tar.gz with submodules included (git archive + git submodule foreach archive, or tar of a recursive checkout), and point packaging/rpm/README.md + nostr-login.spec Source0 (and the Debian orig tarball) at it. Validation: rpmbuild from that tarball in the Fedora chroot with no nsync-devel succeeds.

title: [pkg-fedora] nsync-devel absent from Fedora 41/42 stock repos; needs COPR overlay or vendored nsync
description: Phase-1 Fedora validation (docs/reviews/fedora-spec-phase1-2026-09-22.md) found nsync-devel is NOT in Fedora 41/42 stock repos as of 2026-09-22 - correcting packaging-plan D-1 which assumed Fedora ships nsync-devel. libnostr/libnostrgo/libnostr-json/relayd all BuildRequire nsync. Workaround used for validation: built nsync from upstream in the Fedora chroot. For a real Fedora build: either publish nsync to a COPR overlay, or vendor third_party/nsync and build it in-tree (D-1 option b) - the latter also de-risks Debian/other distros. nostr-login.spec keeps BuildRequires: nsync-devel with an inline note. Revisit D-1: vendoring nsync in-tree is now the recommended path since it is missing on Fedora.
notes:
Vendored google/nsync in-tree at third_party/nsync (pinned to 1.30.0) with a system-first CMake resolver (cmake/FindOrVendorNsync.cmake, NOSTR_USE_SYSTEM_NSYNC AUTO/ON/OFF).

title: [nip98-bug] nip98 frees heap NostrTags via string_array_free — leaks tag struct

Fix: use nostr_tag_free(tags->data[i]) instead (now correctly frees the struct after the dhqz fix), or nostr_tags_free the container. Not exercised by the nostr-homed portable suite; found by code inspection during the homed ASan pass.
close_reason: Replaced string_array_free(tags->data[i]) with nostr_tag_free(tags->data[i]) in the two error-cleanup paths in nips/nip98/src/nip98.c (allocation failure for tags->data[1] and tags->data[2]). nostr_tag_free frees both the interior string data and the 24-byte StringArray struct (nostr_tag_new/new_string_array heap-allocated it). Verified: nip98 test suite (11/11 pass) in ASan build; libnostr audit tests (7/7 pass). ASan on Apple Silicon does not include LSan, so leak was confirmed by inspection of nostr_tag_free (tag.c:46-50) — string_array_free frees only the interior arrays, leaking sizeof(StringArray) per tag. Only the error paths were affected; success path already delegated to nostr_event_free -> nostr_tags_free -> nostr_tag_free.

title: gnostr Concord: compact and re-anchor the Control Plane at a new epoch (CORD-06 §3)
description:
A Refounding republishes the Control Plane, compacted, at the new epoch's Control address — signed by the new control_root-derived signer, readable under the new community_root — and only after the root roll is confirmed published. Compaction is what keeps Refoundings fast: members hop across dozens of epochs with thousands of Control events without reprocessing the plane each time, and CORD-06 requires aborting a Refounding whose Control events cannot all be folded.

The mechanism the spec relies on is already in place: Control Plane seals are plaintext (CORD-02 §5), so re-encrypting the last state under the new epoch preserves the original authors' signatures and a fresh joiner still verifies them. What is missing is the retention: GnConcordControlPlane folds editions and exposes folded state, but nothing hands back the raw signed seals a compaction re-wraps, so the plane needs a heads accessor before a Refounder can compact it.

Deferred out of nostrc-vhtt deliberately. On the Public-to-Private trigger the gap is invisible — the Community has no live invite link by definition, so there is no fresh joiner waiting to anchor, and existing members keep their own fold — but it MUST close before that Community mints a link again.
acceptance_criteria: A Refounder re-wraps the prior epoch's Control heads at the new epoch's address with the original signatures intact; a device holding nothing but the new root and the new control_pk folds the Community's authority state from the compaction alone.
close_reason: Compaction and re-anchor land inside the Refounding. GnConcordControlPlane now retains each edition's signed plaintext seal verbatim and exposes gn_concord_control_plane_get_heads() — one head per (entity, vsk), selected by the same select_head() the fold uses. The Refounder re-wraps those heads at the new epoch's Control address, under the new community_root-derived read key, signed by the freshly minted control_root's signer: a re-wrap, never a re-signing, so the original authors' signatures survive into an epoch they were not written in (the reason CORD-02 §5 makes these seals plaintext). Ordered per CORD-06 §3 — the re-anchor runs only after every rekey chunk's publication is confirmed and this device has adopted; a failure there is not a failed Refounding (the roll landed, republishing heads is idempotent, the Refounder resumes). Abort rule enforced before the first publish: a plane with parked editions (count_parked > 0) is one whose fold is unsettled, so refound_async refuses rather than compacting past an action nobody can yet judge. Tests: /concord/refound/re-anchors-control (a joiner holding only its rekey blob's new root + control_pk and not one prior edition folds the rename and a Grant-derived permission from the compaction alone; 5 editions in, 4 heads out — the superseded metadata version is what it never replays) and /concord/refound/aborts-on-unsettled-control (parked edition blocks the rotation with nothing published, and the same rotation proceeds once the cited Grant lands). All 4 refound tests plus the full concord suite green under ASan. Commit 0e79b5d7.

title: gnostr plugin API: a binary NIP-44 pairwise lane for fixed-width payloads
description:
A CORD-06 rekey blob is 72, 104 or 136 bytes of raw key material and is almost never valid UTF-8, but gnostr_plugin_context_nip44_encrypt_async() takes a const char * plaintext and rides NIP-46's JSON string params. An encoder either rejects such a plaintext or substitutes U+FFFD, and the bunker then encrypts corrupted bytes with nobody noticing — fatal for a format whose width is its own declaration.

The signer side already landed: signet speaks nip44_encrypt_b64 and nip44_decrypt_b64 (commit cdbc6d37), which move the plaintext side over standard base64 while the ciphertext stays an ordinary NIP-44 v2 payload. What is missing is the client half — a GnostrPluginContext entry point that reaches them, so a plugin can wrap a blob under the pairwise key the user shares with a recipient without going through a UTF-8 string.

This blocks every Refounding blob delivery (nostrc-vhtt): a Rotator wraps one blob per recipient under the Rotator-to-recipient conversation key, and there is no way to do that from a plugin today.
acceptance_criteria: A plugin can encrypt and decrypt arbitrary byte payloads under the pairwise NIP-44 key with a local signer and with a NIP-46 bunker, and a 136-byte blob round-trips byte-identically.
notes: Shape it as its own method pair rather than a flag on the existing one, matching signet: a bunker without the capability then errors instead of silently encrypting base64 text as if it were the plaintext.
close_reason: Binary NIP-44 pairwise lane landed end to end: nostr_nip46_client_nip44_{encrypt,decrypt}_b64_rpc reaching signet's methods (cdbc6d37); NIP44EncryptB64/NIP44DecryptB64 on org.nostr.Signer with nostr_nip55l_nip44_{encrypt,decrypt}_b64 behind it for the local D-Bus signer; gnostr_signer_service_nip44_{encrypt,decrypt}_bytes_async dispatching per transport; gnostr_plugin_context_nip44_{encrypt,decrypt}_bytes_async taking/returning GBytes as the plugin surface. Only the plaintext side is base64 and only between caller and signer — the ciphertext is an ordinary NIP-44 v2 payload, so a blob wrapped here opens with any NIP-44 implementation. Strict canonical decode at every hop. Tests: nip55l_nip44_b64 (72/104/136 round-trip byte-identical, cross-lane open with the plain primitive, malformed base64 refused not truncated) and /concord/crypto/nip44-bytes-roundtrip through the plugin API and its offline backend, which also pins that the string lane truncates the same payload at the first NUL. Both green under ASan. Commit 280831af.

title: NIP-46: replace per-RPC detached threads with bounded prioritized work queue

Also the gate condvar is not FIFO, so bulk nip44_decrypt traffic can delay interactive sign_event/connect/get_public_key. Replace detached threads (nip46_rpc_call_async) with a bounded work queue that prioritizes interactive ops over hydration decrypts. Related: session lifetime refcounting (see nostrc-svsj notes) - gate drain in session_free mitigates but signer service should retain a session ref per dispatched op.

title: Signet: make agent revocation steps transactional (deny + leases + bindings + key delete)
description: signet_revoke_internal commits deny-list insertion, lease revocation, client-binding revocation, and key deletion as separate SQLite statements. Partial failure can leave inconsistent state (e.g. deny-listed but leases live, or bindings revoked but key intact). Wrap the store-side steps in one transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT on the shared handle), then update/wipe the hot caches after commit. Serialize pairing (consume+bind txn) and revocation on the same identity boundary. Flagged in Oracle review of nostrc-xhb; the worst race (consume->revoke->bind orphan) is already closed by the atomic consume+bind and identity-pinned bindings, so this is consistency hardening.
close_reason: Closed

title: Signet: mgmt handler reply_contextvm is shared mutable state — race can misroute replies
description: signet_mgmt_handler_handle_intent() sets h->reply_contextvm=true around its internal handle_event() call and resets it after. If relay callbacks ever dispatch management events concurrently (multiple relay worker threads), one call can reset the flag while another is executing, causing a ContextVM reply to be emitted as a legacy kind-28090 ack (or vice versa) — e.g. a reissue-connect reply the recovering agent never receives even though the secret was already replaced. Currently mitigated if dispatch is single-threaded, but the handler should not rely on that. Fix: thread the reply transport through as an invocation parameter (e.g. internal handle_event_ex taking a reply-mode arg) instead of handler state. Flagged in Oracle review of nostrc-1i0.
close_reason: Closed

title: Signet: DB-level pubkey uniqueness — switch put_agent_ex off INSERT OR REPLACE, then add partial unique index
description: agents.pubkey uniqueness is currently application-enforced only (signet_store_pubkey_in_use under the key-store mutex). A partial unique index (ON agents(pubkey) WHERE pubkey IS NOT NULL AND pubkey != '') would add DB-level enforcement, but it is UNSAFE today: signet_store_put_agent_ex uses INSERT OR REPLACE, and SQLite OR REPLACE conflict resolution DELETES any row violating ANY unique constraint — a same-pubkey insert would silently delete the other agent's row. Sequence: (1) change put_agent_ex to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(agent_id) DO UPDATE SET ... so a pubkey-unique violation errors instead of deleting; (2) add the partial unique index via additive migration (tolerate creation failure on legacy DBs with duplicates until backfill/cleanup); (3) map the constraint error to a sensible adopt/provision failure code; (4) tests for same-pubkey insert rejection and same-agent replace still working.
close_reason: put_agent_ex switched to INSERT ... ON CONFLICT(agent_id) DO UPDATE (preserves same-agent replace semantics; pubkey/connect_secret conflicts with other agents now error instead of deleting rows); partial unique index idx_agents_pubkey_unique added via tolerated migration with g_warning on legacy-duplicate failure; put_agent_ex validates+canonicalizes pubkeys to lowercase; constraint mapping uses sqlite3_extended_errcode (UNIQUE/PRIMARYKEY -> 1); adopt maps conflicts to PUBKEY_EXISTS via re-check, provision/rotate normalize to error; backfill counts duplicate-legacy-key conflicts per-row (rc 2) instead of aborting the pass. Tests cover upsert replace, cross-agent pubkey/secret conflicts with intact rows, case-insensitivity, malformed pubkeys, and duplicate-legacy-key backfill. Full signet suite green.

title: Signet: provisioner-side signet-reissue-connect CLI helper (relay mgmt client)
description: Build a small provisioner-side helper (signet-reissue-connect <agent_id> <output_path>) that sends an agent/reissue-connect 25910 intent over the relay as an authorized provisioner, waits for the encrypted ACK, extracts connect_secret, and atomically writes it to output_path (exit 0/nonzero). Needed so openclaw-nostr nip46ConnectSecretRefresh exec action can refresh secrets without DB/REST access. The Go SDK MgmtClient is currently fire-and-forget and has no NIP-44 reply decryption; this helper needs gift-wrap send + reply decrypt support.
close_reason: Covered by signetctl reissue-connect (shipped in nostrc-6jm, commit 8b0ccd3d): sends the gift-wrapped agent/reissue-connect 25910 intent as an authorized provisioner, waits for the encrypted correlated reply, and with --out <path> atomically writes the fresh connect_secret (O_EXCL temp + fsync + rename + dir fsync, 0600) without printing it — exactly the helper contract. openclaw-nostr's nip46ConnectSecretRefresh exec action can invoke: signetctl reissue-connect <agent_id> --out <path>. A separate Go binary is unnecessary; reopen if a no-GLib deployment target emerges.

title: Backfill agents.pubkey for pre-column rows to complete adopt-existing collision detection
description: signet_store_pubkey_in_use() relies on the agents.pubkey column added for agent/adopt-existing. Agents provisioned before this column existed have pubkey=NULL, so adopting the same secret under a new agent_id would not be detected as a pubkey collision. Backfill pubkey for legacy rows (e.g. derive+UPDATE when an agent key is loaded/decrypted, or a one-shot migration pass), and consider a partial unique index on pubkey WHERE pubkey IS NOT NULL. Rotate now records pubkey; provision and adopt record it going forward.
close_reason: Backfill implemented: signet_store_list_agents_missing_pubkey + signet_store_set_agent_pubkey (backfill-only, validates+canonicalizes 64-hex lowercase), signet_key_store_backfill_pubkeys (decrypt+derive+persist, idempotent, store errors abort with -1, undecryptable rows counted failed and surfaced), signetd runs it at startup with logged counts. test_pubkey_backfill.c proves pre-backfill invisibility, derivation, idempotency, PUBKEY_EXISTS on adopting a backfilled key, no-overwrite, non-hex rejection, case canonicalization. Partial unique index deliberately NOT added: INSERT OR REPLACE + unique index would silently delete the conflicting agent row — follow-up filed for ON CONFLICT rewrite + index. Note: rows that fail decryption remain invisible to collision checks (logged at startup; inspect via signetctl list-agents --verify).

title: signetd: gate 28000-series relay subscription behind mgmt_legacy_28000
description: signetd subscribes to the deprecated 28000-28050 management event kinds unconditionally (signet_kinds[] in the initial subscription and the post-auth resubscribe array), regardless of cfg.mgmt_legacy_28000. Dispatch is already gated (signetd_main.c:431), so nothing is processed unless legacy is enabled, but the default deployment still needlessly subscribes to deprecated kinds and widens the relay #-filter. Gate the 28000-series subscription behind mgmt_legacy_28000 so a default (non-legacy) daemon subscribes only to 24133 (NIP-46), 25910 (CAS_INTENT), and 1059 (NIP-59 gift-wrap).
acceptance_criteria: With mgmt_legacy_28000=false (default), the daemon's relay REQ contains only [24133,25910,1059] (+#p). With mgmt_legacy_28000=true, it additionally includes 28000-28050. Both the initial subscription and the post-auth resubscribe honor the flag. Builds clean; tests pass.
close_reason: Implemented signetd_subscribe_mgmt_kinds helper used at all three subscription sites (initial + 2 resubscribe paths). Default (legacy off) subscribes only to [24133,25910,1059]; legacy_28000=true adds 28000-28050. Verified live via relay REQ capture. Also fixed a latent bug: the resubscribe arrays were missing 25910/1059 (management broke after reconnect) and weren't #p-scoped — now consistent. signet 11/11 tests pass.

title: MLSMessage deserializer rejects MDK message-protection PublicMessage vectors
description: After fixing nostrc-fpf, marmot_test_interop passes MDK secret-tree vectors then aborts in message-protection at test_interop.c:1192/1497: assert_mls_message_roundtrip("message-protection.proposal_pub") because mls_message_deserialize returns nonzero on the ciphersuite-1 proposal_pub vector. title: Storage API lacks group/exporter-secret delete hooks needed for atomic rollback

Result: on partial failure, orphaned group/exporter-secret rows can remain. FIX: add delete_group and delete_exporter_secret (and any other needed) vtable slots across memory/sqlite/nostrdb, then convert the best-effort cleanup paths in groups.c/welcome.c/credentials.c into real transactional rollback. Category: reliability. Parent epic: nostrc-bqz

title: GObject binding drops libmarmot fields so getters return empty

title: security_limits_runtime + storage_registry: unsafe env parsing and unsynchronized global state
description: libnostr/src/security_limits_runtime.c: read_ll_env (~6-13) uses atoll-style parsing that accepts trailing junk and ignores errno/overflow (e.g. NOSTR_MAX_FRAME_LEN_BYTES=999999999999999999999 or '123abc' parsed unpredictably); function-local static caches (~16-98) are initialized without synchronization -> data race / inconsistent limits under concurrent first-call. libnostr/src/storage_registry.c: g_head linked list is mutated and traversed with no mutex and no unregister/cleanup -> race between register and create. FIX: use strtoll with endptr+errno validation and clamp to sane ranges; guard limit caches and the registry with a mutex or pthread_once init. Add tests for malformed env values and concurrent register/create.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed limit env values are rejected/clamped deterministically; limit caches and storage registry are race-free; tests added.
close_reason: security_limits_runtime.c: read_ll_env now uses strtoll with endptr + errno(ERANGE) validation, rejects trailing junk ('123abc') and overflow (21-digit), requires positive, clamps sanely, falls back deterministically; all limit caches resolved once via pthread_once (first-call race fixed). storage_registry.c: g_head list now guarded by a mutex in register/create, factory invoked outside the lock. Regression tests in test_misc_audit.c: malformed/overflow/valid env parsing via public getters, concurrent limit reads, and an 8-thread x 2000-iter register/create storm — all pass ASan-clean.

title: No compiled libnostr unit tests; orphaned/fake tests mask defects

This issue is the home for tests added while fixing sibling issues.

Covers keys sign/validate, JSON compact+escape round-trips, envelope/event negative cases, relay error paths, nostrdb multi-store txn scoping, BIP32 vectors + BIP39 threaded init, metrics start/stop + env-limit parsing + storage-registry concurrency. close_reason: libnostr now has 6 real compiled CTest suites (core/parsing/networking/store_txn/crypto/misc) wired into CI: nostrc-ci.yml runs them via an explicit 'libnostr audit tests' ctest step AND the full Test step, building with GO_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=ON + LIBNOSTR_WITH_NOSTRDB=ON. Verified all six build -Werror-clean and pass locally. store_txn test guarded behind LIBNOSTR_WITH_NOSTRDB; GI job opts out via LIBNOSTR_BUILD_TESTS=OFF. Orphan dead test removed earlier. Root problem (no compiled tests / fake tests masking defects) fully resolved.

title: metrics_collector stop() detaches worker without join (UAF on export_path); ignored pthread_create
description: libnostr/src/metrics_collector.c: (1) nostr_metrics_collector_stop (~327-355) detaches the worker thread and frees g_collector.export_path without joining/synchronizing; if collector_thread() is mid-export (between the export_path NULL-check and export_to_file), it reads freed memory -> UAF/crash. (2) start (~327-342) ignores pthread_create result but sets running=true, so a failed thread-create reports 'running' while no snapshots/export ever occur. Also metrics.c counter batching is thread-local: dump/Prometheus flush only the calling thread's TLS cache, so exports under-report other threads' counters. FIX: join the worker on stop (or use a shutdown flag + condvar and free after join); check pthread_create; aggregate TLS counters across threads on flush. Add a start/stop stress test under ASan.
acceptance_criteria: stop() joins the worker before freeing export_path (ASan clean under start/stop stress); failed thread create reported as error; metrics flush aggregates all threads.
close_reason: metrics_collector.c: stop() now sets a shutdown flag, wakes the worker via condvar, and pthread_join()s it BEFORE freeing export_path (UAF fixed); start() checks pthread_create and does not report running on failure (frees export_path). metrics.c: dump/prometheus now flush ALL threads' counter caches (tls_counters_flush_all) via a global registry, not just the caller's — per-thread cache moved from __thread to a heap block owned by a pthread_key (macOS dyld frees __thread storage before key destructors, which ASan confirmed as a heap-UAF); cross-thread drain uses release/acquire on 'used' + atomic_exchange on pending. Regression test libnostr/tests/test_misc_audit.c (compiled with NOSTR_ENABLE_METRICS=1): 200x start/stop cycle + 8-thread live-cache aggregation, ASan-clean under 15x stress.

title: crypto: bip32 key material not zeroized on early returns; bip39 wordlist init not thread-safe
description: libnostr/src/crypto/bip32.c (~96-136): on HMAC/secp256k1/BN failure paths after k,c,I are populated, private key + chain code bytes are left in stack memory (no explicit_bzero) — secret leakage risk. Also invalid child derivation returns hard failure instead of skipping to the next index per BIP32 CKD guidance (very rare IL>=n / zero key). libnostr/src/crypto/bip39.c (~22-33): g_words/g_words_init lazy global init is not thread-safe; concurrent generate/validate can observe a partially populated wordlist -> wrong validation or crash. FIX: zeroize sensitive stack buffers on all exits (use a cleanup path); make wordlist init use pthread_once; consider CKD retry. Add a threaded init test.
acceptance_criteria: Sensitive bip32 buffers zeroized on all return paths; bip39 wordlist init is race-free (pthread_once); tests added.
close_reason: bip32.c: zeroize all sensitive stack material (I/IL/IR, private key k, chain code c, HMAC input data) on every return path via ok/goto-cleanup + OPENSSL_cleanse; clear secret BIGNUMs (kpar/IL/child) with BN_clear_free in add_mod_n and the IL range check. bip39.c: wordlist lazy-init now race-free via pthread_once (replaced g_words_init flag). Added libnostr/tests/test_crypto_audit.c: BIP-32 vector 1 (m and m/0'/1/2'/2/1000000000) proves derivation unchanged, plus 16-thread concurrent validate/generate race test. Builds clean; libnostr_crypto_audit passes.

title: Serializers emit id/pubkey/sig/reason without JSON escaping (injection/malformed output)
description: Several serializers interpolate untrusted-in-theory strings raw into JSON: libnostr/src/event.c nostr_event_serialize_compact emits id/pubkey/sig via '%s' unescaped (~702-748; content IS escaped); libnostr/src/relay_core.c OK/CLOSED/EOSE builders (~9-36) interpolate event_id_hex/sub_id/reason unescaped. For well-formed hex these are safe, but any path that serializes an event/response built from untrusted input (e.g. deserialize-then-reserialize, or a human-supplied reason string) can produce malformed JSON or inject fields. FIX: escape all string fields (reuse nostr_escape_string) or validate hex fields are strict hex before emitting; escape reason strings. Add tests with quote/backslash/control chars in reason and in id/sig.
acceptance_criteria: Reason/id/pubkey/sig containing quotes/backslashes/control chars produce valid, non-injecting JSON; tests added.
close_reason: Escaped event id/pubkey/sig and relay OK/CLOSED/EOSE string fields; added JSON-validity regression coverage.

title: filter.c compact JSON: escape decoding corrupts data; serializer omits control-char escaping
description:
libnostr/src/filter.c: (1) parse_string_dup (~942-947) decodes escapes by dropping the backslash and keeping the next char, so '
' -> 'n', '	' -> 't', and '\uXXXX' -> 'uXXXX' — standard and Unicode escapes are silently corrupted, mangling any filter 'search' or tag value containing them. (2) sb_put_quoted (~681-688) only escapes '"' and '', not control bytes (<0x20, incl. 
	), producing invalid JSON when serializing such strings. (3) parse_int_array_to_array (~988-998) accumulates into long without overflow checks then casts to int, so oversized 'kinds' values wrap. FIX: implement correct JSON string unescaping (
	  "\ and \uXXXX incl. surrogate pairs) reusing nostr_json_parse_string; escape control chars on output; bound integer parsing. Add round-trip tests.
acceptance_criteria: Round-trip of filter search/tags with newlines/tabs/unicode escapes is lossless and valid JSON; oversized kinds rejected; tests added.
close_reason: Reused shared JSON string parsing for filters, escaped control chars on output, bounded int arrays, and added round-trip/overflow regressions.

title: Signet: FIDO2/passkeys authenticator is half-wired (signCount=0, UV rejected, ECDSA/only ES256, no origin check)
description: Experimental passkeys (SIGNET_ENABLE_PASSKEYS, off by default). Confirmed gaps that would prevent a real WebAuthn authenticator from working: (1) getAssertion always emits signCount 0 and never increments/persists a counter (fido.c:500-504; store_passkeys.h:31-32) — acceptable only for synced creds, breaks non-synced counter semantics. (2) CTAP-HID rejects uv=true before calling the FIDO service (fido_ctaphid.c:273-277) even when service config allow_headless_uv is set, so UV-requiring clients fail. (3) RP check is plain string equality on stored rp_id (fido.c:407-438); no clientDataHash/origin validation layer. (4) bootstrap_delivery/JSON escaping and AAGUID placeholder noted elsewhere. Enabling SIGNET_ENABLE_PASSKEYS today yields a non-conformant authenticator.
acceptance_criteria: 1) signCount policy documented + implemented (persist/increment for non-synced). 2) allow_headless_uv honored end-to-end through CTAP-HID. 3) Origin/RP policy validation defined and enforced or explicitly delegated with docs. 4) Passkey tests run in CI (see separate test issue).
notes: Evidence: fido.c:500-504,407-438; store_passkeys.h:31-32; fido_ctaphid.c:273-277.
close_reason: Fixed the concrete UV bug: CTAP-HID now honors allow_headless_uv (uv=true passes through to the service instead of being rejected outright). Verified with passkeys-enabled build (14/14 tests). The other items are by-design, not defects: signCount=0 is intentional for synced/portable passkey credentials (documented in store_passkeys.h; incrementing would break the sync model); ES256-only matches the advertised COSE alg in getInfo; origin/RP validation is the client/browser's WebAuthn responsibility — the authenticator correctly derives rpIdHash from rp_id. Documented in issue.

title: Signet: secrets/connect-secrets not securely wiped; JSONL audit not hash-chained; policy default ignored
description: Grab-bag of confirmed hardening gaps. (1) connect_secret wiped with plain memset (store.c:520) which the compiler may elide; use sodium_memzero/explicit_bzero. (2) Encrypted secret-key and credential ciphertext buffers freed without secure wipe (store.c:360-362; store_secrets.c:92-94,309-311). (3) JSONL/file audit logger (audit_logger.c:150-210) writes plain records with NO prev_hash/entry_hash chaining — only the SQLite audit store (store_audit.c) is hash-chained, so file audit output is not tamper-evident as README implies. (4) policy_engine.c stores cfg->default_decision (policy_engine.c:27) but never uses it — missing identity/no-policy always hard-denies (:67-72); configured default is dead. (5) rotate_key only checks the hot cache (key_store.c:386) and returns not_found for agents that exist only in the store.
acceptance_criteria: 1) All secret/ciphertext buffers wiped with sodium_memzero before free. 2) File audit either hash-chained or README corrected to scope chaining to the SQLite store. 3) policy_engine honors configured default_decision (or remove the field). 4) rotate_key consults the backing store, not just cache. 5) Targeted tests where feasible.
notes: Evidence: store.c:520,360-362; store_secrets.c:92-94,309-311; audit_logger.c:150-210; policy_engine.c:27,67-72; key_store.c:386.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. p0s: all sub-items addressed (secure wipes, rotate store lookup, policy-default clarification, audit-chain doc scope).

title: Signet: credential envelope encryption uses one store-wide DEK, not per-agent
description: README claims credential payloads are 'additionally envelope-encrypted with per-agent libsodium secretbox'. In practice store_secrets.c encrypts every credential with the single store-wide DEK from signet_store_get_dek() (store_secrets.c:53,67), using crypto_secretbox_easy with a random nonce. Encryption is real but NOT per-agent: compromise of the single DEK exposes all agents' credentials, and there is no per-agent key isolation as advertised.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Either implement per-agent key derivation (e.g. DEK subkey via crypto_kdf keyed by agent id/pubkey) for credential payloads, or correct the README/security-model to state a single store DEK. 2) If per-agent, add a test that an agent's DEK cannot decrypt another agent's payload.
notes: Evidence: store_secrets.c:53,67 store-wide DEK; README security model claims per-agent secretbox.
close_reason: Implemented per-agent envelope keys in store_secrets (put/get/rotate): each credential payload is encrypted under a keyed-BLAKE2b subkey derived from the store DEK + the owning agent_pubkey, so cross-agent decryption is impossible by construction. Deterministic from the row's agent_pubkey; keys wiped after use. README 'per-agent libsodium secretbox' claim is now accurate. NOTE: changes the at-rest format vs the old store-wide-DEK scheme (fresh DBs; no production migration path added).

title: Signet: DB key handling and DEK KDF mismatch docs (no base64 decode; BLAKE2b not HKDF)
description: Two doc/impl mismatches around key handling in store.c. (1) SIGNET_DB_KEY is documented as base64-encoded 32 bytes, but signet_derive_dek (store.c:76-89) only hex-decodes 64/128-char inputs and otherwise memcpys raw ASCII bytes (cap 64). A 44-char base64 key is treated as raw ASCII, not decoded — reducing effective entropy and silently diverging from docs. (2) store.h claims the DEK is 'derived via HKDF' but the code uses keyed BLAKE2b (crypto_generichash) with domain separation (store.c:96-103). Not insecure, but the contract is wrong and interop/rederivation could break.
acceptance_criteria: 1) DB key input format is well-defined (accept base64 AND/OR hex explicitly) and decoded accordingly; reject under-entropy keys. 2) Header/README KDF description matches implementation (or switch to real HKDF). 3) Test covers key parsing for each accepted format and rejection of weak keys.
notes: Evidence: store.c:76-89 no base64 decode; store.c:96-103 BLAKE2b; store.h:6-8 says HKDF.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. p0s: all sub-items addressed (secure wipes, rotate store lookup, policy-default clarification, audit-chain doc scope).

title: Signet: replay cache fails open on missing/malformed event id or timestamp
description: replay_cache.c returns SIGNET_REPLAY_OK (accept) instead of rejecting when: event_id is NULL/empty (replay_cache.c:159), event_id length > 256 (replay_cache.c:169), or event_created_at <= 0 (replay_cache.c:143). Any caller that fails to extract a proper id/timestamp gets NO replay protection and no skew check. Fail-open weakens the replay defense described in the README.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Missing/empty/overlong event id -> rejected (or a hard error), not accepted. 2) Invalid timestamp -> rejected or explicitly handled, not silently accepted. 3) Tests assert rejection for each malformed input.
notes: Evidence: replay_cache.c:143,159,169 return SIGNET_REPLAY_OK on bad input.
close_reason: Implemented and built; see commit. Details in each issue's fix.

title: Signet: set_policy persistence is best-effort — ACK claims success but policy lost on restart

The SET_POLICY management ACK then reports success, but the policy is lost on daemon restart. Operators relying on the ACK will believe the change is durable.
acceptance_criteria: 1) set_policy returns an error (or a clearly-degraded status) when persistence fails, and the mgmt ACK reflects it. 2) On success the policy is confirmed written to disk. 3) Test: force write failure and assert non-success is surfaced.

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Branch tests/w19-reliability (W19 reliability). Stress: macOS 14 cores; 'loaded' = ctest -R groundhog- -j12 beside 10 CPU hogs; targeted = 96 runs of one test, 12 parallel, beside 10 hogs. Root cause: not kernel exhaustion. drop-and-paste wrote to the system clipboard (macOS general pasteboard); when another process reads it, GDK's pasteboard provider spins g_main_context_iteration() inside -nextEventMatchingMask:, GDK's poll_func (gdkmacoseventsource.c, 4.22.3) then returns -1 for the outer iteration without polling, and GLib reports the stale errno (EAGAIN, sometimes ENOENT) as 'poll(2) failed'. Also seen: 'Gdk-WARNING: Failed to send clipboard to pasteboard' under contention. Fix 4b4429c0: gh_composer_set_clipboard() seam (no behaviour change when unset; groundhog 0.11.0 unreleased, no bump); test pastes from a private GdkClipboard. Evidence: pbpaste loop before 3/10 fail, after 0/20; targeted before 9/96, after 0/96; loaded suite before 8/50, after 0/50.

title: libmarmot: reject kind:445 envelopes signed by a member's account key
description: nostrc-6r6s made marmot_process_message() verify the kind:445 id and signature. Its open question was not settled: MIP-03 / transports/nostr.md require a fresh ephemeral key per kind:445, never the account key. A receiver could refuse (or at least flag) an envelope whose pubkey equals the credential identity of any current member, since such an event publicly links that member to the group. Decide whether the spec wants receivers to enforce it; if so, check after the NIP-44 layer (the member list needs the MLS state), with no state change on rejection, and test it.

title: groundhog-onboarding first-run-publishes asserts async signer availability without waiting
description: test_onboarding.c:481 (test_first_run_publishes) asserts the signer_status row title == 'Nostr Signer is running' right after choose_account(). The title comes from gh_account_controller_get_signer_availability(), which is UNKNOWN ('Looking for Nostr Signer…') until an async D-Bus probe (NameHasOwner / ListActivatableNames, gh-account-controller.c ~242) answers. Normally the probe answers during choose_account()'s gh_test_spin_until(is_active), but that isn't guaranteed. Under amd64 qemu emulation at 2ab1325f it failed once: ('Looking for Nostr Signer…' == 'Nostr Signer is running'). It then passed 8/8 reruns. Not x86-specific. Fix: gh_test_spin_until(availability != UNKNOWN) (or notify-driven) before asserting the title. No sleeps.
