title: libnostr: the client SSL_CTX hardening in websocket_callback never runs
description: Found while fixing nostrc-0d0d. libwebsockets calls LWS_CALLBACK_OPENSSL_LOAD_EXTRA_CLIENT_VERIFY_CERTS once per vhost from lws_tls_client_create_vhost_context() with a zeroed fake wsi (lib/tls/tls-client.c, lws 4.3/4.5), so lws_get_opaque_user_data() is NULL and websocket_callback returns at its 'if (!conn) return 0' guard before the switch. The case that sets TLS1.2 minimum, AEAD-only ciphers, X25519:P-256 groups, SSL_OP_NO_COMPRESSION|NO_RENEGOTIATION and SSL_SESS_CACHE_SERVER (libnostr/src/connection.c) is dead code: libnostr's client TLS runs on lws/OpenSSL defaults. Decide which of those settings are still wanted (e.g. a fixed groups list would drop OpenSSL 3.5's X25519MLKEM768 default), then apply them where they take effect: handle the reason before the conn guard, or use lws_context_creation_info (client_ssl_cipher_list, client_tls_1_3_plus_cipher_list, ssl_client_options_set). Test with a ClientHello fixture like tests/test_connection_tls_no_resumption.c.

title: Groundhog attachments: refuse downloads whose public name resolves to a private address
description: W17 review #3 fix (branch groundhog/w17b-media-cache): GhBlossomClient refuses a sender's download URL whose host is a literal loopback/private/link-local/CGNAT/ULA/multicast address, a single-label or localhost/.local/.lan/.internal/.home.arpa name, or a non-canonical numeric form, and any URL that is not <origin>/<x>[.ext]. Not caught: a public DNS name that resolves to a private address (DNS rebinding) in System or No Proxy mode (Tor resolves at the exit, which refuses private addresses). Fix: in GhNetHttp, for attachment downloads, check the connected peer address at G_SOCKET_CLIENT_CONNECTED (the message's network-event, where gh_net_tls_no_resumption already hooks) and abort the request when it is not public; test with a resolver fake (as test-groundhog-net records lookups) mapping a public-looking name to 127.0.0.1. Also note: URLs that do not end in the blob's sha256 (NIP-96-style, e.g. some nostr.build links) are now refused; decide whether to accept them for kind 15 from other clients.

title: Groundhog onboarding: guard build still says 'through Tor' (W17 review #5)
description: docs/reviews/groundhog-w17-review-2026-09-29.md non-blocking #5. gh-onboarding-view.c sync_check_note() picks the Tor copy ('Checking connects to the ticked relays through Tor...') from the network-mode setting alone. In a build without G09 (GROUNDHOG_WITHOUT_TOR / GROUNDHOG_HAVE_RELAY_GUARD) the relay guard connects to nothing in Tor mode, so the note is false (the per-relay results do show the guard's reason, gh-inbox-setup.c). The onboarding view is its own library (groundhog-onboarding), built without the executable's GROUNDHOG_HAVE_TOR, so the fix needs the build fact passed in: a GhOnboardingConfig field (e.g. tor_available, set by gh-app-services.c from GH_FEATURE_TOR / gh_relay_guard_mode_allowed), new copy for Tor-without-Tor ('Groundhog won't connect to relays while the network setting is Tor, which this version doesn't have'), and a test_onboarding case for both builds. W16 addendum note 2 asked nostrc-dod2 for this; dod2 was closed as a duplicate of nostrc-6v0i, which did not touch onboarding.

title: libnostr: nostr_event_sign leaves the private key and keypair on the stack
description: W17b re-review N-b: nostr_event_sign() (libnostr/src/event.c, ~703-785) decodes the hex key into privkey_bin and builds a secp256k1 keypair on the stack without wiping them. libmarmot's marmot_sign_ephemeral() wipes its own copies, but the ephemeral key survives in libnostr's frame (and likewise account keys signed through this path). Wipe privkey_bin and the keypair (secure_wipe) on every return path; same for nostr_event_sign_secure if it copies.

title: libmarmot: classify Commits as privileged by proposal set, not by state difference
description: W17 review N4: marmot_commit_authorize() derives privileged/ordinary from the pre/post state difference (members or extensions changed). Legacy MIP-03 allows non-admins only self-update and SelfRemove-only Commits; the adopted spec defines privileged by the authorization rule. A non-admin Commit carrying e.g. PSK proposals with a path is accepted by libmarmot but rejected by MDK. Classify from the Commit's proposal types (and keep the state checks).

title: Groundhog on libadwaita 1.5: a dialog closed within two frames of presenting never closes
description: libadwaita 1.5 (Ubuntu 24.04; Groundhog's minimum, CMake libadwaita-1>=1.5) opens an AdwDialog's sheet two frame-clock ticks after it maps (adw-dialog.c map_tick_cb). adw_dialog_close()/force_close() before then calls adw_floating_sheet_set_open(FALSE) on a sheet that is already closed, a no-op; the tick then opens it and it stays, and 'closed' never fires. Later libadwaita (1.9) handles a never-opened sheet (has_been_open) and map_tick_cb bails when force_closing. nostrc-qp24.88 fixed the tests (tests/ui/gh-test-dialog.h). Product exposure: GhConversationInfoDialog::on_model_changed (src/ui/gh-conversation-info-dialog.c) detaches and force-closes when its room leaves the model; if that happens within ~2 frames of opening Info (account switch, block/forget elsewhere) the detached dialog stays open on 1.5. Not reachable by user input timing; decide whether to defer the close until the content maps on libadwaita < the fixing version, or raise the minimum.

title: Groundhog: kind-15 interop test against an independent client's upload
description: qp24.11 asks for interop with an independent client. G21 (nostrc-qp24.39) covers the cipher with an independent AES-256-GCM vector (Node/Go, 16-byte nonce, what Amethyst/0xchat upload; tests/media/test_media.c interop-vector) and parses hex key/nonce as Amethyst, 0xchat and gnostr write them. Still missing: a captured kind-15 rumor plus ciphertext produced by a real independent client (e.g. Amethyst or 0xchat export, or nostr-share --private) checked in as a fixture and opened end to end (tags, size semantics: some clients put the plaintext size in size, Groundhog writes the ciphertext size; both fit the min(size, cap)+1 KiB download bound), and the reverse: a Groundhog upload opened by that client.

AT-7 is tested dynamically (no GET until download; test-groundhog-blossom, test-groundhog-privacy-e2e, conversation-view file-message). Add a static tests/check_privacy.py rule (with a --self-test mutation fixture) that allows those calls only in src/media/ and the G22 attachment card's activation handler (src/ui/gh-attachment-card.c), so no future receive, render, notification or prefetch path can download on its own.

title: Groundhog: signer approval UX for room sends (2 per recipient + self-copy)
description: NIP-17 room sends (W17, nostrc-qp24.78) need a NIP-44 encryption and a seal signature per recipient plus the self-copy: up to 22 signer operations for a 10-person room, and a signer that prompts per operation asks that many times. title: Groundhog: S4 random order and spacing for room retries and republishes
description: W17 (nostrc-qp24.78) implements charter §4.5 S4 (a room's per-recipient wraps in random order, U(0,3) s apart) through outbox_events.not_before at T-seal. Later retry rounds, a manual Retry and republishes after a restart start every due recipient wrap at once, in stored order, so a relay on several recipients' lists can see them back to back. The direct GhDmSender path (gh_dm_sender_send_room, used outside the outbox) never spaces them. Apply a fresh random order and spacing per round, in-memory per round rather than rewriting not_before, and cover it on the fake clock like /groundhog/multi-send/wire/spacing.

title: libnostr: COUNT serializer conflates NIP-45 request and response
description: Found while auditing nostr_envelope_serialize_compact() for nostrc-ptwq. The COUNT branch always writes {"count":N} and then any filters, so a client request serializes as ["COUNT","sid",{"count":0},{filter}...]; NIP-45 requests are ["COUNT",sid,filter...] and only relay answers carry {"count":N}. It round-trips through libnostr's own parser (which detects the count object), but a relay may read {"count":0} as a filter. libnostr's subscription.c builds its COUNT request by hand, so only direct callers of the envelope serializer are affected (none in-tree today). Decide how the envelope distinguishes request from answer (e.g. omit the count object when filters are present), keeping the ABI, and extend tests/test_envelope.c. PATCH or MINOR per AGENTS.md.

title: libgo: blocking channel waiters can miss wakeups with GO_CHANNEL_REFINED_SIGNALING=OFF (stale was_empty/was_full snapshots)
description: Found while fixing nostrc-75rv (MPMC slot protocol). With the default GO_CHANNEL_REFINED_SIGNALING=ON every send/receive signals cond_empty/cond_full, so this is latent. With it OFF, lock-free try_send/try_receive broadcast only when was_empty/was_full, computed from in/out loads taken before their CAS. Those snapshots can be stale against concurrent lock-free peers: e.g. a sender loads tail=k-1 (one element present), a lock-free receiver takes k-1, a blocking go_channel_receive then waits on cond_empty with in==out, and the sender's CAS/publish of ticket k computes was_empty=false and skips the broadcast, leaving the blocking receiver asleep with data available (symmetrically for blocking senders on cond_full). select waiters are unaffected (always signalled). Fix options: signal unconditionally in MPMC mode, or recompute emptiness under chan->mutex relative to the published ticket. Add a test that builds with REFINED_SIGNALING=0 and mixes lock-free senders with blocking receivers.
notes: Widened per the nostrc-75rv review (F5). Besides the lock-free try paths' pre-CAS snapshots (mpmc_push occ_before uses a tail loaded before the CAS), the blocking paths compute was_empty/was_full as (chan->in - chan->out) -- two loads in unspecified order, taken before the transfer -- in go_channel_send, go_channel_receive and go_channel_receive_with_context (search for '(chan->in - chan->out) == 0' / '== chan->capacity'). A concurrent lock-free receive can make the difference wrap, so the flags read false. With REFINED_SIGNALING=ON (default) they only feed metrics and ARM SEV; with OFF they gate the broadcasts. Fix: take go_channel_occupancy() (out-first loads) after the transfer, or signal unconditionally in MPMC mode. Note the BUSY waits added in the review follow-up (mpmc_wait_busy) use a 1 ms deadline precisely so they cannot hang on a skipped broadcast in the OFF configuration.

title: nostr_testing mock relay REQ path crashes in binaries that load json-glib (json_object_iter_next clash)
description: Found while writing the nostrc-qp24.10.6 regression test. Testing/src/mock_relay_server.c (static lib nostr_testing, jansson) uses json_object_foreach in filter_matches_event_json. In an executable that also links json-glib (e.g. via nostr_gobject), the jansson macro's json_object_iter_next call binds to json-glib's same-named symbol (macOS: link order puts libjson-glib before libjansson), aborting with 'Json-CRITICAL: json_object_iter_next: assertion iter_real->object != NULL failed' on the first REQ. test_relay_connect never sends a REQ so it does not hit it. title: nostr-gobject GNostrSubscription leaks its background context, core subscription and filters
description: Found by the Groundhog ASAN/UBSAN (detect_leaks=1) job (nostrc-qp24.15.2). gnostr_subscription_new() (nostr-gobject/src/nostr_subscription.c) creates a go_context_background() for nostr_relay_prepare_subscription() and never releases it; gnostr_subscription_finalize() hands the core NostrSubscription to nostr_subscription_free_async() and abandons it (a detached thread that may not have run by exit) and drops owned_filters without freeing them (its comment accepts the leak). nostr_subscription_close() also leaks the result channel of its CLOSE write (nostr_relay_write), and nostr_subscription_dispatch_closed() one allocation per CLOSED. Every GNostrSubscription Groundhog's gnostr scope transport closes and unrefs leaks this way. gnome/groundhog/tests/lsan.supp suppresses exactly these allocation sites; remove each suppression as it is fixed (unref the background context after prepare, free filters after the async cleanup, free the write result).

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: Also: libnostr write_operations() (relay.c:842/847) leaks the Error it sends into a write's answer channel, and connection.c:1300's queued WebSocketMessage, when the writer's caller or the connection is gone first. title: GhAccountRelays never applies GhAuthPolicy OWN_LIST_DISCOVERY (ephemeral AUTH)
description: Found by the G24 privacy harness. gh-auth-policy.h documents OWN_LIST_DISCOVERY -> EPHEMERAL with GhAccountRelays as its caller, but gh-account-relays.c never calls gh_auth_policy_apply(): its discovery REQs authenticate with nothing (NONE). Privacy-safe (charter 4.3 allows 'none, or ephemeral'), but on a discovery relay that requires NIP-42 AUTH for reads the account's own kind-10050/10002 are CLOSED auth-required, the lists stay unknown and the inbox never subscribes, while the contact directory (CONTACT_DIRECTORY, ephemeral) works on the same relay. Either apply the policy's EPHEMERAL identity per discovery URL (and add an NT-1 row) or change the policy table to NONE for this purpose. The harness keeps an open discovery relay beside an AUTH-gated one so own-list discovery works.

title: Groundhog: conversation row context menu Mute…/Info/Delete… via GhConversationActions
description: Charter §7.4 row context menu (Pin, Mute…, Mark as Read/Unread, Info, Delete…) and the conversation header menu (§7.4 conversation_menu) can reuse G19's src/app/gh-conversation-actions.{c,h} (store + notifier withdraw) and win.conversation-info. Not done in G19 to keep gh-conversation-row/gh-conversation-view edits minimal while W13c/G13 edit them.
close_reason: Implemented and integrated on master (W16, Groundhog 0.9.0); reviewed docs/reviews/groundhog-w16-review-2026-09-29.md + addenda APPROVED; Groundhog/EOSE/MLS 84/84 locally.

comments.text: Hosted Linux/Xvfb CI (run 36554068900) fails this item's GUI test; fix tracked in nostrc-qp24.88 (P0).

title: Groundhog: per-contact block for multi-party NIP-17 rooms (contacts.blocked)
description: G19's block is per room (conversations.request_state = BLOCKED), which covers a 1:1 DM completely. A blocked person can still reach the account in a new multi-party NIP-17 room (a different participant set) or a new request. The schema's contacts.blocked column is unused. Decide (with G18 Requests 'Block') whether blocking a person also records contacts.blocked and makes T-admit hide/notify-suppress their messages in any room; add tests (NO-2).

title: Groundhog forget: test key-before-unlink order and explain quit during a forget (W13b non-blocking 4b/4c)
description: W13b review non-blocking #4: (b) ST-8 asserts the end state, not that the key item goes before the unlink; FakeSecret could record whether store.db still existed when the item was deleted. (c) Ctrl+Q stays available while Preferences is locked for a forget; quitting abandons it (at best after the key step), and the next start shows KEY_MISSING without explanation. 4a (toast, in-memory key step) was done in W13c.

title: Groundhog: replying in a room with unloaded unread history marks that history read
description: W13c keeps unloaded unread messages unread when a room is opened (gh_conversation_mark_read reads only listed messages; W13b review B1). An own message still moves the durable read marker to itself (T-admit, gh-store-conversations.c; 'replying implies having read what came before'), so replying in a room with more than a page of unloaded unread history marks those unread too. The view opens at the top and lists one older page first, so this needs >100 unread in one room. Decide whether an own message should stop at the floor (keep unread_older) or whether the reply semantic stands; either way test it on the executable wiring (tests/app/test_account_store.c --gui).

title: groundhog-onboarding first-run-publishes flakes under parallel ctest load
description: Seen once in W13c (macOS, ctest -j6 over groundhog-*): tests/ui/test_onboarding.c:474 asserted the signer status row title 'Nostr Signer is running' while it still read 'Looking for Nostr Signer…'. Passes alone and 10/10 with --repeat. Likely the test reads the row before the signer probe settles; it should wait on the status instead of asserting once.

title: Groundhog sidebar header: title truncated ('Grou...') and account button shows a missing icon
description: Composer screenshots (G13, macOS, 960px): the sidebar AdwWindowTitle 'Groundhog' ellipsizes to 'Grou...' with account subtitle, and the account button next to search renders the missing-image glyph (icon not in Adwaita/hicolor on this host). Bundle the symbolic icon in the gresource (like send-symbolic) or use one guaranteed by adwaita-icon-theme; give the header title room (hide the redundant app name when an account subtitle exists, or move account into the menu).
close_reason: Implemented and integrated on master (W16, Groundhog 0.9.0); reviewed docs/reviews/groundhog-w16-review-2026-09-29.md + addenda APPROVED; Groundhog/EOSE/MLS 84/84 locally.

title: Contact directory: contact's 10002 write relays as lookup sources
description: Charter §4.3 allows a contact's own kind-10002 write relays as additional contact-directory sources. G10 asks discovery-relays only. Cache the contact's 10002 in the directory table (kind 10002 row) and add its write relays (bounded, never the account's own relays; lookup-sources rule) to background refreshes.

title: GhAccountRelays own-list discovery: ask GhAuthPolicy (OWN_LIST_DISCOVERY)
description: The policy assigns OWN_LIST_DISCOVERY = EPHEMERAL (lazy, only when a relay demands AUTH); gh-account-relays.c still leaves its discovery-relays REQ at NONE, so an AUTH-gated discovery relay refuses it. Route its scope URLs through gh_auth_policy_apply_scope().

comments.author: Biz
comments.text: G24 privacy harness evidence: with a discovery relay that requires NIP-42 AUTH for every REQ, GhAccountRelays' own-list REQ is CLOSED auth-required (never signed, as NONE), so the account's 10050 stays unknown and GhDmInbox never subscribes; GhContactDirectory authenticates ephemerally on the same relay and works. tests/privacy/test_privacy_e2e.c therefore pairs an open discovery relay (E) with the AUTH-gated one (G); once this lands, PT-4 can assert an ephemeral own-list AUTH on G too.

title: Groundhog notifications: freedesktop backend body markup at preview level
description: GhNotifier sets the preview body as plain text (line breaks collapsed, controls dropped, <=120 graphemes). GNOME uses GLib's GTK backend (no markup). Outside GNOME/portals, GLib's freedesktop backend passes the body to Notify, and servers advertising body-markup may interpret // from a sender's text. Decide whether to escape (and how that renders on GTK/portal backends) or detect the backend; only affects the non-default preview level.

title: Groundhog metainfo: 'messages are not kept after it closes' is wrong since G04 (encrypted store keeps them)
description: data/org.nostr.Groundhog.metainfo.xml:9 still says messages are not kept after Groundhog closes. With G04 the encrypted store keeps them; only a build without SQLCipher/libsecret or 'Continue Without Saving Messages' is memory-only (and re-fetches from relays on restart since the W13 B1 fix, nostrc-qp24.60). Update the description with the next release notes/version bump.
close_reason: Already fixed by 47f3cb68 (gschema run-in-background text; metainfo no longer says messages aren't kept); verified in W16 polish.

title: Refresh local/groundhog-ci:24.04 image with sqlcipher and blueprint-compiler
description: The local Docker image local/groundhog-ci:24.04 predates the Groundhog store: it lacks libsqlcipher-dev, blueprint-compiler, gnome-keyring and desktop-file-utils, which .github/workflows/groundhog-ci.yml installs. In it the store, account store, groundhog-background and groundhog-blueprint targets are silently disabled. G15 verification used a derived local/groundhog-ci:24.04-g15 with those packages added.

title: Groundhog gschema: run-in-background description still says Reserved
description: G15 (76097c1f) made run-in-background live (hold on window close, autostart for a confirmed choice), but data/org.nostr.Groundhog.gschema.xml still describes it as 'Reserved; not used yet.' Only G01 edits the gschema in this wave, so G15 left it. Update the description (e.g. 'Keep receiving messages after the window is closed; when you confirm it, also start at login.').
close_reason: Already fixed by 47f3cb68 (gschema run-in-background text; metainfo no longer says messages aren't kept); verified in W16 polish.

title: Outbox: prune stored signed wraps 7 days after settle (charter §3.3)
description: Charter §3.3 says outbox_events.event_json is NULLed 7 days after the message settles. G06 keeps the signed wraps (ciphertext only) until the message is purged or deleted; nothing prunes them after SETTLED. Add a store primitive (or extend T-purge, G07) that NULLs event_json for events of SETTLED entries whose last target attempt is older than 7 days, and make the outbox never republish an event without JSON (it already skips them).
acceptance_criteria: Settled entries older than 7 days carry no event_json; unsettled ones keep theirs; store test covers the cutoff.

title: Groundhog store mode: rumor refused by GhStore bounds is retried (signer prompt) every session
description: Found during G05 (nostrc-qp24.22). In store mode, gh-store-conversations.c delegate_admit passes the verified rumor to gh_store_admit, which rejects text that is not valid UTF-8 or exceeds GH_STORE_MAX_* (title is already cut to GH_STORE_MAX_TITLE). If GhMessage/libnostr ever accept such a rumor (e.g. invalid UTF-8 in content passing the JSON parser), admission fails with GH_STORE_ERROR_INVALID -> GH_CONVERSATION_ADD_FAILED -> GhDmInbox defers it and holds the checkpoint, so every later session unwraps it again (1-2 signer approvals) and never advances past it. Fix: treat GH_STORE_ERROR_INVALID from gh_store_admit as a final verdict (record the wrap id in seen ns GH_STORE_SEEN_REJECTED_WRAP, count it rejected), or validate UTF-8 in gh_message_new_from_rumor. Needs a reproducer first (does libnostr's parser pass invalid UTF-8?).

title: GhSigner closes a private D-Bus connection per signer call: transient GLib EBADF warning on macOS
description: gnome/groundhog/src/identity/gh-signer.c revokes a pending approval by g_dbus_connection_close() on the operation's private sender connection (cancel_pending, and after every reply). On macOS GLib polls with select(); closing a connection whose worker still has a read source attached makes the next select() fail with EBADF and GLib logs 'poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor' (transient: the cancelled read source is dispatched and removed on the next iteration; Linux poll() reports POLLNVAL silently). In tests the warning was fatal (~1/100 groundhog-dm-inbox bounded-concurrency runs under load). W13's tests/common/nostrc-test-bus now forgives up to 64 of exactly that warning on macOS, so tests no longer abort. In production it only prints a warning. Options: accept and document; report upstream to GLib (gdbusprivate close path vs select-based g_poll); or revoke without closing while a read is pending. Test-only change was made; no production change yet.
notes: docs/reviews/groundhog-w13-review-2026-09-28.md non-blocking 9: GhSigner per-call private connection close logs a non-fatal EBADF poll warning on macOS in production; consider reusing a connection per operation batch.

title: groundhog-relay-publish-wire: auth/ephemeral-two-relays wait_for_count times out (0 == 1) under parallel ctest on macOS
description: Seen once in 4 runs of 'ctest -R "groundhog-|gnostr-test-signer-nip55l-identity|gnostr-test-nwc-wallet-agent" -j8 --repeat until-fail:5' on macOS during W13 (D-Bus test reliability): /groundhog/relay-publish-wire/auth/ephemeral-two-relays failed at gnome/groundhog/tests/relay/wire-relay.h:290 wait_for_count: assertion failed (*counter == count): (0 == 1) after its 18 s deadline; tests 1-5 had passed. No D-Bus is involved (local libsoup WebSocket relays), so it is not the GTestDBus/EBADF issue fixed in W13. Related to the groundhog-relay-wire flake noted in nostrc-qp24.8.5. Next: reproduce with repeated -j8 runs under CPU load, find whether the expected frame never arrives (real bug in the NIP-42 AUTH path from d12fcc89) or the wait misses a wakeup, and make the wait event-driven.

title: groundhog-store-key KC-4 libsecret case times out under parallel ctest on macOS
description: On macOS (Homebrew GLib 2.90), ctest -j4 -R 'groundhog-store|marmot' failed groundhog-store-key with a 30 s timeout: /store-key-libsecret/kc4-unavailable aborted with 'GLib-FATAL-WARNING: poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor' and left its GTestDBus dbus-daemon orphaned. The same test passes alone (0.13 s) and in a serial run. Seen at baseline 24587ad4 before any G23 change (found while verifying nostrc-qp24.41). Likely a GTestDBus/fd interaction with concurrently running fork-based crash-harness tests or a GLib 2.90 poll change; CI (Linux, serial ctest) is unaffected. Reproduce: build with BUILD_GROUNDHOG=ON, run ctest -j4 -R 'groundhog-store'.

title: libmarmot: linkable, parameterized storage contract suite
description: libmarmot/tests/test_storage_contract.c keeps its 25 cases static beside its own main(), and test_snapshot_lifecycle asserts MARMOT_ERR_UNSUPPORTED for every backend, so an external MarmotStorage (Groundhog's GhStoreMarmot, G23 / nostrc-qp24.41, which implements real snapshots) cannot run the upstream cases and carries a faithful port instead (gnome/groundhog/tests/store/test_store_marmot.c). Split the cases into a small test library, e.g. tests/storage_contract.{c,h} with marmot_storage_contract_run(name, storage, opts{persistent, snapshots_supported}), keep libmarmot's own runner on it, and switch GhStoreMarmot's test to it. Also fix marmot-storage.h: find_key_packages_by_pubkey says 'Find active key packages' but the memory, SQLite and nostrdb backends all return every package of the owner (GhStoreMarmot follows the backends). Version: test-only split is no bump; the header comment fix is a doc change (assess per AGENTS.md).

title: DM inbox: a permanently failed or AUTH-declined inbox relay holds the checkpoint forever
description: The inbox checkpoint advances only when every own 10050 relay is at EOSE and fully paged. A relay that is down for good, or whose sign-in the user declined (GH_DM_INBOX_RELAY_AUTH_REQUIRED, remembered per generation by GhAccountAuth), keeps the checkpoint where it was, so every later session's since window grows and eventually hits the paging bound. Decide the policy (e.g. exclude a relay after N sessions of failure or after an explicit decline, per charter §4.5, and surface it in Relay Status), then implement it.

title: Relay scope: follow-up REQ on the same connection (inbox paging without reconnect and re-AUTH)
description: GhDmInbox (nostrc-qp24.10.10) pages a truncated relay backwards with a fresh one-shot GhRelayScope per page, because a scope's filters are fixed and src/relay has no follow-up-REQ API. Each page is a new connection, and on an AUTH-gated own inbox relay a new NIP-42 AUTH signature (GhAccountAuth re-signs after an approval; a signer that prompts per signature prompts per page, up to GH_DM_INBOX_MAX_PAGES). Add a scope/transport operation that issues another REQ (new filters, same URL) on an existing authenticated connection, and switch the inbox pages to it.

title: GhStore: message search index migration (FTS5 missing in Ubuntu SQLCipher 4.5.6)
description: Charter §3.3 lists an optional messages_fts (FTS5) table. G02 left it out of schema v1 because Ubuntu 24.04 libsqlcipher 4.5.6 is built without FTS5 (Homebrew 4.17 has it; both have FTS3/FTS4). When search is designed, add it as schema migration v2: FTS4, or FTS5 behind a compile-option check, with triggers kept in sync on purge and forget, which must delete index rows too.

title: GhStore: prepared-statement cache for the admission/backfill hot path
description: gh_store_admit/enqueue/seal and seen_insert prepare and finalize about 5 statements per call. A backfill of thousands of gift wraps pays the parse/plan cost each time. Add a small per-GhStore statement cache (reset and clear bindings after use, finalized in close) once G05 measures admission throughput. Performance only; no behaviour change.

title: GhStore: quick_check on every open scales with store size
description: G02 runs PRAGMA quick_check on every file-backed open, as charter §3.5 requires. With SQLCipher every page is decrypted and HMAC-verified, so startup and account-switch cost grows with store size (including the planned 200 MiB media cache). Measure on a large store, then decide: keep it, run it in the background after open, or do a full check only periodically. Keep STORE_CORRUPT detection either way. gh-store.c store_initialize().

title: GhDmInbox: expose why it is in ERROR (local failure vs every relay failed)
description: gh-inbox-status.c (G11) tells an inbox ERROR caused by every inbox relay failing (banner 'Can't reach your message relays') from a local failure (seen-set/filter; sidebar error page) by whether the inbox has relay URLs (gh_dm_inbox_get_relays). A filter-build failure after the URLs are set would read as 'unreachable'. Expose a reason (enum or a relays-failed flag) from GhDmInbox and use it in gh_inbox_status_map().

title: GhStoreKey: real-service tests for interactive unlock and keyring-creation prompts
description: G03's KC-6 (tests/store/test_store_key_keyring.c) covers store/lookup/delete, isolation, malformed items and the locked keyring in background mode against a real gnome-keyring, but the INTERACTIVE paths that make the service prompt (SECRET_SEARCH_UNLOCK on locked items, secret_service_unlock of the default collection after an empty search, secret_service_store prompting to unlock/create the default keyring, prompt dismissal -> LOCKED) are only exercised through the in-process FakeSecret. Add a scripted prompter on the private test bus (e.g. gcr's mock prompter / org.gnome.keyring.SystemPrompter replacement answering accept/dismiss) and assert: accepted unlock returns the key, dismissed unlock returns GH_STORE_KEY_ERROR_LOCKED without hanging, and interactive first open with no default keyring creates one.

title: check_privacy: extend §7.2 enforcement (CSS variables, denylist refresh)
description: G01 blueprint-denylist covers classes after Adw 1.5/GTK 4.14 as of libadwaita 1.9 / GTK 4.22 headers (hand-maintained list in tests/check_privacy.py). Follow-ups: (1) §7.2 also requires named colors (@accent_bg_color) instead of CSS variables var(--accent-bg-color) (Adw 1.6) in data/style.css; add a rule plus mutation fixture. (2) When hosts ship libadwaita 1.10+/GTK 4.24+, add their new classes (or derive the list from ADW_AVAILABLE_IN_*/GDK_AVAILABLE_IN_* when headers are present, keeping the pinned list as fallback). Needs a follow-up edit to G01's allowlist per charter §8.4.

title: GNostrRelay: plain reads of atomic state; disconnect() emits on the calling thread
description: nostr-gobject/src/nostr_relay.c after nostrc-qp24.4.5: gnostr_relay_get_state/get_connected/publish/connect_async/authenticate and the property getters read self->state plainly while worker threads store it atomically (mixed access). gnostr_relay_disconnect() emits state-changed synchronously on whatever thread calls it (Groundhog publish owner threads do) and writes emitted_state there, racing the default-context idle. Pre-existing semantics; make reads atomic and route disconnect emission through the main context (keeping the barrier).

title: Groundhog tests: aborted GTestDBus runs leak orphan dbus-daemon processes
description: When test-groundhog-account aborts on a failed g_assert (e.g. a mutation check of gh-nip17-inbox.c), the GTestDBus private bus daemon is not torn down and is reparented to launchd/init (ppid 1). Observed ~10 orphan 'dbus-daemon --config-file=.../g-test-dbus-*' processes on the dev box, and a piped test run hung because the orphan kept stdout open. Consider g_test_dbus teardown via an atexit/abort handler, or running the bus via dbus-run-session in the CTest command.

title: Groundhog UI: explicit focus target per status page; cross-check app id in gh-window.blp
description: W11 Blueprint review findings 3-4: account-ui focus now targets whatever child an AdwStatusPage has (implicit contract; a spinner or button box child would focus oddly) — name the focus widget explicitly per page. gh-window.blp hard-codes icon-name org.nostr.Groundhog; check_data.py should cross-check it against the app id.
acceptance_criteria: Focus target is an explicit, tested per-page widget; check_data.py fails if gh-window.blp icon-name/app id diverges.
close_reason: Superseded per charter §8.5 by nostrc-qp24.29

title: groundhog-account / groundhog-relay-wire flaky under parallel ctest -j8 on macOS
description: Seen while verifying nostrc-qp24.8.3 (Blueprint migration; neither test touches changed code): full 'ctest -j8 --timeout 300' on macOS failed groundhog-relay-wire once and groundhog-account (30s TIMEOUT) on a second run. Both pass 5/5 with --repeat until-fail:5 and the full serial suite passes 289/289. groundhog-account normally takes ~4s serially, so a 30s timeout under -j8 suggests a timing-sensitive wait (worker thread / GSettings memory backend / local relay) starved under CPU contention. Reproduce with repeated full -j8 runs, find the starved wait, and make it event-driven or give it a load-tolerant deadline.
notes: Likely root cause found in G03 follow-up 2e9daf7e: on macOS, GDBus closing a connection while the worker's control-message read source is attached makes GLib's select() fail with EBADF, which g_test_init makes fatal ('poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor'); the GTestDBus dbus-daemon inherits ctest's pipe and is never killed on macOS, so ctest reports a 30 s timeout and the daemon is orphaned. Fix pattern: hold one session-bus connection for the test's lifetime (avoid repeated connect/close) and supervise daemons with a lifeline pipe.
close_reason: Fixed in 07f7b445: groundhog-account's failures were EBADF aborts (GTestDBus teardown closes; now nostrc-test-bus) plus starved spin_until waits (GTask drops its source ref on the worker thread after queueing the callback; waits now re-check on a 10 ms tick). account 50/50 + 200/200 x2 under 14 hogs, 8 concurrent. Separate relay-wire flake: nostrc-5ztr.

title: nostrc CI ASAN runs with detect_leaks=0, hiding libmarmot leaks
description: .github/workflows/nostrc-ci.yml sets ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 on Linux and macOS, so LeakSanitizer never runs. libmarmot's Commit processor leaked the staged group clone on every rejected Commit (76 leaks / 27152 bytes in test_mls_group per macOS leaks(1)) until 7f99ca5f, and CI could not see it. Enable detect_leaks=1 at least for the marmot_test_* CTests on Linux (LSan is unsupported on macOS arm64; leaks(1) --atExit works there), triaging any remaining leaks rather than suppressing them.

title: libmarmot cannot emit by-reference Commits; mls_commit_serialize ignores is_ref
description: mls_commit_serialize() always writes ProposalOrRef type 1 and serializes proposal bodies inline, even when MlsProposal.is_ref is set, so a deserialized by-reference Commit does not round-trip and libmarmot has no committer path for proposals received by reference (needed for W2a admins committing members' AppDataUpdate/Update/Remove proposals, parent nostrc-qp24.5.1). The W10 regression (7f99ca5f) had to build its Add-by-ref Commit from exported primitives in the test. Either reject is_ref in the serializer or emit type 2 + ProposalRef, and add a committer API that takes stored proposal messages; keep adopted producer OFF until the adopted admission gates pass.

title: libmarmot CMake marmot.pc Requires is incomplete
description: libmarmot/marmot.pc.in declares Requires: libsodium openssl only, but libmarmot links libsecp256k1, libnostr and nostr_nip44_core (and optionally sqlite3/lmdb); a static libmarmot.a installed via CMake cannot be linked from its .pc. Meson's generated libmarmot.pc (1a085500) already lists libsecp256k1 and Requires.private nostr/libnostrgo/sqlite3/lmdb. Align the CMake template (Requires.private / Libs.private), gated on the nip44 install bead. Version: PATCH (pkg-config contract).

title: libnostr nostr.pc omits libnostrgo and static link dependencies
description: libnostr/libnostr.pc.in: Libs is only -lnostr and Requires is only GLib (when NOSTR_WITH_GLIB). Public <nostr-tag.h> includes libnostrgo's string_array.h and libnostr's tag code calls string_array_* from libnostrgo, and a static libnostr.a also needs libwebsockets, OpenSSL, secp256k1 (and nsync via libnostrgo). pkg-config consumers must currently add libnostrgo themselves (libmarmot/meson.build does, 1a085500). Add Requires(.private): libnostrgo and the static Libs.private/Requires.private closure. Also note the installed prefix is configure-time (CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX), so cmake --install --prefix yields a non-relocatable .pc.

title: nips/nip44 installs headers only: no nostr_nip44_core library or pkg-config file
description: nips/nip44/CMakeLists.txt only installs include/nostr/nip44 headers; nostr_nip44_core (a static library libmarmot links unconditionally) is never installed and there is no .pc. Installed-mode consumers therefore cannot link NIP-44: libmarmot's standalone Meson default (pkg-config) path now stops at configure with an explicit error (1a085500), and an installed static libmarmot cannot be linked. Add an install(TARGETS nostr_nip44_core ...) rule and a pkg-config file (e.g. nostr-nip44.pc Requires: nostr), then switch libmarmot/meson.build pkg-config mode to it. Verified via staged cmake --install of libnostr/libgo/nips/nip44 to /tmp: copying libnostr_nip44_core.a next to libnostr was the only missing piece for libmarmot Meson 20/20.

title: nips/nip29: group-id charset and equal-timestamp replacement lag the NIP-29/NIP-01 spec
description:
Found while building Groundhog's NIP-29 core (nostrc-qp24.12.1), which reuses nostr_group_t merges.
1) group_id_is_valid() (nips/nip29/src/nip29.c:21) restricts ids to [a-z0-9-_]. NIP-29 dropped that rule on 2026-05-20 (nostr-protocol/nips 175ad951: 'remove poorly-thought group identifier recommendation'); ids are now 'a random string of any length'. naddr parsing, nostr_group_address_is_valid and every merge helper reject otherwise valid groups. The legacy host'id form legitimately keeps the charset.
2) nostr_group_merge_in_*_event reject only created_at < last_*_update, so equal-timestamp snapshots replace each other by arrival order instead of NIP-01's lowest-id rule. Groundhog enforces the tie-break above the helper; Gnostr's nip29-groups plugin does not. Fixing it in the library needs per-kind id tracking (public nostr_group_t layout change -> assess version impact).
Acceptance: regression tests for a mixed-case/extended id via naddr and the merges, and for equal-timestamp order independence; Groundhog can then drop its charset restriction (GH_NIP29_ERROR_INVALID_GROUP_ID).

title: Groundhog GTestDBus tests leak dbus-daemon on macOS after an assertion abort
description: When test-groundhog-account aborts on a failed assertion on macOS, the GTestDBus watcher and dbus-daemon children outlive the test. They hold the stdout pipe (ctest reports Timeout instead of the failure) and leave orphaned dbus-daemon processes; several from earlier sessions were still running on 2026-09-27. Consider a teardown or at-exit hook that calls g_test_dbus_down/kills the daemon, or run the bus fixture per-subprocess.
notes: Likely root cause found in G03 follow-up 2e9daf7e: on macOS, GDBus closing a connection while the worker's control-message read source is attached makes GLib's select() fail with EBADF, which g_test_init makes fatal ('poll(2) failed due to: Bad file descriptor'); the GTestDBus dbus-daemon inherits ctest's pipe and is never killed on macOS, so ctest reports a 30 s timeout and the daemon is orphaned. Fix pattern: hold one session-bus connection for the test's lifetime (avoid repeated connect/close) and supervise daemons with a lifeline pipe.
close_reason: Fixed in 07f7b445: Groundhog GTestDBus tests moved to tests/common/nostrc-test-bus (lifeline-supervised daemons, logs off ctest's pipes). macOS: 293 mid-run SIGKILL/SIGABRT kills, Linux: 100 SIGKILLs (60 with gnome-keyring), 0 daemons/dirs left.

title: Groundhog relay transports call gnostr_relay_disconnect (joins workers) on the owning thread
description: Both gh-relay-gnostr.c (scope) and gh-relay-publish-gnostr.c (publisher) call gnostr_relay_disconnect() from close on the owning (UI) context. nostr_relay_close() closes channels then go_wait_group_wait()s for worker goroutines, and the publisher closes a connection on every terminal outcome, so a slow lws teardown can stall the main loop. Measure; if material, dispatch disconnect to a GTask worker holding a GNostrRelay ref (handlers are already disconnected). Found during nostrc-qp24.4.4.
close_reason: Superseded per charter §8.5 by nostrc-qp24.27

title: Make pre-push gate worktree-safe and validate Groundhog
description: W5 review F7: effective Beads hook now chains scripts/pre-push in all worktrees, but the script requires _build, destroys it, masks configure failure via a pipeline, builds default options only (excluding Groundhog), and tests the working tree rather than necessarily the pushed commit. Tighten the gate without disabling Beads integration or weakening build/test requirements.
acceptance_criteria: Push gate uses an isolated clean build directory for the exact candidate checkout, fails on configure/build/test errors, includes Groundhog when relevant, and works from a fresh worktree while preserving existing build artifacts.
notes:
W7 reviewed hook fix integrated locally as 1db000b6 (worktree commit 23dc3e4c): tracked Beads hook captures/refeeds push stdin; scripts/pre-push validates exact candidate in isolated temp worktree, preserves caller _build, rejects empty input/configure/build/test/zero CTest; Groundhog opt-in selected for direct/shared dependency paths. scripts/test-install-hooks.sh and scripts/test-pre-push.sh pass locally, installer idempotent; independent review addendum APPROVED final commit after earlier REQUEST CHANGES. Developer tooling only, no component bump. Leave open until an actual push runs this new active gate and succeeds.
2026-09-27 real active-hook proof: git push origin master of 995cd8dd ran tracked Beads input replay, validated exact refs/heads/master candidate in isolated /tmp checkout, initialized required submodules, selected BUILD_GROUNDHOG=OFF for hook/docs-only diff, completed clean build and 347/347 registered CTests (one pre-existing NIP-5F skip), and pushed 82707261..995cd8dd. Main _build preserved, temporary checkout removed, main HEAD matches origin/master and status clean. Focused installer/pre-push tests and independent final APPROVED review passed. No component bump: developer tooling only.
close_reason: Tracked Beads hook and verifier now replay Git ref input, validate exact candidate in isolated worktree, fail on empty refs/zero tests/configure/build/CTest; tests and independent review pass; real push 995cd8dd completed clean build and 347/347 CTests without touching main _build.

title: Guard Groundhog focus changes during active editing
description: W5 review F6: gh-account-ui update grabs focus on every actual account-state page transition. A later signer/network transition could steal focus from an editable composer once messaging UI exists. Keep state announcements but avoid focus theft when window is inactive or focus is in an editable widget.
acceptance_criteria: GTK test covers active editor and inactive window: state change announces appropriately without stealing focus; action-button focus remains available for genuine empty/error transitions; real GNOME keyboard/screen-reader smoke recorded.
notes: Absorbed by G13 (nostrc-qp24.31): gh-account-ui.c never moves focus out of a mapped editable (GtkEditable/GtkTextView: search field, composer); on a mapped window it decides in an idle after the transition settles (a conversation that left with the account has taken the composer off screen), defers the move for an inactive window until activation, and announces only to an active window (charter §7.14). Tests: groundhog-composer /focus-guard (typing in composer across a no-op refresh, typing in search across an account-page transition, genuine transition moves focus to the page action when active) and groundhog-account-ui. Remaining for acceptance: the real GNOME keyboard/Orca smoke (UX-10).

title: nostr-gtk tests do not build with BUILD_APPS=OFF (gnostr-widget-test-support lives under apps/gnostr)
description: With -DBUILD_APPS=OFF and nostr-gtk on (the lab configuration; Debian avoids it via BUILD_NOSTR_GTK=OFF), five nostr-gtk tests fail to build: test_note_card_measure.c includes <nostr-gobject-1.0/gnostr-identity.h> without nostr-gobject's include dir, and test_nostr_gtk_{bind_latency_budget,widget_churn_leaks,thread_view_bounded,listview_recycle_stress} link -lgnostr-widget-test-support which is only built under apps/gnostr. Fix: gate nostr-gtk tests on the support target existing (if(TARGET gnostr-widget-test-support)) or move the support lib into nostr-gtk/tests; add nostr_gobject's include dir to test_note_card_measure. Pre-existing: no nostr-gtk commits since 55bb44e5; observed on aarch64 lab fresh clone of e3e41b7b (all 107 wave ctests pass otherwise).

title: lws_context_destroy closes fd 0 with plugin-enabled libwebsockets: testing/ mock relay, relayd, grelay, test fixtures
description: Found fixing nostrc-jc2o. An lws built with LWS_WITH_PLUGINS (Homebrew 4.5.8; any build with libwebsockets-test-server plugins installed) always loads its test-server plugin dir and mounts every plugin on its internal 'system' vhost (VH_INSTANTIATE_ALL_PROTOCOLS, no pvo) - not configurable via plugin_dirs / pvo / EXPLICIT_VHOSTS. The demo plugin lws_raw_test close()s a zero-initialised fifo fd on PROTOCOL_DESTROY when it got no fifo-path pvo -> every lws_context_destroy() closes the process's fd 0. libnostr's client context no longer gets destroyed (930bedc2), but these still do: Testing/src/mock_relay_server.c (nostr_mock_server_stop -> fd 0 gone for the rest of a test process; seen at the end of nostr-gobject test_relay_connect), apps/relayd/src/relay_server.c, apps/grelay/src/grelay_main.c, libnostr/tests/test_subscription_dispatch.c, tests/test_connection_idle_writable.c. Daemons: only at shutdown (low impact) unless they restart the server in-process. Options: keep one context per process in the mock server; or reserve fd 0 (open /dev/null onto fd 0 at startup when closed) in test harnesses; report upstream to warmcat (raw_test fifo init should be -1 / system vhost should not instantiate plugins).

title: test_syncd_broker_seed_drop writes porthome-status.json into the real user's ~/.local/state
description: tests/integration/test_syncd_broker_seed_drop.c spawns nostr-home-syncd --check with NOSTR_HOMED_SYNCD_HOME/STATE_DIR overridden but HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME/XDG_CACHE_HOME left as the caller's, so the status writer, pin ring and cache dir resolve to the real user's dirs (on the lab that is the live syncd's ~/.local/state/nostr-homed/porthome-status.json). Switch it to tests/integration/nh_syncd_spawn.h (added by nostrc-5y2t), which sandboxes HOME + XDG dirs.

title: nostr-home-syncd: snapshot state lives as a full jansson tree (hundreds of MB for a 200k-entry home)
description: Follow-up from nostrc-5y2t (worker O). The loader now stream-parses snapshot.json (no raw copy), but nh_syncd_state keeps the whole document as a live jansson object for the daemon's lifetime: a 220k-entry / 71 MB snapshot costs ~360 MB RSS in test_syncd_state on aarch64, and the lab's 64 MB snapshot sets the daemon's baseline MemoryPeak (see 5y2t report). Options: compact per-entry struct + hash table built from a streaming parse; binary/sqlite state; or at least intern chunk address strings. Keep the on-disk schema v1 readable.

title: nostr-share: offer a BUD-02 delete of a blob a failed public attempt uploaded before switching to private
description: Since nostrc-k95e the dialog refuses to switch a share to Private (NIP-17) when a failed public attempt already uploaded a file unencrypted (NsFile.uploaded): the blob is public on that Blossom server. The error tells the user to delete it there, but gives no way to. Offer (dialog + CLI hint) a BUD-02 DELETE of that sha256, authorised through org.nostr.Signer, with a clear 'best effort: the server or mirrors may keep copies' warning, then allow the switch. From the k95e Oracle review (P0 item: refusal is necessary but strands the blob).

title: session relay: per-connection 'cache write, do not federate' marker on relay.sock
description: Remaining half of nostrc-elgy (wJ implemented the author pre-check: no outbox row / fsync for events provably not by a local account, and hint-only writes without fsync). Still unsolved without the writer telling us: (1) a gift wrap an app caches from the user's own inbox relays (p = the user) is re-sent to the user's 10050 relays (answered duplicate:, a liveness hint) because it cannot be told apart from the user's outbound self-copy; (2) the user's OWN old events an app syncs from remote relays into the session cache are re-queued and re-published upstream. Design sketch: the client declares intent on the WebSocket upgrade (e.g. GET /?federate=0 or path /cache) -> relay_server.c reads WSI_TOKEN_GET_URI at LWS_CALLBACK_ESTABLISHED into ConnState; protocol_nip01 passes it to storage -- not through NostrStorage.put_event (no context parameter): either store cache-connection events via the ingest path (the tee's ingest bypasses federation; it would then need to record relay-list hints itself) or add an optional after-store hook to NostrRelayServerConfig carrying per-connection info. Needs a consumer (gnostr caching, nostr-dav sync) to agree on the spelling; add a ws_test_client variant that upgrades with the marker. Owner: apps/relayd + first caching client.
notes: After the elgy review (81a224d6) the no-outbox-row path applies only when federation_accounts is set; with signer-learned accounts (the default) every cached foreign event still costs one durable row + fsync until clients can mark cache writes. That is now part of this bead's scope.

title: gnostr: NIP-17 kind-15 decryption-key/nonce read as base64; other clients (and nostr-share --private) write hex
description: apps/gnostr/src/util/dm_files.c encodes and decodes the kind-15 decryption-key / decryption-nonce tags as base64. Amethyst / 0xchat and nostr-share --private (nostrc-k95e, gnome/nostr-share/src/ns-private.c) use lower-case hex (64 / 24 chars). A hex key given to gnostr's from_base64() decodes to 48 bytes and the file cannot be opened; a gnostr-sent file cannot be opened by the others. Suggested: accept both on read (64-hex -> 32 bytes, else base64), write hex.
close_reason: Merged to master in 5d8d9c1c (worker P, fix/gnostr-kind15-signer-service); tests verified by orchestrator (worker died at report step on usage cap).

title: session relay: superseded / cancelled outbox events emit no UpstreamStatusChanged
description: Found by wJ (nostrc-jedb test). README rule 6 says UpstreamStatusChanged fires on every transition, but nsr_outbox_supersede() and nsr_outbox_cancel_ref() (called from route_one for a newer replaceable version / a NIP-09 kind 5) settle events without an observer call, so a publisher following an event id never sees 'superseded' / 'cancelled' (GetEventUpstream does report it). Fix: have both return the affected ids (or take a callback) and notify(f, id, '', 'cancelled', detail, state) per event; add to test_session_federation (retarget test currently checks rl1 via the outbox).

title: gnostr-test-nip46-e2e fails on master: nostr_nip46_session_get_secret() does not return the connect-URI secret (2/23)
description: Seen by wave-4 worker L on macOS at 1e9e5d01 + L's commits (none of which touch nips/nip46 or apps/gnostr/tests/test_nip46_e2e.c; the test links only nostr_nip46_core + libnostr). ctest -L gnostr: 51/52 pass; gnostr-test-nip46-e2e reports 21/23 with 'FAIL: secret mismatch' (test_nip46_e2e.c:288, expects nostr_nip46_session_get_secret()=='sec' after parsing a bunker:// URI with secret=sec) and 'FAIL: secret not updated' (:790, a second connect with secret2 should replace it). Either the nip46 client stopped storing the URI secret (recent nips/nip46 changes: 3e824501 nostrc-8hc9, 19f2ead8 nostrc-pvha, bb67bee9 nostrc-zcll.7) or the test is stale. Owner: nips/nip46.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (worker N, branch fix/libs-nip59-relay-nip46): not a nip46 regression — the gnostr test is stale. C1 hardening (6cf770b9 nostrc-ot2c.2 / 42355dcd) split the bunker/nostrconnect URI secret= into the session's connect_token (nostr_nip46_session_get_connect_token) and made nostr_nip46_session_get_secret() return the client's 64-hex TRANSPORT private key (generated for client sessions). This is documented in nip46_types.h and pinned by nips/nip46/tests/test_client_connect.c (asserts get_secret != 'sec'), homed's test_broker_login_nip46*, and relied on by apps/gnostr/src/ui/gnostr-login.c:1360 (persists get_secret as the transport key). Making get_secret return the URI token would store an attacker-chosen string as a key. FIX (apps/gnostr, P's area, so not committed by N): in apps/gnostr/tests/test_nip46_e2e.c replace nostr_nip46_session_get_secret -> nostr_nip46_session_get_connect_token at :286 (expects 'sec') and :787 (expects 'secret2'). Verified out-of-tree against unchanged nip46: 23/23 (unpatched 21/23), also under ASan. Patch: /tmp/wN/udsy/udsy.patch (2 hunks, 3+/2-).
close_reason: Fixed on master in 5056b438 (test used get_secret for the URI secret; now get_connect_token). 23/23 pass.

title: gnostr nip29-groups: migrate participation to a moved group and keep the user's kind:10009 in sync
description: Follow-up from nostrc-7n4t. The plugin now detects that a group's admins list it on another relay and offers 'Open There' (tracks relay'id; forks are separate groups). NIP-29 also says the client should offer, if the user wishes, to migrate their participation to the new relay, updating the current user's kind:10009 (NIP-51 simple groups). The plugin never reads or writes the user's 10009 at all (join/leave/track don't update it either) and has no untrack API. Needed: (1) gn_nip29_group_service_untrack_group(); (2) fetch the user's newest 10009 from their relays, change/add the ['group', id, relay, name] entry (keep all other tags and the possibly NIP-44-encrypted content untouched), sign and publish - and never publish when the current list could not be fetched (would clobber other clients' groups); (3) 'Move Here' in the relocation banner = track new + untrack old + 10009 update; (4) consider updating 10009 on join/leave too.

title: gnostr-signer Permissions page: 'Approval policy' radios and Orbot switch are unwired mock controls
description: apps/gnostr-signer/data/ui/page-permissions.blp shows 'Approve basic actions' / 'Manually approve each app' radio rows and a 'Connect through your Orbot setup' switch; page-permissions.c binds none of them, so they change nothing. The page now also lists the daemon's real grants (nostrc-yjky). Either wire them to real settings (the daemon has no 'basic actions' auto-approve concept; bunker has bunker-auto-approve-kinds) or remove them.

title: gnostr-signer-daemon: TCP IPC lane never decrements active_connections (lockout after max_connections)
description: apps/gnostr-signer/daemon/ipc.c tcp_ipc_accept_thread increments s->active_connections per accepted connection but nothing decrements it when the connection thread ends (the old nip5f_conn_thread ignored carg->ud; nip55l_nip5f_serve_unidentified has no close callback into ipc.c either). After NOSTR_SIGNER_MAX_CONNECTIONS (default 100) connections the accept loop only polls and never accepts again. Opt-in build (ENABLE_TCP_IPC). Fix: pass a close notification (e.g. a Nip5fServerHooks.close wrapper or a callback arg to nip55l_nip5f_serve_unidentified) that decrements and updates stats.

title: nostr-gobject: gnostr_relay_connect_async succeeds for a refused ws:// port; publish then waits for an OK that never comes
description: Found in nostrc-4gf4 (apps/gnostr/tests/test_plugin_publish_ack.c). gnostr_plugin_context_publish_event_to_relay_ack_async() to ws://127.0.0.1:1 (nothing listening): gnostr_relay_connect_async() completes with TRUE, gnostr_relay_publish() accepts the event (state reads CONNECTED), no state-changed to DISCONNECTED/ERROR is emitted, and only later the reconnect loop logs '[RECONNECT] Connection lost to ws://127.0.0.1:1'. Callers that wait for OK therefore report the failure only after their OK timeout (15 s) instead of at connect time. Expected: connect_async fails (or state goes to ERROR) when the TCP/WS handshake fails. Owner: nostr-gobject (nostr_relay.c connect_async_thread / libnostr connection).
close_reason: Merged to master in e011e74d (worker N, fix/libs-nip59-relay-nip46). Follow-ups: dcqz, k1ym (P2 mock-relay tests never run in Linux CI), hg1n.

title: nostr-gobject/libnostr: GNostrRelay teardown closes fd 0 asynchronously; after gnostr_relay_disconnect()+unref the next lws context fails (ZERO RANDOM FD, client SSL init)
description: Found while testing nostrc-4gf4 (apps/gnostr/tests/test_plugin_publish_ack.c, macOS, lws 4.5.8, in-process testing/ mock relay). Evidence: (1) In an early version the new plugin API called gnostr_relay_disconnect() and then dropped its last reference on the registry-shared GNostrRelay (gnostr_relay_new() returns the shared relay, nostrc-kw9r). After that one publish, fcntl(0, F_GETFD) went from 0 to -1: fd 0 (stdin) was closed. The next libwebsockets context then got fd 0 for /dev/urandom ('E: ZERO RANDOM FD'), 'lws_create_vhost: lws_context_init_client_ssl failed', every later connection failed ('error opening websocket'), and OpenSSL RAND_bytes in nostr_event_sign failed ('Failed to generate random bytes'). (2) Without the explicit disconnect (only unref, as ui/gnostr-main-window-publish.c does per its nostrc-pub1 comment) all rounds pass, yet fd 0 is still found closed a moment later: something on a background thread closes fd 0 after a connection's teardown (a zero-initialised fd being closed?). No direct close() exists in libnostr/libgo/nostr-gobject, so look at the lws teardown paths in libnostr/src/connection.c (lws_context_destroy) and at what the reconnect/teardown threads close. Impact: stdin is lost silently; and any code that disconnects a shared relay can make TLS/new connections fail process-wide. Fix: never close fd 0 unless owned; make disconnect+unref idempotent (single lws_context_destroy).
close_reason: Merged to master in e011e74d (worker N, fix/libs-nip59-relay-nip46). Follow-ups: dcqz, k1ym (P2 mock-relay tests never run in Linux CI), hg1n.

title: ASan workspace build: 31 pre-existing ctest failures outside relayd (libgo, libnostr, tests/, otel, nip46/nip55l)
description: Found by wJ while verifying nostrc-abk1 on aarch64 (GCC 13, GNOSTR_ENABLE_ASAN=ON, BUILD_APPS=OFF, WITH_NOSTRDB=ON, default ASAN_OPTIONS after abk1 removed the json_interface ODR abort). Full ctest: 31/193 fail, identical at baseline (1e9e5d01 libjson link + detect_odr_violation=0: 32, extra test_json_event_fuzzlite), so none are caused by abk1: GoContextCancelTest GoSelectCancelTest GoHashMapTest2 libnostr_networking_audit libnostr_subscription_dispatch libnostr_misc_audit test_nip46_signed_response_admission nip55l_dbus_contract test_otel_{producer,consumer,replay,roundtrip} test_nostr test_relay test_relay_shutdown test_pool_redial test_subscription_{lifecycle,backpressure,backpressure_long,blocking_depth} test_relay_unsubscribe test_connection_shutdown_order test_connection_idle_writable test_json_event test_json_envelope test_json_filter_fuzzlite test_event_canonical concurrency_subscription_shutdown{,_asan} profile_fetch_{simulation,stress}. Confirmed cause for the three test_json_* ones: LeakSanitizer only (pass with detect_leaks=0) -- tests/test_json_event.c make_event_with_tags() overwrites e->tags without freeing the tags nostr_event_new() allocated. Others not triaged (rerun with --output-on-failure). All 13 relayd ctests pass.

title: relayd on macOS: Unix-socket clients upgrade but frames never reach nostr_cb (Homebrew libwebsockets 4.5.8)
description: Found by wJ after nostrc-tvoi made apps/relayd build on macOS. With Homebrew libwebsockets 4.5.8 (plugins built in: lws-sshd-demo, raw-test, server-status log 'callback_lws_sshd_demo: Can't open ...', 'handler_server_protocol_init: requires upload-dir pvo'), nostr-session-relayd accepts relay.sock, answers the WebSocket upgrade (101), but REQ/EVENT frames get no reply: relayd_session_relay_ws, relayd_session_relay_storage and relayd_req_contract fail/time out on macOS while passing on Linux (lws 4.3.3). Same symptom class as nostrc-q9ba (adopted connection bound to a protocol other than nostr_cb). Look at relay_server.c context creation: disable plugin loading (info.plugin_dirs / LWS_SERVER_OPTION_...), make sure the adopted vhost's default protocol is 'nostr', and check lws_adopt_socket_vhost() on 4.5. Owner: apps/relayd.
notes: Reproduced on master 5056b438 (macOS, Homebrew lws 4.5.8): relayd_req_contract (Timeout), relayd_session_relay_ws, relayd_session_relay_storage fail; all other 84 wave-related ctests pass. Linux unaffected.

title: gnostr-signer: desktop entry is DBusActivatable but no org.gnostr.Signer D-Bus service file is installed
description: Found in nostrc-jppi. apps/gnostr-signer/data/org.gnostr.Signer.desktop sets DBusActivatable=true, but apps/gnostr-signer/CMakeLists.txt installs only org.nostr.Signer.service (the daemon). Launching GNostr Signer through its desktop entry (GDesktopAppInfo, Shell) therefore tries D-Bus activation of org.gnostr.Signer, which fails silently. This matters more with nip55l 0.4.0: org.gnostr.Signer is the only approval UI, and clients (gnostr now offers 'Open GNostr Signer') need a reliable way to start it. Either install an org.gnostr.Signer.service (Exec=<bindir>/gnostr-signer --gapplication-service) or drop DBusActivatable. gnostr works around it by spawning gnostr-signer from PATH. Owner: apps/gnostr-signer (M).
close_reason: Merged to master in 5d8d9c1c (worker P, fix/gnostr-kind15-signer-service); tests verified by orchestrator (worker died at report step on usage cap).

title: nostr-dispatcher: check org.gnostr.gnostr and org.gnostr.Client share a pid before Handler1 handoff
description: Follow-up from nostrc-46h7 (Oracle suggestion on prqu.3). gnostr owns org.gnostr.Client (GApplication id) and, on its primary instance, the alias org.gnostr.gnostr (desktop id) for org.nostr.Handler1. nostr-dispatcher hands fetched events to the Handler1 bus name derived from the desktop id. Before calling OpenEvent it should verify (GetConnectionUnixProcessID / credentials) that the owner of org.gnostr.gnostr is the same process as org.gnostr.Client, so another process that grabbed the alias first cannot receive events meant for GNostr. Owner: gnome/nostr-dispatcher (not apps/gnostr).

title: session relay: superseded replaceable/addressable versions likely stay stored and served (nostrdb has no delete)
description: Found while fixing nostrc-9tdc (wJ). protocol_nip01 stores a newer replaceable/addressable version and then calls vt->delete_event(old_id), but components/nostrdb/src/nostrdb_storage.c ndb_delete returns -ENOTSUP, and vendored nostrdb defines is_replaceable_kind() without using it at ingest. So a REQ for {authors,kinds:[30023],#d:[x]} probably returns both the old and the new version, while NIP-01 says relays keep only the latest per (pubkey,kind[,d]). Not yet verified end to end: extend test_session_relay_storage (check_addressable already stores v1 then v2) to assert v1 is NOT served for the #d REQ; fix either by filtering superseded versions at query time in the relay core (keep newest per coordinate) or via the nostrdb delete primitive tracked by nostrc-8rxk. Owner: apps/relayd.

title: libmarmot adopted profile follow-ups: marmot-gobject wrapper, GI ergonomics, engine support
description: From prqu.9 (wave4 G). (1) marmot-gobject: expose validate/select for the ADOPTED profile (and the producer once enabled). (2) GI: MarmotAccountSignFunc is synchronous-only (documented); add a GDestroyNotify-style variant if bindings need async. (3) Engine: AppDataUpdate + app-component group state (0x8003 admin policy etc.) so MARMOT_ENABLE_ADOPTED_KEY_PACKAGE_PRODUCER can default ON (Groundhog W2). (4) MDK interop test adding a libmarmot KeyPackage to an MDK-created group (prqu.10 asked for it; needs the Rust toolchain).

title: nostr-dispatcher NIP-89 follow-ups: fallback-kind suggestions, query batching, kind-5 invalidation
description: From the prqu.1 review (wave4 G). (1) Offer a low-priority NIP-89 suggestion also when a known kind resolved only via a generic '*' fallback handler (rate-limited per kind via the cache). (2) Privacy: batch discovery REQs for recently failed kinds into one query instead of one per failed open; document the #k leak in the security notes. (3) Treat a cached kind-5 deletion (or a superseding 31990) for an offered address as invalidating the offer. (4) Consider IDN/confusable host display (punycode) in the offer button.

title: nostr-shell-extension-state-node: tests/run-tests.js is ESM but runs as CommonJS on Node < 22 (SyntaxError: import outside a module)
description: Found by the worker-H aarch64 sweep 2026-09-26: the test is only registered when find_program(node) succeeds (gnome/nostr-shell-extension/CMakeLists.txt:51-55), so D's nostrc-m4y1 sweep never ran it; Node 18.19.1 has since been installed on the lab and the test fails in 0.08 s: run-tests.js uses 'import * as S from ../lib/state.js' with no package.json "type":"module" and a .js extension, which Node only auto-detects as ESM from v22.7. Ubuntu 24.04 ships Node 18. Fix: rename to tests/run-tests.mjs (lib/*.js are imported by gjs as ESM, so do not add a package-wide type=module without checking gjs), or add a tests/package.json {"type":"module"} if lib imports resolve; keep nostr-shell-extension-state-gjs as the gjs twin.
notes: K: 3590d1a1 on fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups (not merged).
close_reason: Merged to master (worker K, fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups). Lab: syncd watches 65,145 → 0 (8,192 cap with seed). Follow-ups: 5y2t (P1 snapshot >32MiB), p8y6, ix3n, ixra.

title: porthome-fuse-fixture: unchecked snprintf truncation fails -Werror=format (3 sites, porthome_fuse_fixture.c)
description: Found by the worker-H aarch64 sweep with CMAKE_C_FLAGS='-Werror -Wformat -Werror=format' (GCC 13, -O3, _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2): of 1318 targets only gnome/nostr-homed/tests/integration/porthome_fuse_fixture.c fails, with 3 -Wformat-truncation errors: :228 snprintf(abs[8192], "%s/%s", root, rel); :374 snprintf(tmp[1024], "%s.tmp", path[1024]); :382 same for gtmp/gpath. The target compiles with -Wno-error, which hides these under plain -Werror, but a specific -Werror=format overrides it. These are real silent-truncation paths (a long state_dir makes tmp == a truncated path, so the rename targets the wrong file). Fix: check the snprintf return (>= sizeof -> fail), or size tmp as path+5; then drop the target's -Wno-error. Also replace the deprecated SHA256_Init/Update/Final (OpenSSL 3) with EVP_Digest* while there.
notes: K: 9571296c on fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups (not merged).

title: ASan workspace build: ODR violation on libnostr json_interface (static libnostr + libnostr-json.so)

title: session relay federation: cheap path for cache writes (no fsync/outbox row for non-account events)
description: Follow-up of nostrc-7d96. Every stored event that passes the static contract gets a durable outbox row (fsync) before the author check, so an app bulk-caching other authors' events into relay.sock pays one fsync per event and the rows settle 'skipped'. Also cached inbound gift wraps addressed to the user are re-sent to the user's own 10050 relays (duplicate: acks; a liveness hint to those relays) because a self-copy cannot be told apart from an inbound wrap. Options: author check in the tee when the account set is known (enqueue only on unknown author), and/or a per-connection 'cache write, do not federate' marker on relay.sock (needs relay-core per-connection context in put_event).
notes: branch fix/relayd-federation-followups (wJ, not pushed): 4aa861e6 + 81a224d6 (review: restricted). No outbox row/fsync for foreign authors when federation_accounts is set; hint-only ingests commit synchronous=NORMAL. Signer-learned accounts still queue (safety). Remaining (default config, inbound gift wraps, own-history sync): nostrc-pw0d (per-connection cache marker). title: session relay federation: retarget pending deliveries when a relay list changes
description: Follow-up of nostrc-7d96. Targets are resolved once at routing (documented point-in-time). title: gnostr nip29-groups: create-group sends metadata tags on kind:9007 instead of a follow-up kind:9002
description: Found by the nostrc-rxxx audit (pre-existing, not from the revision range). build_action_event_json() in apps/gnostr/plugins/nip29-groups/gn-nip29-group-service.c puts name/about/picture/banner/private/restricted/hidden/closed tags on the kind:9007 create-group event. NIP-29's moderation table gives 9007 no tags; metadata is set with kind:9002 edit-metadata. Relays that follow the table create the group with default metadata and silently drop the fields. Fix: publish 9007 (h only), then on OK publish 9002 with the metadata tags (and, for subgroups, the optional parent tag).
notes: branch fix/gnostr-followups-2 (worker L, not merged): 2e93233b + 0ce56c8c (test stabilisation). Tests: gnostr-test-nip29-events, gnostr-test-plugin-publish-ack (mock relay, 10/10). Filed: nostrc-jc2o (fd 0 closed by relay teardown), nostrc-oz77 (connect_async succeeds for refused port).

title: gnostr nip29-groups: detect group migration/forks via admins' kind:10009 (NIP-29 MUST when the group relay is unreachable)
description: Found by the nostrc-rxxx audit (db5fe3d). NIP-29 'Detecting migrations and forks': clients SHOULD periodically -- and MUST if the primary relay for a group is offline -- read the kind:10009 of the group's admins (cached from 39001) and of trusted friends; a changed relay hint for the id means the group moved or forked, and the client should tell the user and offer to fetch from / migrate to the new relay, updating the user's own 10009. apps/gnostr/plugins/nip29-groups keeps saved groups in saved-groups.json only; it neither reads nor writes 10009 and does not cache admin pubkeys across sessions. Plugin already keys groups by relay'id, so a fork is naturally a separate tracked group once offered. Documented as a known divergence in docs/reviews/nip29-conformance-2026-09-26.md.
notes: branch fix/gnostr-followups-2 (worker L, not merged): 04e35e5c + 50715411. Test: gnostr-test-nip29-migration. Filed: nostrc-kyvy (migrate participation + user's 10009), nostrc-1b4j (nip29 lib 10009 helper).
close_reason: Merged (worker L): NIP-29 MUST — detect migration/fork via admins' 10009 when the group relay is unreachable, notify with 'Open There'. Optional 'move my participation' → nostrc-kyvy.

title: nostr-notify: NIP-29 notifications keyed by bare h tag conflate forks of the same group id on different relays (owner: E)
description: Found by the nostrc-rxxx NIP-29 audit (db5fe3d migration/forks). gnome/nostr-homed/src/notify/notify_gnotification.c group_withdraw_id() builds 'grp:<h>' and the title falls back to the bare h tag; the planned 39000 display-name cache (notify_subs.c dispatch_on_main comment) is also keyed by h. NIP-29 now says the same id can be different communities on different relays, so two forks' messages coalesce into one notification (one withdraws/replaces the other) and would share a cached display name. Fix: key the withdraw id and the metadata cache by (relay_url, h) -- e.g. grp:<sha256(relay_url)[:8]>:<h> to keep the id bounded. No change needed for the other revisions: 39005 pins, 9010, subgroups and banner are not notification-worthy and notify correctly subscribes only to kinds 9-12; kind 10011 is not subscribed.
notes: K: 3d8bf36a on fix/homed-syncd-notify-followups (not merged).

title: nostr-home-fuse: clean SIGTERM stop exits 6 (unit ends failed)
description: Found during nostrc-ipvk lab proof. fuse_main() returns non-zero when the loop is ended by a signal (libfuse sets se->error = sig; helper maps loop res!=0 to 7/8), and nostr-home-fuse.c maps any non-zero to exit 6 ('mount failed'). So 'systemctl --user stop nostr-home-fuse' after a successful mount logs 'Main process exited, status=6/NOTCONFIGURED' and leaves the unit failed (Restart=on-failure does not trigger on stop, but it is noise and hides real mount failures). Fix: replace fuse_main with fuse_new/fuse_mount/fuse_set_signal_handlers/fuse_loop and treat a loop return equal to SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP as clean exit 0.

title: nips/nip47: kind-13194 info event content/notifications shape diverges from NIP-47
description: Found while fixing nostrc-iq04. nostr_nwc_info_build() writes content as JSON {"methods":[...]} and a ["notifications","true"|"false"] tag; nostr_nwc_info_parse() requires that JSON content. NIP-47 specifies content as a plaintext space-separated capability list (e.g. 'pay_invoice get_balance notifications') and the notifications tag as a space-separated list of notification types ('payment_received payment_sent'). A spec wallet's info event therefore fails nostr_nwc_info_parse (methods missing). iq04 fixed only the encryption tag (spelling + single space-separated value). Fix: emit/parse the spec shapes (accept the legacy JSON content on parse), update test_nwc_info. nostr-wallet-agent parses 13194 itself (nwa-nwc.c) so it is unaffected.

title: libgo: int_array_add/string arrays on a zeroed struct heap-overflow (capacity 0 doubles to 0)
description: Found under ASan by the relayd REQ-contract test (nostrc-prqu.14): libgo/src/int_array.c int_array_add() grows by capacity*=2; on a zero-initialised IntArray (capacity 0, e.g. a calloc'd NostrFilter) that stays 0, realloc(NULL,0) returns a minimal block and the write overflows the heap. relayd was fixed to use nostr_filter_new() (commit 1dab5499), but the container should be robust: grow to max(capacity*2, INITIAL) and check the same pattern in string_array_add and siblings. Owner: libnostr/libgo.
notes: Fixed in 5179ae01 on branch fix/libnostr-dav-packaging-followups (not pushed); ASan clean.
close_reason: Merged aa84da77 (D branch, 11 commits a2b93d96..dfade292). Details in the merge message; ctest matrix docs/reviews/ctest-sweep-aarch64-2026-09-26.md.

title: libnostr: filter deserializer ignores "limit":0 (limit_zero never set)
description: Found by relayd REQ-contract work (nostrc-prqu.14, branch fix/session-relay-followups). nostr_filter_deserialize() / nostr_filter_deserialize_compact() never set NostrFilter.limit_zero for an explicit "limit":0, so it is indistinguishable from an absent limit (grep limit_zero in libnostr/src: only init/copy/accessors). NIP-01 limit:0 means 'no stored events, EOSE now'. Consequence: relayd cannot honor limit:0 and runs an unbounded (max_limit-clamped) backfill instead. Fix in libnostr (both compact and backend paths) + a parsing test; then relayd handle_req can EOSE immediately when every filter has limit_zero (see apps/relayd/src/protocol_nip01.c handle_req).
notes: Fixed in 37bf2378 on branch fix/libnostr-dav-packaging-followups (not pushed); relayd handle_req can now use limit_zero.

title: Nostr Settings: grant/revoke wallet read access per app (allow_read)
description:
nostr-wallet-agent's per-app allow_read flag ('can see balance and history') can only be set by ticking 'Always allow this app' in the agent's approval dialog. Nostr Settings shows it read-only (nss-page-wallet.c, from budgets.json) and cannot revoke it.

The GNOME Shell extension (nostrc-33f1) was briefed to say 'Grant access in Nostr Settings' when it has no read grant. Since Settings cannot grant, it instead offers an explicit 'Allow balance access…' menu item that makes one GetBalance call, which the agent answers with its dialog.

Wanted: an agent method (e.g. SetReadAccess(app_id, b)) that the agent always confirms with its own dialog, unless the caller is trusted. Settings then gets a per-app switch; revoking should need no confirmation. The Shell extension could then point to Settings > Wallet as well. Note that gnome-shell's identity is exe:/usr/bin/gnome-shell, so the grant covers every shell extension; the Settings row should say so.
notes: Done on branch fix/agent-followups (not pushed): 5d74eb0f. ListApps/SetReadAccess/AppsChanged; grant-admin tier = installed nostr-settings (exe path+inode) or Flatpak trusted-apps; budget raises still confirmed (oracle). Installed Settings verified trusted on lab. Follow-up: nostrc-muhk (read vs receive split).

title: nostr-wallet-agent: non-interactive read (deny instead of prompt) for panel/status callers
description:
org.nostr.Wallet1 read calls (GetBalance/GetInfo/ListTransactions) always PROMPT for an identified app without allow_read (nwa-policy.c), and there is no way to ask 'answer only if you would not ask the user'. The GNOME Shell extension (nostrc-33f1) must never prompt from the panel. It therefore re-implements the agent's caller identification (port of nwa_caller_parse_cgroup + exe fallback) and reads allow_read from budgets.json before calling GetBalance.

That duplicates agent policy in a client. It also cannot rule out a prompt when the agent's own identification disagrees (for example, its PID recheck fails and the caller becomes unidentified, which prompts). Proposal: honour the D-Bus header flag ALLOW_INTERACTIVE_AUTHORIZATION the polkit way. If a read call does not carry the flag and the decision would be PROMPT, reply with a new org.nostr.Wallet1.Error.InteractionRequired instead. Existing GDBus callers don't set the flag, so this changes behaviour for them; alternatively gate it behind an explicit opt-in such as GetBalanceNonInteractive(), or an a{sv} options variant with 'interactive': false. After this lands, drop lib/wallet.js's budgets.json pre-check and caller-id port, and map InteractionRequired to the 'Allow balance access…' item.
