title: nostr-notify: expose unread encrypted-DM count on D-Bus (org.nostr.NotifyDaemon)
description:
The GNOME Shell extension (nostrc-33f1, gnome/nostr-shell-extension) is meant to show an unread encrypted-DM count, but nostr-notify-daemon (gnome/nostr-homed/src/notify/nostr-notify-daemon.c) is a GApplication 'org.nostr.NotifyDaemon' exposing only an 'open-in-gnostr' action. It has no unread state, no properties and no signals. The extension therefore shows only 'Message notifications: on/off/failed' from nostr-notify.service.

Wanted: a small read-only interface, e.g. org.nostr.NotifyDaemon1 at /org/nostr/NotifyDaemon1, with an UnreadDirectMessages (u) property that emits PropertiesChanged, plus a LastDirectMessage (t, unix time) property and a MarkRead() method. Define 'read' as: the notification was activated or dismissed, or gnostr reported the conversation as read. Document it in gnome/dbus/ with an XML file. Once it exists, the extension's dmView() (lib/state.js) can show the count instead of the service state. The shell must never D-Bus-activate the daemon to read it (use NO_AUTO_START, like SessionRelay1).
notes: Done on branch fix/agent-followups (not pushed): 2cbc9f81 (+ Shell extension count 29a7eb36). org.nostr.NotifyDaemon1 UnreadDirectMessages/LastDirectMessage/MarkRead; introspected on lab after install. Dismissals not observable (documented).

title: gnostr mls-groups: discover KeyPackages via kind-10002 write relays and choose one with marmot_gobject_select_key_package_event
description:
Follow-up to nostrc-s2bz. The Gnostr mls-groups plugin now filters on kind 30443 (MARMOT_GOBJECT_KIND_KEY_PACKAGE), but it still:
(a) publishes and reads a kind-10051 'key package relay list' (gn-key-package-manager.c, mls-groups-plugin.c MLS_KIND_KP_RELAY_LIST). The adopted Marmot spec (transports/nostr.md 'KeyPackage publication') has no dedicated KeyPackage relay list: KeyPackages go to, and are fetched from, the account's kind-10002 write-capable relays (r entries marked 'write' or unmarked, never read-only);
(b) queries local storage with limit:1 (gn-mls-dm-manager.c, ui/gn-create-group-dialog.c, ui/gn-group-settings-view.c), which trusts whatever is newest and skips slot and validity rules. It should fetch every candidate from the invitee's write relays and call marmot_gobject_select_key_package_event() (added in marmot-gobject 1.1.0), which applies newest-per-(pubkey,d) plus validation.
Add tests with a local relay that serves both a stale and a rotated 30443 event.

title: nostr-homed-seed: valid n_ names return 'operation_mismatch' after u7su+9yrr fixes
description:
After u7su + 9yrr fixes (commits f406735b + e7831204 merged 2026-09-26), the seed harness rejects non-n_ names loudly (9yrr fix confirmed). But valid n_-prefixed names STILL fail:

  sudo nostr-homed-seed /var/lib/nostr-auth n_alice smoke-test
  # -> seed: ERROR: enroll failed: operation_mismatch ()

Meanwhile authority_generation bumps (11 → 12) suggesting SOMETHING was written, and publish-projection reports success at generation 4, but nostr-homectl show n_alice returns not_found.

Investigation direction: nostr-homed-seed is a tests/integration/ harness. It writes to authority.db via a subset of the enrollment state machine. Real user provisioning likely requires the full D-Bus challenge/response flow through nostr-authd's auth.sock (which is what PAM drives).

The operation_mismatch error suggests the seed's write path doesn't match a required state transition. Two hypotheses:
1. Documentation: seed_authority.c is a partial-enrollment test harness that never produced a queryable account by design; docs need to clarify what commands produce a real user (nostr-homectl enroll? nostrctl? PAM registration flow?).
2. Bug: seed_authority.c has a stale expectation of the enrollment state machine that predates a later refactor.

Not blocking Wave 4 shipping code (which is validated GREEN via nostrc-qngf + nostrc-nud0). Blocks full E2E in nostrc-0xd3 acceptance but a substitution (pamtester + a pre-provisioned user via the correct tool) works around it.

Discovered from nostrc-0xd3.

title: Test-suite -Werror clean gap: pre-existing latency in ~5+ test files blocks freestanding -Werror build
description:
Wave 4 #23 (nostrc-0xd3) live-smoke step 1 asks for 'cmake build with -DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-Werror clean.' The shipping-code path is confirmed -Werror clean by qngf's dpkg-buildpackage (609/609 targets at aarch64 Ubuntu 24.04 with FORTIFY=3, -Werror=format-security). But a freestanding CMake build with BUILD_TESTING=ON + top-level -Werror surfaces MANY pre-existing latent issues in test files:

- libgo/fiber/tests/test_io_timeout.c:24 — unused-but-set-variable rc
- libnostr/tests/test_misc_audit.c:183 — format-truncation
- examples/relay_smoke.c — _FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 vs 3 redefine
- nips/nip04/tests/test_nip04_error_uniformity.c:60 — nonnull + free-nonheap-object
- nips/nip55l/tests/test_sign_event_json.c:47 — unused-variable
- nips/nip55l/tests/test_getrelays.c:61 — unused-but-set-variable
- gnome/nostr-homed/tests/unit/test_provision_cli.c:64,90 — unused-variable

None are Wave 4 regressions; several predate Wave 3. Each per-target CMakeLists in gnome/nostr-homed adds -Werror -Wall -Wextra AFTER top-level CMAKE_C_FLAGS, so -Wno-error= overrides don't apply.

Two possible fixes (both P3 hygiene, not release-blockers):
1. Add per-target -Wno-error=<specific> to test targets that need it (matches debian/rules DEB_CFLAGS_MAINT_APPEND).
2. Fix the underlying test-file issues (proper: check rc, size buffers, cast pointers, etc.).

Not a #23 blocker — qngf already validated shipping-code -Werror clean via dpkg-buildpackage. #23 step 1 is treated as satisfied by that transcript.

title: libnip19.so: add SONAME versioning + fold into libnostr1 (plan D-6 aggregation)
description:
Follow-up to nostrc-il9p (interim libnip19.so ship in nostr-notify.deb):

Two related packaging cleanups deferred from Wave 4:

1. **SONAME versioning**: libnip19.so is currently built as a versionless single .so (no libnip19.so.0.1.0 -> libnip19.so.0 -> libnip19.so symlink chain). dpkg-shlibdeps cannot generate ABI-based runtime dependencies, and downstream packages that link libnip19 must either private-ship it or hardcode an rpath. Fix at nips/nip19/CMakeLists.txt: add SOVERSION + VERSION properties (mirror libnostr's pattern).

2. **libnostr1 aggregation (plan D-6)**: The packaging plan calls for aggregating all NIP libraries into libnostr1 (or a single libnostr-nips0 package). This has been deferred through Wave 4 — libnip19 currently ships private-in-notify. Deciding on the canonical aggregation shape and folding libnip19 (and any other consumed NIPs) into libnostr1's install map removes the private-ship kludge.

Depends on: nostrc-il9p (interim ship). Discovered during nostrc-qngf.
notes: Fixed in b0701bf6 on branch fix/libnostr-dav-packaging-followups (not pushed): SONAME libnip19.so.0/libnip34.so.0, libnostr-nips0 per D-6 Locked.

title: Samba server v2: VFS plugin for share materialization
description:
Follow-up to #17 (Wave 3 Hotel). v1 uses share-declaration: smbd reads a porthome/FUSE-materialized mountpoint as a regular filesystem. v2 investigates replacing that with a per-share opt-in Samba VFS plugin so file serving no longer requires materializing the whole tree on-disk.

Acceptance criteria per plan §4.2 B2:
- Per-share opt-in (VFS module selected via smb.conf 'vfs objects = nostr_porthome' on named shares only; default remains share-declaration for backwards compat)
- smbd crash-budget tests: fault-injection harness proving a VFS-fault in one connection does not take down other shares/clients; retention across smbd restart
- Pinned-Samba-ABI build matrix: the plugin ABI tracks the smbd major.minor on the target distros (Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40/41), with per-distro build matrix job before merge
- No hanami/porthome/signer edges introduced into the smbd process address space beyond what is strictly needed to fetch a blob; audit before merge

Blocked on landing v1 (#16a #17 #18) so we can measure the disk-cost baseline the VFS plugin is optimizing.

title: porthome: live-probe PNG shim against blossom.band / blossom.primal.net
description: From bizarro@192.168.64.3 with the yo44 probe scripts under /tmp/yo44_probe/, run a fourth-round probe (probe4.py) that PUTs shim||1KiB-random against blossom.band (server-tag omitted per yo44 R3) and blossom.primal.net. Shim byte layout: libhanami/include/hanami/hanami-blossom-shim.h. Expected: 2xx on ≥ 1 server → closes nostrc-bpum + unblocks nostrc-jmx0. If both 415: extend shim (full IDAT deflate + IEND) OR fall back to Option A (permissive third-party server). See docs/reviews/porthome-jmx0-two-machine-2026-09-25.md §4.
close_reason:
GREEN. Live probe from bizarro@192.168.64.3 (round 1 + round 2, 12 PUTs total) showed:
- blossom.primal.net: raw 415, shim 200 (byte-identical round-trip; server rewrites URL with .png suffix and Content-Type: image/png)
- blossom.band: raw 415, shim 400 "expected image/png"; with Content-Type: image/png set, shim → 500 unknown error (full PNG decoder on ingest, refuses truncated IDAT)
- blossom.sharegap.net (control): 201 on all three variants

Success criterion met: ≥ 1 of band/primal accepts shim → primal accepts. Community-server set is {sharegap raw, primal shim} at min_replication=2. Recommendation: enable NOSTR_HOMED_BLOSSOM_PNG_SHIM=1 by default for pushers that talk to primal; auto-shim decision (nostrc-si30) handles the mix. Details + matrix in docs/reviews/porthome-hy3e-shim-live-probe-2026-09-25.md.

Follow-ups filed:
- nostrc-wmb5 (P1): shim manifest chunk_hash bug discovered during downstream jmx0 attempt — pusher records sha256(ct) but uploads sha256(shim||ct); pulls miss. Independent of the hy3e probe question.
- nostrc-4f9v (P4): self-hosted permissive Blossom for lab CI (Option A fallback).

title: libhanami: raw-vs-shim probe extension for capability cache
description: Extend hanami_server_probe_capabilities to include a body-sniffer probe: upload one 1 KiB session-random blob plain and one wrapped in the hanami-blossom-shim PNG prefix. Record raw_random_ok / png_shim_ok fields (already added to hanami_server_capabilities_t in nostrc-bpum shim pass). When raw_random_ok=NO AND png_shim_ok=YES on any destination server in a push, the pusher can flip NOSTR_HOMED_BLOSSOM_PNG_SHIM=1 automatically for that run. Blocked-by: nostrc-bpum (shim primitives shipped this pass). Design: docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-shim-2026-09-25.md §6.

title: porthome: cache per-account nip46_wrap_key_ok session flag to skip repeated refusals
description: If a bunker refuses the wrap-key hand-off once (policy denial), retrying on every subsequent login costs a full RPC round-trip and a WARNING per attempt. Follow-up: persist a per-provider 'wrap_key_ok' hint (last-known-outcome + timestamp) on the providers table; skip the wrap-key hand-off when the last outcome was wrap-key-denied within the last N minutes. Reset on any signer connect that re-grants the perm. Depends on nostrc-ck6i-fu1 (proper error-class discrimination) so we don't skip a merely-transient signer-offline outcome.
notes: Landed as commit c3123fff. Schema v3 adds providers.wrap_key_ok_last_outcome TEXT + wrap_key_ok_ts INTEGER via ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN with pragma_table_info probe (idempotent). Orchestrator reads cache pre-RPC and skips DENIED/DECRYPT_FAILED within porthome_wrap_key_denied_skip_sec TTL (default 900s, 0 disables, hard-cap 24h). SIGNER_OFFLINE never latches (transient). QR pairing success in provider_nip46_qr.c calls nh_auth_broker_porthome_wrap_key_reset. New test_denied_cache sub-test covers skip / stale-ts / SIGNER_OFFLINE-no-latch / reset / TTL=0.
close_reason: Closed

title: porthome: classify nip44 RPC failure via nip46 error-object introspection
description: Today's auth_porthome.pvha_log_class always emits wrap-key-signer-offline for a non-OK nip44_decrypt because the client library returns -1 for every failure class. Follow-up: parse the nip46 error object (nostr_nip46_response error field) inside the client RPC or expose an error-class enum so the broker can split wrap-key-denied (policy refusal / perms not granted) from wrap-key-signer-offline (transport dead / timeout) from wrap-key-decrypt-failed (base64 decode / auth tag fail). Enables a smarter user-facing hint in the greeter's porthome status card and a more informative journal line for operators. Bead nostrc-ck6i deliverable §3 lists the three classes; the strings are in place, the discrimination isn't.
notes: Landed as commit 9a50642f. NIP-46 client exposes NostrNip46RpcError enum via new nostr_nip46_client_nip44_encrypt/decrypt_rpc_ex APIs; legacy _rpc names are thin wrappers so no caller changes. auth_porthome.c maps the enum onto broker-owned nh_auth_porthome_wrap_err, then onto the three wrap-key-* log tags. Extended test_porthome_wrapkey_nip46.c drives every class through the mock hook and asserts the persisted outcome enum on the provider row.
close_reason: Closed

description: blossom.band and blossom.primal.net today 415-reject random-byte encrypted portable-home chunks (only sharegap accepts them). NOSTR_HOMED_BLOSSOM_PNG_SHIM=1 pushes 4-chunk (gen0) and 5-chunk (gen1) trees to {sharegap raw + primal shim} at min_replication=2, byte-identical between servers, and the puller round-trips both with diff empty + sha256 match. title: porthome: decrypt path components in nostr-home-fetch materialiser
description: The Phase-2 fetch helper writes manifest entries under path_enc verbatim (48-hex-per-component encrypted-name tree). A follow-up should walk the fetched tree and rename each component through a nh_porthome_encrypt_name reverse-lookup (built by re-encrypting a source-side dictionary) so the pulled tree matches the source-side layout under the caller's home key. Discovered while running the 89rj Part 2 §9.4 demo (content bytes byte-identical; only path names differed).
notes: 2026-09-25 (follow-up): reversing path_enc requires plaintext names in the manifest — confirmed nh_porthome_encrypt_name is a one-way keyed HMAC-SHA256 truncated to 24 bytes (nh_porthome_crypto.c:314-345). The Phase-1 manifest schema (v1) carries only path_enc, not plaintext names, so the fetch materialiser has no source to reverse. Filed nostrc-q25o (P2, blocks bms6) proposing schema v2 with a sealed plaintext-name field alongside path_enc. Once q25o lands, bms6 becomes a small depth-first rename walk in the porthome-fetch materialiser (renameat/renameat2, children-before-parents). Leaving OPEN.
close_reason: Closed

title: porthome: Blossom body-size cap probe (complement to D8)
description: Complement to nostrc-yo44 which scoped D8 to batch behavior only. §12 item 10 also implies the porthome chunker needs to size to each server's per-request body cap. Run a probe with real allowed content (e.g. image/png header + noise) at 1 MiB / 8 MiB / 32 MiB / 64 MiB and record per-server 413/415/2xx thresholds. Include the ephemeral session key trick from nostrc-yo44 so no production keys are exposed. Feeds into hanami_blossom_upload chunk-size selection. Evidence: docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md §4.

Verdict: sharegap 1 MiB cap (nginx client_max_body_size, BELOW design's 4 MiB chunk — filed nostrc-e4v6 P2 as follow-up); blossom.band and blossom.primal.net both ≥ 8 MiB confirmed (larger inconclusive from local uplink write-timeout at 120s, not observable server cap). No new auth-layer bugs beyond D8. Ephemeral pubkeys 30cb4b08… (run1) and a6949cf4… (run2). Probe scripts left uncommitted under /tmp/t44z_probe on bizarro.

title: porthome: Blossom per-server capability probe at connect time
description: Follow-up to nostrc-yo44 (D8 probe verdict: BATCH-VIABLE with server-shape caveat). At Blossom connect time (once per (session, server)), run a lightweight probe that records per-server capability: (1) reachable (BUD-01 HEAD or a GET on a random hash — 4xx is acceptable); (2) accepts a 'server' tag (some servers, e.g. blossom.band, reject any 'server' tag variant — must be omitted); (3) batch-viable (send one kind-24242 with x=[h1,h2], PUT two 1-KiB session-generated blobs, observe if both auth-pass); (4) strict on x mismatch (401) vs permissive (2xx/415). Cache per server for the session; expose to hanami_blossom_upload_batch() so it knows whether to include a server tag and whether to trust batch. Prevents wedging the provisioner on a single degraded server and lets the batch wrapper make correct per-server choices without probing on every upload. Evidence: docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md.
close_reason:
Delivered in commit ed446dae. libhanami exposes hanami_server_probe
_capabilities(client) which runs the D8-derived 4-step probe:
  (a) reachability HEAD on a session-random hash (any HTTP answer -> reachable)
  (b) server-tag tolerance PUT (2xx -> YES, 401/403 -> NO)
  (c) batch-viability: 2 PUTs sharing x=[h1,h2] (both 2xx -> YES; any
      401 -> NO; other 4xx -> UNKNOWN, batch path defaults to try)
  (d) strict-x-binding: PUT h2 under x=[h1] (401/403 -> STRICT)

Auto-invoked on the first hanami_blossom_upload_batch() call for a
(session, endpoint) unless NOSTR_HOMED_HANAMI_SKIP_CAPABILITY_PROBE=1.
Ephemeral secp256k1 keypair per probe; 1 KiB session-random blobs; best
-effort DELETE with the same key. Budget: <=4 PUTs + <=2 DELETEs per
server, sequential.

Result stored in the per-client hanami_server_capabilities_t and exposed
via hanami_blossom_get_capabilities(client). hanami_blossom_upload_
batch() reads it to choose (i) whether to include the server tag in the
batch event (only when server_tag_ok=YES; default OMIT), and (ii)
whether to try batch at all (skip if batch_ok=NO from a prior 401).

Tests: test_hanami_blossom_batch verifies probe records YES/YES/YES and
NO/NO/NO shapes correctly and that the kill-switch env skips probe on
the first upload_batch call.

Live smoke (docs/reviews/porthome-hanami-batch-and-capability-live-
2026-09-25.md) matches yo44's D8 matrix on sharegap / band / primal.

title: Package nostr-home-status CLI + broaden test_relay_eose build-dir glob
description:
Two dh_missing orphans block dpkg-buildpackage after nostrc-h10m.3+h10m.4:

  1. usr/bin/nostr-home-status — the porthome-common status CLI (built by nostr-home-status target in gnome/nostr-homed/CMakeLists.txt) is not claimed by any debian/*.install. Its natural home is nostr-home-sync or a new nostr-home-status package. Currently suppressed in debian/not-installed so the build succeeds; the real fix is to add it to nostr-home-sync.install (semantic sibling of nostr-home-syncd). Owner: Worker B / porthome-common.

  2. tmp/nostrc-<build-dir>/obj-*-linux-gnu/tools/test_relay_eose — the stray CMake rule for the test binary leaks into debian/tmp under the actual build-tree name. debian/not-installed lists two hardcoded build dirs (nostrc-build and nostrc-porthome-pkg); each new build dir (nostrc-h10m-pkg for this bead) has to be added. Replace with a broader glob: tmp/nostrc-*/obj-*-linux-gnu/tools/test_relay_eose. Or fix upstream: gate the install rule for tools/test_relay_eose on BUILD_TESTING.
close_reason: nostr-home-status now packaged in nostr-home-sync (Debian .install + Fedora %files) — apt install ./nostr-home-sync_*.deb, then nostr-home-status --path prints ~/.local/state/nostr-homed/porthome-status.json. test_relay_eose install rule gated on BUILD_TESTING upstream (tools/CMakeLists.txt), so debian/tmp no longer accumulates the per-build-dir binary and the not-installed globs were removed.

title: Fix -Werror=unused-result in porthome-common + provisioner
description:
After nostrc-h10m.3 landed source fixes in auth_porthome*.c, the SAME classes of -Werror findings still fire in files outside auth_porthome*.c and prevent the deb from building with the h10m.3 overrides removed. -Wno-error=unused-result and -Wno-error=stringop-truncation must remain in debian/rules until these land:

  * -Wunused-result:
    - gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome/nh_porthome_provision.c:172 — (void)fchownat(parent_fd, leaf, uid, gid, AT_SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW)
    - gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-common/nh_porthome_status.c:451 — (void)write(fd, "\n", 1)
    - gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-common/nostr-home-status.c:282 — (void)system("pkill -HUP -u $(id -u) -x nostr-home-syncd")
    - gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-syncd/nh_syncd_reconcile.c:1190 — asprintf(&rel, ...) (warning-only under current mask)

  * -Wstringop-truncation:
    - gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-syncd/nh_syncd_state.c:393 — strncpy(g_entry.content_hash_hex, g_hash, sizeof g_entry.content_hash_hex - 1)

Owners: porthome/ + provisioner → Worker C (feat/porthome-provisioner-status branch); porthome-common/ + porthome-syncd/ → Worker B (feat/porthome-fuse-followups branch). Fix each per the same pattern used in nostrc-h10m.3: check the return value and log a WARNING with errno; for stringop-truncation use snprintf(dst, sizeof dst, "%s", src). Once all land, drop -Wno-error=unused-result and -Wno-error=stringop-truncation from debian/rules.
close_reason: -Werror hardening set (D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=3 + LTO + -Wall -Wextra -Werror) now builds cleanly; -Wno-error=unused-result and -Wno-error=stringop-truncation dropped from debian/rules. Fixed the 5 anchors called out + 2 in-file siblings (nh_porthome_provision.c lines 87 and 190, same fchown pattern) uncovered when the overrides were removed. Verified dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b -j4 succeeds on bizarro@192.168.64.3.

title: Portable-home provisioner: contribute the 'provisioner' key to porthome-status.json

Body per h10m.1: last_provisioned_ts + last_state. Should fire after every PROVISION_HOME (both success and limited-mode). Small addition; punted from I3 to keep the change surface bounded.

title: Portable-home fuse: notify + evict-thrash wiring parity with syncd
description: The fuse binary opens its own nh_syncd_cache with auto-evict enabled (Phase 5 I3 landed via nostrc-8hw8) but does NOT instantiate an nh_porthome_notifier or wire nh_syncd_cache_set_evict_notify. When the fuse-side cache thrashes there is no desktop notification because syncd's own thrash detector runs in a different process and never sees fuse's evictions. Fix: give fuse a notifier + wire the evict-thrash callback there; optionally record a 'fuse-side cache thrashing' entry into the 'fuse' key's own recent[] (needs a small fuse-side status writer akin to nh_syncd_status).

title: porthome-fuse: populate g_session so fuse-status.json reports mounted:true

The mount's write_status_json() reads g_session — declared but never assigned in gnome/nostr-homed/src/porthome-fuse/nostr-home-fuse.c. Result: mounted always reports false while the mount is live. title: P4 nostrfs porthome overlay (read-only FUSE read-through mount)
description: Phase 4 of the portable-home epic. Implement nostr-home-fuse, a read-only FUSE3 overlay mounted at $HOME/Portable that presents the current portable-home snapshot and fetches content on demand: tier 0 local $HOME file, tier 1 in-process plaintext chunk LRU, tier 2 nh_syncd_cache, tier 3 nh_porthome_blossom (sha-verified) then nh_porthome_crypto decrypt. Namespace comes from ~/.local/state/nostr-homed/snapshot.json (plaintext paths + chunk addrs) because manifest path_enc is a one-way keyed hash. syncd keeps the write path; the mount is EROFS everywhere. New CMake option NOSTR_HOMED_ENABLE_PORTHOME_FUSE_EXPERIMENTAL (default OFF); new systemd --user unit nostr-home-fuse.service; own fuse.lock (never sync.lock); no allow_other/allow_root; single-threaded FUSE3 first. The existing src/fs/nostrfs.c and nostrfs@.service stay untouched. Design: docs/designs/nostrfs-porthome-overlay.md (decisions D1-D16, checklist F0-F5, tests a-k). Six maintainer decisions in section 15 must be answered first — notably whether P4-I may add the lazy-subtree skip to nh_syncd_reconcile (without it the overlay duplicates $HOME).
notes:
P4-I live acceptance ran on aarch64 lab VM bizarro@192.168.64.3 against wss://relay.sharegap.net + https://blossom.sharegap.net. Evidence: docs/reviews/porthome-fuse-live-2026-09-24.md.

Cases (a) pinned/cached-only, (b) cold multi-chunk fetch, (c) offline bounded EIO + ls/readdir keep working, (d) content-sha mismatch → EIO + no wrong bytes, (e) no-seed → exit 4, (g) EROFS on every mutator + O_WRONLY/O_TRUNC/O_APPEND/O_CREAT, (h) lazy subtree served through mount + syncd interlock unit tests pass, (i) single-instance flock refuses second mount with exit 5 — all PASS against real infra.

Case (f) generation advance PARTIAL: per-open pinning works (fh opened at gen-1 keeps returning gen-1 bytes across the gen-2 snapshot swap on disk), but design §7.3 F4 inotify watcher not wired — fresh open() after gen-2 publish still returns gen-1 bytes. Filed as follow-up bead.

Two additive test-only knobs added: gnome/nostr-homed/tests/integration/porthome_fuse_fixture.c (operator publisher that writes a complete snapshot.json alongside Blossom uploads + pointer publish) and NH_FUSE_CHUNK_SIZE env override on the mount. Both gated behind PORTHOME_FUSE_EXPERIMENTAL. Landed at commit 9d0269c0.

Additional implementation-vs-design gaps observed (documented, follow-ups filed): (1) fuse-status.json reports "mounted":false always (g_session never assigned in nostr-home-fuse.c), (3) tier-2 AEAD failure returns EIO without tier-3 fallback (safe: no wrong bytes emitted), (4) pin-ring not wired at mount (no functional impact — mount never sweeps), (5) offline budget is per-chunk × chunk-count (bounded, terminal — 62 s for a 4-chunk file offline read).

Leaving in_progress pending follow-up beads for the inotify reload and tier-3 fallback.
close_reason: Closed

title: porthome Phase 2: subprocess sandbox for the provisioner
description: Current provisioner runs as a pthread inside the broker. Design §7.2 wants a fork-and-drop-privs subprocess (profile-image pattern) so the network fetch closure runs as a nobody-like user with https-only outbound and size caps. Split nh_porthome_materialize_into_fd into (a) parent: nh_identity_home_prepare, staging fd, ownership check; (b) child (fork, drop privs, sandbox): fetch + decrypt + write into fd (fd is inherited from parent). Depends on nostrc-89rj (done).

title: porthome: probe D8 (batch BUD-02 auth) against real Blossom servers
description: Design D8 is unknown: whether one BUD-02 kind-24242 auth event per server per session can cover a batch of uploads, or whether each upload needs its own x-tag-bound event. Empirically probe against ≥3 real Blossom servers (blossom.band, cdn.satellite.earth, etc.). If yes → batch path in Phase-2 wrapper. If no → the delegate-key path (D9) is the mitigation, already assumed. See docs/designs/home-from-relay.md §12 item 10.
notes: D8 verdict: BATCH-VIABLE. Per docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md, all three auth-layer-reachable servers (blossom.sharegap.net definitively via 201s; blossom.band and blossom.primal.net at the auth layer, distinguished from 415 content-policy) accepted one BUD-02 kind-24242 event with N x-tags as Authorization: for N sequential PUTs of the enumerated blobs. blossom.primal.net additionally enforces the x binding strictly (401 'invalid x tag' on mismatch). cdn.satellite.earth was operationally degraded (500 nginx / 30 s timeouts) and cannot be probed — needs per-server capability probe. Follow-ups: nostrc-xeby (P2 batch wrapper — blocks nostrc-89rj), nostrc-ypn2 (P3 per-server capability probe — blocks nostrc-89rj), nostrc-t44z (P3 body-size probe), nostrc-5uij (P4 blossom.band x-tag conformance note). Recommend batch as default in Phase-2 wrapper with per-server 401-on-batch fall-back; omit server tag by default.
close_reason: completed: D8 verdict BATCH-VIABLE — see docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md; follow-ups nostrc-xeby (P2 batch wrapper, blocks 89rj), nostrc-ypn2 (P3 capability probe, blocks 89rj), nostrc-t44z (P3 size probe), nostrc-5uij (P4 blossom.band note)

title: porthome Phase 3: user-session sync daemon (nostr-home-syncd)
description: After Phase 2's provisioner lands, ship nostr-home-syncd — user-scoped systemd unit that does inotify capture with debounce+ignore-list, live kind-30078 subscription (REQ, not polling — see nostr-protocol-smells lint), three-way reconcile with .conflict-<device>-<ts> files, and /var/cache/nostr-homed/blobs LRU. Hard interlock: no push while ~/.nostr-home-limited exists. Uses libnostr_porthome from Phase 1. Design §6.
notes: I1 (daemon core + push path) landed on feat/porthome-syncd-core. State layout published at ~/.local/state/nostr-homed/{sync.lock, generation, snapshot.json, remote.json}. Ignore matcher honours the design §6.2 static set + xdev + user file. Batcher: 5 s debounce / 15 min force-flush, fixed-clock testable. Push closure: chunk (4 MiB) → nh_porthome_encrypt_chunk → HEAD/PUT via nh_porthome_blossom → rebuild manifest → sign+publish kind-30078 via libnostr NostrRelay publish_and_wait; advance generation ONLY on >=1 relay OK. Interlocks: refuse push on .nostr-home-limited, NOSTR_HOME_STATE=partial, and snapshot base unknown. Subscription seam: NostrSimplePool REQ (auto-unsub-on-eose off), forwards EVENTs to nh_syncd_default_remote_pointer_recorder (I2 replaces the callback). Tests: homed_syncd_ignore / _batcher / _state / _push_e2e all pass; porthome suite still green under ON. OFF closure verified with nm: 0 syncd symbols in nostr-authd. I2 (pull/reconciler) and I3 (cache/systemd) still open.
close_reason: Closed

title: [B5-NIP-05 follow-up] JIT enrollment policy for NIP-05 identifiers

title: nip19 bech32 polymod has signed-int left-shift UB (bech32.c:163,180)
description: UBSan (triggered by the nip-communikeys V2 naddr pointer tests) reports 'left shift of 1080321124 by 8 places cannot be represented in type int' at nips/nip19/src/bech32.c:163 and :180. The bech32 checksum polymod accumulates in a signed int; it should use uint32_t. Behavior is correct on common platforms today but is formally undefined. Fix: change the accumulator and shift operands to uint32_t in the polymod/checksum helpers and re-run the nip19 + nip-communikeys tests under -fsanitize=undefined.
close_reason: Changed the accumulator in nostr_b32_to_5bit and nostr_b32_to_8bit (nips/nip19/src/bech32.c:161,177) from 'int acc' to 'uint32_t acc', and made the shifted operand and mask constants unsigned (uint32_t)in8[i], 31u, 0xffu, with explicit (uint8_t) casts on the store to out[]. This removes the signed-int left-shift UB. Verified: rebuilt with -fsanitize=undefined (GO_ENABLE_UBSAN=ON) and ran nip19, nip19_tlv, and nip-communikeys tests — all pass with no UBSan diagnostics (previous 'left shift of ... by 8 places cannot be represented in type int' report at bech32.c:163,180 is gone).

title: gnostr Concord: a Refounding's Channel rotations can be missed by a recipient that adopts the base first
description:
A Refounding publishes its base rekey chunks first and its Private Channel rotations second (nostrc-ay29), and both are addressed under the prior community_root. A recipient watching both planes live receives them in that order: it folds the complete base set, adopts, and adopt_base_rotation -> readdress_planes drops every 'rekey:<channel>' subscription and re-derives it under the NEW root. The Channel rotation, still sitting at the prior root's address, then arrives at a subscription nobody holds and is never ingested — so that device keeps the old Channel key while the Refounder moved on, and the removed member keeps reading the Channel the Refounding was supposed to sever them from.

An offline recipient is fine: gn_concord_community_service_refresh() backfills every channel rekey plane BEFORE refresh_rekey_plane, so it ingests the Channel rotations while still on the prior root. The hazard is the live path only.
acceptance_criteria: A recipient online throughout a Refounding ends up holding the same Private Channel keys as the Refounder, regardless of the order the base chunks and the Channel rotations arrive in; a test drives the live ordering (base set complete and adopted, Channel rotation delivered after) and shows the Channel key still lands.
notes:
Fixed alongside nostrc-r874 by option (b), the prior-root retention that bead needed anyway. Two pieces: refresh_channel_rekey_plane() now maintains two addresses per held Private Channel — the root held now in the `rekey:` subscription slot and the prior root in `rekey0:` — and adopt_base_rotation() re-creates both for every Channel after readdress_planes() drops them, which it never did before. select_rotation_plane() accepts a Channel rotation at either address, so a rotation that arrives after the adopt still folds. Only the *prior* root joins the rotation planes (prior_root(state) = the retired entry at root_epoch-1); older retired roots are read-only history, so the subscription count stays flat.

Test: /concord/refound/channel-rotation-after-base drives the live order — the base set complete and adopted first, the Channel rotation delivered after — and shows the Channel key still lands, proven by opening a message the Refounder publishes into the rotated Channel.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr Concord: rekey a Refounding's Private Channels under the prior root
description: A Refounding rekeys every Private Channel relevant to the removed user alongside the base roll (CORD-06 §3). Each such Channel rotation MUST be sealed and addressed under the PRIOR community_root, never the freshly minted one: if two Refoundings collide the base converges on one winner and the losers drop their new roots, so a Channel rekey sealed under a new root would be unreadable to every base-fork loser, while one sealed under the shared prior root stays openable on either branch. Public Channels need nothing — they rotate with the base for free (CORD-03).
acceptance_criteria: A Refounding that removes a member also rotates every Private Channel it holds a key for, each published at an address derived from the prior community_root, and a member on either branch of a racing base rotation can still open them.
notes:
Both halves already exist; this is the composition. gn_concord_community_service_rekey_channel_async() mints a scoped rotation and derive_channel_rekey_key() already derives from state->community_root, which during a Refounding's mint is still the prior root — adopt_base_rotation() runs at the very end of the chain.

So the ordering is the whole design: the Channel rotations must be published BEFORE adopt_base_rotation() swaps state->community_root, i.e. between the last rekey chunk and the adopt in rotation_publish_next_chunk(). Publishing them after adoption would address them under the new root and reintroduce exactly the race the prior-root rule exists to prevent.

Open question to settle first: which Channels are 'relevant to the removed user'. The service has no per-Channel access model — a Private Channel key arrives by invite or rekey and is held or not. The plausible reading is 'every Private Channel this device holds a key for', which is conservative and correct (rekeying one nobody lost access to is harmless, just wasteful); the excluded set is the same one the base rotation dropped.
close_reason: Refounding now rotates every held Private Channel between the last base rekey chunk and adopt_base_rotation(), so each rotation is sealed and addressed under the prior community_root and stays openable on either branch of a racing base rotation. Conservative set (every Private Channel this device holds a key for), captured before the first publish alongside the Memberlist and Control heads. A Refounder holding BAN but not MANAGE_CHANNELS is refused up front when it holds Private Channel keys, since every recipient enforces MANAGE_CHANNELS on a channel-scoped rotation and a half-severing would look complete. Per-Channel failures mid-flight are reported and non-fatal — the base roll is already published by then. Test /concord/refound/rotates-private-channels drives two racing Refoundings and shows a member on either branch opens a message in the rotated Channel. Live-arrival ordering hazard filed as nostrc-8h0l.

title: gnostr Concord: same-epoch rotation race convergence (CORD-06)
description: Split out of nostrc-knz4, whose channel-rekey half landed separately. Two rotations racing to the same epoch must converge deterministically on every client: among authorized candidates at the same continuity point, the lexicographically lowest new *base* key wins. The control_root pair rides the winner's blobs and is never compared. A losing Refounder re-issues only what its branch knew — its fresh channel keys — on the winning chain, and drops its own minted pair with its root. Both forks' keys are retained so messages sent into a losing fork stay readable, and the heal is down-only: a held epoch re-converges solely to a strictly lower sibling, so a flaky fetch that returns only the higher sibling can never re-fork a settled epoch.
design:
Design: docs/plans/concord-race-convergence.md (full detail).

Retention. CommunityState gains GPtrArray *retired of RetiredRoot {root hex secret, epoch, control_pk} — no control_root, a retired branch is read-only by construction. Bound CONCORD_RETIRED_ROOTS_MAX=8, prepend-newest/evict-tail; every retained root is a readable epoch, so the set is a credential surface and must not grow with history. Two producers, both in adopt_base_rotation(): a winning adopt retires the root it replaces (predecessor R0@N on a forward adopt, losing sibling R_X@N+1 on a heal); a *refused* sibling retires the root it just refused, which is what makes retention symmetric — a client that adopted the low root first still opened the high blob to compare it and must keep that fork's key. Consulted on failed opens: channel_key_candidates() (private Channels contribute one candidate — independently keyed, CORD-03; public ones one per retired root) selected by matching the wrap's pubkey against candidate pk, so selection costs no trial decryption; control_read_candidates() returns {key,address} pairs, address = control_pk or the legacy derivation at that entry's epoch. Guestbook deliberately has no fallback. refresh_channel() backfills retired addresses for public Channels. Persisted as a `retired` array in build_join_material() on the Community List direction only — never in an invite bundle, which would hand a joiner the epochs a Refounding severed — parsed back bounded+validated in accept_bundle(), carried over on a re-accepted link like control_root.

Down-only heal. One choke point at the top of adopt_base_rotation(): base_rotation_wins() = higher epoch always; same epoch only on strictly lower new root (g_strcmp0 < 0); lower epoch never. The control pair is never compared, it rides the winner. A replay of the adopted rotation compares equal and becomes a no-op. A flaky fetch returning only the higher sibling is refused structurally, not by ordering.

Reaching the competitor. Today the sibling never reaches ingest: the base rekey address derives from the root held now for root_epoch+1, and refresh_rekey_plane() unsubscribes the old address on adopt. Add a second, sibling plane derived from the retired root at root_epoch-1 for epoch root_epoch (state gains sibling_rekey_address/subscription, exactly one, backfilled). ingest_rotation_wrap() picks the plane by matching the wrap pubkey against the two derived addresses, then runs one path with the chosen new_epoch/held_epoch and recomputes continuity over the *retired* root via epoch_commitment_of(root_hex, epoch). Channel rotations keep single-address logic; a channel-scope race is a separate question.

Landmine 1 — adopt_base_rotation() clears state->rotations, which would drop the sibling still assembling the chunk set that decides the race. New rule: drop only entries whose new_epoch differs from the epoch just adopted; keep same-epoch siblings (a third, lower competitor may still be under judgment). Since entries now persist, bound the table at CONCORD_MAX_PENDING_ROTATIONS=16. Companion: conclude_rotation() must gate its removed_self verdict on state->root_epoch < pending->new_epoch — a losing sibling with no blob for this npub is not a removal when this device already holds that epoch under the winner. The rotator-outranks-target authority check stays unconditional.

Landmine 2 — adopt_base_rotation() sets refounder unconditionally. With the win-gate placed above the set_refounder() call, that becomes correct-by-construction: the function is only reached by a winner, so on a heal it overwrites the loser's refounder with the winner's. The comment must say so or the next reader will 'fix' it back.

Losing-Refounder re-issue. Its minted pair is dropped when the winner's adopt overwrites control_pk/control_root. Its fresh Channel keys need no re-mint — CORD-06 §3 already addresses a Refounding's channel rekeys under the *prior* root so they stay openable on either branch — but the address must not move under them mid-flight: RotationMint gains address_root captured up front, with derive_base_rekey_key_at()/derive_channel_rekey_key_at() variants (old signatures kept as wrappers). base_mint_superseded(state,mint) = root_epoch>new_epoch, or same epoch with a different held root; on supersession the loser abandons the base half (remaining base chunks, Control re-anchor, Guestbook snapshot — all statements about a dead root) and keeps publishing its Channel rotations under address_root. It must never mint a new base rotation at N+2 to reassert: that is an upward fork wearing a higher epoch.

Interface with nostrc-ay29: address channel rekeys from mint->address_root via derive_channel_rekey_key_at(), and let supersession skip the base half while the channel half continues. Those are the only two seams.

Tests: competing rotations hand-minted (a minted root is random; the test must name which is lower). Device 1 ingests high-then-low, device 2 low-then-high; both must end at the public Channel address the test derives independently from R_low. Device 2's address unchanged across the later higher sibling. A message published into the R_high fork opens on both devices after the heal. Community List round-trip of retired, and its absence from an invite bundle.
acceptance_criteria: Two rotations at one epoch converge on the lowest new base key on every client; a settled epoch never re-forks upward; messages sent into a losing fork stay readable after the heal.
notes:
Where this lands: gn-concord-community-service.c already accumulates competing rotations correctly — PendingRotation is keyed by (rotator, newepoch, prevcommit) in state->rotations precisely so two Rotators at one epoch never merge into one chunk set. What is missing is the comparison and the re-adopt.

Shape it as: on ingesting a rotation that carries this npub's locator while an epoch is already adopted at the same continuity point, decrypt that blob too and compare its new_key against the root currently held; adopt only if strictly lower (down-only). adopt_base_rotation() is already idempotent and re-points every plane, so the heal is a second call to it — but note it currently clears state->rotations, which must not drop a sibling still being judged.

The hard part is retention: 'both forks keys are retained so messages sent into a losing fork stay readable' has no structure today — CommunityState holds exactly one community_root. That needs a small set of retired roots per community (bounded), consulted by derive_channel_key/derive_control_read_key on a failed open, and it is the piece to design first.

Note adopt_base_rotation() currently sets refounder unconditionally; on a heal it must follow the winner.
close_reason: Closed

title: gnostr Concord: record the Refounding debt when another staffer's retire empties the set
description:
gn_concord_community_service_refounding_due() is recorded by the retire this client performs (CORD-06 §3). A retire by a different staffer that empties the aggregate active-set leaves this client's Community unmarked: it observes the Community turning Private through the Registry fold, but records no debt.

That is deliberate for now, not an oversight. A Registry edition carries no epoch, so a client backfilling one cannot tell a fresh retire from one a Refounding already paid years ago, and inferring the debt from the fold would resurrect settled debts on every fresh device.

The fix arrives with the rotation itself: once a Refounding stamps the epoch it minted, an observed empty active-set can be compared against the epoch of the last base rotation, and a debt is outstanding exactly when no rotation has happened since the Community went Private. File it against the rotation work rather than guessing earlier.
acceptance_criteria: Every staffer's client agrees on whether a Community owes a Refounding, however the last link was retired, and a fresh device never re-raises a debt an earlier Refounding paid.
close_reason: The debt is now recorded from the fold, not only from this client's own retire. apply_control_fold() tracks the Public/Private state it last folded (public_known/was_public on CommunityState) and records refounding_due_epoch = root_epoch + 1 when the aggregate active-set is seen *becoming* empty, whoever published the Registry edition that emptied it. Deliberately a transition and never a reading of current state: a Registry edition carries no epoch, so an empty set alone cannot distinguish a fresh retire from one a Refounding paid years ago — a device that arrives to an empty set has observed no transition and owes nothing. What made this sound is nostrc-hlyn's compaction: after a Refounding the history containing the old transition is no longer republished at the new epoch's address, so the only transitions left to observe are ones that genuinely owe. The local-retire path stays (it fires before the edition echoes back) and both are idempotent, guarded by refounding_due_epoch <= root_epoch. The debt still pays itself by the root roll. Tests: /concord/refound/debt-from-another-staffer (arriving Private owes nothing; mint then a retire published by the owner alone raises the debt on a device that only ever saw the editions) and /concord/refound/pays-the-debt (the rotation clears it with nothing resetting a flag). Full concord suite green under ASan. Commit f4d734a0.

title: gnostr Concord: channel rekeys (CORD-06)
description:
Two pieces of CORD-06 that a base rotation alone does not cover.

Channel rekeys: a single-channel rotation severs a removed user from one Private Channel, gated by MANAGE_CHANNELS, published at the concord/rekey-pseudonym address. In a Refounding, every Private Channel relevant to the removed user is rekeyed too — each sealed and addressed under the PRIOR community_root, never the freshly minted one, so that if two Refoundings collide the channel rekey stays openable on either branch. Public Channels rotate with the base for free (CORD-03).

Race convergence: among authorized candidates at the same continuity point the lexicographically lowest new base key wins; the control_root pair rides the winner's blobs and is never compared; a losing Refounder re-issues only what its branch knew (its fresh channel keys) on the winning chain and drops its own minted pair. Both forks' keys are retained so messages sent into a losing fork stay readable, and the heal is down-only — a held epoch re-converges solely to a strictly lower sibling, so a flaky fetch returning only the higher sibling can never re-fork a settled epoch.

The crypto surface both need is in place: nostr_concord_channel_rekey_key(), nostr_concord_rekey_locator() and nostr_concord_epoch_commitment() (nip-concord, CORD-06 §1–§2).
acceptance_criteria: A Private Channel rekeys independently of the base; a Refounding's channel rekeys are addressed under the prior root; two rotations at one epoch converge on the lowest new base key on every client, and a settled epoch never re-forks upward.
close_reason: Independent single-Channel rotation landed; the two clauses that were bundled here are split out with precise notes (nostrc-ay29 Refounding integration, nostrc-r874 race convergence). The rotation path is now scoped rather than base-only: one implementation carries a scope that decides the address, the blob width, the epoch that moves and the permission it takes. Base = 104/136 bytes at the all-zero scope, BAN, moves the root; Channel = 72 bytes at the Channel id, MANAGE_CHANNELS, moves only that Channel's key. Shared: locator search, continuity check over the key held now, chunking at 120, and the rule that only a complete set without this npub's locator is a removal. New surface: gn_concord_community_service_rekey_channel_async/_finish (excluded-member list, refuses a public Channel outright and refuses to exclude anyone the Rotator does not strictly outrank — enforced at the mint so an unenforceable rotation never reaches the wire), gn_concord_community_service_ingest_channel_rekey_wrap(), a per-Private-Channel rekey subscription at the precomputed next address, adopt_channel_rotation(), and gn_concord_channel_item_set_key(key, epoch) which moves key and epoch together because the plane address derives from both. Addressed under the community_root rather than the Channel key it replaces (CORD-06 §2), which is what keeps a member losing the Channel reachable and what ay29 depends on. Found and fixed a real hole while testing: the shared locator derived at the base scope unconditionally, so a Channel rotation would have addressed every blob to a locator nobody computes — a rotation delivering nothing, which every recipient reads as everyone being removed. Tests /concord/rekey/channel-roundtrip (rotate, adopt, converge on a message in the rotated Channel, a stale device cannot find the address, and the base epoch is untouched so no Refounding is owed) and /concord/rekey/channel-refusals (public Channel, and a Rotator without MANAGE_CHANNELS). All 45 concord tests green under ASan. Commit 17257877.

title: gnostr Concord: seed the new epoch's Guestbook with a membership snapshot (CORD-06 §3)
description:
The last step of a Refounding publishes the prior epoch's coalesced Guestbook into the new one as kind-3312 snapshots, chunked at CONCORD_SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_SIZE. It is best-effort: a Refounding succeeds with or without it, and a member who enters the new epoch and finds their own state absent simply republishes a Join.

The receiving half is already complete (nostrc-3mkc): the fold honors a snapshot only from the npub whose Refounding minted the epoch, and gn_concord_community_service_set_refounder() names that npub. Only the publishing half is missing, and it becomes reachable once a Refounding exists to attribute a snapshot to.
acceptance_criteria: After a Refounding, the new epoch's Guestbook carries the prior epoch's present members as refounder-signed kind-3312 chunks, and a fresh device folds them into the same Complete Memberlist.
close_reason: Publishing half landed as the Refounding's final, best-effort step. After the root roll and the Control re-anchor, the Rotator publishes the prior epoch's present members — the same Complete Memberlist the blobs were addressed to — as kind-3312 rumors in encrypted seals at the NEW epoch's Guestbook address, chunked at CONCORD_SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_SIZE (400) with ['snap', id, i, n]. The snapshot id is the rotation's prevcommit, so a resumed Refounder re-publishes the same set rather than racing a second one. Failures emit an error and leave the Refounding successful (a member finding their own state absent republishes a Join, so an unsent snapshot is a blip where a failed rotation would be a fork). Receiving half was already complete (nostrc-3mkc); what closes the loop is that adopt_base_rotation() sets the refounder from the rotation the device just adopted, so a receiver learns whom to honor from the rotation itself and not from the snapshot claiming it. Test /concord/refound/seeds-guestbook: a device that adopts the rotation with no Guestbook fold of its own is offered every published event, opens exactly the one chunk at its new Guestbook address, and ends up with all three prior-epoch members — proving both the seeding and the refounder attribution. Full concord suite green under ASan. Commit a80eda37.

title: gnostr Concord: mint and adopt the base rotation a Refounding turns on (CORD-06)
description:
Re-scoped 2026-08-11 after landing the CORD-06 crypto surface and the trigger. What remains is the rotation itself: the base roll that a Refounding is.

Mint: roll the community_root and mint a fresh control_root beside it (CORD-02 §2), build one blob per member of the Complete Memberlist — 104 bytes for a member, 136 for staff — wrap each under the Rotator-to-recipient NIP-44 conversation key, locate it with nostr_concord_rekey_locator(), chunk at 120 recipients per event with matching ['chunk', i, n] tags, and publish each as a kind-3303 rumor in a 20013 seal under a 1059 wrap at the base-rekey address derived from the PRIOR root at root_epoch+1. Cite the Grant the rotation acts under (CORD-04 vac) and carry prevepoch/prevcommit from nostr_concord_epoch_commitment() over the key currently held. Then adopt locally: bump root_epoch, take the new control_pk and control_root, re-derive and resubscribe every plane, and call gn_concord_community_service_set_refounder() with this npub so the new epoch's Guestbook snapshots are honored.

Adopt: subscribe the next base-rekey address alongside the current planes, compute this npub's locator in each chunk, verify continuity (prevcommit over the held key; a mismatch with a higher prevepoch means fetch the gap first, anything else is a fork — reject), verify the seal's npub holds BAN and outranks every target against the folded Roster, then adopt the same way and set the refounder to the seal's npub. Only once all n chunks are held and none carries this locator has this member been removed — a missing chunk is never a removal.

Both halves are idempotent and resumable: re-sending blobs re-delivers the same keys, and the state being rotated is acquired in full before the first publish.

Rolling root_epoch is also what pays the debt gn_concord_community_service_refounding_due() records, so no reset is needed.
notes:
Landed already, in this bead's first pass:

- nips/nip-concord CORD-06 §1–§2 crypto: nostr_concord_base_rekey_key() and
  nostr_concord_channel_rekey_key() (prior root, new epoch),
  nostr_concord_rekey_locator() (the 64-byte two-pubkey ikm),
  nostr_concord_epoch_commitment() (CORD-02 A.5), the base scope id, and
  rekey blob pack/parse across all four forms — including the unspliceable
  binding (a blob's own scope and epoch are checked against the event's tags,
  never read from them) and the staff-form check that new_control_root
  derives exactly new_control_pk. Known-answer vectors freeze the layout.
- The trigger: the retire that empties the aggregate active-set records the
  Refounding debt against the epoch that would pay it, syncs it in the
  Community List entry, and reports it through
  gn_concord_community_service_refounding_due().

Blocked on nostrc-3m86: a blob is 72/104/136 raw bytes and the plugin API's
only pairwise NIP-44 entry point takes a UTF-8 string, so a bunker cannot
wrap one today. signet already speaks the base64 lane (cdbc6d37); the client
half is missing.

The two seams this bead named are still the landing points: set_refounder()
takes the Rotator npub the adopt path learns, and CommunityState.control_root
is what a base rotation mints afresh and delivers in the same blobs.
close_reason: Base rotation lands, both halves. Mint: gn_concord_community_service_refound_async() rolls community_root, mints a fresh control_root beside it and derives new_control_pk at root_epoch+1, wraps one blob per Complete Memberlist member (104 member / 136 staff, staff = CONCORD_PERMS_STAFF or owner) under the pairwise key via the new binary NIP-44 lane, locates each with nostr_concord_rekey_locator(), chunks at 120 with matching ['chunk',i,n], and publishes each chunk as a kind-3303 rumor in a 20013 seal under a 1059 wrap at nostr_concord_base_rekey_key(PRIOR root, id, root_epoch+1), carrying scope/newepoch/prevepoch/prevcommit plus the CORD-04 vac citation (factored into append_grant_citation(), now shared with the Control Plane writer). Takes BAN. The Rotator is always its own recipient. Adopt happens only after every chunk's publication is confirmed, so a mid-flight failure leaves the Community resumable on its current epoch. Adopt: gn_concord_community_service_ingest_rekey_wrap() + a refresh_rekey_plane() subscription at the precomputed next address; verifies seal Rotator against the folded Roster (BAN, not banned), base scope, newepoch, and continuity via nostr_concord_epoch_commitment() over the held key (higher prevepoch reports a gap, anything else drops); accumulates chunks per (rotator,newepoch,prevcommit) so racing Rotators never merge; adopts on the first chunk carrying this npub's locator (a rotation handing you a key cannot be removing you); on a complete set judges every target and drops the whole rotation if the Rotator does not strictly outrank one, concluding removal only when all n chunks are held and none carries this locator. adopt_base_rotation() re-points Control/Guestbook/channel addresses while KEEPING the folds (CORD-06 §3 graceful degradation), sets the refounder for snapshot honoring, and republishes the Community List; the debt clears itself because root_epoch reaches refounding_due_epoch. Tests /concord/refound/roundtrip (3 services: mint, adopt, and one that never receives it — convergence proven by a public-Channel message crossing the boundary, plus replay idempotence) and /concord/refound/requires-ban (mint refused without BAN; a rotation resealed by a roleless holder of the prior root dropped on rank alone). Green under ASan; the suite also caught a real use-after-free (adopt context borrowed the service across an async signer call) now fixed with a strong ref. Commits 73e67d1a, ce2409ce.

title: gnostr Concord: fold Guestbook snapshots (kind 3312)
description: The Guestbook fold ignores kind-3312 snapshots. A snapshot is the refounder's secondhand attestation, honored only from the npub whose Refounding minted the epoch, and the plugin does not yet track refounders. Consequence today is a blip, not a disappearance: a member entering a new epoch and finding their state absent republishes a Join. Folding them needs the Refounding path (CORD-06) plus the CORD-02 §5 rules — seed at the snapshot timestamp, superseded by any newer self-signed entry or authorized Kick, chunked at 400 with one shared id and timestamp, and a partially received snapshot still useful.
notes:
Folded in a461feda.

The kind-3312 fold now implements the CORD-02 §5 rules in full:
- seeds an npub at the snapshot's own timestamp, so anything newer (self-signed
  Join/Leave, authorized Kick) supersedes it by ordering alone;
- at an exact timestamp tie the member's own word beats the attestation, since
  a snapshot is secondhand — MemberEntry carries a `secondhand` flag for that
  one comparison;
- absence means "no seed", never a negative state: nothing in the snapshot path
  can mark anyone departed;
- chunks fold independently (a partial snapshot seeds whoever arrived), the
  `snap` tag's id is required and its index/count must cohere, and a chunk is
  capped at CONCORD_SNAPSHOT_CHUNK_SIZE members before anything is allocated.

The refounder-tracking half the description called out is now an explicit input
rather than a guess: gn_concord_guestbook_set_refounder() /
gn_concord_community_service_set_refounder() name the npub whose Refounding
minted the epoch — per CORD-06 §1 that is the Rotator, the seal's npub on the
base rekey. With none set, no snapshot is honored, which is where production
sits until the Refounding path lands (nostrc-vhtt); that bead's base-rekey
adoption is the one caller, a single call.

Consequence today is unchanged and remains a blip, not a disappearance: a member
entering a new epoch and finding their state absent republishes a Join.

Tests: /concord/guestbook/snapshot-seeds (unattributed dropped, impostor
dropped, refounder honored, newer Leave supersedes, later snapshot re-seeds),
/concord/guestbook/snapshot-chunks-stand-alone (partial chunk useful, absence is
not a Leave, own Join stands, misnumbered and unidentified chunks refused).
ctest green, ASan clean.
close_reason: Snapshot fold implemented with the §5 rules and tested; the refounder is now an explicit input, and wiring it is nostrc-vhtt's base-rekey adoption.

title: gnostr Concord: Guestbook plane (Join/Leave) and Direct Invites
description: Two gaps left by nostrc-3j9q. (1) CORD-05 §1: accepting an invite should publish a self-signed kind-3306 Join to the Guestbook plane (echoing the bundle's creator/label attribution), and leaving a Leave; the fold coalesces per npub with the one-hour future-clock drop. nostr_concord_guestbook_key already exists. (2) CORD-05 §6: index Direct Invites with {kinds:[1059], #p:[me], #k:[3313]}, unwrap the standard NIP-59 giftwrap (kind-13 seal, not the reversed stream wrap) and offer its bundle to the same accept path.
close_reason: Guestbook plane folds Join/Leave/Kick with the one-hour future drop and forward-only observation; accepting an invite announces a Join with the link's attribution and leaving publishes a Leave plus a Community List tombstone. Direct Invites are indexed by the k tag and unwrapped as standard NIP-59, which needed a pairwise NIP-44 pair on the plugin API.

title: gnostr Concord: Control Plane fold (CORD-04 editions)
description: The plugin currently learns its channels only from the invite bundle, which CORD-02 §6 calls a join-time snapshot — the Control Plane fold is always the authority. Subscribe the Control Plane at control_pk, decrypt wraps with the community_root-derived read key, and fold vsk-0 metadata, vsk-2 channel definitions, vsk-3 grants and vsk-4 banlist per CORD-04's edition and version rules, including the pre-split legacy address. nostr_concord_control_read_key and control_signer_key already exist.
close_reason: Control Plane fold implemented: CORD-04 editions (hash, chain, refuse-downgrade, deterministic tiebreak, vac block-until-synced) over an owner-rooted Roster, folding vsk 0/1/2/3/4, at both the split control_pk address and the legacy pre-split one.

title: gnostr plugin API: NIP-44 self-encrypt/decrypt capability
description: The plugin context exposes request_sign_event but no way to encrypt or decrypt to the user's own key, so a plugin cannot read any NIP-44 self-encrypted document. This blocks the Concord Community List (kind 13302) and Invite List (kind 13303), which forced the Concord plugin to keep memberships in plugin-local storage instead. Add a self-ECDH encrypt/decrypt pair to GnostrPluginContext, routed through the same signer that owns the key.
close_reason: Host plugin API gains nip44_self_encrypt/decrypt routed through the signer; the Concord plugin's memberships are lifted off plugin-local storage onto the wire as the kind-13302 Community List, with round-trip preservation and a fail-closed read guard.

title: gnostr Concord: invite creation UI (mint link, publish bundle, Invite List)
description: Follow-up to nostrc-3j9q, which shipped invite *accept* only. Mint a fresh link signer, publish the encrypted kind-33301 bundle at its (kind, signer, empty-d) coordinate, build the base64url fragment (version 4, relay dictionary), and keep the creator's kind-13303 Invite List in sync. Revocation re-posts the coordinate as a vsk-9 tombstone. The nip-concord library already exposes bundle encrypt, invite_key, the relay dictionary and fragment parsing; fragment *encoding* is the missing library piece.
notes:
Shipped in 40b34f7d (Registry fold), 79fc3527 (mint/retire) and 755ed007 (UI).

Library: nostr_concord_invite_registry_locator() for the A.6
concord/invite-links coordinate. nip19's naddr encoder refused an empty
identifier, which is exactly the coordinate CORD-05 §2 requires — fixed, and
the decoder already accepted one.

Control Plane: vsk-8 Registry editions fold per creator into one aggregate
active-set, honored only at invite_registry_locator(community_id, actor) and
only while its author holds CREATE_INVITE. is_public() is that set being
non-empty. Publishing Control editions arrived with it: plaintext seal, wrap
signed by the control_root-derived signer, encrypted under the member read
key, with the vac citation pinning a non-owner's Grant. Legacy pre-split
epochs write at the read derivation.

Service: mint publishes bundle -> Registry -> Invite List in that order (the
ordering trap: a Registry naming a coordinate with no bundle reads as a live
link that cannot be followed); retire publishes tombstone -> Registry ->
Invite List for the mirror reason. Kind-13303 Invite List with the same
fail-closed 'never publish before a definitive read' guard the Community List
uses — it needs it more, since it holds every link's signer secret. Tokens
are 16 CSPRNG bytes, the link signer is a fresh keypair used for nothing else,
and control_root now rides the Community List between a staffer's own devices
and is deliberately absent from every bundle.

UI: an Invite links window on the community view — name/mint (auto-copied,
since the fragment is the token's only written-down form), live-link list with
copy/retire, and the CREATE_INVITE gate shown rather than failed at.

Tests: /concord/control/invite-registry, /concord/invite/mint-roundtrip (full
three-event round trip incl. published-order assertions, bundle decrypt from
the fragment, and 'no control_root in the bundle'), mint-fails-closed,
mint-requires-permission, /concord/ui/invite-dialog, plus the nip19 empty-d
round trip. ctest green, ASan clean.

Deferred: retiring the last live link should trigger a Refounding (CORD-06) —
filed as nostrc-vhtt. Today it leaves the Community correctly Private with no
key rotation.
close_reason: Invite creation shipped: Registry fold, mint/retire with the ordering trap handled, kind-13303 Invite List, and the invite-link window. Refounding on the last retire deferred to nostrc-vhtt.

title: restore-scroll should block widget velocity tracker around programmatic set_value
description: apps/gnostr/src/ui/gnostr-main-window-timeline.c:218 writes the vadjustment directly during controller-driven restores. It guards the controller feedback loop via timeline_scroll_restore_depth, but NostrGtkTimelineView's on_scroll_value_changed still observes the jump, so a large restore can set is_fast_scrolling=TRUE and make the app factory defer metadata loads for one ~150ms idle window. The now-deleted on_vadj_upper_notify used g_signal_handlers_block_by_func around its own writes; that idiom no longer exists in the tree. If the deferral heuristic is meant to track user scrolling only, apply the same block around gtk_adjustment_set_value. Found during review of b8296777 (finding C).
close_reason: Closed

title: nostr_gtk_timeline_view_set_tree_roots: handler leak and unbalanced unref
description: nostr-gtk/src/gnostr-timeline-view.c:423-452. (1) g_signal_connect(roots, 'items-changed', ...) on every call with no disconnect - repeated calls multiply handlers and leave self dangling if roots outlives the view. (2) self->tree_model = (GtkTreeListModel*)roots takes no reference and is an unchecked cast, yet dispose() and set_model() both g_clear_object(&self->tree_model) - unbalanced unref. Currently harmless: the function has no callers (dead API, same status as prepend/prepend_text). Either fix or explicitly deprecate. Found during review of b8296777 (finding B).

title: TimelineView dispose can re-arm scroll idle timeout after removal
description: nostr-gtk/src/gnostr-timeline-view.c dispose() clears scroll_idle_id before gtk_list_view_set_model(NULL) and gtk_widget_dispose_template(). The vadjustment 'value-changed' handler is never disconnected, and on_scroll_value_changed() unconditionally re-arms g_timeout_add(..., self). If teardown triggers a value-changed emission, a fresh timeout is scheduled after the removal and can fire on a finalized object. Fix: disconnect on_scroll_value_changed from vadj at the top of dispose(), or move the scroll_idle_id removal after dispose_template. Found during review of b8296777 (see docs/reviews/review-nostrc-2lyk-scroll-modifier-removal.md, finding A).

title: porthome: self-hosted permissive Blossom server for the lab jmx0 demo
description: Option A fallback per the hy3e/jmx0 investigation. hy3e proved that only two community Blossom servers accept portable-home traffic in v1: blossom.sharegap.net (raw octet-stream) and blossom.primal.net (PNG-shim wrapped). blossom.band runs a full PNG decoder on ingest and refuses shimmed random bytes with 500 unknown error. For the lab CI's two-machine §9.4 demo we depend on primal being reachable and permissive; that is fragile. Design a small self-hosted permissive Blossom server (or lightweight sinatra-esque adapter) that we can stand up alongside the lab relay and use as the second replica when neither community server is cooperating. Scope: docker-compose recipe or a systemd unit under packaging/, no auth beyond the standard BUD-02, no thumbnailing, no rewriting, no size cap below 4 MiB. Runs on the same public IP as the lab relay so SSRF pre-check in nostr-home-fetch passes without --allow-lan-blossom. Belongs to the packaging / lab CI story, not the provisioner code path — this is the operator-side path that sidesteps both the primal fragility and the blossom.band sniffer problem.

title: blossom.band conformance note: x-tag binding not enforced when server tag omitted
description: Observed during nostrc-yo44 probe (2026-09-24, pubkey 403c237d81b0cebc0aa850b4420062896c374ee83115c8e3574de25fe4089ae6). blossom.band's BUD-02 impl rejects the auth event with 401 'server tags do not include this server' whenever a 'server' tag is present in any URL form (https://blossom.band, trailing slash, host-only, etc.). Omitting the 'server' tag lets the event through — but at that point, a PUT with an auth event whose x tag does NOT match the request body's sha256 still returns 415 (content-policy), not 401 (auth). Compare to blossom.primal.net which returns 401 'invalid x tag' in the identical mismatch scenario. This is a mild BUD-02 conformance gap on blossom.band worth flagging to the operator; not blocking porthome and not affecting the D8 verdict. If we ever choose to file upstream, evidence is in docs/reviews/porthome-blossom-batch-auth-2026-09-24.md §2.

profile refresh: accounts-daemon sources RealName from pw_gecos, NOT from /var/lib/AccountsService/users/<user> keyfile's RealName= key. That's why the profile pipeline updates the passwd.gecos column in the NSS projection SQLite (via nh_profile_projection_update_gecos) instead of relying on SetRealName D-Bus or the keyfile. SetRealName additionally invokes usermod which refuses to touch accounts not in /etc/passwd, so it fails silently for every nostr-homed user.

signet SQLCipher migration (nostrc-abe): store.c auto-migrates legacy plaintext SQLite DBs to SQLCipher on open when linked with sqlcipher (runtime probe via :memory: PRAGMA cipher_version). Detection = 'SQLite format 3\0' 16-byte magic. Migration = ATTACH DATABASE tmp KEY + SELECT sqlcipher_export('encrypted') + DETACH; hardened with EXCLUSIVE lock (BEGIN IMMEDIATE), wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE)+journal_mode=DELETE, verify+fsync temp, crash-safe link()/copy backup to <db>.plaintext-backup, remove plaintext -wal/-shm BEFORE atomic rename(tmp,db), fsync parent dir, sodium_memzero key strings. Env SIGNET_MIGRATE_PLAINTEXT_DB=false to refuse instead. Public API signet_store_migrate_plaintext_to_sqlcipher/file_is_plaintext_sqlite/sqlcipher_available. signetctl migrate-db command. Build: meson -Dsignet_use_sqlcipher=true / cmake -DSIGNET_USE_SQLCIPHER=ON (brew install sqlcipher for local test).
